headline: Smith finished with an interception and 11 tackles (five solo) in Sunday's 41-23 win over the Colts.
story: The inside linebacker was characteristically all over the field in Baltimore's convincing win. Smith recorded at least 130 tackles in all three of his previous seasons with the Ravens, and he remains at the center of the team's defense.

headline: The Ravens aren't expected to deal Henry before Tuesday's trade deadline, Adam Schefter of ESPN reports.
story: With Baltimore sitting at 4-5 and having lost its top two QBs in Lamar Jackson (thumb) and Tyler Huntley (toe) for the foreseeable future and rest of the season, respectively, there has been speculation Henry may be available via trade, but the team has informed the running back that it doesn't intend to consider such a transaction. Instead, the Ravens have dealt for quarterback Jacoby Brissett from the Cardinals to help stabilize the offense, which may help Henry end his streak being held under 100 yards rushing at four contests. Overall, Henry has racked up 689 yards and eight touchdowns on 175 carries for a career-low 3.9 YPC in his nine appearances in 2026.

headline: Henry rushed 17 times for 57 yards in the Ravens' 33-10 loss to the Jaguars on Thursday night. He also completed one pass attempt for minus-3 yards.
story: With Joe Fagnano under center, the Jaguars unsurprisingly had the luxury of loading up to slow down Henry, and Jacksonville already came into the contest boasting an elite run defense to begin with. Henry therefore ran into a proverbial brick wall for most of the night, and he finished under 60 rushing yards for the fourth consecutive game. However, help is on the way, as impending trade acquisition Jacoby Brissett could be ready to make his first start for the Ravens as soon as a Week 10 home matchup against the Chargers on Monday night, Nov. 16.

headline: Henry rushed 11 times for 53 yards and a touchdown and brought in both targets for seven yards in the Ravens' 36-10 loss to the Bills on Sunday.
story: It was a nightmare of an afternoon for the Ravens offense, which lost both Lamar Jackson (thumb) and Tyler Huntley (toe) during the first half and struggled to move the ball with emergency quarterback Joe Fagnano at the helm. Henry's rushing opportunities ultimately suffered as Baltimore's deficit grew, but he managed to punch in a two-yard touchdown run late in the first quarter before matters got out of hand. It's been a relatively rough three-game stretch for Henry following a 102-yard effort on the ground against the Falcons in Week 5, and with reports emerging Jackson will be placed on injured reserve, the talented back's best hope for reasonable game scripts for the foreseeable future lies in Huntley's ability to regain health.

headline: Henry rushed 17 times for 45 yards and brought in one of two target for four yards in the Ravens' 35-13 loss to the Bengals on Sunday.
story: Henry averaged below 3.5 yards per carry for the second consecutive game against a divisional opponent, and Sunday's inefficiency also dropped his season per-carry average under 4.0 (3.9). The bruising back does have seven rushing touchdowns on the season, but none have come within the last three games. Henry will look to bounce back to his usual level of production in a Week 8 road showdown against an improved Bills run defense next Sunday.

headline: Henry rushed 17 times for 58 yards and brought in his only target for two yards in the Ravens' 13-10 loss to the Browns on Sunday. He also lost a fumble.
story: Henry looked like he was on his way to one of his signature performances when he rattled off 11- and 17-yard gains on Baltimore's opening possession, but the veteran back found running room at a premium for most of the rest of the contest. Henry finished without a touchdown for the second straight game and tallied his lowest rushing yardage total of the campaign, while his early fourth-quarter fumble led to a Browns game-tying touchdown. Henry will aim to bounce back in a Week 7 home divisional matchup against the Bengals next Sunday.

headline: Henry rushed 24 times for 102 yards while catching one of two targets for an 18-yard touchdown in Sunday's 30-23 overtime win over the Falcons. He also ran in a two-point conversion.
story: Henry unsurprisingly worked as the focal point of Baltimore's offense in the absence of Lamar Jackson (ankle). The star running back pulled the Ravens within two points with his 18-yard touchdown catch in the third quarter. Baltimore's two-point conversion attempt after that touchdown failed, but Henry took matters into his own hands to convert a game-tying two-point conversion out of the wildcat formation with 40 seconds left in the fourth quarter. He then tacked on 32 rushing yards on Baltimore's touchdown drive in OT to top the century mark on the ground for the first time since Week 1. Henry has opened his 11th NFL season with a five-game touchdown streak, producing seven rushing touchdowns and one receiving score ahead of a Week 6 trip to Cleveland.

headline: Henry carried the ball 23 times for 73 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 24-18 win over the Titans. He also caught both his targets for six yards.
story: The star RB found the end zone for a fourth straight game to begin the season, rumbling in for a five-yard score on the Ravens' first possession. Henry already has seven rushing TDs, putting him firmly on pace for his ninth straight season in double digits, to go along with 374 rushing yards on 4.2 yards per carry. He'll look to extend his TD streak in in a Week 5 road trip to Atlanta.

headline: Henry rushed 26 times for 89 yards and two touchdowns while catching his lone target for no gain in Sunday's 34-31 win over the Cowboys.
story: Henry scored a four-yard rushing touchdown in the first quarter and a three-yard rushing touchdown in the second quarter, but he was denied the hat trick in the fourth quarter, when a would-be third rushing score was ruled down at the 1-yard line on replay, and Henry's subsequent effort to get in on fourth down was stuffed. The 32-year-old Henry is showing no signs of slowing down, as he has six touchdowns through three games and is averaging just over 100 rushing yards per game heading into a Week 4 home game against the winless Titans.

headline: Henry carried the ball 16 times for 68 yards and a touchdown and caught all three of his targets for 19 yards in Sunday's 24-17 loss to the Saints.
story: The five-time Pro Bowler punched it in from one yard out on a wildcat snap late in the first quarter to open the scoring. Henry wasn't able to break any big gains, however, with his longest run going for just eight yards. He's made four trips to the end zone in two games to begin the season, piling up 214 rushing yards and 38 receiving yards as well, and Henry will look to keep rolling in a Week 3 road trip to Dallas.

headline: Henry rushed 24 times for 144 yards and three touchdowns and brought in his only target for 19 yards in the Ravens' 41-23 win over the Colts on Sunday.
story: Much like he'd done at the expense of the Bills in Week 1 of last season, Henry turned in one of his signature performances right out of the gate, and he struck for his first two touchdowns in the first half from four and 32 yards away. The superstar running back added a three-yard scoring run early in the fourth quarter, and he consistently ripped off chunk gains throughout the afternoon at the expense of an overwhelmed Colts front. Henry's workload won't change under new head coach Jesse Minter if Sunday is any indication, and the perennial Pro Bowl back carries a stellar outlook for a Week 2 home matchup against a Saints defense that the Lions' Jahmyr Gibbs gashed for 156 rushing yards and two touchdowns Sunday.

headline: Hibner logged one reception for five yards on two targets in Thursday's loss to Baltimore.
story: Hibner ranked second among Baltimore tight ends with 30 offensive snaps, just behind Mark Andrews (32). The former didn't do much with the opportunity, but it was a very quiet game for the Ravens' passing game as a whole, as starting QB Joe Fagnano threw for just 60 yards. Baltimore will likely have the recently acquired Jacoby Brissett starting behind center for the team's next game (Monday, Oct. 16 versus the Chargers), but Hibner has just six catches across eight contests this season, so he's not a viable fantasy option regardless of who is throwing him the ball.

headline: Hibner (hand) was a full participant at practice Thursday.
story: Hibner managed a full practice Thursday for the first time since he hurt his hand back in Week 5 at Atlanta, suggesting he'll more than likely be available in Week 7 versus the Bengals. Before getting hurt, he was operating as Baltimore's secondary tight end, filling a complementary role relative to veteran starter Mark Andrews.

headline: Hibner (hand) was a limited participant in Wednesday's practice.
story: The rookie tight end didn't practice in any fashion last week before being ruled out ahead of an eventual 13-10 loss to the Browns, but he took a step forward in his recovery from the injury by getting back on the field for the Ravens' first Week 7 session. Per Jonas Shaffer of TheBaltimoreBanner.com, Hibner had his left hand heavily taped during Wednesday's practice, and he may need to upgrade to full participation by Friday in order for the Ravens to feel comfortable making him available for Sunday's contest versus the Bengals.

headline: Hibner (hand) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Browns.
story: Hibner was held out of practice all week due to a hand injury that he sustained during the Ravens' Week 5 overtime win over the Falcons. Per Brian Wacker of The Baltimore Sun, Hibner is not considered to be a candidate for injured reserve, so the rookie tight end could be back in action as soon as Week 7 against the Bengals. In Hibner's absence, Josh Cuevas and Nick Vannett are both in line for more snaps on offense while operating behind TE1 Mark Andrews.

headline: Hibner (hand) did not practice Thursday.
story: Hibner injured his hand in Sunday's overtime win over Atlanta. While he managed to return to the contest, he has since missed the Ravens' last two practice sessions. Hibner will likely need to practice Friday if he hopes to avoid an injury designation ahead of Sunday's game against Cleveland. If he can't get on the field in Week 6, Josh Cuevas and Nick Vannett would presumably see more targets behind Mark Andrews.

headline: Hibner (hand) did not participate at practice Wednesday.
story: Hibner was able to play through the hand injury he suffered during Sunday's game at Atlanta, but it looks like it's still bothering him as the Ravens begin preparing for Week 6. He'll likely need to get back on the practice field Thursday or Friday to give himself a realistic chance to play Sunday at Cleveland.

headline: Hibner (hand) has returned to action Sunday night against the Falcons, Jeff Zrebiec of The Athletic reports.
story: Hibner sustained a hand injury in the first half but has returned to the field after the break. The tight end will operate as the No. 2 option at his position behind Mark Andrews for the final stretch of the contest.

headline: Hibner (hand) is questionable to return to Sunday night's contest against the Falcons.
story: Hibner suffered a hand injury in the first quarter, and his availability for the rest of the contest is now uncertain. In his absence, Mark Andrews will continue to handle the lion's share of the workload at tight end.

headline: Hibner caught both of his targets for 34 yards in Sunday's 24-18 win over the Titans.
story: Both Hibner and Mark Andrews played 37 of 64 offensive snaps against Tennessee, though Andrews ran 24 routes to Hibner's 10, as the latter is more of the blocking complement to Andrews in the pass-catching role. The fourth-round rookie Hibner has secured all five of his targets for 70 yards and a touchdown through four games.

headline: Hibner caught his only target for 13 yards in the Ravens' 41-23 win over the Colts on Sunday.
story: Hibner played 23 offensive snaps in the contest, shifting into the offense when the Ravens lined up for 13-personnel packages. The fourth-round rookie also played nine special-teams snaps, displaying his versatility.

headline: Lane did not draw a target Thursday in a loss to Jacksonville.
story: Lane logged 32 offensive snaps, third-most among Baltimore wideouts behind Zay Flowers (37) and Rashod Bateman (35). However, Lane failed to haul in a pass (and to even see a target) for the first time this season. That can be partly attributed to quarterback play, as Ravens starting QB Joe Fagnano threw for just 60 yards. Jacoby Brissett, who Baltimore recently traded for, will likely start behind center in Week 10 against the Chargers on Monday, Nov. 16, which would improve Lane's outlook to some degree. However, he's caught one or fewer passes in three of his five games so far this season, so Lane isn't a recommended fantasy play regardless of who is starting at QB for Baltimore.

headline: Lane caught his only target for 13 yards in Sunday's 36-10 loss to the Bills.
story: The rookie wideout ran 21 routes on 30 dropbacks by Baltimore's three quarterbacks, but his one target represented just a 3.8 percent share. With Lamar Jackson (thumb) and Tyler Huntley (toe) both injured, Joe Fagnano (ankle) could be in line to start Thursday night against the Jaguars. It would be a downgrade for all Ravens skill players.

headline: Lane caught three of five targets for 25 yards during Sunday's 35-13 loss to the Bengals.
story: Lane finished second on the team in targets behind fellow wideout Zay Flowers (11), and he was able to reel in at least three passes for the second straight week. With Lamar Jackson (ankle) nearing a return to action, Lane may be able to establish himself as a reliable red-zone threat for Baltimore moving forward this season. The rookie's next chance to record his first career touchdown will come in Week 8 versus the Bills.

headline: Lane brought in four of five targets for 40 yards in the Ravens' 13-10 loss to the Browns on Sunday.
story: Lane was making his return from a four-game stint on IR due to a wrist injury, and he set new career highs across the board after having gotten hurt in Week 1. He tied for second in receptions and targets while slotting in third in receiving yards on the afternoon for the Ravens. Lane's chemistry with Tyler Huntley was encouraging, but the rookie wideout's fantasy upside could truly be unlocked once he has a stretch of games to work with Lamar Jackson (ankle).

headline: Lane (wrist) is active for Sunday's game against the Browns.
story: After injuring his left wrist in the Ravens' Week 1 win over the Colts and landing on injured reserve, Lane was cleared to resume practicing Wednesday. The rookie wideout proceeded to turn in three consecutive full sessions, and the Ravens came away satisfied enough with his health to bring him back from IR. Lane could immediately settle in as the Ravens' No. 3 wideout behind Zay Flowers and Rashod Bateman as he makes his return to the lineup.

headline: Lane (wrist) was activated from injured reserve by Baltimore on Saturday.
story: Although Lane is still listed as questionable, his activation from IR puts the rookie wide receiver on track to return for Sunday's game against the Browns. Lane was one of the Ravens' standout players during training camp, so he could be featured prominently in the offense alongside Zay Flowers and Rashod Bateman in his return.

headline: Lane (wrist) is "good to go" after practicing fully this week and is expected to be activated from injured reserve ahead of Sunday's game against the Browns, Jeremy Fowler of ESPN reports.
story: Lane strung together a trio of full practices to draw the questionable tag for Week 6. It looks like the Ravens will have their rookie third-round wide receiver back on the field for Sunday's AFC North showdown, and Lane could slide right back into the WR2 role behind Zay Flowers and in front of Rashod Bateman. Lane fractured his wrist during the Ravens' Week 1 win against the Colts, when he caught one of three targets for 11 yards (with two of those targets occurring in the end zone).

headline: Lane (wrist) is listed as questionable for Sunday's game at Cleveland.
story: A full practice participant throughout the week, Lane will need to be taken off injured reserve on Friday or Saturday to play in Sunday's game. If that happens, he'll likely be Baltimore's third or fourth wide receiver, perhaps sharing snaps with Devontez Walker behind veteran starters Zay Flowers and Rashod Bateman (both cleared to play after being listed on the injury report this week).

headline: Lane (wrist) was a full participant in practice Wednesday after being designated for return from injured reserve.
story: The Ravens opened Lane's 21-day evaluation window to begin Week 6 prep after the rookie wideout missed the team's last four games while recovering from left wrist surgery. The rookie wideout was apparently able to stay on top of his conditioning while he was sidelined from practice over the past month, as he faced no limitations in his return to the field. If Lane is able to maintain full practice activity Thursday and Friday, the Ravens could bring him back from IR ahead of Sunday's game in Cleveland.

headline: Lane (wrist) "is expected to return to practice," and per head coach Jesse Minter "has a shot" to play Sunday against the Browns, Mike Garafolo of NFL Network reports.
story: Minter said Monday that Lane could be designated to return from injured reserve this week, and it now appears likely he will do so. His participation in practice -- or lack thereof -- from Wednesday through Friday will likely determine whether or not he is ultimately activated for Week 6.

headline: Head coach Jesse Minter said Monday that the Ravens could designate Lane (wrist) to return from injured reserve as soon as Wednesday, Jonas Shaffer of the Baltimore Banner reports.
story: The rookie third-rounder's offseason momentum was stymied when he fractured his wrist during the Ravens' Week 1 win over the Colts. Minter noted that Lane has kept up his conditioning while on IR, and there's a chance that the 22-year-old wideout could be back on the field for practice as soon as Wednesday, though it's unclear whether he'll be cleared to return for Week 6 against the Browns on Oct. 18.

headline: Ravens coach Jesse Minter said Friday that Lane (wrist) is "doing really well" and "has put himself in a great position to be ready to roll when the time permits."
story: Lane is eligible to return from injured reserve for Week 6, and while Minter didn't get into specifics, it does sounds like the rookie wideout is expected back fairly soon. Lane underwent surgery in mid-September after fracturing his wrist in a Week 1 win over the Colts. He played 24 snaps on offense in the first half of that game, catching one of three targets for 11 yards, with a short TD catch called back due to a penalty. Lane could be the team's No. 2 or 3 wide receiver when he returns.

headline: Coach Jesse Minter said Lane underwent wrist surgery Wednesday, and the Ravens placed the rookie wide receiver on injured reserve, Brian Wacker of The Baltimore Sun reports.
story: Lane left the Ravens' Week 1 win at Indianapolis with a wrist injury that eventually was confirmed to include a fracture. With his move to IR, he'll be required to miss at least the next four games, meaning his next chance for game action will come Oct. 18 at Cleveland. As long as Lane is sidelined, Zay Flowers (hamstring), Rashod Bateman, Devontez Walker (groin), Elijah Sarratt and LaJohntay Wester will be among those that could see additional action at wide receiver for Baltimore.

headline: Lane (wrist) is expected to undergo surgery in the coming days, potentially as soon as Wednesday, Matt Zenitz of CBS Sports reports.
story: Lane suffered a fractured wrist in the Ravens' Week 1 win over the Colts on Sunday, and now that he's set for surgery, the rookie is hoping to miss only "about a month," according to Zenitz. With Zay Flowers (hamstring) also less than 100 percent, the Ravens could be dipping into their wideout depth early in the 2026 campaign. Rashod Bateman, Chris Moore and LaJohntay Wester picked up the slack against Indy, but Devontez Walker (groin) and rookie Elijah Sarratt could join the mix Sunday against the Saints.

headline: Ravens head coach Jesse Minter said that Lane will receive second and third medical opinions on his injured wrist this week before a timeline for his return is established, Sam Cohn of The Baltimore Sun reports.
story: Lane's NFL debut in Sunday's 41-23 win over the Colts came to an early end due to the wrist injury, which was confirmed to be a fracture after the game. An upcoming MRI along with additional testing on the wrist should help the Ravens gain a better understanding of the severity of the fracture, but at the very least, the rookie third-round pick is expected to miss the team's Week 2 game against the Saints. Lane's likely absence could open up more opportunities for Devontez Walker (groin) and Eljiah Sarratt (coach's decision), both of whom sat out the season opener.

headline: Lane (wrist) suffered a fractured wrist in Sunday's 41-23 win over the Colts and will undergo further testing Monday, including an MRI, Mike Garafolo of NFL Network reports.
story: Lane is expected to face a multi-week absence due to the fractured wrist he sustained in his NFL debut, which led to the rookie third-round pick exiting the game after catching one of three targets for 11 yards. A more precise timetable for Lane's recovery will likely be established after the results of his MRI come in, but he will almost certainly sit out Week 2 against the Saints.

headline: The Ravens announced that Lane has been ruled out for the remainder of Sunday's game against the Colts due to a wrist injury.
story: The rookie's early exit could force the Ravens to finish the season opener with just three receivers; Devontez Walker (groin) and Elijah Sarratt (coach's decision) are inactive for the contest, while Zay Flowers is questionable to return after tweaking his hamstring in the first half. Lane had a quiet showing in his injury-shortened NFL debut, finishing the day with an 11-yard reception on three targets.

headline: Cuevas didn't garner a target in Thursday night's 33-10 loss to the Jaguars.
story: Cuevas split time with nine snaps on both offense and special teams. This game marked the fourth time this season that the rookie had zero targets. Prior to Thursday night, the 23-year-old saw multiple targets in four straight games. He will likely have a similar role as the season continues.

headline: Cuevas caught one of two targets for 15 yards during Sunday's 36-10 loss at Buffalo.
story: Cuevas played 13 offensive snaps in Week 8, again trailing behind veteran Mark Andrews (29) and rookie fourth-rounder Matthew Hibner (21). With that said, Cuevas ran routes on most of those snaps, and he drew multiple targets for the fourth straight game Sunday. He still won't be a viable fantasy option in most formats as long as Andrews and Hibner remain healthy.

headline: Cuevas caught two of three targets for 35 yards during the Ravens' 35-13 loss to the Bengals on Sunday.
story: Cuevas connected with Tyler Huntley on a 16-yard pass on the Ravens' first offensive play of the game, but the duo didn't find each other again until late in the third quarter on a 19-yarder. Cuevas had only one catch for 14 yards through the first four games of the regular season, but the rookie fifth-rounder has an 8-105-1 line on 10 targets over his last three outings. That coincides with Huntley being under center, but the Ravens are expecting Lamar Jackson (ankle) to return for Week 8 against the Bills on Nov. 1.

headline: Cuevas caught four of five targets for 44 yards and a touchdown during Sunday's 13-10 loss to Cleveland.
story: Cuevas got the scoring started Sunday, reeling in a two-yard score from quarterback Tyler Huntley in the first quarter. The touchdown was the first of his career, and he finished tied for second on the team in both targets and catches in Week 6. Cuevas has now reeled in multiple passes in consecutive games, but he will continue to be hard to count on from a fantasy perspective as long as starting tight end Mark Andrews is available.

headline: Walker didn't garner a target in Thursday night's 33-10 loss to the Jaguars.
story: Walker made little impact in Thursday night's loss, playing 15 offensive snaps behind Ja'Kobi Lane (32), Rashod Bateman (35) and Zay Flowers (37). Walker will likely see a similar role as the season progresses.

headline: Walker caught one of his two targets for 19 yards during Baltimore's win over the Titans on Sunday.
story: Walker managed to record his second reception of the season, as he continues to make a limited impact offensively even with Ja'Kobi Lane (wrist) on injured reserve. Walker will look to be more productive during the Week 5 matchup versus the Falcons.

headline: Walker caught one of his two targets for 47 yards in Sunday's 24-17 loss to the Saints.
story: Walker saw 17 of the Ravens' 58 offensive snaps in Sunday's contest. The wide receiver also saw eight special-teams snaps. Walker saw nearly half as many offensive snaps as LaJohntay Wester (31), even though Zay Flowers (hamstring) was unavailable. The 2024 fourth-rounder sees most of his usage as a deep threat, but he appears hard-pressed to expand his role much beyond that of an occasional deep threat.

headline: With Zay Flowers (hamstring) listed as doubtful, Walker should have a role on offense in Sunday's game against the Saints, Ryan Mink of the Ravens' official site reports.
story: Walker missed Week 1 with a groin injury and now joins an offense that's likely without Flowers and won't have Ja'Kobi Lane (IR - wrist) for at least the next four weeks. Veteran starter Rashod Bateman is the de facto No. 1 receiver, with Walker, LaJohntay Wester, Chris Moore and Elijah Sarratt all candidates for significant playing time as well. Walker was in competition with Lane this summer for the No. 3 receiver job alongside Flowers and Bateman.

headline: Walker (groin) was a full participant at the Ravens' practice Wednesday.
story: Walker appears to have fully recovered from the groin injury that forced him to miss the team's 41-23 win over the Colts in Week 1. The wide receiver will be a welcomed addition Week 2 versus the Saints after rookie Ja'Kobi Lane (wrist) was placed on injured reserve Wednesday.

headline: Walker (groin) is inactive for Sunday's clash with the Colts.
story: The wide receiver logged limited practice sessions throughout the week leading up to the game and entered the weekend with a questionable tag. Ravens coach Jesse Minter described the injury as "minor" Tuesday, per Jonas Shaffer of TheBaltimoreBanner.com, but it's at least serious enough to keep Walker out for Week 1.

headline: Bateman caught one of two targets for six yards in Thursday night's 33-10 loss to the Jaguars.
story: That's back-to-back one-catch games for Bateman with Joe Fagnano at quarterback for the Ravens. With Zay Flowers also healthy, Bateman has little fantasy appeal in season-long formats, though things could change when Jacoby Brissett takes over as Baltimore's starting quarterback in Week 10.

headline: Bateman caught one of three targets for 22 yards in Sunday's 36-10 loss to the Bills.
story: Bateman actually led the Ravens in receiving yards on a day in which three quarterbacks attempted passes for Baltimore. Since posting a 7-88-1 receiving line in Week 2 against the Saints, Bateman has totaled 12 grabs for 200 yards and no scores over his last six games. He has minimal fantasy appeal while Zay Flowers is healthy.

headline: Bateman caught two of four targets for 33 yards during Sunday's 35-13 loss to the Bengals.
story: Bateman was able to handle a full workload for the first time since Week 5 after dealing with a shoulder injury, and the wide receiver was on the field for 74 percent of the team's offensive snaps. He finished tied for third on the team in targets with running back Justice Hill and tight end Mark Andrews, and Bateman's 33 receiving yards ranked third. The wide receiver and the rest of the team's pass catchers would stand to see an increase in production if Lamar Jackson (ankle) is able to return to action in Week 8 versus Buffalo.

headline: Bateman (shoulder) was a full participant in Thursday's practice.
story: A limited practice participant to begin the week after he exited this past Sunday's loss to the Browns due to the shoulder issue, Bateman cleared up any concern about his health by taking every rep during Thursday's session. While he'll be ready to play Sunday versus the Bengals, Bateman's standing as the No. 2 wideout on the depth chart behind Zay Flowers could be threatened after rookie Ja'Kobi Lane produced well in his return from injured reserve last week, logging four catches for 40 yards on five targets.

headline: Bateman (shoulder) was a limited practice participant Wednesday.
story: Per Jonas Shaffer of TheBaltimoreBanner.com, Bateman was sporting a no-contact jersey during the session, but his presence on the field in any capacity was a promising sign after he was unable to return to Sunday's 13-10 loss to the Browns. If he's able to take contact in practice at some point over the next two days, Bateman should be in good shape to play this weekend against the Bengals.

headline: Bateman (shoulder) is taking part in Wednesday's practice, Brian Wacker of The Baltimore Sun reports.
story: Bateman sustained a shoulder injury during this past Sunday's loss at Cleveland and wasn't able to return. Head coach Jesse Minter told Jeff Zrebiec of The Athletic on Monday that Bateman "should be OK," and the wide receiver's ability to mix into drills only days after the incident indicates he's trending in the right direction. Wednesday's practice report will reveal Bateman's activity level to begin Week 7 prep.

headline: Ravens head coach Jesse Minter said Monday that Bateman (shoulder) "should be OK" after exiting late in the second quarter of Sunday's 13-10 loss to the Browns, Jeff Zrebiec of The Athletic reports.
story: Listed on Ravens injury reports the past two weeks due to a shoulder issue, Bateman appeared to aggravate the injury late in the first half of Sunday's contest. He failed to haul in his lone target while running 11 routes in the game before the injury kept him out for the entire second half. Fortunately for Bateman, he seems to have avoided a major setback, but his practice activity over the next few days will likely determine whether he suits up next Sunday versus the Bengals. It's also worth noting that rookie Ja'Kobi Lane returned to action Sunday and saw five targets from Tyler Huntley.

headline: Bateman (shoulder) has been ruled out of Sunday's game in Cleveland.
story: Bateman appears to have aggravated the shoulder injury that bothered him during Week 6 prep. Now that it's confirmed Bateman won't return Sunday, he'll finish the contest with no catches (on one target). Ja'Kobi Lane, Devontez Walker and LaJohntay Wester are the Ravens' available wide receivers behind top option Zay Flowers.

headline: Bateman sustained a shoulder injury during Sunday's game at Cleveland, Brian Wacker of The Baltimore Sun reports.
story: Bateman tended to a shoulder injury during Week 6 prep, as he logged an LP/DNP/FP practice regimen. His listing Sunday indicates he aggravated the issue, which has left him questionable to return. Bateman didn't haul in his only target before exiting late in the first half.

headline: Bateman (shoulder) doesn't have an injury designation for Sunday's game at Cleveland.
story: A full practice Friday erases the concern about Bateman's shoulder injury, whereas QB Lamar Jackson (ankle) still isn't practicing and won't play this week.

headline: Bateman (shoulder) didn't practice Thursday.
story: Head coach Jesse Minter told Jamison Hensley of ESPN.com on Wednesday that Bateman "should be fine" for Sunday's game against the Browns, but it's unclear if the Ravens remain as confident in the wideout's health a day later. After opening Week 6 prep as a limited participant, Bateman took a step back in terms of activity Thursday. As long as he can get back on the field in some capacity Friday, Bateman will be in good shape to play this weekend, but another missed practice will put him at risk of missing his first game of the season.

headline: Bateman (shoulder) was a limited participant in Wednesday's practice.
story: Per Cordell Woodland of 105.7 The Fan Baltimore, Bateman was spotted with a non-contact jersey Wednesday and was able to fit in some on-field work behind closed doors after not working out with the team during the open portion of the session. Though the wideout is on the injury report for a second straight week on account of the shoulder issue, head coach Jesse Minter said after Wednesday's practice that Bateman "should be fine" for Sunday's game against the Browns, according to Jamison Hensley of ESPN.com.

headline: Bateman caught five of six passes for 62 yards during the Ravens' 30-23 overtime win over the Falcons on Sunday.
story: Bateman ended up leading the Ravens in receiving yards while finishing second in catches and targets to Zay Flowers (eight catches on nine targets). Bateman played a crucial role in Baltimore's come-from-behind victory, with the veteran wide receiver logging catches of 11, seven and 20 yards late in the fourth quarter (all for first downs), with the drive ending on a seven-yard touchdown pass from Tyler Huntley to Devontez Walker. Bateman has a 16-233-1 receiving line on 20 targets over his last four games, but his role on offense would likely decrease once rookie third-round wide receiver Ja'Kobi Lane (wrist) returns from injured reserve, which could happen as soon as Week 7 against the Browns on Oct. 18.

headline: Bateman (shoulder) was a full participant in Thursday's practice.
story: According to Cordell Woodland of 105.7 The Fan Baltimore, Bateman was donning a red no-contact jersey during the open portion of Thursday's practice, but he was evidently able to do enough on the field to upgrade to full activity after a limited listing Wednesday. Though Bateman looks like he'll be ready to go for Sunday's game in Atlanta, he could be at the receiving end of passes from Tyler Huntley, who directed the first-team offense for a second straight day Thursday while starting quarterback Lamar Jackson (ankle) remained sidelined at practice. The Ravens likely will decide on Jackson's status for Sunday following Friday's session.

headline: Bateman (shoulder) was limited in Wednesday's practice.
story: It's a new injury for Bateman, and the same can be said for Zay Flowers, who was limited with a foot injury Wednesday. With Lamar Jackson (ankle) set to miss Week 5 against the Falcons, Bateman is an uninspiring fantasy bet if he plays.

headline: Bateman caught both of his targets for 46 yards in Sunday's win over the Titans.
story: With Zay Flowers getting even closer to 100 percent with his hamstring injury and Mark Andrews and Derrick Henry seeing most of the money opportunities in the red zone, Bateman is left fighting for scraps. Bateman's days as a fantasy starter are likely over with Flowers nearing a full-time role, as the former has five targets over the last two games since Flowers' return.

headline: Bateman caught two of three targets for 37 yards in Sunday's 34-31 win over the Cowboys.
story: Bateman finished second on the team in receiving yards behind Zay Flowers, who compiled 84 receiving yards in the latter's return from a one-game absence due to a hamstring injury. Bateman stepped up with seven catches for 88 yards and a touchdown while Flowers was sidelined in Week 2, but Flowers is the clear No. 1 option in Baltimore's wide receiver room, as Bateman was held without a catch when Flowers was active for the season opener. Up next for Bateman and the Ravens will be a Week 4 home game against the Titans.

headline: Bateman caught seven of nine targets for 88 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 24-17 loss to New Orleans.
story: With Zay Flowers (hamstring) unavailable, Bateman stepped up as Lamar Jackson's top downfield option and hauled in a 22-yard TD just before halftime, giving the Ravens a 14-3 lead. The veteran wideout made a mental error that may have cost his team the game, however -- on Baltimore's final possession as the Ravens were looking to tie it up, he cut a route short and saw Jackson's pass attempt sail over his head for a game-ending interception. Flowers could be back as soon as next week, which would relegate Bateman to a supporting role again for a Week 3 road trip to Dallas.

headline: With teammate Zay Flowers (hamstring)  listed as doubtful, Bateman has a big opportunity Sunday against the Saints, ESPN.com's Jamison Hensley reports.
story: Quarterback Lamar Jackson told reporters that Bateman "is actually going to get a lot more targets, I believe." The Ravens may not have any other choice after losing Flowers and Ja'Kobi Lane (IR - wrist) to injuries during a Week 1 win over Indianapolis. Bateman played 80 percent of Baltimore's snaps in the contest, including 85 percent before halftime when Flowers and Lane were still in the game. Bateman likely will handle another lofty snap share this Sunday, and his target rate may rise with Flowers' usual snaps/routes being split between lesser players like Devontez Walker, LaJohntay Wester and Chris Moore.

headline: Bateman did not bring in his lone target during Baltimore's 41-23 win over Indianapolis on Sunday.
story: Bateman and Lamar Jackson connected on a 19-yard pass late in the second quarter, but that play was called back due to offensive holding. Jackson and Bateman failed to connect on a throw early in the third quarter, and the latter finished with zero catches for the fourth time since the beginning of the 2025 season. Bateman ended up leading all wide receivers with 53 offensive snaps, and despite the early dud, his role in the offense should expand for as long as rookie Ja'Kobi Lane is sidelined by a fractured wrist, and even more so if Zay Flowers (hamstring) were to miss time. The Ravens host the Saints on Sept. 20 in what is Baltimore's home opener.

headline: Hill rushed nine times for 85 yards and a touchdown and brought in all three targets for seven yards in the Ravens' 33-10 loss to the Jaguars on Thursday night.
story: Hill provided the sole offensive highlight of the night for the moribund, Joe Fagnano-led offense, making one cut after getting the handoff from the rookie quarterback halfway through the fourth quarter and bursting through the defense up the right side of the field for a 65-yard touchdown run. Hill's yardage total was both a team- and season-high figure for the veteran change-of-pace back, who should benefit from the pending trade acquisition of Jacoby Brissett from the Cardinals whenever the veteran signal-caller is able to take the reins of the offense.

headline: Hill (groin) was a full participant in Tuesday's practice.
story: After the Ravens estimated him as a limited practice participant Monday on their initial Week 9 injury report, Hill took every rep Tuesday to clear up any concern about his availability heading into Thursday's game against the Jaguars. Hill should serve in his familiar role as the Ravens' top passing-down back in Week 9, with Derrick Henry continuing to lead the way on the ground.

headline: Hill (groin) was estimated as a limited participant on Monday's practice report.
story: It's a new injury for Hill, as it's the first time this season he's been listed on the injury report. In Sunday's loss to the Bills, Hill rushed three times for 15 yards and posted season highs in catches (four) and targets (eight) for 20 receiving yards.

headline: Hill rushed three times for 15 yards while catching four of eight targets for 20 yards during Sunday's 36-10 loss to the Bills.
story: Hill garnered a team-high eight targets as Baltimore saw the departure of both starting quarterback Lamar Jackson (thumb) and Tyler Huntley (toe) in the first half. Undrafted rookie Joe Fagnano completed 10 of 21 passes for 91 yards while throwing an interception in the loss, and he may be asked to start Thursday's contest against the Jaguars. Hill has now turned 24 carries into 155 yards while reeling in 17 of 25 targets for 104 yards over eight games to open the 2026 campaign.

headline: Hill took three carries for seven yards and caught three of four targets for 26 yards during Sunday's 35-13 loss versus the Bengals.
story: Baltimore led for most of the game Sunday before falling behind late in the third quarter, and from that point on, the game script favored Hill. Even still, his snap count at running back in Week 7 (29) lagged behind that of starter Derrick Henry (33). When Lamar Jackson (ankle) returns to action, it should give a boost to the entire Ravens offense.

headline: Hill caught all three of his targets for nine yards during the Ravens' 13-10 loss to the Browns on Sunday.
story: Hill was on the field for 24 of the Ravens' 57 offensive snaps (42.1 percent), which wasn't far behind lead back Derrick Henry (33). That was more due to game script, as the Ravens' offense struggled to move the ball down the field against a tough Browns defense. The offensive outlook for Hill and the rest of Baltimore's skill position players would improve dramatically if Lamar Jackson (ankle) is cleared to play in Week 7 against the Bengals on Oct. 25.

headline: Hill turned four carries into 73 yards and caught two of four targets for five yards during the Ravens' 30-23 overtime win over the Falcons on Sunday.
story: Hill was responsible for each of the Ravens' two longest offensive plays of the game. He turned his first carry into 21 yards early in the first quarter before breaking away for a 47-yard scamper midway through the third, which led to an 18-yard touchdown pass from Tyler Huntley to Derrick Henry two plays later. Hill's 73 rushing yards were his most in a game since Week 4 against Kansas City (76), although he's firmly entrenched as the Ravens' change-of-pace RB2 behind Henry. The Ravens will stay on the road for Week 6 against the Browns on Oct. 18.

headline: Hill rushed one time for three yards in Sunday's 24-18 win over the Titans. He added two catches for 22 yards on three targets.
story: Hill continues to handle change-of-pace and passing-down work behind Derrick Henry out of the Baltimore backfield. Across four games, Hill has accumulated 60 yards on 14 carries and five catches for 44 yards on six targets. Hill's role likely will only expand in the event the Ravens are chasing points on the scoreboard or if Henry suffers an injury.

headline: Hill rushed twice for six yards and caught two targets for 12 yards in Sunday's 24-17 loss to the Saints.
story: Hill was on the field for 27 of the Ravens' 58 offensive snaps. The running back saw usage as both runner and receiver, providing a fast contrast to Derrick Henry's bulk. It appears Hill may be on track for more consistent complementary opportunities than last season behind Derrick Henry in Baltimore's new offense.

headline: Hill turned six carries into 18 yards and added a 10-yard catch during the Ravens' 41-23 win over the Colts on Sunday.
story: Hill saw an uptick in usage in the fourth quarter with the Ravens firmly in control of the game. He played 31 of 68 offensive snaps, which wasn't that far behind bell cow Derrick Henry's 37 snaps, though Hill is firmly entrenched as the Ravens' RB2, with Rasheen Ali being the distant third option. Hill will continue to serve as the change-of-pace back for the Ravens heading into Week 2 against the Saints on Sept. 20.

headline: Mark Andrews' Week 10 fantasy outlook
story: Mark Andrews' Week 10 fantasy outlook

headline: Andrews secured both targets for 19 yards in the Ravens' 33-10 loss to the Jaguars on Thursday night.
story: The veteran tight end actually led the Ravens in receiving yards with his modest total, as fill-in signal-caller Joe Fagnano averaged just 3.3 yards per attempt and totaled 60 passing yards overall. Andrews opened the season with back-to-back 49-yard tallies on 10 total catches, but he's been stuck at 28 receiving yards or fewer in his seven subsequent games. Andrews will hope to benefit from the pending trade acquisition of Jacoby Brissett, who should bring some stability and productivity to Baltimore's currently embattled quarterback situation.

headline: Andrews caught three of four targets for 14 yards in Sunday's 36-10 loss to the Bills.
story: Though Lamar Jackson (ankle) made his long-awaited return to the lineup, his stay lasted just one offensive snap Sunday before he suffered a serious thumb injury. Tyler Huntley then exited the game with a toe injury in the second quarter, forcing undrafted rookie Joe Fagnano into emergency QB duties. No Ravens player produced even 25 receiving yards against Buffalo. Andrews has been in an extended slump and won't be a trustworthy fantasy tight end for Thursday night against the Jaguars.

headline: Andrews caught three of four targets for 23 yards in Sunday's 35-13 loss to the Bengals.
story: Andrews reeled in three or fewer passes for the second straight game and third time overall this season, and he has now gone five games in a row without recording 30-plus receiving yards. The tight end's production will likely go up once Lamar Jackson (ankle) is able to return, but he no longer appears to be a must-roster asset in fantasy football. Through seven games this season, Andrews has caught 26 of 37 targets for 204 yards and one touchdown.

headline: Andrews caught one of three targets for four yards during the Ravens' 13-10 loss to the Browns on Sunday.
story: Andrews saw only three pass attempts from Tyler Huntley on Sunday, and it was the first time that the veteran tight end saw less than five targets in a game this season. Andrews' 41 offensive snaps were most among Ravens tight ends, but his receiving line was below rookie fifth-rounder Josh Cuevas (4-44-1 on five targets). Baltimore will head back home for Week 7 against the Bengals on Oct. 25, and Andrews' scoring floor will be boosted if Lamar Jackson (ankle) is cleared to return from a two-game absence.

headline: Andrews caught four of six targets for 28 yards and lost a fumble in Sunday's 30-23 overtime win over the Falcons.
story: Andrews finished third on the team in catches and receiving yards behind wide receivers Zay Flowers and Rashod Bateman, but the veteran tight end had a forgettable night full of miscues. Atlanta's first touchdown came on a 36-yard Jessie Bates return of Andrews' first-quarter fumble, and Andrews also failed to come down with a pair of catchable balls in the end zone, one of which would have resulted in a touchdown, while the other was an attempted two-point conversion. Andrews' ceiling would rise if the Ravens get starting QB Lamar Jackson (ankle) back in Week 6 at Cleveland, but Sunday night's quiet performance was due primarily to Andrews' own miscues rather than any shortcomings on the part of backup QB Tyler Huntley.

headline: Andrews caught five of six targets for 27 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 24-18 win over Tennessee.
story: While the veteran tight end failed to reach 50 receiving yards for a fourth straight game to begin the year, Andrews did get into the end zone for the first time in 2026 on a three-yard toss from Lamar Jackson (ankle). Jackson's injury isn't believed to be serious, but if Tyler Huntley is under center instead in a Week 5 road trip to Atlanta, it likely won't impact Andrews' outlook all that much given his lackluster 18-149-1 line on 24 targets through four games.

headline: Andrews caught three of five targets for 24 yards during Sunday's 34-31 win over the Cowboys.
story: Andrews was limited by a hand injury that he suffered in the second quarter, and he was on the field for only 33 of the team's 64 offensive snaps. The tight end has recorded at least three catches in each of the team's first three games, reeling in 13 of 18 targets for 122 yards so far this season. Andrews has yet to reach the end zone this year, and his next chance will come against the Titans in Week 4.

headline: Andrews (hand) returned after halftime of Sunday's game against the Cowboys in Rio de Janeiro, Jeff Zrebiec of The Athletic reports.
story: Andrews missed some time in the second quarter due to a hand injury, but it won't stop him from rejoining Baltimore's offense after a spell in the locker room. He'll be looking to add to his one catch (on three targets) for nine yards prior to his exit.

headline: Andrews exited Sunday's game versus the Cowboys in Rio de Janeiro due to a hand injury.
story: Before he departed in the second quarter Sunday, he reeled in just one of three targets for nine yards. For as long as Andrews is sidelined, WRs Zay Flowers and Rashod Bateman likely will serve as the top pass catchers in Baltimore's offense.

headline: Andrews caught six of seven targets for 49 yards in Sunday's 24-17 loss to the Saints.
story: With Zay Flowers (hamstring) and Ja'Kobi Lane (wrist) out for this one, Andrews finished second on the team in targets, two behind Rashod Bateman, who posted 7-88-1 receiving on his nine looks. Andrews ran 28 routes on Lamar Jackson's 38 dropbacks and is seeing a bigger piece of the pie at tight end this season with Isaiah Likely and Charlie Kolar now off the team. Through two games, Andrews has 10 catches for 98 yards on 13 targets. He'll be a TE1 next Sunday against the Cowboys in Brazil.

headline: Andrews secured four of six targets for 49 yards in the Ravens' 41-23 win over the Colts on Sunday.
story: Andrews commemorated his return to a clear-cut TE1 role with a strong season-opening performance, finishing second in receptions and tying for the team lead in targets on the afternoon. The veteran flashed his customary chemistry with Lamar Jackson, and while his elevated involvement in the air attack was encouraging, it bears noting that it was partly due to Zay Flowers' early exit due to a hamstring injury. Flowers' injury could linger, however, so Andrews should remain an appealing option at his position in a Week 2 home matchup against the Saints next Sunday.

headline: Fagnano completed 10 of 18 passes for 60 yards with no touchdowns and two interceptions while adding three rushes for 13 yards in the Ravens' 33-10 loss to the Jaguars on Thursday night.
story: Fagnano drew the start with both Lamar Jackson (thumb) and Tyler Huntley (toe) on injured reserve, and the undrafted rookie signal-caller unsurprisingly had a difficult night after also struggling in emergency duty against the Bills just four days earlier. Fagnano had been dealing with an ankle injury stemming from his aforementioned NFL debut and had little practice time on a short week, so offensive coordinator Declan Doyle kept the game plan simple and focused on the short areas of the field, resulting in Fagnano averaging just 3.3 yards per attempt. Both of Fagnano's second-half picks also led to Jacksonville field goals, making it a forgettable night overall. With the Ravens reportedly putting the finishing touches on a trade with the Cardinals for veteran quarterback Jacoby Brissett, Fagnano is likely to move into a reserve role as soon as a Week 10 road matchup against the Titans on Sunday, Nov. 15.

headline: Trade acquisition Jacoby Brissett is not expected to be available for Baltimore until Week 10, leaving Fagnano as the team's projected starting quarterback for Week 9, Adam Schefter of ESPN reports.
story: With Lamar Jackson bound for IR with a thumb injury on his throwing hand and Tyler Huntley expected to miss the rest of the season with turf toe, coach Jesse Minter named Fagnano as the Ravens' starting quarterback for Week 9 on Tuesday. However, news broke Wednesday that Baltimore is finalizing a trade to acquire quarterback Jacoby Brissett, casting doubt on Fagnano's place in the pecking order. It looks like he'll ultimately take a back seat to Brissett starting in Week 10, but since the trade won't be finalized in time for Brissett to be available for the Ravens on Thursday, Fagnano still projects to start versus the Jaguars.

headline: Ravens head coach Jesse Minter confirmed Tuesday that Fagnano (ankle) will start Thursday's game against the Jaguars, Jamison Hensley of ESPN.com reports.
story: The undrafted rookie out of UConn will make his first NFL start with Lamar Jackson (thumb) headed for injured reserve and Tyler Huntley (toe) unlikely to be available. After both Jackson and Huntley made early departures in Sunday's 36-10 loss to the Bills, Fagnano was pressed into action for the first time in his career and finished with 10 completions on 21 attempts for 91 yards and an interception. Fagnano emerged from the contest with a right ankle injury and was sporting a heavy brace during Tuesday's practice, though he did enough on the field to garner a full listing on the Ravens' official injury report. Expect the Ravens to lean heavily on the Derrick Henry-led ground attack to help take the pressure off the inexperienced Fagnano during Thursday's contest, at least for as long as the game script allows for it.

headline: Fagnano practiced Tuesday "with a significant guard/brace on his right ankle," Jeff Zrebiec of The Athletic reports.
story: The Ravens are seemingly being careful with Fagnano's injured ankle, but he was able to get out there Tuesday -- two days prior to his team's Week 9 matchup with the Jaguars. With Lamar Jackson (thumb) headed to injured reserve and Tyler Huntley (toe) unlikely to go Thursday, the banged-up Fagnano is the favorite to start for Baltimore in Week 9.

headline: Fagnano was limited at Monday's walkthrough due to an ankle injury.
story: Fagnano took a hit to his left knee while subbing in for Lamar Jackson (right thumb) and Tyler Huntley (toe) during Sunday's loss at Buffalo, but the former's health concern has been confirmed to be to his ankle. While Jackson is out indefinitely and Huntley "probably" won't play Thursday against the Jaguars, Fagnano has a chance to play in that contest, per head coach Jesse Minter. Being limited to kick off Week 9 prep is a step in that direction, but Fagnano may need to upgrade to full Tuesday and/or Wednesday to avoid a game designation.

headline: Coach Jesse Minter said Monday that Fagnano (knee) "is fighting through a couple things" but has a chance to play Thursday against the Jaguars.
story: Baltimore's QB room experienced a cascade of injuries during Sunday's loss at Buffalo, with Lamar Jackson requiring thumb surgery and an upcoming IR stint, Tyler Huntley likely tending to a turf-toe injury and Fagnano dealing with a left knee issue and seemingly at least one more health concern. Jackson is feared to be out for the season, and Minter said Huntley "probably" won't play Thursday, which leaves Fagnano as the likely starter, assuming he's healthy enough to suit up.

headline: Fagnano acknowledged that he's not 100 percent healthy after taking a hit to his left knee during Sunday's 36-10 loss to the Bills, but he said that he hopes to be ready to play in Thursday's game against the Jaguars, Jonas Shafferof TheBanner.com reports.
story: Fagnano -- who was inactive for Sunday's contest as the Ravens' emergency No. 3 quarterback -- ended up being pressed into action after starter Lamar Jackson (thumb) and Tyler Huntley (toe) left the game early. The undrafted rookie out of UConn ended up directing the offense for most of the afternoon, completing just 10 of 21 pass attempts for 91 yards and an interception while adding three yards on three carries and losing a fumble in what was his NFL debut. Per Jamison Hensley of ESPN.com, Fagnano was spotted clutching his knee in discomfort after Bills defender Ed Oliver took him down on a play in which he was ultimately flagged for roughing the passer, but the quarterback was able to remain in the game. With Jackson ticketed for injured reserve and Huntley at risk of sitting out the game against Jacksonville, Fagnano could be in line to start Thursday, provided he's not too banged up to handle the assignment.

headline: Fagnano (coach's decision) is inactive but will serve as the Ravens' emergency third quarterback Sunday against the Bills.
story: Fagnano operated as the Ravens' backup quarterback behind Tyler Huntley for each of the team's prior three games in the absence of Lamar Jackson, who has been cleared to return for Sunday's contest against Buffalo. As the emergency QB3, Fagnano is not allowed to play unless both Jackson and Huntley are taken out of the game due to injury, illness or ejection.

headline: Fagnano (coach's decision) is inactive but will serve as the Ravens' emergency third quarterback against the Titans on Sunday.
story: Fagnano will be the Ravens' emergency QB3 for a fourth consecutive game, meaning he cannot play Sunday unless both Lamar Jackson and Tyler Huntley leave the game due to injury, illness or ejection.

headline: Fagnano (coach's decision) is inactive for Sunday's game against Dallas but will be available as the team's emergency quarterback if needed.
story: Fagnano was also the Ravens' emergency signal-caller for the first two games of the 2026 campaign. That trend will likely continue as long as Lamar Jackson and Tyler Huntley are available.

headline: Fagnano (coach's decision) is inactive for Sunday's game versus the Saints but serving as the emergency third quarterback, Ryan Mink of the team's official site reports.
story: Fagnano is inactive once again but will serve as the Ravens' emergency signal-caller in Week 2. However, unless Lamar Jackson and Tyler Huntley are injured during the contest, Fagnano won't be on the field Sunday.

headline: Fagnano (coach's decision) is inactive for Sunday's matchup with the Colts.
story: The preseason standout is third on the depth chart behind Lamar Jackson and Tyler Huntley, and he will need both to be unavailable to have a chance to enter the game Sunday. Fagnano completed 74.7 percent of his passes during the preseason for 509 yards and three touchdowns.

headline: Flowers brought in three of six targets for six yards and rushed three times for 17 yards in the Ravens' 33-10 loss to the Jaguars on Thursday night.
story: Joe Fagnano drew the start with both Lamar Jackson (IR, thumb) and Tyler Huntley (IR, toe) out of action, and the rookie undrafted signal-caller averaged a microscopic 3.3 yards per attempt and threw two interceptions. Therefore, Flowers once again put forth a forgettable receiving line, although he at least got on the board with a trio of catches after being blanked on five targets in the Week 8 loss to the Bills. The Ravens tried to boost Flowers' touches with his trio of rush attempts, and he was reasonably effective with those. While fantasy managers have gotten next to nothing from the talented receiver over the last two games, Jacoby Brissett, who Baltimore is finalizing a trade for with the Cardinals, could be ready to suit up as soon as a Week 10 home matchup with the Chargers on Monday night, Nov. 16.

headline: Flowers failed to bring in any of his five targets in the Ravens' 36-10 loss to the Bills on Sunday.
story: Lamar Jackson suffered a thumb injury on his first pass attempt, and Tyler Huntley subsequently exited the game with a toe injury before halftime after putting the ball up just four times in his own right. That left the offense in the hands of emergency quarterback Joe Fagnano for the rest of the afternoon, and Flowers unsurprisingly failed to gain any traction. Flowers was held without a catch for the first time in his career, and with Jackson reportedly headed to injured reserve, the star receiver's best chance at fantasy relevance over the next several games will seemingly be tied into Huntley's availability and/or the Ravens signing a veteran signal-caller as a free agent.

headline: Flowers brought in eight of 11 targets for 137 yards and a touchdown in the Ravens' 35-13 loss to the Bengals on Sunday.
story: The standout receiver had a big hand in staking the Ravens to a 13-0 halftime lead, and although Baltimore couldn't muster a single point in the second half, Flowers still finished with team-high reception, receiving yardage and target totals. Flowers also had a game-long 48-yard catch, which qualified as his third touchdown of the season. Flowers has shown excellent chemistry with both Lamar Jackson (ankle) and Tyler Huntley, and reports indicate the fleet-footed receiver is likely to have the former under center for a Week 8 road showdown against the Bills.

headline: Flowers brought in six of 11 targets for 66 yards and rushed once for one yard in the Ravens' 13-10 loss to the Browns on Sunday.
story: Flowers set the pace for the Ravens in receptions, receiving yards and targets on the afternoon, displaying solid chemistry with Tyler Huntley once again. The speedy wideout has no fewer than five catches and 53 receiving yards in any game this season, and he's recorded a 14-118-0 line over the last two games alone with Huntley under center. Flowers will remain a must-play wideout regardless of who's helming the Ravens offense in a Week 7 home matchup against the division-rival Bengals next Sunday.

headline: Flowers (toe) has been cleared to play in Sunday's game at Cleveland.
story: The Ravens added Flowers to their injury report Thursday as a limited participant, and while he remained limited Friday, his game availability isn't in doubt. Tyler Huntley is making another start at quarterback with Lamar Jackson (ankle) ruled out again.

headline: Flowers (toe) is practicing Friday after being added to the injury report Thursday, Jamison Hensley of ESPN.com reports.
story: Flowers was a limited participant Thursday due to the toe injury, and it apparently isn't serious enough to keep him off the field at Friday's practice. His level of participation and any game designation on the Ravens' final injury report should provide more clarity.

headline: Flowers (toe) was a limited participant at Thursday's practice.
story: Flowers has been no stranger to the injury report this season, having missed a game due to a hamstring injury in Week 2 while also dealing with a foot injury. It's unclear if this latest toe injury is related to his previous foot issue, through which Flowers played in the Week 5 win over Atlanta. Flowers caught eight passes for 53 yards from backup QB Tyler Huntley in that game, and Huntley could be under center again for Sunday's game against the Browns, as Lamar Jackson (ankle) has yet to return to practice. Flowers' practice participation will bear monitoring Friday, though he could still avoid an injury designation for Sunday's game, especially if he practices without limitations Friday like he did Wednesday.

headline: Flowers (foot) caught eight of nine targets for 53 yards and added a 13-yard rush in Sunday's 30-23 overtime win over the Falcons.
story: Flowers led the Ravens in catches and targets from backup QB Tyler Huntley while finishing nine receiving yards short of Rashod Bateman's team-leading total as the Ravens escaped with a road win Sunday night despite the absence of starting QB Lamar Jackson (ankle). Jackson reportedly has a chance to return as soon as Week 6 in Cleveland, but Flowers showed he can still be reasonably productive with Huntley throwing him passes. Flowers also took a two-yard sack on a trick play and had a would-be 26-yard catch negated on Baltimore's final drive of regulation because the Ravens instead accepted a 29-yard pass-interference penalty that he drew. The speedy wideout sat out Week 2 due to a hamstring injury and was listed as questionable heading into Sunday's OT win due to a foot injury, but he should be expected to continue suiting up barring a setback.

headline: Flowers (foot) is listed as active for Sunday's game in Atlanta.
story: Flowers endured practice restrictions during Week 5 prep, only this week he was dealing with a foot injury as opposed to the hamstring issue that had plagued him since the season opener. Despite Flowers entering the weekend as questionable to play, Adam Schefter of ESPN reported Sunday morning that the wide receiver was slated to suit up. Now that that's been confirmed, Flowers may have less sway in fantasy terms with QB Tyler Huntley directing the offense instead of Lamar Jackson (ankle), the latter of whom is inactive.

headline: Flowers (foot) is slated to play in Sunday night's game in Atlanta, Adam Schefter of ESPN reports.
story: Flowers swapped out his previous hamstring injury for a foot issue this week, which limited him Wednesday through Friday and left him questionable for Sunday. His status for Week 5 will be confirmed approximately 90 minutes before an 8:20 p.m. ET kickoff, and if he suits up, he'll be the preferred No. 1 pass catcher for QB Tyler Huntley, who is subbing in for an absent Lamar Jackson (ankle). That may result in a reduced target count for Flowers if the Ravens lean more on the run, but he's still put together an 18-352-2 line on 22 targets through parts of three contests this season.

headline: Flowers (foot) is listed as questionable for Sunday night's game against the Falcons.
story: With Flowers having been limited in practice throughout the week due to the foot issue, his status remains up in the air heading into Sunday night. He's been playing through injuries all season up to this point and could be looking at another muted workload in Atlanta. If Flowers can't play, WR Rashod Bateman and TE Mark Andrews will be Tyler Huntley's top targets.

headline: Flowers (foot) is listed as questionable for Sunday night's game at Atlanta, Adam Caplan of SiriusXM NFL Radio reports.
story: Flowers is no longer listed with a hamstring injury, instead having his practice participation limited (Wednesday through Friday) due to a foot issue. There hasn't been much to suggest it's a serious concern, but fantasy managers will still want to keep one eye on the situation this weekend ahead of an 8:20 p.m. ET kickoff for the Ravens and Falcons. Quarterback Lamar Jackson (ankle) didn't practice this week and has been ruled out, leaving Tyler Huntley to direct Baltimore's offense.

headline: Flowers (foot) was limited in practice Thursday.
story: It was the second straight limited practice for Flowers, who is now working through a foot injury in advance of Week 5. Flowers has been dynamic when on the field this year with 18 grabs for 352 yards and two touchdowns, but he's been limited to just 88 snaps across three games. Look for Flowers' status to gain more clarity Friday when the final injury report of the week is posted.

headline: Flowers was a limited participant in Wednesday's practice due to a foot injury.
story: While he was managing a hamstring strain, Flowers sat out the Ravens' Week 2 loss to the Saints and had his practice activity limited the following two weeks, but he's tending to a new injury in Week 5. The wideout was able to get some work in during Wednesday's session, but it didn't come during the media-viewing period. The Ravens' outlook on offense is already tenuous, with Lamar Jackson's ankle injury preventing him from practicing Wednesday and threatening his availability for Sunday's game in Atlanta. Flowers still has time to ramp up to a full practice before the end of the week to put himself on a path to playing this weekend.

headline: Ravens head coach Jesse Minter said that Flowers (hamstring) was a limited participant in Wednesday's practice, Brian Wacker of The Baltimore Sun reports.
story: Though Flowers wasn't present on the field for the media-access portion of practice, the fourth-year wideout was apparently able to get in some work behind the scenes Wednesday. The Ravens haven't indicated that Flowers has experienced any setbacks with his hamstring since returning from a one-game absence to play in both of the previous two contests, so his limitations to begin Week 5 prep were most likely maintenance-related. Flowers still appears likely to head into Sunday's game in Atlanta without an injury designation, though his fantasy appeal may be more limited than usual with Tyler Huntley trending toward drawing the Week 5 start in place of the injured Lamar Jackson (ankle).

headline: Flowers caught eight of 10 targets for 118 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 24-18 win over the Titans.
story: The fourth-year wideout didn't appear hampered by the minor hamstring issue he's been playing through, as he led the Ravens in catches, targets and receiving yards while connecting with Lamar Jackson (ankle) for a 19-yard score early in the second quarter. Jackson's day was done at halftime and he was seen in a walking boot after the game, but per Jonas Shaffer of TheBaltimoreBanner.com, coach Jesse Minter suggested the QB might have tried playing in the second half if it seemed necessary to preserve the win. If Tyler Huntley is under center in Week 5 against the Falcons instead of Jackson, it could impact Flowers' ability to produce big numbers again. In three games, Flowers has delivered an 18-352-2 line on just 22 targets.

headline: Flowers (hamstring) is listed as active Sunday against the Titans.
story: Flowers has been tending to a hamstring injury since before halftime of the Ravens' Week 1 win at Indianapolis, but he was able to play last Sunday versus the Cowboys in Brazil, recording a 5-84-0 line on six targets on a 33 percent snap share. Despite entering this weekend as questionable, he isn't expected to be on a "pitch count" Sunday, per Jeremy Fowler of ESPN, meaning a full workload is on tap for the fourth-year wide receiver.

headline: Flowers (hamstring) is expected to play in Sunday's game against the Titans, Ian Rapoport of NFL Network reports.
story: Flowers carried a questionable tag into the weekend due to a lingering hamstring issue, but he's slated to suit up in Week 4 for a second straight week. Last Sunday against the Cowboys in Brazil, he handled a 33 percent snap share and hauled in five of six targets for 84 yards, but per Jeremy Fowler of ESPN, Flowers isn't expected to be on a "pitch count" this Sunday, so he appears set for a full workload.

headline: Flowers (hamstring) is questionable for Sunday's game against the Titans after being limited in Friday's practice.
story: After upgrading to full participation Thursday, Flowers took a step back Friday, but it's possible the Ravens just rested him some considering the addition of "rest" alongside his name on the injury report, per Jonas Shaffer of TheBaltimoreBanner.com. Flowers is likely better than 50/50 to play Sunday against the Titans. He's a locked-in WR2 in fantasy with big-time upside when available.

headline: Flowers (hamstring) was a full participant at Thursday's practice, Jamison Hensley of ESPN.com reports.
story: After being limited Wednesday, Flowers upgraded to full participation Thursday, putting him on track to avoid an injury designation for Sunday's game against the Titans. The speedy wideout injured his hamstring in the season opener against the Colts and sat out the Week 2 loss to the Saints before returning for the Ravens' Week 3 win over the Cowboys in Rio de Janeiro. Despite missing a game, Flowers easily leads the team with 234 receiving yards.

headline: Flowers (hamstring) was limited in Wednesday's practice, Sam Cohn of The Baltimore Sun reports.
story: Baltimore is continuing to exercise caution with its star receiver, who is working his way back to 100 percent from a hamstring injury. Flowers was effective in his return Sunday but logged only 21 (33 percent) offensive snaps. He didn't aggravate the injury Sunday, though his practice reps remain limited for now.

headline: Head coach Jesse Minter said Monday that he expects Flowers to carry a full workload in Week 4 against the Titans on Sunday, Clifton Brown of the Ravens' official site reports.
story: Flowers had his workload limited during Sunday's 34-31 win against the Cowboys in Brazil. Despite playing only 21 snaps on offense, the fourth-year wide receiver finished with five catches on six targets for 84 yards to lead Ravens pass catchers in all three categories. Flowers will be Lamar Jackson's favorite target heading into Week 4 against a Titans defense that ranks eighth in the league in passing yards allowed per game (189.0).

headline: Flowers (hamstring) caught five of six targets for 84 yards and added a 20-yard rush in Sunday's 34-31 win over the Cowboys.
story: Flowers led the Ravens in catches, targets and receiving yards in his return following a one-game absence due to a hamstring injury. His most consequential catch was a 27-yard reception on the game's penultimate play, which set up Tyler Loop's game-winning 56-yard field goal. Per Jonas Shaffer of the Baltimore Banner, Flowers knew for a while that he would be suiting up Sunday, but he was limited in practice due to concerns about the quality of the field in Rio de Janeiro. Flowers has seemingly put the injury behind him heading into a Week 4 home game against the Titans.

headline: Flowers (hamstring) is active for Sunday's game against the Cowboys in Rio de Janeiro, Adam Schefter of ESPN reports.
story: Flowers' active status is a bit of a surprise considering he's logged just one limited practice since suffering a hamstring injury in the first half of a Week 1 win at Indianapolis. On top of that, the field conditions in Brazil appear to be less than ideal, but it won't stop the Ravens from making him available to handle snaps Sunday. How many plays that may translate to remains to be seen, but Flowers and Rashod Bateman presumably will be the top wide receivers at the disposal of QB Lamar Jackson.

headline: The Ravens continue to view Flowers (hamstring) as a game-time decision leading up to Sunday's tilt with the Cowboys in Rio de Janeiro, and the wide receiver is expected to be limited to "somewhere in the realm of 20 to 30 plays" if he suits up, Ian Rapoport of NFL Network reports.
story: After turning in a limited practice Friday, Flowers went through a pregame workout Sunday and appeared to be moving around well while testing out both his left hamstring and the soggy field conditions in Brazil. The Ravens are still contemplating whether to make Flowers available for the Week 3 contest, with an official call on his status expected to arrive when the team releases its inactive list 90 minutes prior to the 4:25 p.m. ET kickoff. Even if Flowers gets clearance to play, he looks like he could handle well under a full workload, making him a less appealing fantasy option than he normally would be as the Ravens' No. 1 wide receiver.

headline: Flowers (hamstring) "looked good" during a pregame workout, but he remains questionable for Sunday's game against the Cowboys in Rio de Janeiro, and the Ravens are still mulling whether he'll play, Adam Schefter of ESPN reports.
story: The field conditions in Brazil are a major factor in the Ravens' decision regarding the status of Flowers, who is nursing a hamstring injury and sat out the Week 2 loss to the Saints. He remained sidelined for the Ravens' first two Week 3 practices back in the United States before making the trip to Brazil and turning in a limited practice Friday. Flowers seemingly responded well both to that practice and during his pregame work, but he still looks to be a true game-time call leading up to the 4:25 p.m. ET kickoff. Even if Flowers gains clearance to play, the Ravens could manage his snaps to some degree.

headline: Flowers (hamstring) will participate in a pregame workout to determine his status for Sunday's game against the Cowboys in Rio de Janeiro, but the Ravens don't appear as if they expect him to play, Adam Schefter of ESPN reports.
story: Both Schefter and Ian Rapoport of NFL Network are calling Flowers a "true pregame decision," but the field conditions in Brazil ultimately appear to be a factor in whether or not the wide receiver will be cleared for game action, according to Mike Garafolo of NFL Network. Such a call won't be made by Baltimore until about 90 minutes before Sunday's 4:25 p.m. ET kickoff, but if Flowers ends up missing a second game in a row, Rashod Bateman will serve as the team's No. 1 wideout.

headline: Flowers (hamstring) is expected to "test his injury" prior to Sunday's game against the Cowboys, and if he suits up he "will likely be on a pitch count," Jeremy Fowler of ESPN.com reports.
story: Flowers was limited on Friday's injury report and given a questionable designation for Week 3, so the door is open for him to take the field Sunday in Brazil. However, it appears a final call on his availability will not be made until the Ravens release their inactives 90 minutes prior to Sunday's 4:25 p.m. ET kickoff, and even if Flowers is active he may not handle a full complement of snaps. Rashod Bateman would be the favorite to pick up the slack if Flowers is limited or unavailable altogether.

headline: Isaac (hamstring) is questionable to return to Thursday night's contest against the Jaguars.
story: Isaac is nursing a hamstring injury, and his status for the rest of the game is now uncertain. The linebacker operates primarily as a special-teams option, so his absence doesn't have any impact on Baltimore's defensive approach.

headline: Huntley (toe) was placed on injured reserve Thursday.
story: Huntley and Lamar Jackson (thumb) were both placed on injured reserve Thursday. The latter still has at least a slim chance to return this season, while Huntley's injury has been confirmed to be season-ending. Joe Fagnano is set to start Thursday's game against the Jaguars before reinforcements arrive under center in the form of Jacoby Brissett, for whom the Ravens are expected to finalize a trade over the weekend.

headline: Huntley (toe) has reportedly sustained a season-ending turf toe injury, Adam Schefter of ESPN reports.
story: Ravens head coach Jesse Minter previously noted that Huntley could be a candidate for injured reserve, and Schefter's report suggests that such a transaction is looming. With star QB Lamar Jackson out indefinitely due to a right thumb injury, Joe Fagnano is in line make his first career NFL regular-season start Thursday night against the Jaguars, while Kedon Slovis is on hand to serve as his backup. Beyond that, it's likely that the Ravens will add further QB depth in the coming days.

headline: Ravens head coach Jesse Minter said Tuesday that Huntley (toe) could be a candidate for injured reserve, Sam Cohn of The Baltimore Sunreports.
story: Following Sunday's 36-10 loss to the Bills, Minter confirmed that Lamar Jackson required thumb surgery and was ticketed for IR, and Huntley looks like he could join Jackson in being deactivated. Minter said that he expects to know by Wednesday whether Huntley will require an IR stint, as the Ravens are presumably still waiting on test results on the signal-caller's right toe injury. At the very least, Huntley is tracking toward sitting out Thursday's game against the Jaguars, as Minter announced Tuesday that undrafted rookie Joe Fagnano will serve as the Ravens' Week 9 starter.

headline: Huntley (toe) wasn't spotted practicing Tuesday, Jamison Hensley of ESPN.com reports.
