Tee Higgins (adductor) is expected to be a limited participant in Wednesday's practice, so if one or both of Cincinnati's top two wideouts are sidelined, receiver Dohnte Meyers and tight end Mike Gesicki could be in store for notable spikes in their target shares.

headline: Chase (concussion) has been ruled out for the rest of Sunday's game against the Jaguars.
story: Chase was taken out of the game to be checked for a possible concussion after his facemask was pulled at the end of a four-yard catch in the second quarter. With the superstar wide receiver done for the day, Tee Higgins will be Joe Burrow's top target in the passing game, with Dohnte Meyers, Mitchell Tinsley, running back Chase Brown and tight end Mike Gesicki all in line for bigger roles for the rest of the game. Chase will need to clear the league's five-step concussion protocol in order to be available for Week 5 against the Dolphins on Sunday, Oct. 11.

headline: Chase is under evaluation for a possible concussion during Sunday's game versus the Jaguars.
story: Chase was ripped down by his facemask on a four-yard catch by a Jacksonville defender in the second quarter and remained on the turf before hitting the sidelines and eventually going to the locker room. If he ends up entering the protocol for head injuries, he'll be out for the rest of Week 4, and Tee Higgins, Dohnte Meyers and Mitchell Tinsley will be tasked with WR duties for the rest of Sunday.

headline: Chase brought in nine of 12 targets for 98 yards and a touchdown in the Bengals' 30-27 loss to the Steelers on Sunday.
story: Chase paced the Bengals in receptions, receiving yards and targets, taking his customary position at the top of the team's pass-catching corps. The All-Pro wideout recorded his touchdown on a three-yard grab with just under six minutes remaining in the first quarter to answer a Steelers opening-drive score, marking his third trip to the end zone already this season. Chase will aim to stay just as productive when the Jaguars pay a visit for a Week 4 showdown next Sunday.

headline: Chase brought in seven of nine targets for 75 yards and two touchdowns in the Bengals' 20-6 win over the Texans on Sunday.
story: Chase recorded what already profiles as a Catch of the Year candidate on the first of his two touchdowns, one that saw him exhibit elite body control while making a narrowly inbounds, spinning grab from 32 yards out late in the second quarter. He went on to add an 18-yard TD reception in the latter portion of the third quarter as well, and he finished with the team lead in receptions while checking in as the runner-up to Tee Higgins in both receiving yards and targets. The rewarding fantasy day atoned for a quiet two-reception and scoreless Week 1 for the perennial Pro Bowler, who'll next tangle with the Steelers defense in a Week 3 road matchup next Sunday.

headline: Chase said Thursday that his knee feels great, Kelsey Conway of the Cincinnati Enquirer reports.
story: Chase sustained a knee injury in practice Aug. 25 but hasn't seemed bothered by it recently, as he suited up for the Week 1 win over the Buccaneers and has been practicing without limitations ahead of Sunday's road matchup with Houston. The star wide receiver had a disappointing 12 receiving yards against the Buccaneers, but starting slow has become the norm for Chase, who had 39, 62 and 26 receiving yards in the preceding three season openers. He bounced back from his 26-yard Week 1 showing in 2025 with 165 yards and a touchdown in Week 2.

headline: Chase brought in two of four targets for 12 yards in the Bengals' 33-27 win over the Buccaneers on Sunday.
story: Despite the Bengals shaking off their usual Week 1 offensive doldrums, it was still a relatively modest day for the air attack. Joe Burrow threw for a respectable 254 yards, but Chase wasn't prioritized anywhere near the norm and actually finished behind all of Mike Gesicki, Tee Higgins and Chase Brown in targets. Chase will continue to be the focal point of opposing defenses every week, but he should be in line for more opportunity in a Week 2 road matchup against a Texans defense that was surprisingly gashed by the Bills on Sunday.

headline: Burrow completed 24 of 29 passes for 271 yards and three touchdowns in Sunday's 34-17 win over the Falcons. He added seven yards and a TD on three carries.
story: It was a nearly flawless performance from Burrow, as he hit Ja'Marr Chase for a 47-yard score in the first quarter and tossed a pair of shorter TDs to Tee Higgins later in the contest. The superstar QB also got into the end zone on a goal-line sneak in the second quarter. It's the fourth straight game in which Burrow has produced at least four touchdowns, an incredible stretch in which he's completed 77.0 percent of his passes for 1,215 yards with a 16:3 TD:INT plus two more scores on the ground. The Bengals, not coincidentally, are 4-0 in that span. Burrow will look to stay locked in for a big AFC North clash against the Steelers in Week 10.

headline: Eric Moody: Joe Burrow, Ja'Marr Chase are matchup-proof in fantasy
story: Eric Moody: Joe Burrow, Ja'Marr Chase are matchup-proof in fantasy

headline: Burrow completed 38 of 48 passes for 462 yards with five touchdowns and three interceptions and added three carries for 10 yards and another score in the Bengals' 43-36 overtime win over the Titans on Sunday.
story: A Titans offense that had been mostly moribund all season unexpectedly came to life Sunday, requiring Burrow to remain aggressive throughout the afternoon. While that helped lead to his season-high three interceptions, it was also unsurprisingly a boon for his fantasy production, as the 2020 first overall pick finished with his second 400-yard performance of the season and a season-high five TD tosses. Burrow had his rapport with top receivers Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins working throughout the afternoon, as he connected with the duo a combined 21 times for 296 yards and three touchdowns. Burrow's other two scoring strikes went to Mike Gesicki and Jack Endries, and the prolific quarterback then sealed the win himself with a nine-yard scoring run at the seven-minute mark of overtime. Burrow and the Bengals now make the transatlantic flight to Madrid, Spain, where they'll face the Falcons next Sunday in a Week 9 matchup.

headline: Burrow completed 22 of 30 passes for 292 yards with four touchdowns and no interceptions while adding two rushes for 12 yards in the Bengals' 35-13 win over the Ravens on Sunday.
story: Burrow couldn't lead the Bengals to a single point in the first half, but the 2020 first overall pick came out of intermission locked in. He helped spearhead five consecutive scoring drives to start the second half, capping four of them with touchdown passes to Mike Gesicki (six yards), Tee Higgins (13 yards), Ja'Marr Chase (two yards ) and Drew Sample (16 yards). The game marked Burrow's second straight with four scoring tosses and zero interceptions, and both his passing yardage total and 73.3 percent completion rate were his second highest of the season. He'll take 1,653 passing yards and a 15:3 TD:INT into a Week 8 home matchup against the Titans next Sunday.

headline: Burrow completed 23 of 32 passes for 190 yards with four touchdowns and no interceptions and rushed four times for 10 yards in the Bengals' 31-24 win over the Dolphins on Sunday.
story: Burrow averaged only 5.9 yards per attempt and finished with a season-low passing yardage total, but he offset the modest numbers by throwing a season-high number of touchdown passes. The prolific signal-caller benefited from having both Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins available after each carried questionable designations into Sunday, and he connected with Mike Gesicki (four yards), Samaje Perine (six yards), Tanner Hudson (two yards) and Ja'Marr Chase (45 yards) for his quartet of scoring tosses. Burrow spread the ball around to nine different targets overall, and he'll take an 11:3 TD:INT into a Week 7 road matchup against the Ravens on Sunday, Oct. 25, following a Week 6 bye.

headline: Burrow completed 39 of 54 passes for 428 yards with one touchdown and two interceptions while rushing three times for six yards and another score in the Bengals' 22-17 loss to the Jaguars on Sunday. He also committed a fumble recovered by Cincinnati.
story: Burrow's passing yardage total was made all the more noteworthy by the fact he lost Ja'Marr Chase to a concussion in the first half. The prolific 2020 first-round pick put up new season highs in completions, pass attempts and passing yards, while also generating his first multi-interception tally of the campaign. The first of Burrow's picks came right after the two-minute warning in the first half at the Jaguars' 37-yard line and led to a Jacksonville touchdown. Nevertheless, he continued to battle as the Bengals trailed throughout the rest of the contest, and despite also losing Tee Higgins to an adductor injury with just under six minutes left, Burrow drove Cincinnati all the way down to the Jags' nine-yard line before losing the ball on downs with 56 seconds remaining. Prior to that point, Burrow had put his team in position for a potential game-winning touchdown via a 15-yard scoring toss to Mike Gesicki in the third quarter and a one-yard QB sneak with just over three minutes remaining for his first rushing score of the season. Burrow and the Bengals will look to regroup and potentially get Chase and Higgins back for a Week 5 road matchup against the Dolphins next Sunday.

headline: Burrow completed 28 of 37 passes for 282 yards with three touchdowns and no interceptions while adding two rushes for 13 yards in the Bengals' 30-27 loss to the Steelers on Sunday. He also lost a fumble.
story: Burrow was impressive throughout the majority of the afternoon, taking just one sack from Pittsburgh's aggressive defense and connecting with Ja'Marr Chase, Tee Higgins and Mike Gesicki for his trio of scoring tosses. Burrow spread the ball around to nine different targets overall on an afternoon he entered already down Andrei Iosivas (thumb, IR) and during which he then lost promising rookie Colbie Young (knee). However, a would-be game-tying or game-winning drive was short-circuited by the franchise signal-caller, as he lost the handle on the ball on a sack with under a minute remaining, snuffing out any chance of Cincinnati being able to at least force overtime. The highly untimely turnover aside, Burrow has looked comfortable with an offensive approach that has him under center more often than previous seasons, and he'll next take aim at the Jaguars in a Week 4 home matchup next Sunday.

headline: Johnson (ankle) is listed as active Sunday against the Falcons in Madrid.
story: Johnson suffered an ankle injury last Sunday versus the Titans, and he subsequently followed a DNP/LP/FP practice regimen during Week 9 prep before getting a questionable designation ahead of Sunday's international matchup. Now that he's confirmed to be active, he should be good for his normal 20-30 percent weekly defensive snap share.

headline: Johnson (ankle) is listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the Falcons in Madrid, Spain.
story: Johnson upgraded to a full participant in Friday's practice after missing consecutive sessions to start Week 9 prep. The reserve defensive end has a decent chance to suit up for Sunday's contest after such a large leap in practice participation.

headline: Johnson (ankle) has been ruled out for the rest of Sunday's game against the Falcons.
story: Johnson injured his ankle in the fourth quarter and will not return. Shemar Stewart should see more rotational snaps at defensive end for the rest of Sunday's contest.

headline: Johnson recorded four total tackles (three solo), including 2.0 sacks, during Sunday's 20-6 win over Houston.
story: Johnson was able to get to C.J. Stroud for a pair of sacks in the fourth quarter, and he has already matched his career high with 2.0 sacks this season. The defensive lineman was only on the field for 30 percent of the team's defensive snaps against Houston, and he's unlikely to repeat his performance Week 3 versus the Steelers.

headline: Howell (wrist) was placed on injured reserve by the Bengals on Tuesday.
story: Howell suffered a right wrist injury during Sunday's overtime win against the Titans, and he will now be forced to miss at least four contests as a result. The defensive lineman has already undergone surgery, per Mike Petraglia of CLNSCincy.com, and in Howell's absence, Shemar Stewart will stand to see an increase in workload at defensive end.

headline: Howell (wrist) has been ruled out for the rest of Sunday's game against the Titans.
story: Howell suffered a right wrist injury during the second half and will be sidelined for the rest of Sunday's contest. Shemar Stewart is in line for more defensive snaps in Howell's absence.

headline: Tinsley (coach's decision) is inactive for Sunday's game against Tennessee.
story: Tinsley has played in each of the Bengals' last three games and has logged four catches on eight targets for 56 yards over that span. He will observe Sunday's contest from the sidelines, and his next opportunity to play is Week 9 against the Falcons on Nov. 8.

headline: Tinsley caught three of his seven targets for 49 yards in the Bengals' 22-17 loss to the Jaguars on Sunday.
story: Tinsley's seven targets were fourth most among Bengals pass catchers behind Tee Higgins' (groin) 16, Chase Brown's 11 and Dohnte Meyers' nine. Tinsley stepped up after Ja'Marr Chase exited the contest with a concussion. Tinsley signed with the active roster Sept. 29 and likely will remain on it while the team deals with extensive injuries to the wide receiver corps.

headline: The Bengals signed Tinsley off the Texans' practice squad to the active roster Tuesday.
story: The Bengals needed to replenish their depth at wide receiver due to the injury absences of Andrei Iosivas (thumb, IR) and rookie fourth-rounder Colbie Young (knee), the latter of whom has already been ruled out for Week 4 against the Jaguars. Tinsley appeared in 17 regular-season games for the Bengals in 2025, finishing with an 8-117-2 receiving line on 24 targets, though he joined the Texans' practice squad Sept. 1 after failing to make Cincinnati's 53-man roster at the end of training camp. Now that he's back with the Bengals, Tinsley will contribute both on special teams and in a rotational role on offense.

headline: Young went without a target while playing 19 of the Bengals' 74 snaps on offense in Sunday's 43-36 overtime win over the Titans.
story: Though quarterback Joe Burrow set season highs in passing yards (462) and passing touchdowns (five), Young didn't see any involvement while the targets were highly concentrated among Ja'Marr Chase, Tee Higgins and Chase Brown. The fourth-round pick out of Georgia has held a bit role so far during his rookie season, recording two catches for nine yards on two targets through five appearances.

headline: Young (knee) was not listed on the Bengals' injury report Wednesday.
story: Young missed each of the Bengals' two games prior to the Week 6 bye due to a knee injury. The extra rest has paid dividends for the rookie fourth-rounder, who is on track to be available for Sunday's AFC North showdown against the Ravens. He's operated in a minimal role offensively this season, having logged only two catches on as many targets for nine yards across three games.

headline: Young (knee) is inactive for Sunday's game versus the Dolphins.
story: Young will miss a second consecutive contest. However, with Ja'Marr Chase (concussion) and Tee Higgins (groin/neck) active, Young likely wouldn't have seen much attention from Joe Burrow even if he were available.

headline: Young (knee) is listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the Dolphins, Paul Dehner Jr. of The Athletic reports.
story: A knee injury prevented the rookie fourth-rounder from playing against the Jaguars in Week 4, a game that saw both star wideouts Ja'Marr Chase (concussion) and Tee Higgins (groin/neck) sustain injuries. Chase and Higgins were both full participants in Friday's practice and also are listed as questionable, so if Young is cleared to play versus Miami, he'll be in line for a larger workload if one or both of Chase and Higgins cannot suit up.

headline: Young (knee) was a full-go at practice Thursday.
story: Young hurt his knee in Week 3 against Pittsburgh and didn't play last Sunday versus Jacksonville. However, his ability to practice in full Thursday makes him likely to suit up this Sunday against Miami. Ja'Marr Chase (concussion) and Tee Higgins (groin/neck) are both iffy to suit up against the Dolphins, so Young could have a key role in the Bengals' passing game if he's indeed ready to return.

headline: Young (knee) was a limited participant in Wednesday's practice, Jay Morrison of SI.com reports.
story: Young was unable to play against the Jaguars this past Sunday due to a knee injury that he picked up against the Steelers in Week 3. He's opened the week with a limited session, and if he can upgrade to a full practice participant over the next two days, then the rookie fourth-rounder would be in line to return against the Dolphins this Sunday. Young's availability would be even more crucial if one or both of Ja'Marr Chase (concussion) or Tee Higgins (groin) were unable to play against Miami.

headline: Young (knee) is not expected to play in Week 4 against the Jaguars, Jay Morrison of SI.com reports.
story: Young suffered a left knee injury in the first quarter of Sunday's 30-27 loss to the Steelers, and he was forced to miss the remainder of the contest. Head coach Zac Taylor provided an update Monday, explaining the wide receiver isn't dealing with a long-term injury, but he will be sidelined for at least one game. The Bengals are expected reevaluate the injury after Week 4 and then determine the next steps for Young.

headline: Young (knee) has been ruled out for the rest of Sunday's game against the Steelers.
story: Young injured his knee in the first quarter and was considered doubtful to return. He won't return for the second half, and the Bengals could have an update on the rookie fourth-rounder following Sunday's game. Dohnte Meyers and Ke'Shawn Williams will operate in expanded roles in Young's absence.

headline: Young (knee) is doubtful to return to Sunday's game against the Steelers.
story: Young was serving as the Bengals' WR3 due to the absence of Andrei Iosivas (thumb, IR), but the former injured his left knee while hauling in a two-yard pass from Joe Burrow. Dohnte Meyers and Ke'Shawn Williams are both in line for more work on offense in Young's absence.

headline: Bengals head coach Zac Taylor confirmed Wednesday that All has been diagnosed with a torn ACL in his right knee and will require season-ending surgery, Jay Morrison of SI.com reports.
story: All, who sustained the injury in Sunday's win over the Ravens, has now torn the ACL in his right knee three times during his career. He first tore the ACL during his final collegiate season at Iowa in 2023, then had his 2024 rookie campaign with the Bengals cut short after damaging the ligament again. Given the timing of the injury along with the fact that he'll be working his way back from a third surgery of the same knee, All is far from guaranteed to be ready to play when the 2027 season gets underway.

headline: The Bengals placed All (knee) on injured reserve Tuesday.
story: Though All will be eligible to return from IR as soon as Week 12, Ian Rapoport of NFL Network relays that the third-year tight end is feared to have sustained a season-ending ACL tear of his right knee during Sunday's 35-13 win over the Ravens. All will likely undergo further testing over the next day or two before the Bengals provide an updated diagnosis, but if the ACL tear is confirmed, the 26-year-old could be sidelined into the 2027 season. He previously tore the ACL in the same knee in 2023 during his final collegiate season at Iowa and during his 2024 rookie campaign with Cincinnati.

headline: All (knee) has been ruled out for the rest of Sunday's game against the Ravens.
story: All appeared to suffer the injury while making a catch in the third quarter. He'll be sidelined for the rest of Sunday's game, so Drew Sample and Jack Endries are both in line for more snaps the rest of the way.

headline: All notched two receptions (on three targets) for five yards during Sunday's 20-6 win versus the Texans.
story: All logged 25 offensive snaps in Week 2, finishing behind Drew Sample (36) and Mike Gesicki (21). After not garnering any attention from Joe Burrow in the 33-27 win over the Buccaneers in Week 1, the 26-year-old was targeted three times versus the Texans. All finished his rookie 2024 campaign with 20 receptions for 158 yards, but he didn't play in 2025 due to a knee injury. While All should have a weekly presence in the offense as long as he's healthy, he won't carry much fantasy value as long as Gesicki, Ja'Marr Chase, Tee Higgins and Chase Brown are available.

headline: All saw 20 offensive snaps but didn't get a target during Sunday's 33-27 win over the Buccaneers.
story: The 2024 fourth-round pick operated as the third tight end behind Drew Sample (41 snaps) and Mike Gesicki (21 snaps). All made 20 catches as a rookie two years ago before missing the 2025 campaign with a right knee injury. He doesn't seem like much of a factor in the passing game for the time being.

headline: Mafe finished Sunday's 35-13 win over the Ravens with five tackles (three solo), including 1.5 sacks.
story: Mafe got to Tyler Huntley for a six-yard sack midway through the first quarter before splitting another sack with Bryan Cook in the fourth. Mafe has logged at least 1.0 sacks in three consecutive games and is up to 4.5 sacks through six regular-season games, which already surpasses his total from 2025 with Seattle (2.0 sacks across 17 regular-season contests).

headline: Harden recorded five tackles (four solo), including 2.0 sacks, and one pass defense during the Browns' 23-22 overtime loss to the Saints in Week 9.
story: Harden took down Tyler Shough for 10- and six-yard sacks in the third and fourth quarters, respectively, which were the former's first sacks of his three-year NFL career. The 2024 seventh-rounder is up to 33 tackles (19 solo), including 2.0 sacks, and seven pass defenses (including one interception) through nine regular-season games.

headline: Harden (hamstring) is active for Sunday's game against the Steelers, Kelsey Russo of the Browns' official site reports.
story: Harden was initially tagged as questionable due to a hamstring injury that he sustained against the Titans in Week 7, but he's been cleared to play Sunday after recovering over the weekend and going through pregame warmups without suffering a setback. The third-year pro has accumulated 25 tackles (13 solo) and six pass defenses (including one interception) through seven regular-season games.

headline: Harden (hamstring) is listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the Steelers, Mary Kay Cabot of The Cleveland Plain Dealer reports.
story: Harden was limited in practice all week by a hamstring injury that he picked up in the Browns' Week 7 win over the Titans. Mekhi Blackmon and Emmanuel McNeil-Warren figure to be the top candidates for more defensive snaps in the secondary if Harden is not cleared to play in Sunday's AFC North tilt.

headline: Harden (hamstring) was a limited participant at practice Wednesday.
story: Harden hurt his hamstring during Sunday's game at Tennessee, and now his availability for Week 8 is in question. He'll probably have to manage a full practice Thursday or Friday to avoid carrying an injury designation into the weekend.

headline: Harden (hamstring) is questionable to return to Sunday's game against the Titans, Daniel Oyefusi of ESPN.com reports.
story: Harden tweaked his hamstring in the third quarter, and he's being evaluated by medical staff to determine whether he can return. Mekhi Blackmon will see more defensive snaps for as long as Harden is out of the game.

headline: Schwesinger (wrist) was a limited participant in Wednesday's practice, Mary Kay Cabot of The Cleveland Plain Dealer reports.
story: Schwesinger may have tweaked his wrist during the Browns' 23-22 overtime loss to the Saints in Week 9, when he logged a season-high 15 tackles (10 solo), including 2.0 sacks, and one forced fumble. He has two more chances to log a full practice ahead of Sunday's game against the Texans.

headline: Schwesinger notched 10 tackles (four solo) in Sunday's 27-6 loss to the Steelers.
story: Schwesinger led the Browns in tackles during the lopsided Week 8 loss. The 2025 second-round pick has 74 tackles (30 solo) this season, having cracked double digits in four of eight games.

headline: Schwesinger finished Sundays' 27-24 win over the Titans with eight tackles (four solo).
story: Schwesinger finished third on the Browns in tackles Sunday behind both Quincy Williams and Ronnie Hickman (10 each). Schwesinger has played every single defensive snap through seven regular-season games and has logged at least eight stops in six of those contests. He's up to 64 total tackles on the year, which leads the Browns and is sixth-most in the NFL.

headline: Schwesinger (ankle) was a limited participant at the Browns' practice Thursday.
story: Schwesinger was able to return to the field after missing the team's first practice of the week while tending to his lingering ankle injury. The linebacker has been able to play through the injury the last few weeks, and he seems likely to be good to go Sunday versus the Titans.

headline: Schwesinger (ankle) did not participate at practice Wednesday, Daniel Oyefusi of ESPN.com reports.
story: Schwesinger was able to play through his lingering ankle injury in Week 6 versus the Ravens, recording a season-high 13 total tackles in that game. The Browns may simply be exercising an abundance of caution, but Schwesinger's activity at practice as the week continues will still be worth keeping an eye on ahead of Sunday's contest at Tennessee.

headline: Schwesinger logged 13 tackles (five solo) and one forced fumble during the Browns' 13-10 win over the Ravens on Sunday.
story: Schwesinger was nursing an ankle injury during Week 6 prep, but he was given the green light to play after going through pregame warmups. He ended up leading the Browns in stops while playing every single defensive snap, and he made arguably the most important play of the game when he punched the ball out of Derrick Henry's hands early in the fourth quarter, and the Browns' offense capitalized with a two-yard rushing touchdown by Audric Estime seven plays later. Schwesinger has logged double-digit stops in three of six regular-season games and is up to 56 combined tackles, which is tied with Nakobe Dean and Anthony Hill for fifth-most in the NFL.

headline: Schwesinger (ankle) is active for Sunday's game against the Ravens.
story: Despite sustaining a Grade 1 right ankle sprain in last week's loss to the Jets and managing just one limited practice during Week 6 prep, Schwesinger has been cleared to suit up Sunday after making it through a pregame workout no worse for the wear. After taking home NFL Defensive Rookie of the Year honors in 2025, Schwesinger is off to another strong start to the current campaign, having compiled 43 tackles, including 1.0 sacks, a forced fumble and a pass breakup through five games.

headline: Schwesinger (ankle), who is listed as questionable for Sunday's contest against the Ravens, will go through a pregame workout before the Browns make a call on his status, Ian Rapoport of NFL Network reports.
story: The reigning NFL Defensive Rookie of the Year is nursing a Grade 1 right ankle sprain coming out of this past Sunday's loss to the Jets and was contained to one limited practice during Week 6 prep. Schwesinger showed enough during Friday's session for the Browns to keep the door open for him to play Sunday, but he'll need to check out well in his pregame work in order to get the green light to suit up. Official word on the linebacker's status will arrive when the Browns post their inactive list 90 minutes prior to the game's 1 p.m. ET kickoff.

headline: Schwesinger (ankle) is listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the Ravens.
story: Schwesinger was held out of the first two practices of Week 6 prep due to a Grade 1 ankle sprain that he picked up during the Browns' Week 5 loss to the Jets. He was able to practice in a limited fashion Friday to draw the questionable tag, but if he cannot play Sunday, then Winston Reid and rookie fifth-rounder Justin Jefferson would be the top candidates to start at linebacker.

headline: Schwesinger (ankle) did not participate at practice Thursday.
story: Schwesinger suffered a Grade 1 right ankle sprain in the Browns' contest against the Jets in Week 5, and his status for Week 6 is now in serious doubt. Unless he's able to get back on the practice field Friday, it's unlikely he'll be able to suit up Sunday versus the Ravens.

headline: Schwesinger sustained a Grade 1 right ankle sprain during the Browns' 17-12 loss to the Jets on Sunday, Ian Rapoport of NFL Network reports.
story: Schwesinger was spotted wearing a walking boot on his right foot following Sunday's loss, when he played every single defensive snap and logged eight tackles (five solo), including 1.0 sacks, one pass defense and one forced fumble. The Grade 1 sprain is a best-case scenario for the second-year linebacker, and he has not been ruled out for Week 6 against the Ravens, though his practice participation will provide clarity on whether he'll be cleared to play this coming Sunday. Winston Reid and rookie fifth-rounder Justin Jefferson figure to be the top candidates to start at linebacker if Schwesinger were to miss time.

headline: Schwesinger (lower leg) was seen in a walking boot after the Browns' 17-12 loss to the Jets on Sunday, Mary Kay Cabot of The Cleveland Plain Dealer reports.
story: Schwesinger sustained a lower-leg injury during Sunday's loss but did not receive an official injury designation. It is unclear how significant the injury to the defensive captain and signal caller is.

headline: Schwesinger made nine tackles (three solo) in the Browns' 27-24 win over the Steelers on Thursday.
story: Schwesinger played all 64 of the Browns' defensive snaps in the contest. The middle linebacker and defensive signal caller has played all 262 defensive snaps for the team through four regular-season games in 2026. Schwesinger's nine total tackles led the Browns and tied Steelers inside linebacker Payton Wilson for the most in the game.

headline: Schwesinger logged six tackles (one solo) in the Browns' 21-18 win over the Panthers on Sunday.
story: Schwesinger played all 74 defensive snaps in Sunday's contest. He has played all 196 defensive snaps for the Browns through three regular-season games. The middle linebacker and signal caller for the defense did not have any incredible box-score feats in the Week 3 win but practiced stellar communication that helped enable Mason Graham's 2.0 sacks and Ronnie Hickman's game-winning interception.

headline: Schwesinger recorded 10 tackles (five solo) during Sunday's 23-19 win at Tampa Bay.
story: Schwesinger followed up his strong Week 1 performance with a virtual repeat in Week 2, and he has now recorded 10-plus tackles in nine of his last 10 games going back to last season. He's an elite IDP option in most formats going into a Week 3 matchup versus the Panthers.

headline: Schwesinger finished with 10 tackles (three solo), including one for a loss, in Sunday's 34-10 loss to the Jaguars.
story: It was not the best day for the Cleveland defense, but its middle linebacker again was all over the field. Schwesinger won Defensive Rookie of the Year in 2025 after recording 156 tackles (67 solo), including 2.5 sacks, and three pass breakups, including two interceptions.

headline: Ward (quadriceps) was a limited participant at practice Wednesday, Mary Kay Cabot of The Cleveland Plain Dealer reports.
story: Ward was on the field for 73 of the Browns' 75 defensive snaps in Week 9, and his presence at practice Wednesday suggests his injury is likely not severe. If he can log a full practice Thursday or Friday, there's a solid chance he'll be able to avoid carrying an injury designation into the weekend.

headline: Ward (hand) is active for Sunday's game against the Titans.
story: Ward popped up on Friday's injury report due to a hand injury, logging a limited session in the process. A late addition to the injury report isn't typically a good sign, but the veteran cornerback has been given the green light to play in Sunday's road game. Ward has 25 tackles (15 solo), three pass defenses (including one interception) and two forced fumbles through six regular-season games.

headline: Ward (hand) is listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the Titans, Zac Jackson of The Athletic reports.
story: Ward appeared on the Browns' Friday injury report with a new hand injury. The cornerback managed to log a limited session despite the issue, but it remains uncertain whether he will be able to play through the injury in Sunday's contest. If Ward cannot suit up, Mekhi Blackmon or Toriano Pride will start at outside cornerback across from Tyson Campbell.

headline: Ward logged four tackles (three solo) and had one pass defensed for an interception in the Browns' 27-24 win over the Steelers on Thursday.
story: Ward intercepted Aaron Rodgers early in the second quarter on a deep throw. The cornerback came down with the ball at the Browns' 44-yard line, and the team's offense quickly marched down for a four-play, 56-yard touchdown to tie the game at seven. Ward also played all 64 of the Browns' defensive snaps in the contest.

headline: Williams (hamstring) was a limited participant in Wednesday's practice, Mary Kay Cabot of The Cleveland Plain Dealer reports.
story: Williams has been working through a hamstring issue as of late, although he was cleared to play against the Saints in Week 9, when he logged seven tackles (five solo) in a 23-22 overtime loss for the Browns. He's opened Week 10 prep with a limited session, and he has two more chances to log a full practice and avoid an injury designation ahead of Sunday's game against the Texans.

headline: Williams has no injury designation ahead of Sunday's game against the Saints, Scott Petrak of the Elyria Chronicle-Telegram reports.
story: Williams finished the week with back-to-back limited practices heading into Week 9 against the Saints. Williams has recorded 55 total tackles (32 solo), including 1.0 sacks, and four forced fumbles in eight games this season.

headline: Williams (hamstring) was a limited participant in Thursday's practice, Zac Jackson of The Athletic reports.
story: Head coach Todd Monken stated he is "optimistic" Williams will be available for the Week 9 meeting with the Saints. Although the 30-year-old was limited Thursday, it seems he's at least moving in the right direction. Williams has appeared in all eight of Cleveland's games this season, amassing 55 total tackles (32 solo), 1.0 sacks and four forced fumbles.

headline: Williams (hamstring) did not participate in practice Wednesday, Chris Easterling of the Akron Beacon Journal reports.
story: Williams missed Wednesday's practice with a hamstring injury, which likely occurred at some point during the Browns' Week 8 loss to the Steelers. However, head coach Todd Monken said he is "optimistic" that the 30-year-old will be ready for Week 9. Williams will need to upgrade his practice status by Friday for a chance to play.

headline: Williams finished Sunday's 27-24 win over the Titans with 10 tackles (seven solo).
story: Williams was working through neck and back injuries during Week 7 prep, but he was cleared to play Sunday and ended up playing every single defensive snap while co-leading the Browns in tackles with Ronnie Hickman. It was the second time in three games that Williams recorded double-digit stops, and he is up to 50 tackles (30 solo), including 1.0 sacks, two pass defenses and three forced fumbles through seven regular-season contests.

headline: Williams (neck) is active for Sunday's game against Tennessee.
story: Williams was limited in Friday's practice, an upgrade from his inactivity both Wednesday and Thursday. That was enough for him to draw the questionable tag for Week 7, and the veteran linebacker has been cleared by medical staff after going through pregame warmups. Williams has tallied at least six total tackles in four of his last five games.

headline: Williams (neck) is listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the Titans but expressed optimism Friday that he will play, Zac Jackson of The Athletic reports.
story: Williams didn't practice Thursday due to a neck injury, but he was cleared to return for Friday's session, for which he was listed as a limited participant. The veteran linebacker told reporters that he was at full speed during Friday's practice, but his official status may not be known until 90 minutes before Sunday's 1:00 p.m. ET kickoff, which is when the Browns will announce their list of inactive players. If Williams cannot play, then Justin Jefferson and Winston Reid would be the top candidates to start alongside Carson Schwesinger and Easton Mascarenas-Arnold at linebacker.

headline: Williams (neck) did not participate at the Browns' practice Thursday.
story: Williams was added to the injury report with an apparent neck injury Thursday, and he was forced to miss practice. The linebacker will have another chance to return to the field for the team's final practice Friday, but if he is unavailable in Week 7, Justin Jefferson would be a top candidate to draw a start at strongside linebacker versus the Titans.

headline: Burton (calf) didn't practice Wednesday, Mary Kay Cabot of The Cleveland Plain Dealer reports.
story: Burton suffered a calf injury against the Saints in Week 9. He was cleared to return to that contest, but he's still working through the injury and was held out of Wednesday's practice. Burton will have two more opportunities to practice ahead of Sunday's contest against the Texans.

headline: Burton (calf) has returned to Sunday's matchup against New Orleans, Daniel Oyefusi of ESPN.com reports.
story: Burton exited due to a calf injury in the first half and was deemed questionable to return. However, he was able to return to action before halftime. Burton should thus continue to get occasional snaps at fullback while also helping out on special teams.

headline: Burton (calf) is questionable to return to Sunday's game against the Saints, Daniel Oyefusi of ESPN.com reports.
story: Burton exited the first half of Sunday's game with a calf injury. The fullback may return to the contest pending further evaluation. If Burton cannot return, one of the Browns' three active tight ends will likely take on the role of fullback in select packages.

headline: Howard has cleared the league's concussion protocol and doesn't carry an injury designation into Sunday's game against the Steelers, Chris Easterling of the Akron Beacon Journal reports.
story: Howard has been cleared to play Sunday despite not logging a single practice during Week 8 prep. He's slated to start at right tackle, with Dawand Jones providing depth at the position.

headline: Howard (concussion) didn't participate in Cleveland's practice Wednesday.
story: Howard is in the league's concussion protocol after exiting Sunday's win over the Titans due to a concussion. Dawand Jones is in line to start at right tackle if Howard is unable to clear the concussion protocol before Sunday's matchup versus the Steelers.

headline: Howard is being evaluated for a possible concussion and is questionable to return to Sunday's game against the Titans.
story: Howard was taken to the locker room in the second half and is being evaluated by medical staff to determine whether he can return. Dawand Jones has taken over at right tackle in Howard's absence.

headline: Howard (knee) does not have an injury designation against Baltimore on Sunday.
story: Howard ended Week 6 prep with a full practice Friday. That's enough for him to avoid an injury tag for Sunday, and he'll continue to start at right tackle.

headline: Howard (knee) did not participate at the Browns' practice Wednesday.
story: Howard suffered a knee injury in the fourth quarter of the team's Week 5 loss to the Jets and he was unable to return to the contest. He has now opened the week as a non-participant at the team's first practice, and he'll have two more chances to return to the field before Sunday's matchup with Baltimore.

headline: Howard (knee) is questionable to return to Sunday's game against the Jets.
story: The new starting right tackle suffered a knee injury in the fourth quarter of Sunday's contest. With Howard absent, Dawand Jones may need to finish the game at right tackle for the Browns' offense.

headline: Browns head coach Todd Monken said Wednesday that Jenkins has cleared the league's concussion protocol, Tom Withers of The Associated Press reports.
story: Jenkins practiced fully Wednesday, putting him on track to play in Sunday's game against the Jets. He missed the Browns' Week 4 win over the Steelers while recovering from the concussion.

headline: Jenkins (concussion) is officially listed as out for Thursday's game versus the Steelers.
story: Jenkins was unable to practice during the week after entering concussion protocol, and he'll now spend at least one game on the sidelines as he recovers. In his stead, Luke Wypler projects to start at center in Week 4.

headline: Jenkins didn't participate at practice Tuesday due to a concussion, Daniel Oyefusi of ESPN.com reports.
story: Jenkins entered the concussion protocol in the wake of Sunday's 21-18 win over the Panthers. With no listed participation in the Browns' first two Week 4 sessions, Jenkins could have a tough time clearing the protocol ahead of Thursday's game against the Steelers. If Jenkins can't play Thursday, Luke Wypler would likely be in line to start at center.

headline: Jenkins (back) does not carry an injury designation into Sunday's game against the Buccaneers.
story: Jenkins was limited by a back injury in each of the first two practices of the week. He's been given the green light to play Sunday after logging a full practice Friday, and Jenkins will once again serve as the Browns' starting center while rookie fifth-rounder Parker Brailsford (thumb) provides depth at the position.

headline: Jenkins (back) was a limited participant in practice Thursday, Scott Petrak of the Elyria Chronicle-Telegram reports.
story: The starting center was limited Wednesday as well. If the issue is serious enough to keep Jenkins out of Sunday's game against the Buccaneers, Parker Brailsford (thumb) and Luke Wypler are in line to step in.

headline: Fannin (groin) was limited in Wednesday's practice, Mary Kay Cabot of The Cleveland Plain Dealer reports.
story: Fannin dealt with the groin issue in practice last week but ultimately avoided an injury designation ahead of last Sunday's overtime loss to the Saints. In that contest, Fannin caught both of his targets for 42 yards and a touchdown. He had been silent for much of the game before producing a 39-yard touchdown in the extra frame. The overall TE7 in half-PPR points per game this season, Fannin has 37 catches for 453 yards and four touchdowns on 53 targets through nine appearances.

headline: Fannin caught both his targets for 42 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 23-22 overtime loss to the Saints.
story: With Shedeur Sanders under center for the first time in place of Deshaun Watson (concussion), Fannin did little in regulation as the second-year QB instead looked for rookie wideouts Denzel Boston and KC Concepcion. Sanders went back to a more familiar target in OT, however, connecting with Fannin on a 39-yard TD in the extra frame that saw the tight end flatten a couple defenders with stiff arms on his way to the end zone. Fannin had a slow start to the season, but over the last three weeks he's amassed an 18-287-1 line on 23 targets, giving him plenty of momentum heading into a Week 10 clash with the Texans no matter who is throwing him passes.

headline: Fannin (groin) will play Sunday against the Saints, Daniel Oyefusi of ESPN.com reports.
story: Coach Todd Monken said Fannin is "a little sore" but will be out there against New Orleans. On paper, it's a great spot for Fannin, but playing at less than 100 percent knocks him down a peg as a backend TE1 for fantasy.

headline: Fannin (groin) is practicing Friday, Daniel Oyefusi of ESPN.com reports.
story: After being listed as a limited participant Thursday, Fannin appears to be back on the field ahead of Sunday's game against the Saints. His Friday activity is a positive sign for his availability, but it doesn't confirm whether he'll carry an injury designation into the weekend.

headline: Fannin (groin) was a limited participant in Thursday's practice, Scott Petrak of the Elyria Chronicle-Telegram reports.
story: Fannin wasn't listed on Wednesday's injury report, so his appearance on it a day later is notable. It remains to be seen if Thursday's listed limitations were maintenance related or indicative of a setback, but the tight end may need to work fully Friday in order to approach Sunday's game against the Saints without an injury designation.

headline: Fannin brought in 10 of 12 targets for 154 yards in the Browns' 27-6 loss to the Steelers on Sunday. He also lost a fumble.
story: Fannin was one of the few bright spots for the Browns on either side of the ball in the ugly loss despite an early fumble, setting new career highs in receptions, receiving yards and targets. Cleveland's gradual shift to a pass-centric approach as its deficit grew was a boon for Fannin's production, and the second-year tight end now has a combined 16-245-0 line on 21 targets over the last two games alone. Fannin will aim to carry over the elite caliber of play into a Week 9 road matchup against the Saints next Sunday.

headline: Fannin caught six of nine targets for 91 yards in Sunday's 27-24 win over the Titans.
story: The second-year tight end delivered a season high in receiving yards, and Fannin's last catch was his biggest. With the game tied at 24-24 in the final minute of the fourth quarter, Fannin took a short pass over the middle from Deshaun Watson and tacked on about 30 yards after the catch to set up Andre Szmyt's game-winning field goal. Fannin will take a 25-257-3 line on 39 targets through seven games into a Week 8 clash with the Steelers.

headline: Fannin brought in one of three targets for nine yards in the Browns' 13-10 win over the Ravens on Sunday.
story: Fannin was quiet for a second straight game while Jerry Jeudy surprisingly paced the Browns' air attack with a season-high 69 receiving yards. Fannin's production has been hard to trust during the first few weeks of the season, as he's recorded five or more catches just twice and three receptions and 27 receiving yards or less in his other four games. Fannin will look for a boost in his numbers during a Week 7 road matchup against the Titans on Sunday.

headline: Fannin caught one of four targets for four yards in Sunday's 17-12 loss to the Jets.
story: Fannin was neutralized by New York's defense in rainy conditions at MetLife Stadium. The 2025 third-round pick's sophomore season is off to an inconsistent start, as Fannin has failed to exceed 27 yards on three occasions while recording at least 51 yards on two occasions. He had scored three times during a brief two-game touchdown streak that was snapped in Sunday's dud. Fannin will try to get back on track in Week 6 against the Ravens.

headline: Fannin secured three of five targets for 27 yards and a touchdown in the Browns' 27-24 win over the Steelers on Thursday.
story: After surging over the last pair of contests, Fannin had a quiet night somewhat reminiscent of his Week 1 performance against the Jaguars. However, the second-year tight end still rewarded fantasy managers by crossing the goal line for the third time in the last two games on a two-yard catch late in the first half. Fannin does have at least five targets in three straight games, and he should have a good chance of continuing to serve as a key target for a resurgent Deshaun Watson in a Week 5 road matchup against the Jets on Sunday, Oct. 11.

headline: Fannin brought in seven of nine targets for 51 yards and two touchdowns in the Browns' 21-18 win over the Panthers on Sunday.
story: The second-year tight end led the Browns in receptions, receiving yards and targets on the afternoon, and he capped off Cleveland's upset victory with a 14-yard touchdown grab at the 1:48 mark of the fourth quarter. The score proved to be the difference in the game, and it was preceded by a two-yard scoring reception just before halftime. After a quiet Week 1, Fannin has come alive with a combined 12-125-2 line on 15 targets over the last pair of contests, affording him plenty of momentum heading into a Week 4 divisional home showdown against the Steelers on Thursday night.

headline: Fannin secured five of six targets for 54 yards in the Browns' 23-19 win over the Buccaneers on Sunday.
story: The second-year tight end bounced back from a quiet Week 1 to post a productive stat line Sunday akin to many he'd generated during an impressive 2025 rookie campaign. Fannin tied for second on the day in receptions and targets for Cleveland while also checking in as the runner-up in receiving yards, serving as a frequent security blanket for Deshaun Watson. Fannin should continue seeing plenty of opportunity as his chemistry with Watson grows, and he'll next take aim at the Panthers' defense in Week 3 home matchup.

headline: Fannin brought in two of three targets for 21 yards in the Browns' 34-10 loss to the Jaguars on Sunday.
story: Deshaun Watson mostly struggled against an aggressive Jaguars defense that sacked him five times and picked him off once, so Fannin's generally disappointing numbers don't look quite as bleak within that context. The talented second-year tight end still is projected to remain a critical piece in the Browns' passing game, and Fannin could see a larger role as soon as a Week 2 road matchup against the Buccaneers.

headline: Browns head coach Todd Monken said Wednesday that Hickman is in concussion protocol, Daniel Oyefusi of ESPN.com reports.
story: Hickman suffered a concussion in Week 9 against the Saints. He will have multiple steps to work through, but has the full week to clear concussion protocol. The fourth-year pro has 57 tackles (26 solo), four pass deflections and one interception in nine regular-season games this season.

headline: Hickman registered 10 tackles (six solo) and a fumble recovery during Sundays' 27-24 win over Tennessee.
story: Hickman and Quincy Williams co-led the Browns in tackles Sunday, with the former playing every defensive snap for the sixth time this season. Hickman's 10 tackles were his most of the season, and the fourth-year safety is up to 41 tackles (19 solo), including 1.0 sacks, two pass defenses (including one interception) and two fumble recoveries through seven regular-season contests.

headline: Hickman logged five tackles (one solo) and one pass defensed in the Browns' 27-24 win over the Steelers on Thursday.
story: Hickman played all 64 of the Browns' defensive snaps in the contest. The free safety's pass defensed marked his second of the season, with his first coming in Week 3 as a key interception against the Panthers. Hickman also played three special-teams snaps in the contest, helping the Browns on kick coverage.

headline: Hickman made eight tackles (three solo) and had one pass defensed for an interception in the Browns' 21-18 win over the Panthers on Sunday.
story: Hickman intercepted Bryce Young on a third down with 16 seconds left in the game while the Browns were up by three points. The turnover sealed the game, securing the Browns consecutive wins for the first time since December 2023. The free safety played all 74 defensive snaps in the contest.

headline: Boston isn't slated to practice Wednesday due to a toe injury, Daniel Oyefusi of ESPN reports.
story: Boston logged a 93 percent offensive snap share in this past Sunday's 23-22 overtime loss to the Saints en route to hauling in six of his seven targets for 98 yards. However the rookie WR emerged from the contest with a toe issue that will make his status worth watching ahead of this weekend's game against the Texans. If Boston -- who's expected to return to practice Thursday, per Mary Kay Cabot of The Cleveland Plain Dealer -- ends up being available, he'll be catching passes once again from Deshaun Watson, while Week 9 starter Shedeur Sanders will revert to serving as the Browns' QB2.

headline: Boston caught six of seven targets for 98 yards in Sunday's 23-22 overtime loss to the Saints.
story: The 98 yards led the Browns on the afternoon, and Boston showed some immediate chemistry with Shedeur Sanders, connecting with the QB on a 60-yard strike in the third quarter that nearly resulted in a touchdown. The rookie receiver was also the target on a two-point conversion attempt that would have won the game in OT, but the pass got broken up. Boston also set a new career high in receiving yards with the performance, and if Sanders takes over for Deshaun Watson (concussion) under center on a permanent basis, it could lead to plenty more big plays. Through his first nine NFL games. Boston has delivered a 32-507-3 line on 61 targets.

headline: Boston (calf) was a full participant in Friday's practice and doesn't have an injury designation for Sunday's game at New Orleans, Chris Easterling of the Akron Beacon Journal reports.
story: With Boston upgrading from limited sessions Wednesday and Thursday to full participation Friday, he should be fine for his usual role as a near-every-down player in a young Cleveland offense. It'll be his first chance to work with Shedeur Sanders extensively outside of a practice environment, as the Browns reportedly won't start Deshaun Watson (head) even if he clears concussion protocol before the game.

headline: Boston (calf) remained limited in Thursday's practice, Mary Kay Cabot of The Cleveland Plain Dealer reports.
story: Boston dealt with a foot issue a couple weeks ago, but the calf injury is new this week. The rookie wideout has been scuffling after a hot start to the season. Perhaps the likely insertion of Shedeur Sanders this Sunday against the Saints can help Boston regain his big-play ability. Boston is a low-floor, upside WR4 for fantasy.

headline: Boston was a limited participant in Wednesday's practice due to a calf injury, Scott Petrak of the Elyria Chronicle-Telegram reports.
story: Boston made appearances on the injury report in Weeks 6 and 7 due to a foot issue, but he's tending to a new health concern coming out of this past Sunday's 27-6 loss to the Steelers. The rookie wideout will have two more chances this week to upgrade to full practice, and if he does, he should head into Sunday's game in New Orleans without an injury designation.

headline: Boston caught six of 11 targets for 37 yards during Sunday's 27-6 loss to the Steelers.
story: Boston entered Week 8 having caught just four of 13 targets for 42 yards over the previous two games, so Sunday's output was a step in the right direction. The wide receiver's 11 targets were a new career high, and he ranked second behind tight end Harold Fannin (12) in the category versus Pittsburgh. Boston has now reeled in 26 of 53 targets for 409 yards and three touchdowns over the first eight games of the 2026 campaign.

headline: Boston caught three of eight targets for 27 yards in Sunday's 27-24 win over the Titans.
story: The wide receiver was the favorite for the Offensive Rookie of the Year after the first five weeks of the season, but he's now posted back-to-back subpar games against the Ravens and Titans. During those two contests, Boston has four catches for 42 yards on 13 targets. He's been extremely inefficient with his looks and isn't getting loose for big plays over the top of the defense. He'll try to get back on track next Sunday in Pittsburgh.

headline: Boston (foot) doesn't have an injury designation for Sunday's game against the Titans, Zac Jackson of The Athletic reports.
story: Boston played through the same injury last week and took 92 percent of Cleveland's snaps on offense in a 13-10 win over the Ravens. He caught just one of five targets for 15 yards, showing the downside of being a deep threat in an offense with poor QB play.

headline: Boston (foot) remained limited at Thursday's practice.
story: Boston has been bothered by a foot injury since the start of Cleveland's Week 6 preparations against the Ravens. He suited up for that game after three limited practices but was held to one catch, and the rookie second-round pick has opened Week 7 prep with a pair of limited sessions. Boston will look to increase his practice participation Friday and avoid an injury designation for Sunday's game against the Titans.

headline: Boston (foot) was a limited participant at Wednesday's practice, Chris Easterling of the Akron Beacon Journal reports.
story: Though he didn't end up practicing fully at any point in Week 6 while managing the same foot injury, Boston still avoided a designation for this past Sunday's 13-10 win over the Ravens and ended up logging more than 90 percent of the offensive snaps. As long as he maintains or increases his current level of practice activity throughout the week, Boston should be ready to handle his usual playing time this coming Sunday versus the Titans.

headline: Boston caught one of five targets for 15 yards in Sunday's 13-10 win over the Ravens.
story: It was easily the rookie wideout's least productive game of the season, but the Browns struggled as a whole to get anything going against Baltimore's pass defense. Deshaun Watson amassed just 164 passing yards. Boston was still second on the team in targets, seeing just one fewer than KC Concepcion. Boston will try to rebound in a softer matchup with the Titans next Sunday.

headline: Boston (foot) doesn't have an injury designation for Sunday's game against the Ravens, Chris Easterling of the Akron Beacon Journal reports.
story: A limited practice participant throughout the week, Boston should be fine for his usual workload unless there's an in-game setback Sunday. He's rarely left the field for Cleveland this season, and his big plays have been about the only bright spot on offense.

headline: Boston (foot) remained limited at Thursday's practice.
story: Boston has logged back-to-back limited practices to kick off Week 6 prep. The rookie wideout could still avoid taking an injury designation into Sunday's pivotal home game against the Ravens, especially if he can upgrade to full participation Thursday. Fellow rookie WR KC Concepcion (concussion) was also limited both Wednesday and Thursday. More opportunities could be available for Jerry Jeudy and Isaiah Bond should one or both of Boston and Concepcion sit Sunday.

headline: Boston was listed as a limited participant in Wednesday's practice due to a foot injury, Chris Easterling of the Akron Beacon Journal reports.
story: The rookie second-round pick is making his first career appearance on the injury report, but his ability to practice on at least a limited basis to begin Week 6 prep is a good sign for his chances of playing Sunday against the Ravens. The current betting favorite for the Offensive Rookie of the Year Award, Boston has opened his career with a 16-330-3 receiving line on 29 targets through five games.

headline: Boston caught three of seven targets for 46 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 17-12 loss to the Jets.
story: Boston's 29-yard touchdown catch with 6:15 left in the fourth quarter gave the Browns a 12-10 lead, but Cleveland failed to hold that advantage. The rookie second-round pick has caught 16 of 29 targets for 330 yards and three touchdowns while exceeding 40 receiving yards in each of his first five NFL outings. KC Concepcion, who was drafted 15 picks ahead of Boston at 24th overall, exited Sunday's loss due to a concussion. Boston could get a larger share of targets from Deshaun Watson if Concepcion doesn't rejoin Cleveland's WR room in Week 6 against the Ravens.

headline: Boston brought in four of seven targets for 89 yards in the Browns' 27-24 win over the Steelers on Thursday.
story: The impressive start to Boston's NFL career continued Thursday, with the rookie second-round pick leading the Browns in receiving yards and tying for runner-up status with Quinshon Judkins in targets. The bulk of Boston's production came on an impressive 60-yard reception to kick off an early second-quarter possession that culminated in a Judkins two-yard touchdown run. Boston has quickly amassed a 13-284-2 line on 22 targets through his first four career games, affording him plenty of momentum heading into a Week 5 road matchup against the Jets on Sunday, Oct. 11.

headline: Boston caught two of four targets for 41 yards during the Browns' 21-18 win over the Panthers on Sunday. He also caught a two-point conversion.
story: The rookie second-rounder was held without a catch until the fourth quarter, when he caught 28- and 13-yard passes from Deshaun Watson before the duo connected on a two-point conversion late in the fourth quarter to extend the Browns' lead to three points. Boston was unable to record a touchdown catch for a third-straight game, though he still finished Sunday's contest as the Browns' second-leading receiver behind tight end Harold Fannin (51). Boston, Fannin and rookie first-rounder KC Concepcion will continue to serve as Watson's top targets in the passing game, with Jerry Jeudy and Isaiah Bond working in rotation. Boston will take a 9-195-2 receiving line (on 15 targets) into Thursday's AFC North showdown against the Steelers.

headline: Boston caught five of seven targets for 95 yards and a touchdown in the Browns' 23-19 win over Tampa Bay on Sunday.
story: Boston's big play was a 55-yard touchdown late in the third quarter to pull the Browns even with the Bucs at 16-16. The rookie wideout caught a deep crosser and spun off several would-be tackles and dashed to the end zone. It was Boston's second long touchdown in as many weeks to begin his pro career. Through two games, the second-round pick has seven catches for 154 yards and two scores on 11 targets. He's shaping up as a boom-or-bust fantasy WR4 headed into next Sunday's home date with the Panthers.

headline: Boston caught two passes on four targets for 59 yards and a touchdown during the Browns' 34-10 loss to the Jaguars on Sunday.
story: It wasn't until the third play of the fourth quarter that Boston made his first NFL catch, a 13-yard pass from Deshaun Watson, before the duo connected on a 46-yard touchdown pass on the first play following the two-minute warning. Boston finished Sunday's game as the Browns' leader in receiving yards while fellow rookie KC Concepcion led the team in catches (four) and targets (five). There figures to be some growing pains for the Browns' offense this season given the amount of young talent. Cleveland will stay on the road for a Week 2 matchup against Tampa Bay on Sept. 20.

headline: Sanders will return to a backup role for Sunday's game against the Texans after the Browns announced Wednesday that Deshaun Watson (concussion) will draw the Week 10 start, Kelsey Russo of the team's official site reports.
story: Watson led the Browns to a 5-3 record over their first eight games before developing concussion symptoms and being placed in the NFL's five-step protocol last week. Though Watson cleared protocol last Saturday, his lack of on-field reps during the week prompted the Browns to keep him inactive for Sunday's matchup with the Saints. Sanders stepped in under center and overcame a slow start to finish with 297 passing yards, 28 rushing yards, two passing touchdowns and no turnovers in a 23-22 overtime loss, with his performance drawing praise from head coach Todd Monken. Though the Browns will go back to a healthy Watson for Week 10, Sanders' strong outing in New Orleans could put Watson on shakier ground atop the depth chart.

headline: Sanders completed 19 of 31 passes for 297 yards and two touchdowns in Sunday's 23-22 overtime loss to the Saints. He added 28 yards on 10 carries.
story: Making his first start of the season in place of Deshaun Watson (concussion), Sanders put together an impressive performance, hitting KC Concepcion for a 64-yard TD late in the fourth quarter and then connecting with Harold Fannin for a 39-yard score in OT. Todd Monken elected to go for the win with a two-point conversion rather than giving the ball back to New Orleans, but Sanders' attempt to hit Denzel Boston in the corner of the end zone failed, although the play would have been wiped out by a holding call anyway. Even if Watson is deemed ready to go ahead of a Week 10 meeting with the Texans, Sanders' strong showing may have given his coach something to think about.

headline: Sanders will start at quarterback Sunday against the Saints, Scott Petrak of the Elyria Chronicle-Telegram reports.
story: Coach Todd Monken said the move is because Deshaun Watson (concussion) missed so much practice time this week. Watson has been one of the worst statistical quarterbacks in the league over the last month, so Sanders could potentially keep the job if he has a good game versus the Saints. Sanders' insertion under center doesn't change the outlook of the offense, as both Watson and Sanders are game-manager types.

headline: Sanders could be needed to start Sunday's game at New Orleans after Deshaun Watson was placed in concussion protocol when he experienced symptoms Monday, Mary Kay Cabot of The Cleveland Plain Dealer reports.
story: During this past Sunday's 27-6 loss to the Steelers, Watson briefly departed the game in the first quarter after a helmet-to-helmet hit from safety Jaquan Brisker. Sanders checked in and completed both of his pass attempts for two yards across four total plays before Watson was cleared to return for the Browns' next possession. However, with the concussion symptoms surfacing a day later, Watson's availability for Week 9 is now in jeopardy. Watson will still have time to clear the five-step protocol ahead of Sunday, but expect Sanders to at least get some reps in with the first-team offense Wednesday during the team's first practice of the week.

headline: Sanders is active as the Browns' backup quarterback for Sunday's game against the Titans.
story: After Deshaun Watson had a listless performance in a blowout loss to the Jaguars in Week 1, Ian Rapoport of ESPN had reported that Sanders could get a chance to start as soon as Week 3 if the Browns continued to languish. Watson has since steadied the ship, leading the Browns to wins in four of their last five games to put them atop the AFC North standings heading into Week 7 action. As a result, Sanders doesn't appear likely to threaten Watson's standing atop the depth chart anytime soon, though Sanders will continue to suit up on game days ahead of rookie Taylen Green, who will once again be inactive Sunday as the Browns' emergency No. 3 quarterback.

headline: The Browns plan to re-evaluate their quarterback situation following Sunday's game against the Buccaneers, with Sanders being next in line to start if Cleveland elects to bench Deshaun Watson, Ian Rapoport of ESPN reports.
story: After winning the battle for the starting job during the preseason, Watson will direct the offense for a second straight game to begin the regular season, but he heads into Sunday's contest with limited job security. In the Browns' season-opening 34-10 loss to the Jaguars, Watson struggled to move the ball throughout the afternoon, completing 16 of 22 attempts for 205 yards and an interception while throwing his lone touchdown with less than two minutes remaining in the fourth quarter. If Watson bounces back with a strong performance against Tampa Bay, he'll likely retain the starting job heading into the Browns' home opener Week 3 versus the Panthers, but another poor showing could set up Sanders to take over as the team's top quarterback.

headline: The Browns announced Wednesday that Watson (concussion) will start Sunday's game against the Texans, Kelsey Russo of the team's official site reports.
story: Watson cleared the NFL's five-step concussion protocol this past Saturday, but because he managed just one limited practice during Week 9 prep, the Browns opted to make him inactive for their matchup with the Saints. Shedeur Sanders drew his first start of the season and threw for 297 yards and two touchdowns in the team's 23-22 overtime loss in New Orleans, but he'll return to the No. 2 role this week while a healthy Watson reclaims the starting job. Though the Browns have gone 5-3 with Watson under center this season, he hasn't been without his flaws (six turnovers, 33 sacks taken). As such, Watson may need a strong showing against the Texans to hold off Sanders for the starting job in the weeks to come.

headline: Watson (concussion) will serve as the Browns' starting quarterback in Sunday's game against the Texans, a source tells Mary Kay Cabot of The Cleveland Plain Dealer reports.
story: Jeremy Fowler of ESPN.com first reported Monday that Watson was in line for the Week 10 start, after his placement in concussion protocol during Week 9 kept him from playing in this past Sunday's 23-22 overtime loss to the Saints. Head coach Todd Monken then said later Monday that he wasn't ready to name a Week 10 starter between Watson and Shedeur Sanders, the latter of whom performed respectably in the loss to New Orleans. Ultimately, the Browns look like they'll go back to Watson, who cleared protocol Saturday and will be able to get in a full week of practice leading up to the matchup with the Texans. Watson guided the Browns to a 5-3 record through the first eight games while completing 65.5 percent of his passes and accounting for eight touchdowns (seven throwing, one rushing).

headline: The Browns are planning for Watson (concussion) to start Sunday's game against the Texans, Jeremy Fowler of ESPN.com reports.
story: After entering concussion protocol following the Browns' Week 8 loss to the Steelers, Watson was able to resume practicing in a limited fashion Friday and then passed neurological tests Saturday. However, because of the lack of prep time leading up to Sunday, Watson ended up being inactive for the Browns' 23-22 overtime loss to the Saints while Shedeur Sanders made his first start of the season. Though Sanders performed capably in the losing effort, Watson -- who helped lead Cleveland to a 5-3 record through its first eight games -- will retain the starting gig and will return to the lineup against Houston following a normal week of practice, barring any setbacks.

headline: Watson (concussion) is inactive for Sunday's game against the Saints, Daniel Oyefusi of ESPN.com reports.
story: Watson, who reported concussion symptoms Tuesday, didn't practice Wednesday or Thursday before being deemed limited Friday and subsequently heading into the weekend with a 'questionable' tag. Though Watson has cleared the NFL's concussion protocol, the Browns have elected to err on the side of caution with the QB who has compiled a 5-3 record as the team's starter to date. With Watson listed as inactive versus New Orleans, Shedeur Sanders will draw the start, while Dillon Gabriel will serve as Cleveland's No. 2 signal-caller. Taylen Green is the team's emergency No. 3 QB.

headline: Watson (concussion) is expected to be inactive for Sunday's game at New Orleans, Ian Rapoport of NFL Network reports.
story: After reporting concussion symptoms Tuesday, Watson didn't practice Wednesday or Thursday before returning to a limited session Friday and earning a questionable tag ahead of Week 9 action. He then cleared the concussion protocol Saturday, per the Browns. Despite Watson getting the thumbs-up from an independent neurologist, head coach Todd Monken already has announced Shedeur Sanders as Sunday's starter, and Jeremy Fowler of ESPN reports that Dillon Gabriel will serve as the No. 2 QB this weekend. In the end, Watson is slated to be back in action next Sunday against the Texans.

headline: Watson cleared the concussion protocol Saturday but remains questionable for Sunday's game at New Orleans.
story: Since Watson reported concussion symptoms Tuesday, he didn't practice Wednesday and Thursday before being limited Friday and earning a questionable tag for Week 9 action. Head coach Todd Monken relayed to Kelsey Russo of the Browns' official site Friday that Shedeur Sanders will be the team's starting quarterback Sunday, so some possibilities for Watson this weekend are active as the backup or inactive as the emergency third QB.

headline: Watson (concussion) is listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the Saints, but Shedeur Sanders will start even if Watson is active Kelsey Russo of the Browns' official site reports.
story: Per Daniel Oyefusi of ESPN.com, coach Todd Monken said Friday that he hasn't decided if Watson will be the team's Week 9 backup, as the QB -- who is in the NFL's concussion protocol -- has yet to be cleared. In any case, if Watson is active come Sunday, he'll merely be the backup. He was a limited practice participant Friday, after missing the previous two days.

headline: Watson (concussion) was present for practice Friday, Daniel Oyefusi of ESPN.com reports.
story: Ian Rapoport of NFL Network previously suggested that Watson "is unlikely to start" Sunday's game against the Saints, but either way, the QB's return to the field, in any capacity, is a positive step toward him advancing through the NFL's concussion protocol. Friday's final injury report will add further clarity to Watson's Week 9 status, but if he isn't cleared to play this weekend, Shedeur Sanders would be in line to start in his place.

headline: Watson (concussion) "is unlikely to start" Sunday's game against the Saints, Ian Rapoport of NFL Network reports.
story: Watson has not practiced since being placed in the NFL's concussion protocol Tuesday, and it appears he will not be cleared to suit up for Week 9. The Browns will provide an official update on Watson's status later Friday, and if he is unable to go, Shedeur Sanders would presumably get the start in his place.

headline: Watson (concussion) remained sidelined from practice Thursday, Daniel Oyefusi of ESPN.com reports.
story: With Watson, who is in the NFL's concussion protocol, in line to log back-to-back DNPs, the QB's status for Sunday's game against the Saints remains cloudy. In the event that Watson doesn't gain clearance to play this weekend, Shedeur Sanders will draw the start in his place.

headline: The Browns listed Watson (concussion) as a non-participant in Wednesday's practice.
story: Early in this past Sunday's 27-6 loss to the Steelers, Watson exited the game to get checked for a concussion following a helmet-to-helmet hit, but he was cleared to re-enter the contest after missing just four offensive snaps. However, after he had some late-surfacing symptoms, Watson entered concussion protocol Tuesday and was a spectator for the Browns' first Week 9 session. According to Daniel Oyefusi of ESPN.com, Watson "felt a lot better" Wednesday and was involved in meetings, but Shedeur Sanders took all the reps with the first-team offense. Sanders appears to be trending toward starting Sunday against the Saints, as Monken acknowledged that it will be difficult for Watson to play even if he ends up clearing the protocol late in the week, per Scott Petrak of the Elyria Chronicle-Telegram.

headline: Watson is expected to face an uphill battle to clear concussion protocol prior to Sunday's game against the Saints, leaving Shedeur Sanders as the Browns' likely Week 9 starting quarterback, Mary Kay Cabot of the Cleveland Plain Dealer reports.
story: After reporting concussion symptoms Tuesday following Sunday's loss to the Steelers, Watson entered the protocol and isn't expected to practice Wednesday. Sanders will take all of the first-team reps Wednesday, and unless Watson can pass through the protocol quickly, the Browns will prepare for the second-year signal-caller to direct the offense in Week 9.

headline: The Browns announced Wednesday that Watson has been placed in concussion protocol.
story: Watson took a helmet-to-helmet hit in the first quarter of Sunday's 27-6 loss to the Steelers, and after being examined by an independent consultant he was cleared to return to the game. Though subsequent tests after the game and Monday morning showed no symptoms of a concussion, Watson informed the Browns on Tuesday morning that he was experiencing symptoms and was "immediately placed in the concussion protocol," per the team. Watson will need to clear the five-step protocol in order to play in Cleveland's Week 9 matchup with New Orleans, but if he's unable to go, Shedeur Sanders would be in line to start at quarterback for the first time this season.

headline: Watson completed 27 of 39 passes for 324 yards with no touchdowns or interceptions while rushing three times for two yards in the Browns' 27-6 loss to the Steelers on Sunday. He also lost a fumble.
story: Watson couldn't lead the Browns to a single touchdown, but he exceeded 300 passing yards for the second straight game since Cleveland was forced into a pass-centric approach. Watson displayed the most chemistry with Harold Fannin (10-154-0 on 12 targets), and he recorded completions to seven different targets overall. Watson also lost the handle on a combined sack by Patrick Queen and Cameron Heyward in the first quarter, which led to a Steelers touchdown. Watson will look to rebound in a favorable road matchup against the Saints in Week 9 next Sunday.

headline: Watson (undisclosed) returned to Sunday's game in Pittsburgh, Scott Petrak of the Elyria Chronicle-Telegram reports.
story: Watson endured a big hit on the Browns' first offensive possession and was required to visit the medical tent for what likely was to check on a possible concussion. He's since been cleared to return to action.

headline: Watson went to the sideline tent in the first quarter of Sunday's game at Pittsburgh, Daniel Oyefusi of ESPN.com reports.
story: Watson took a big hit on the Browns' first offensive possession, and it appears he may be undergoing a check for a possible concussion. Shedeur Sanders will take over for Watson for as long as the latter is sidelined.

headline: Watson completed 25 of 36 passes for 308 yards with an interception in Sunday's 27-24 win over the Titans. He added 19 yards and a touchdown on three carries.
story: While he didn't throw a TD pass for a second straight game, Watson produced a season high in passing yards and scored his first rushing TD since Week 2 of the 2024 season on a nine-yard scamper in the fourth quarter. Watson also led his fifth game-winning, fourth-quarter drive of the year, completing another comeback after the Browns fell behind 14-0 early. The veteran QB will take a 7:3 TD:INT through seven games into a Week 8 meeting with the Steelers.

headline: Watson completed 16 of 26 passes for 164 yards with no touchdowns or interceptions and added eight carries for 29 yards in the Browns' 13-10 win over the Ravens on Sunday.
