Montgomery (abdomen) on IR, the 29-year-old Westbrook-Ikhine will work behind Deion Burks and Anthony Gould as they fill in for the injured Ashton Dulin (ankle).

headline: The Colts informed Taylor that he won't be traded before Tuesday's deadline, Tom Pelissero of Netflix reports.
story: In order to move Taylor, Indianapolis was reportedly seeking a blockbuster trade package on par with what Carolina received in exchange for Christian McCaffrey back in 2022, but Pelissero relays that inquiring teams weren't willing to meet that price tag. As a result, Taylor -- who is under contract through 2028 -- will stick around in Indianapolis through the remainder of the campaign, though it's possible that the Colts entertain trade offers for the 27-year-old running back again during the offseason.

headline: Taylor rushed 13 times for 46 yards and brought in all five targets for 18 yards in the Colts' 27-23 loss to the Cowboys on Sunday. He also lost a fumble.
story: Taylor suited up for what might have been his final game in a Colts uniform with Tuesday's trade deadline looming, and the star running back had a positively ordinary day. Taylor couldn't fully exploit a vulnerable Cowboys defense, and the fumble they forced from him early in the fourth quarter at Dallas' 20-yard line cost Indianapolis what seemed like a sure scoring opportunity. Taylor has seen reduced usage in the last two games as rumors have swirled about a potential trade, and James Boyd of The Athletic reports that Taylor answered "I don't know. I know as much as you" when asked about whether Sunday had marked his last game as a Colt. Taylor declined to confirm whether he'd requested a trade, and the next 48 hours will bring clarity on whether he'll still be helming the team's ground attack in Week 10 against the Dolphins.

headline: The Colts have an offer of "at least a second-round pick and more" on the table for Taylor but are "holding out for more," Mike Garafolo of NFL Network reports.
story: Despite the Colts' 2-6 start to the season, Taylor has remained the engine that drives the offense, racking up 169 touches for 812 yards from scrimmage and eight rushing TDs. The seventh-year pro thus sits 188 total yards shy of reaching 1,000 such yards for the sixth time in his career, so if the right offer crosses Indianapolis' desk, he'd be a vast upgrade for most backfields in the NFL.

headline: Taylor was a full participant at Thursday's practice, and Stephen Holder of ESPN.com reports that both Taylor and head coach Shane Steichen have maintained that Taylor will play Sunday against the Cowboys despite ongoing trade rumors surrounding the star running back.
story: "You can't avoid it," Taylor said of the trade rumors. "But it's more about trying to block that out." Taylor's preparing for what could well be his last game as a member of the Colts. Per NFL reporter Jordan Schultz, the 2-6 Colts have received trade calls on numerous players including Taylor, but Indianapolis doesn't intend to complete any additional trades prior to the conclusion of Sunday's game.

headline: Taylor rushed eight times for 23 yards and brought in four of five targets for 24 yards in the Colts' 42-7 loss to the Jaguars on Sunday. He also lost a fumble.
story: Taylor opened the game in his usual starting role with trade rumors swirling around him, and the star running back finished with a wholly unremarkable performance. Taylor ultimately ceded plenty of snaps to backfield mates Seth McGowan and DJ Giddens, the likeliest heir-apparent candidates if Taylor is indeed moved to another team in the coming days. Taylor had exceeded 90 rushing yards in back-to-back games and on five occasions overall heading into Week 8, so even if his Colts tenure finishes with Sunday's whimper, he'll have plenty to offer in a new destination.

headline: The Colts are fielding trade offers for Taylor, and while the asking price currently appears to be "too high," a deal seems likely to happen, per NFL reporter Jordan Schultz.
story: Adam Schefter of ESPN and Ian Rapoport of NFL Network reported Saturday morning that the Colts are willing to trade Taylor, but Schultz's report includes a new wrinkle, namely that a trade is more likely than not to occur. The Vikings, Giants, Broncos, Bengals and Packers are among the teams mentioned by Schultz that have checked in with Indianapolis regarding the seventh-year pro, who has looked like his usual dynamic self this season with 765 yards from scrimmage and eight rushing TDs on 157 touches in seven contests.

headline: Taylor is being made available via trade by the Colts, Adam Schefter of ESPN  reports.
story: Taylor himself was not requesting a trade earlier in the week, but Indianapolis' recent flurry of moves opened the possibility that the star running back would also be moved in the team's teardown before a rebuild. The Colts moved on from Quenton Nelson and DeForest Buckner and got significant draft capital from the Seahawks and 49ers in return. Now a market is forming for Taylor, 27, who could help put a contender over the top. Per Schefter, the Colts are seeking a deal similar to what the Panthers got in 2022 when they traded Christian McCaffrey.

headline: Taylor told reporters Thursday that he hasn't requested a trade out of Indianapolis, Stephen Holder of ESPN.com reports. "I haven't heard anything, and I can't control that," Taylor said regarding the possibility of being traded. "Obviously, you guys know that I'm always proud to wear the horseshoe, proud to be here."
story: The 2-5 Colts have gone into sell mode after firing GM Chris Ballard. Indianapolis traded away guard Quenton Nelson and defensive tackle DeForest Buckner to Seattle and San Francisco, respectively, but both of those players are on expiring contracts. Taylor signed a two-year, $44 million extension with the Colts in August, so the team may not feel as much urgency to trade him, and the star running back confirmed he hasn't requested a trade. Several teams have reportedly inquired about Taylor's availability.

headline: Taylor carried the ball 18 times for 95 yards and a touchdown and caught two of three targets for 15 yards in Sunday's 16-10 loss to the Vikings.
story: The Colts managed only 218 yards of offense in total, and Taylor had nearly as many rushing yards as Daniel Jones had passing yards. Taylor also scored his team's only TD on a 38-year-old dash in the first quarter. The star RB is still looking for his first 100-yard rushing performance of the season, but he's topped 90 yards in five of seven games and has produced 100-plus scrimmage yards four times while racking up eight scores on the ground. Taylor will face another tough run defense in Week 8 versus the Jaguars.

headline: Taylor carried the ball 21 times for 94 yards and a touchdown and caught two of four targets for 57 yards in Sunday's 26-20 loss to the Titans. He also lost a fumble.
story: For the fourth time in six games, Taylor came up just short of 100 rushing yards, but his 151 scrimmage yards were a season high, and he got into the end zone for the seventh time in 2026 on a four-yard run in the fourth quarter. His fumble was one of three Indy turnovers on the day, however, and it was Taylor's second lost fumble of the year. While he's on pace for double-digit TDs once again, Taylor's 4.0 YPC would be the worst mark of his career. He'll try to find another gear in Week 7 against the Vikings.

headline: Taylor carried the ball 15 times for 45 yards and caught three of four targets for 37 yards in Sunday's 34-22 loss to Pittsburgh.
story: The Steelers were able to keep Taylor from hurting them, and most of the star RB's yardage came on a 24-yard pass from Daniel Jones in the second quarter and a 20-yard run in the fourth, the latter of which helped set up the fifth of Spencer Shrader's five field goals on the afternoon. It's the second time in the last three games that Taylor has fallen short of 90 scrimmage yards, as defenses have crowded the box and focused on stopping him while daring the Colts' depleted WR room to beat them over the top. Taylor should be able to find a little more success in Week 6 against the winless Titans.

headline: Taylor carried the ball 20 times for 95 yards and two touchdowns in Sunday's 30-13 win over the Commanders. He also caught one of four targets for two yards.
story: Both scores came from five yards out in the second and third quarters, as the Colts went with a ground-heavy offense once Marcus Mariota (knee) was knocked out of the game in London, forcing the Commanders to turn to third-string QB Athan Kaliakmanis, a seventh-round rookie. Taylor has six rushing TDs through four games along with 422 scrimmage yards, and he figures to see a hefty workload again on the road in Week 5 against the Steelers.

headline: Travis (knee) is expected to be sidelined 2-4 weeks, Matt Zenitz of CBSSports.com reports.
story: Travis is expected to miss multiple weeks due to the knee injury he sustained during Sunday's loss to Dallas. In his absence, Luke Tentua will likely take over as Indianapolis' starting right tackle.

headline: Travis (knee) has been ruled out for the rest of Sunday's clash against the Cowboys.
story: Travis suffered a knee injury in the third quarter and was initially deemed questionable to return. However, he was ruled out not long thereafter. Luke Tenuta has entered the game at right tackle in Travis' stead.

headline: Travis (knee) is questionable to return to Sunday's game against the Cowboys, Jake Arthur of Roundtable.io reports.
story: Travis exited the second half of Sunday's contest with a knee injury. The second-year right tackle will be replaced by Luke Tenuta as he undergoes further evaluation.

headline: Giddens was active but didn't play in Sunday's 27-23 loss to the Cowboys.
story: Giddens didn't see any action after turning six carries into 43 yards in Week 8 against the Jaguars. With Jonathan Taylor potentially set to be traded before Tuesday's NFL trade deadline, Giddens would stand to operate as the team's No. 2 option in the backfield behind rookie Seth McGowan if Taylor departs.

headline: Giddens racked up 43 yards on six carries in Indianapolis' Week 8 loss to Jacksonville on Sunday.
story: Giddens entered Sunday having not logged a snap this season, but he got an opportunity in the blowout loss and made the most of it, ripping off a pair of 12-yard runs on the way to a team-leading 43 rushing yards. However, it must be noted that he didn't enter until the game was far out of reach in the fourth quarter, so all of his production came in garbage time. Still, it was a meaningful performance by Giddens in the context of Indianapolis fielding trade offers for star RB Jonathan Taylor amidst a lost season. Should Taylor indeed be dealt, Giddens would immediately take on a more prominent role in the Colts backfield along with seventh-round rookie Seth McGowan.

headline: Giddens did not play a single snap during Sunday's 13-10 loss to the Vikings.
story: Giddens dressed for Sunday's game, but he observed the entire contest from the sidelines while Seth McGowan served as the Colts' lone backup to Jonathan Taylor. Giddens has yet to play a snap this regular season, but that could change if the Colts -- who have a 2-5 record -- are sellers at the trade deadline and opt to send Taylor to another team.

headline: Giddens (coach's decision) is inactive for Sunday's game against the Texans.
story: Giddens was a full participant in practice after being unavailable for Week 2 against the Chiefs due to a knee injury. He'll be a healthy scratch for Sunday's AFC South showdown, with Seth McGowan being the lone depth option out of the backfield behind bell-cow running back Jonathan Taylor. Giddens' next opportunity to play is Week 4 against the Commanders on Sunday, Oct. 4.

headline: Giddens (knee) was a full participant in Wednesday's practice.
story: Giddens has yet to participate in a regular-season game this season. The running back missed the Colts' Week 1 loss to the Ravens as a healthy scratch before missing the Week 2 overtime loss to the Chiefs with a knee injury. The No. 3 back is now healthy and should be available for the Week 3 game against the Texans.

headline: Giddens (knee) is inactive for Sunday night's matchup with the Chiefs.
story: Giddens was inactive Week 1 as a healthy scratch, and he will now be forced to miss the team's second contest of the year as he nurses an apparent knee injury. In Giddens' absence, Seth McGowan will operate as the team's primary reserve option behind starting running back Jonathan Taylor versus Kansas City.

headline: Giddens (knee) is listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the Chiefs.
story: Giddens was a healthy scratch for the 41-23 loss to the Ravens in Week 1. He's now dealing with a knee injury, though he was able to practice in full Friday. With that in mind, even if Giddens is healthy, there's a chance he will be inactive. Conversely, if he is active, he's still not a candidate to see much action from scrimmage.

headline: Giddens (knee) did not participate at practice Thursday.
story: Giddens was a healthy scratch in Week 1, so it seems he may have hurt his knee during practice Wednesday. He'll probably have to return to practice Friday to give himself a chance at suiting up Sunday at Kansas City.

headline: Giddens (coach's decision) is inactive for Sunday's game against the Ravens.
story: Giddens missed a big chunk of training camp and the preseason due to a hamstring injury, and he was passed on the depth chart by rookie Seth McGowan as the RB2 behind workhorse back Jonathan Taylor.

headline: Leonard (coach's decision) is inactive for Sunday's game against the Cowboys but is listed as the team's emergency quarterback, Abby Halpin of the team's official site reports.
story: As has been the case throughout the season, Leonard is a healthy scratch. However, he will be available if Daniel Jones and Anthony Richardson exit the contest due to injury, illness or ejection.

headline: Leonard (coach's decision) is inactive but will serve as the emergency third quarterback against the Jaguars on Sunday, JJ Stankevitz of the Colts' official site reports.
story: As the emergency QB3, Leonard is now allowed to see the field Sunday unless both Daniel Jones and Anthony Richardson are taken out of the game due to injury, illness or ejection.

headline: Leonard (coach's decision) is inactive but will serve as the Colts' emergency third quarterback against the Vikings on Sunday.
story: Leonard will continue to serve as the team's emergency QB3, and as such, he is prohibited from playing Sunday unless both Daniel Jones and Anthony Richardson are removed from the game due to injury, illness or ejection.

headline: Leonard (coach's decision) is inactive but will serve as the Colts' emergency third quarterback against the Titans on Sunday.
story: Leonard will once again serve as the emergency QB3, meaning that he is restricted from playing Sunday unless both Daniel Jones and Anthony Richardson leave the game due to injury, illness or ejection.

headline: Leonard (coach's decision) is inactive for Sunday's game against the Steelers, though he is listed as the team's emergency quarterback.
story: Leonard is inactive once again. However, as has been the case in previous weeks, Leonard will be available if Daniel Jones and Anthony Richardson exit the contest due to injury, illness or ejection.

headline: Leonard is inactive for Sunday's game against the Commanders in London as the Colts' emergency No. 3 quarterback.
story: Leonard hasn't been active for any of the Colts' first four games after Anthony Richardson beat him out for the No. 2 job coming out of the preseason. The second-year player out of Notre Dame will only be available in the event both starter Daniel Jones and Richardson are unable to finish the game.

headline: Leonard (coach's decision) is inactive but will serve as the Colts' emergency third quarterback against the Texans on Sunday.
story: For a third consecutive week, Leonard will operate as the emergency QB3 behind starter Daniel Jones and backup Anthony Richardson. That prohibits Leonard from playing Sunday unless both Jones and Richardson were to be removed from the game due to injury, illness or ejection.

headline: Leonard (coach's decision) is inactive, but he'll serve as the Colts' emergency third quarterback for Sunday night's contest against Kansas City.
story: Leonard again will operate as the No. 3 option behind starter Daniel Jones and primary backup Anthony Richardson Week 2. Leonard will only be able to enter the game if both Jones and Richardson are sidelined by injuries.

headline: Leonard (coach's decision) is inactive as the Colts' emergency third quarterback for Sunday's game against the Ravens.
story: Leonard lost out on the QB2 job to Anthony Richardson behind Daniel Jones over the summer. Across five regular-season appearances last season, Leonard completed just 58.2 percent of his 67 pass attempts for 415 yards, two touchdowns and three interceptions, averaging a subpar 6.2 yards per attempt.

headline: Brown was signed to the 53-man roster Tuesday.
story: Brown is currently listed on the depth chart behind Tyler Warren, Mo Alie-Cox and Drew Ogletree, so it doesn't appear he will have a prominent role anytime soon. The 32-year-old has played for the Browns, Texans, Patriots, Seahawks and Cardinals since entering the NFL in 2017, totaling 74 catches (102 targets) for 752 yards and three touchdowns in 92 regular-season appearances.

headline: Mallory did not catch any of his three targets during Sunday's 16-10 loss to Minnesota.
story: Mallory and the other Colts tight ends worked in larger roles offensively Sunday due to the absence of Tyler Warren (groin). However, the former's 21 offensive snaps ranked third behind Mo Alie-Cox (39) and Drew Ogletree (35), and Mallory could not connect with Daniel Jones, with the third and final pass that came his way resulting in an interception by Harrison Smith. Mallory has seen nine targets over his last two games since coming off injured reserve, but his role would shrink against the Jaguars in Week 8 if Warren is given the green light to play in that contest.

headline: Mallory will once again operate in an expanded role after Tyler Warren (groin) was ruled out ahead of Sunday's game against the Vikings, Abby Halpin of the Colts' official site reports.
story: Warren will end up missing a second consecutive game while battling a groin injury, so Mallory and Mo Alie-Cox will serve as the Colts' top tight ends for Sunday's contest. Mallory turned six targets into two catches for 20 yards in a Week 6 loss to the Titans, and he finished that contest third in targets behind Keenan Allen (11) and Josh Downs (eight).

headline: Mallory caught two of six passes for 20 yards during Sunday's 26-20 loss to the Titans.
story: Mallory was cleared to make his 2026 debut Sunday after missing the Colts first five games of the regular season due to a thumb injury that was severe enough for him to go on injured reserve. Although he didn't put up eye-popping stats, he led all Colts tight ends with 43 offensive snaps and finished third on the team in targets behind Keenan Allen (11) and Josh Downs (eight). Mallory's playing time would likely decrease if Tyler Warren (groin) was cleared to return for Week 7 against the Vikings on Oct. 25.

headline: The Colts activated Mallory (thumb) from injured reserve Saturday.
story: Mallory doesn't carry an injury designation into Sunday's game against the Titans and is slated to make his 2026 debut. He should slot into the tight-end mix alongside Mo Alie-Cox and Drew Ogletree behind Tyler Warren (groin). Mallory has 23 career catches for 252 yards across 24 regular-season appearances.

headline: Mallory (thumb) is listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the Titans.
story: Mallory strung together a trio of full practices during Week 6 prep while in the final stages of his recovery from a thumb injury that landed him on injured reserve at the start of the regular season. He would need to be activated from IR by the Colts on Saturday in order to be available for Sunday's AFC South tilt.

headline: Mallory (thumb) has been ruled out ahead of Sunday's game against the Steelers.
story: Mallory was designated to return to practice Wednesday. The tight end remains on injured reserve with a thumb injury but was able to log full practice sessions throughout Week 5 prep. The 27-year-old likely has not yet built up his conditioning enough for the Colts to allow him to suit up for Sunday's contest.

headline: Mallory (thumb) was a full participant at practice Thursday.
story: Mallory's 21-day practice window to be activated from IR was opened by the Colts Wednesday, and it seems like he could be trending towards being available in Week 5. Indianapolis' final injury report of the week Friday will shed more light on his status ahead of Sunday's game at Pittsburgh.

headline: Colts head coach Shane Steichen said that Mallory (thumb) will have his 21-day practice window opened Wednesday, Nathan Brown of The Indianapolis Star reports.
story: After sustaining a thumb injury in August, Mallory was sent to injured reserve at the conclusion of the preseason. The 27-year-old has made good progress in his recovery and after he missed the minimum four games, the Colts have decided to clear him to practice at the first opportunity in which he's eligible to do so. Mallory could make his 2026 debut as soon as this Sunday in Pittsburgh, though he'll likely struggle to earn playing time behind fellow tight ends Tyler Warren, Mo Alie-Cox and Drew Ogletree.

headline: Shrader went 3-for-3 on field-goal tries and made both of his PATs during Sunday's 27-23 loss to the Cowboys.
story: Shrader entered Week 9 having made just three field goals over the team's last three games, but he got back on track Sunday. The kicker made a 47-yard attempt in the third quarter before adding makes from 59 and 50 yards in the final quarter. Shrader has now converted multiple field-goal attempts in six contests this year, and he's gone 22-for-24 on field-goal tries, including 8-for-9 from 50-plus yards, over nine contests so far during the 2026 campaign.

headline: Shrader made his sole PAT in the Colts' 42-7 loss to the Jaguars on Sunday.
story: Shrader did not have a very active night, making the sole kick he was called upon for. He's now 14-for-15 on PATs while remaining 19-for-21 on field-goal attempts through eight regular-season games in 2026.

headline: Shrader went 1-for-3 on field-goal attempts and made his only extra-point try during Sunday's 16-10 loss to the Vikings.
story: Shrader entered Week 7 without having missed a field-goal try over the team's first six contests, but he was unable to remain perfect. The kicker was able to make a 43-yard field goal as time expired in the first half, giving Indianapolis a 10-6 lead at the break. Shrader then missed a 56-yard try wide left in the third quarter before pushing a 48-yard attempt wide right in the fourth quarter. He has now gone 19-for-21 on field-goal tries while making 13 of 14 extra-point attempts over seven contests this season.

headline: Shrader made both of his field-goal attempts and both of his PATs in the Colts' 26-20 loss to the Titans on Sunday.
story: While the Colts' story of the day was a special teams failure due to a blocked punt returned for a Titans touchdown, Shrader had no part in the error. The kicker made field goals from 23 and 43 yards in the contest that kept the game close. Shrader is a perfect 18-for-18 on field-goal attempts and 12-for-13 on PATs through six regular-season contests in 2026.

headline: Shrader made all five of his field-goal attempts and converted on his lone point-after try during Sunday's 34-22 loss to the Steelers on Sunday.
story: Quarterback Daniel Jones led the Colts on six offensive drives during Sunday's loss, though only one of those drives ended with a touchdown. That meant a busy day for Shrader, who made field goals from 57 and 56 yards in the first half before connecting on three more kicks from 22, 40 and 28 yards in the second. His five made field goals were his most in a game since Week 2 of the 2025 season, and he's attempted at least three field goals in each of the Colts' last four games. His 16 made field goals through five regular-season games leads the NFL, and he also leads all kickers with six made field goals from 50-plus yards. The Colts have a juicy Week 6 matchup against the 0-5 Titans on Oct. 18.

headline: Shrader went 3-for-3 on field-goal attempts and made all three of his PATs in Sunday's 30-13 win over Washington.
story: Shrader was able to stay red-hot across the pond in London. The kicker nailed field goals from 48, 52 and 44 yards in the contest, remaining perfect on the season. Through four games, Shrader has gone 11-for-11 on field-goal tries, including 5-for-5 from 50-plus yards, and he's becoming one of the more reliable fantasy options in the league.

headline: Shrader made all four of his field-goal attempts while connecting on his lone extra-point try during the Colts' 19-17 win over the Texans on Sunday.
story: It looked like Shrader was going to observe Sunday's contest from the sidelines after he sustained a groin injury during pregame warmups. However, Shrader was cleared to attempt a field goal in the first quarter, and two of his four made field goals came from 50-plus yards, including a 53-yarder with 19 seconds left in the fourth quarter to give the Colts their first win of the season. Shrader has made all eight of his field-goal attempts (including three from 50-plus yards) and six of seven extra-point tries through the first three games of the regular season.

headline: Shrader (groin) returned in the first quarter of Sunday's game against the Texans, Joel A. Erickson of The Indianapolis Star reports.
story: Shrader appeared to injure his groin during pregame warmups, but he was brought out for a 39-yard field goal with 4:38 remaining in first quarter, which he connected on. He may be limited to extra-point attempts and short field goals for the rest of Sunday's game.

headline: Shrader (groin) is questionable to return to Sunday's game against the Texans, Nathan Brown of The Indianapolis Star reports.
story: Shrader appeared to have injured his groin during pregame warmups, as punter Rigoberto Sanchez was the one who booted the ball for the Colts on the opening kickoff. Sanchez could handle all of the kicking duties Sunday if Shrader is not cleared to return.

headline: Shrader made all three of his field-goal attempts and PATs in Sunday night's 33-30 overtime loss to the Chiefs.
story: All three of Shrader's field goals were under 50 yards, including his game-tying make in overtime from 38 yards. The kicker has made all four of his field goals this season and five of six PATs through two contests.

headline: Shrader converted his only field-goal attempt and two of his three extra-point tries during Indianapolis' loss to the Ravens on Sunday.
story: Shrader's lone make came from 58 yards out, which was a new career long for the 27-year-old. He spent time with three different teams across the last two seasons before beating out Blake Grupe for the Colts' kicking job during training camp, and Shrader will look to keep producing as the season goes on.

headline: McGowan rushed six times for 45 yards and a touchdown and brought in his only target for minus-3 yards in the Colts' 27-23 loss to the Cowboys on Sunday.
story: McGowan recorded his first NFL touchdown on a two-yard run in the first quarter, perhaps a harbinger of a larger role as early as next Sunday's Week 10 matchup against the Dolphins. McGowan came just a rush yard short of equaling his career-best tally in that category, and if Jonathan Taylor is indeed moved off the roster by Tuesday's trade deadline, the former would be in line to serve as the lead back moving forward.

headline: McGowan rushed five times for 29 yards and returned four kickoffs for 103 yards Sunday in a loss to the Jaguars.
story: McGowan's best run was a 16-yarder up the middle midway through the third quarter to take the ball to Jacksonville's three-yard line. That set up Indianapolis' only touchdown in the blowout loss. McGowan logged a modest 15 offensive snaps to starter Jonathan Taylor's 38, but the former outgained Taylor on the ground, 29-23. Meanwhile, DJ Giddens paced the Colts with 43 rushing yards on six totes. The big story, of course, is that the Colts are entertaining trade offers on Taylor, and if the star RB is ultimately dealt, McGowan and Giddens both figure to take on significantly larger roles, though it's unclear which of the two would become the starter. With that in mind, it's worth noting that Giddens didn't enter until the fourth quarter and racked up all of his yardage in garbage time.

headline: McGowan turned 11 carries into 46 yards, caught his only target for two yards and added 140 yards as a kick returner during Sunday's 16-10 loss to the Vikings.
story: McGowan played a season-high 31 percent of the team's offensive snaps, and as a result, he was able to set new highs in both carries and rushing yards. With Jonathan Taylor potentially set to be traded in the coming weeks, the rookie would stand to operate as the team's lead back following Taylor's departure. On the season, McGowan has rushed 34 times for 134 yards and reeled in four of five targets for 12 yards while compiling 566 kickoff-return yards over seven contests so far.

headline: McGowan took four carries for 27 yards during Sunday's 26-20 loss versus the Titans.
story: McGowan played exactly 19 offensive snaps for the third straight week Sunday, and, although he was slightly less involved than he has been of late in terms of touches, he managed a career-best 6.8 yards per carry in Week 6. He's merely a change-of-pace back as long as three-time Pro Bowler Jonathan Taylor is healthy, but he has the physical traits to become a workhorse should that not be the case at any point this season.

headline: McGowan turned six carries into 31 yards and caught one of two targets for seven yards during Sunday's 30-13 win over the Commanders in London. He also returned four kickoffs for 102 yards.
story: McGowan actually saw most of his offensive output in the second quarter with four carries for 18 yards and his seven-yard catch. Most of his on-field production figures to come on special teams as a returner, but the rookie seventh-rounder would be poised for RB1 duties if Jonathan Taylor misses time. The Colts will hit the road for Week 5 against the Steelers this Sunday.

headline: McGowan rushed twice for zero yards and had two kickoff returns for 58 yards in Sunday's 33-30 overtime loss to the Chiefs.
story: McGowan saw just four offensive snaps in the contest, touchding the ball on half of them. The seventh-round rookie did not make a strong impression against the Chiefs' defensive line, but he proved useful on special teams with a 29-yard average on kickoff returns.

headline: McGowan caught his only target for no gain and notched 164 yards on five kickoff returns during Sunday's 41-23 loss to the Ravens.
story: McGowan was only on the field for six of the team's 54 offensive snaps while operating as the top reserve option at running back behind Jonathan Taylor. McGowan definitely made his mark on special teams during the contest, but as long as Taylor is healthy, the former will likely have a limited impact on offense.

headline: The Jaguars designated Green (elbow) to return from injured reserve Wednesday.
story: Green landed on injured reserve in mid-September after suffering an elbow injury in Week 1 against the Browns. The Jaguars now have 21 days to activate Green from injured reserve, otherwise the Colorado product would be sidelined for the rest of the 2026 season.

headline: The Jaguars placed Green (elbow) on injured reserve Wednesday.
story: Green sustained the injury while on punt coverage during the Jaguars' 34-10 win over the Browns in Week 1. The injury is severe enough for him to warrant a stint on injured reserve, meaning he'll be forced to miss at least the next four games. The earliest Green is eligible to return from IR is Week 6 against the Texans on Sunday, Oct. 18.

headline: Green (elbow) has been ruled out for the rest of Sunday's game against the Browns.
story: Green injured his elbow while on punt coverage in the first quarter, and the injury is severe enough that he won't return to Sunday's contest. Danny Striggow will be the primary rotational option at defensive end behind Josh Hines-Allen and Travon Walker in Green's absence.

headline: Green has an elbow injury and is questionable to return to Sunday's matchup with the Browns.
story: The defensive end did not get on the stat sheet before leaving the contest. In Green's absence, Danny Striggow is the only backup end left on the Jags' depth chart.

headline: Walker (ribs) did not practice Wednesday, Michael DiRocco of ESPN.com reports.
story: Walker played through a questionable tag last Thursday night against the Ravens and saw his normal allotment of snaps, playing 68 percent of the downs on defense. The 25-year-old has produced 21 tackles (nine solo), including 3.0 sacks, eight QB hits and one pass breakup across eight games this season.

headline: Walker (ribs) is available for Thursday's game against Baltimore.
story: After carrying a questionable designation ahead of this contest, Walker will suit up versus the Ravens in Week 9. The 25-year-old hasn't missed a game this season, accumulating 18 total tackles (seven solo), including 3.0 sacks, in seven regular-season appearances.

headline: Walker (ribs) is questionable to play Thursday night against the Ravens.
story: Walker remained limited at the team's final practice of the week Wednesday as he continues to nurse an injury to his ribs. If the defensive lineman is unable to go in Week 9, Danny Striggow and Bryan Thomas would be two top candidates to operate in more prominent roles versus Baltimore.

headline: Walker (ribs) was a limited participant at practice Tuesday.
story: Walker suffered a rib injury during the third quarter of Sunday's game versus the Colts, and now his status for Thursday's game at Baltimore is uncertain. He'll probably need to upgrade to full participation at practice Wednesday to avoid carrying an injury designation into gameday.

headline: Walker (ribs) is questionable to return to Sunday's game against the Colts.
story: Walker appeared to sustain the injury in the third quarter. Given the Jaguars' large lead, it wouldn't be surprising if the team elected to keep the 2022 first-rounder sidelined the rest of the way. Bryan Thomas and Danny Striggow are both in line for more defensive snaps in Walker's absence.

headline: Johnson (ankle) has no injury designation ahead of Thursday night's matchup against Baltimore.
story: Johnson was forced to miss the team's Week 8 win over the Colts while nursing an ankle injury, but he appears to be good to go for Week 9. The 25-year-old was a limited participant at the team's final practice of the week Wednesday, so he may not be back to 100 percent, but Johnson should be back in his starting role at free safety versus the Ravens.

headline: Johnson (ankle) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Colts.
story: Johnson injured his ankle against the Texans in Week 6, and despite the extra rest courtesy of the Week 7 bye, he was unable to participate in practice all week. Kaevon Merriweather figures to be the top candidate to start alongside Eric Murray at safety, although Rayuan Lane and Jalen Huskey could also see more defensive snaps. Johnson's next chance to play is Week 9 against the Ravens on Thursday.

headline: Johnson (ankle) sat out practice both Wednesday and Thursday.
story: Johnson missed the second half of Jacksonville's Week 6 loss to Houston due to an ankle injury. The Jaguars were on bye last week, but the time off doesn't seem to have been enough for Johnson to have recovered. Given Johnson's consecutive missed practices to begin Week 8 prep, he's likely trending toward missing Sunday's matchup versus the Colts. If that's the case, Kaevon Merriweather may draw a start at safety.

headline: Johnson (ankle) didn't return to second half of Sunday's 34-31 loss to the Texans, Brent Martineau of CBS 47 Jacksonville reports.
story: The Jaguars had listed Johnson as questionable to return after he left in the second quarter due to the ankle injury, but though he was spotted on the sideline in the second half, he never checked back into the contest. Kaevon Merriweather ended up serving as the primary replacement at safety for Johnson, who will have a Week 7 bye to recover from his injury before potentially returning to action Nov. 1 versus the Colts. Johnson accrued six tackles prior to his departure.

headline: Johnson (ankle) is questionable to return to Sunday's game against the Texans in London.
story: Johnson exited the second quarter of Sunday's international contest with an ankle injury. The safety has not returned to the field, and Kaevon Merriweather has taken over at free safety in his absence.

headline: Rodriguez (hand) was listed as limited in Wednesday's practice, Ryan O'Halloran of The Florida Times-Union reports.
story: While Rodriguez fit some work in on Wednesday, fellow RB Bhayshul Tuten (ankle/foot) was listed as a DNP by the Jaguars. The duo's status is thus worth monitoring closely in the coming days, but if Tuten ends up limited or out this weekend, Rodriguez -- if available -- and Ameer Abdullah would be next up for the team's backfield touches Sunday against the Titans.

headline: Rodriguez rushed 10 times for 19 yards and a touchdown and brought in both targets for 13 yards in the Jaguars' 33-10 win over the Ravens on Thursday night.
story: Rodriguez finished with just two fewer carries than Bhayshul Tuten, who came into the game managing ankle and foot injuries and was able to log a relatively abbreviated workload thanks to game script. Both backs had plenty of trouble against Baltimore's stout run defense, but Rodriguez salvaged his fantasy night with a two-yard TD run just past the midway point of the fourth quarter. Rodriguez now has scored in back-to-back games heading into a Week 10 road matchup against the Titans on Sunday, Nov. 15.

headline: Rodriguez (hand) doesn't carry an injury designation for Thursday night's game against the Ravens.
story: Meanwhile, Bhayshul Tuten (ankle/foot) has been deemed questionable for the contest after being listed as a DNP on each of the Jaguars' injury reports, Monday through Wednesday. Given that Tuten has been the team's lead back this season, his playing status (and potential workload, if he's active Thursday) will provide valuable context related to the Week 9 fantasy prospects of Rodriguez, who could assume a larger backfield role versus Baltimore if Tuten ends up out or limited.

headline: Rodriguez (hand) was listed as a limited participant in Tuesday's practice.
story: Though he's been deemed a limited participant on both of the Jaguars' first two Week 9 practice reports, Rodriguez still looks to be in a better spot on the health front than Bhayshul Tuten (ankle/foot), who has yet to log any practice activity. If Tuten winds up being sidelined for Thursday's game in Baltimore, Rodriguez would be the favorite to lead the Jacksonville ground attack, provided he's not inhibited by his own hand injury.

headline: Rodriguez was listed as limited on Monday's practice estimate due to a hand injury.
story: The Jaguars listed two running backs on their first Week 9 injury report, with No. 1 option Bhayshul Tuten (ankle/foot) going down as a non-participant. There's no telling if Tuten is in danger of missing Thursday's contest at Baltimore, but Rodriguez could be in line for more early down work if he's active and the former is inhibited or sidelined. On the season, Rodriguez is averaging 6.7 touches per game.

headline: Rodriguez registered 41 yards and a touchdown on six carries while reeling in his only target for 17 yards during Sunday's 42-7 win over the Colts.
story: Rodriguez was able to exceed 40 rushing yards for the second straight game after failing to do so in any of the team's first five contests of the year. Additionally, the running back slashed through the Colts' defense for a 26-yard touchdown in the third quarter, reaching the end zone for the third time this season. Rodriguez has now rushed 45 times for 209 yards and three scores while reeling in one of two targets for six yards over seven contests so far during the 2026 campaign.

headline: Rodriguez rushed 11 times for 55 yards while failing to reel in his only target during Sunday's 34-31 loss to Houston.
story: Rodriguez led the team in rushing yards, out-producing fellow running back Bhayshul Tuten's 39 yards on 12 carries. Although the two split the carries almost evenly, Tuten caught all four of his targets for 48 yards and two scores in the contest. Rodriguez has now compiled 168 yards on 39 carries while catching one pass for six yards over six contests to open the 2026 campaign.

headline: Rodriguez rushed twice for five yards and caught his only target for six yards during Sunday's 19-17 win over Philadelphia.
story: Rodriguez was scarcely used in Week 5, logging his fewest carries in a game this season. Starting running back Bhayshul Tuten turned 22 carries into 72 yards, and he's clearly the preferred option over Rodriguez in the backfield, regardless of circumstance. Over five games this season, Rodriguez has rushed 28 times for 113 yards and two touchdowns while catching one pass for six yards.

headline: Rodriguez rushed six times for 35 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 22-17 win over the Bengals.
story: After a slow start to the season, Rodriguez has found the end zone in back-to-back games, this time scoring from 25 yards out for his longest run of the season. Rodriguez has handled exactly six carries in three of the four games and remains a total zero in the passing game with zero targets. He's the definition of a touchdown-or-bust fantasy bet playing behind Bhayshul Tuten.

headline: Rodriguez turned eight carries into 37 yards and a touchdown during the Jaguars' 35-6 win over the Patriots on Sunday.
story: Rodriguez made his way to the end zone for the first time this season on a five-yard rushing touchdown late in the third quarter to extend the Jaguars' lead to 28-3. The 2023 sixth-rounder played only 13 of 62 offensive snaps (21.0 percent), well behind Bhayshul Tuten (30) and just ahead of LeQuint Allen (eight). Rodriguez has 20 carries for 73 yards (3.7 YPC) and a score through three regular-season games, and he'll continue to operate as the backup option out of the backfield behind Tuten. The Jaguars hit the road for a Week 4 tilt against the Bengals.

headline: Rodriguez rushed six times for 13 yards in the Jaguars' 20-13 loss to the Broncos on Sunday.
story: For the second straight game to open the season, Rodriguez operated as the clear RB2 for the Jaguars behind Bhayshul Tuten, who rushed 13 times for 65 yards and a touchdown as the lead back. Tuten also out-targeted Rodriguez two to zero. Through two games, Rodriguez has a meager 36 yards on 12 carries, averaging a pitiful 3.0 yards per carry. He's not usable in fantasy ahead of a tough Week 3 date with New England.

headline: Rodriguez rushed six times for 23 yards in Sunday's 34-10 win over the Browns.
story: Bhayshul Tuten got the start and out-snapped Rodriguez by a 28-23 margin and out-carried him 15 to six in one of the friendliest rushing environments the Jaguars will see all season after Jacksonville jumped out to a 31-0 lead early in the third quarter. The lack of volume and production from Rodriguez in this spot is concerning for his fantasy viability moving forward, as Tuten seemed to have the clear upper hand and averaged 4.4 yards per carry to Rodriguez's 3.8 mark. Tuten also caught a 22-yard pass, while Rodriguez didn't see a target. It was clear against Cleveland that Tuten is the preferred fantasy option in this backfield.

headline: Meyers (ankle) did not participate in Wednesday's practice, Ryan O'Halloran of The Florida Times-Union reports.
story: Meyers was listed with hamstring and ankle injuries last week before playing 68 percent of Jacksonville's offensive snaps and catching four passes for 65 yards in a Thursday blowout at Baltimore. It's unclear if the ankle has worsened or if Wednesday's absence is just a matter of caution/maintenance. Brian Thomas, Josh Cameron and Travis Hunter would all be candidates for additional WR snaps if Meyers were to miss time.

headline: Meyers brought in four of six targets for 65 yards in the Jaguars' 33-10 win over the Ravens on Thursday night.
story: Meyers set the pace for the Jaguars in both receptions and receiving yards on the night, bouncing back nicely from a quiet 2-24-0 line just four days earlier in a blowout win over the Colts. The veteran wideout has multiple catches in all but one game, although Meyers hasn't topped 83 receiving yards in any contest to date in 2026. Meyers remains a key target for Trevor Lawrence, but he could see at least a slight boost in his outlook heading into a Week 10 road matchup against the Titans on Sunday, Nov. 15, if Brian Thomas is moved at the trade deadline.

headline: Meyers (hamstring/ankle) does not carry an injury designation going into Thursday's game at the Ravens.
story: Though Meyers was limited in practice, the Jaguars are not listing him on the injury report going into Thursday's game. The veteran has battled through bumps and bruises throughout the season but has yet to miss a game. He'll be good to go for Week 9 in Charm City.

headline: Meyers (hamstring/ankle) was listed as a limited participant in Tuesday's practice.
story: Though he's managing a pair of lower-body concerns coming out of Sunday's win over the Colts, Meyers' ability to practice in any fashion Tuesday bodes well for his chances of playing Thursday against the Ravens. However, Meyers may need to upgrade to full practice participation Wednesday to avoid taking an injury designation into the Week 9 contest.

headline: Meyers was listed as limited on Monday's estimated injury report due to hamstring and ankle issues.
story: Meyers was capped at Monday's walkthrough as a result of the health concerns that impacted him in practice last week, but he still suited up Sunday versus the Colts, handling a 54 percent snap share and gathering in two of three targets for 24 yards. Considering he was able to play through them in Week 8, he's likely trending toward being available Thursday in Baltimore, but his status nonetheless will be watched to ensure as much.

headline: Meyers logged two catches for 24 yards on three targets in Sunday's 42-7 win against Indianapolis.
story: He put up a subpar fantasy line, but Meyers actually led Jacksonville in targets and tied for the team lead in receptions on a day when quarterback Trevor Lawrence threw only 14 passes, 10 of which he completed. Meyers also logged a 54 percent offensive snap share -- second among Jaguars wideouts behind Parker Washington -- after dealing with a hamstring injury during the week. He's still looking to build some momentum, as Meyers has three or fewer catches in five of his seven contests and topped 40 receiving yards just twice.

headline: Meyers (hamstring) is listed as active for Sunday's game against the Colts.
story: Meyers logged a pair of limited practices this week before sitting out Friday's session entirely, but as reports Sunday morning indicated, he'll ultimately be available to take the field. Following Jacksonville's Week 7 bye, Meyers will look to find the end zone for the first time since Week 3 against a middle-of-the-pack Colts defense allowing 215.9 passing yards per game.

headline: Meyers (hamstring/ankle) is expected to play in Sunday's game against the Colts, Ian Rapoport of NFL Network reports.
story: Meyers dealt with a hamstring injury during Week 8 prep, logging limited sessions Wednesday and Thursday before sitting out Friday's practice entirely. Assuming he's deemed active approximately 90 minutes before Sunday's 1:00 p.m. ET kickoff, he'll be looking to build upon the season-high 83 receiving yards he put up in the Jaguars' last game in Week 6 against the Texans in London.

headline: Meyers (hamstring/ankle) is questionable for Sunday's game against the Colts.
story: Meyers didn't practice Friday, but the Jaguars are leaving the light on for the veteran wideout to face Indianapolis. He's coming off a productive Week 6 game against the Texans in which Meyers caught five of 10 targets for 83 yards. The Jaguars are fresh off their bye. If Meyers can't go, Brian Thomas, Josh Cameron and Travis Hunter would have expanded roles behind Parker Washington.

headline: Meyers (hamstring) was a limited participant in Thursday's practice.
story: Coming out of a bye week, Meyers has had his reps capped in the Jaguars' first two practice sessions of Week 8. The Jaguars haven't indicated that Meyers is at any real risk of sitting out Sunday's game against the Colts, but if he's able to upgrade to full participation Friday, he'll likely head into the weekend without an injury designation.

headline: Meyers (hamstring) was a limited participant in Wednesday's practice due to a hamstring injury.
story: Meyers had previously made appearances on Jaguars injury reports earlier in the season due to a thumb issue, but he's nursing a different health concern coming out of the team's Week 7 bye. Unless the hamstring injury was something that cropped up during Wednesday's practice, Meyers' ability to begin Week 8 prep on the field in some capacity is generally a good sign for his chances of suiting up Sunday versus the Colts.

headline: Meyers caught five of 10 targets for 83 yards in Sunday's 34-31 loss to the Texans.
story: While Parker Washington led the Jaguars with 11 looks from Trevor Lawrence, Meyers paced the club in catches and receiving yards on his largest target volume of the season. The 83 yards were also a season best for Meyers, and the veteran wideout will take a 20-285-2 line on 28 targets into a bye before clashing with the Colts in Week 8.

headline: Meyers caught two of three targets for 37 yards during Sunday's 19-17 win against the Eagles.
story: Meyers was limited to 40 or fewer receiving yards for the fourth time this season, and he finished tied with running back Bhayshul Tuten for fourth on the team in targets Sunday. Meyers has solidified himself as the team's No. 2 wide receiver behind Parker Washington early in the season, but his production hasn't been that notable. Through five games, Meyers has caught 15 of 18 targets for 202 yards and two touchdowns.

headline: Meyers caught three of four targets for 33 yards during Sunday's 22-17 win against the Bengals.
story: Meyers finished second on the team in targets behind tight end Brenton Strange (eight), but his performance was far from noteworthy. The wide receiver has operated as a distant No. 2 option behind Parker Washington at his position this season, and Sunday's performance was his third game with 40 or fewer receiving yards over four contests.

headline: Meyers (thumb) doesn't have an injury designation for Sunday's game against the Bengals.
story: With limited listings earlier in the week, Meyers practiced fully Friday and is fine for his normal workload against Cincinnati. Meyers was targeted a season-high eight times last Sunday against the Patriots but has just 11 targets on the season over three games. He's a low-floor WR4 for fantasy, but this game does have some shootout appeal.

headline: Meyers (thumb) was a limited participant in Thursday's practice.
story: The Jaguars have been restricting Meyers' practice activity through the four weeks of the regular season after he jammed his right thumb during a joint practice with Carolina in training camp, but the issue hasn't kept him from suiting up on game days. He's expected to be cleared to play Sunday in Cincinnati following Friday's practice.

headline: Meyers (thumb) was limited in Wednesday's practice.
story: Meyers dealt with the thumb issue last week but ultimately didn't carry an injury designation into last Sunday's blowout win over the Patriots, where the veteran wideout hung a 7-64-1 receiving line on eight targets. Playing as a clear starter ahead of Brian Thomas, Meyers has 10 catches for 132 yards and two touchdowns on 11 targets through three games this season.

headline: Meyers caught seven of eight targets for 64 yards and a touchdown during Sunday's 35-6 win over New England.
story: Meyers led the team in targets, most notably reeling in a 10-yard score from quarterback Trevor Lawrence in the second quarter. The touchdown was the second of the year for the wide receiver, and he has now caught 10 of 11 targets for 132 yards over three contests in 2026. Parker Washington has established himself as Lawrence's favorite target, but Meyers has found himself on equal footing with fellow wideout Brian Thomas as an unpredictable fantasy asset early in the season.

headline: Meyers (thumb) was a full participant in Friday's practice and doesn't have an injury designation for Sunday's game against the Patriots.
story: Meyers quietly leads the Jaguars with an 86 percent route share, but he's been targeted on just six percent of his routes, taking a backseat to Parker Washington and Brian Thomas, in that order. Thomas' sloppy play in a Week 2 loss at Denver could perhaps push more volume in Meyers' direction, though that's likely to happen in any case even if his thumb injury continues to linger.

headline: Meyers (thumb) was a limited practice participant Thursday.
story: The Jaguars put a cap on Meyers' reps for the second day in a row, but head coach Liam Coen hasn't provided any indication that the wideout is at any real risk of sitting out Sunday's game against the Patriots while he continues to manage a right thumb injury that dates back to training camp. Meyers played through the thumb issue in the first two contests of the season, recording three catches for 68 yards and a touchdown on three targets.

headline: Meyers (thumb) was listed as a limited participant for Wednesday's practice, Ryan O'Halloran of the Florida Times-Union reports.
story: The veteran has been held back in practice for much of the season due to a thumb issue, but it hasn't prevented him from suiting up on Sundays. Look for the Jaguars to continue to manage Meyers' injury cautiously in practices to keep him fresh on gamedays. The wideout still looks to be on track to play Week 3 versus the Patriots.

headline: Meyers secured his only target for 28 yards in Sunday's 20-13 loss to the Broncos.
story: On a day Trevor Lawrence threw for just 189 yards on 29 attempts, Parker Washington and Brian Thomas combined to see 20 of those targets. Meyers dealt with a thumb injury during the practice week but still led all wideouts with 54 snaps against Denver, running a team-high 29 routes. Through two games, Meyers has just three catches for 68 yards and a touchdown on three targets. He's tough to get behind as anything more than a fantasy WR4 ahead of next Sunday's game against the Patriots.

headline: Meyers (thumb) was limited at Friday's practice but doesn't have an injury designation for Week 2 at Denver, Ryan O'Halloran of the Florida Times-Union reports.
story: Brian Thomas (shoulder) also avoided an injury designation despite being limited in practice throughout the week. He picked up his injury during the Week 1 win over Cleveland, whereas Meyers is listed with the same thumb injury that he played through successfully in the season opener.

headline: Meyers (thumb) practiced on a limited basis Thursday.
story: Meyers emerged from preseason Week 2 with a brace on his right hand, but the nature of the injury wasn't confirmed until the Jaguars posted their first injury report of the season last week. Since then, he's been listed as limited on all five of the team's practice reports with a thumb injury, but it didn't stop him from suiting up for this past Sunday's season-opening win against the Browns, when he hauled in both targets for 40 yards and one touchdown and recorded one carry for two yards on a 65 percent snap share. If Meyers follows last week's trajectory this week, he'll enter the weekend without a designation for Sunday's contest at Denver.

headline: Meyers (thumb) was limited in Wednesday's practice.
story: Both Meyers and Brian Thomas (shoulder) were limited in Wednesday's session. Meyers dealt with a thumb injury late in the preseason but was able to give it a go in Week 1, catching two passes for 40 yards and a touchdown. Limited practices may be the norm for Meyers for the time being until his thumb is back to 100 percent, but it certainly didn't stop him from playing well in the opener.

headline: Meyers caught both of his targets for 40 total yards and a touchdown, adding one carry for two yards in Sunday's 34-10 win over the Browns.
story: Meyers did not receive much attention despite a strong offensive day for the Jaguars. Parker Washington earned No. 1 option honors, catching five passes for 83 yards and a touchdown, while Meyers took a more minimal yet efficient role with 20 yards per reception.

headline: Tuten (ankle/foot) was listed as a non-participant in practice Wednesday, Ryan O'Halloran of The Florida Times-Union reports.
story: It remains to be seen if Tuten is simply managing a couple of aches and pains in the wake of Week 9 action or is in danger of missing the Jaguars' next game, so his status is worth tracking ahead of Sunday's game against the Titans. Fellow RB Chris Rodriguez also appeared on Wednesday's injury report after being deemed limited by a hand injury.

headline: Tuten (ankle/foot) rushed 12 times for 29 yards and a touchdown in the Jaguars' 33-10 win over the Ravens on Thursday night.
story: Tuten fought through the pair of lower-body injuries that made him a game-time decision, recording his fourth rushing touchdown of the campaign on a one-yard run to cap off the opening possession of the contest. The second-year back had to grind for every yard he got on the ground, but fortunately for Tuten, the Jaguars built a comfortable enough lead where he was able to benefit from an early end to his night. Tuten has now scored in back-to-back games, and he'll have some extra time to get healthier ahead of a Week 10 road matchup against the Titans on Sunday, Nov. 15.

headline: Tuten (ankle/foot) officially is listed as active for Thursday night's game against the Ravens.
story: It was previously reported that Tuten, who was viewed as a game-time decision for the contest, would be good to go, and now that has been confirmed. Assuming no in-game limitations or setbacks, Tuten is in line to continue to lead the Jaguars backfield in Week 9. If, however, his reps end up being managed at all, added touches could be available for Chris Rodriguez, Ameer Abdullah and LeQuint Allen. When healthy, Tuten has maintained steady volume through seven games, averaging 15.7 carries and 70.3 rushing yards with three rushing scores, while also having recorded a 15-181-3 receiving line in that span.

headline: Tuten (ankle) is on track to play in Thursday night's game against the Ravens, after going through what Jeremy Fowler of ESPN.com describes as an extensive pregame workout.
story: Tuten, who was listed as a DNP on all three of the Jaguars' Week 9 injury reports, was viewed as a game-time decision for Thursday's contest, but it looks like the running back will give it a go after all. Official confirmation of his status will arrive, either way, once the Jaguars' inactives are posted ahead of the team's 8:15 p.m. ET kickoff.

headline: Tuten (ankle/foot) "should be" available for Thursday night's game against the Ravens barring any pregame setbacks, Jeremy Fowler of ESPN reports.
story: Tuten logged DNP listings on all three of the Jaguars' Week 9 injury reports ahead of the contest and had been considered a game-time decision. Fowler's report indicates that the running back is trending toward active status, but those considering Tuten in Week 9 fantasy lineups nonetheless will want to verify his playing status ahead of Thursday's 8:15 p.m. ET kickoff.

headline: Tuten (ankle/foot) is listed questionable for Thursday's game against the Ravens.
story: For the third day in a row, Tuten went down as a non-participant on the Jaguars' injury report, even though head coach Liam Coen suggested the running back would practice in a limited fashion Wednesday, per Cameron Wolfe of NFL Network. The coach added that the Jaguars will be viewing Tuten as a game-time decision for Thursday's tilt, with his availability perhaps hinging on how he fares during a gameday workout. If Tuten ends up missing his first game of the season or is active but available in only a limited capacity, Chris Rodriguez would be in store for a larger role out of the backfield.

headline: Jaguars head coach Liam Coen said Wednesday that Tuten (ankle/foot) is feeling better, but the running back's status for Thursday's contest versus the Ravens is expected to come down to a game-time decision, John Shipley of SI.com reports.
story: Tuten was listed as a non-participant on the Jaguars' first two Week 9 practice reports, but he may be in line to take some reps during Wednesday's session. The 23-year-old looks poised to take a questionable tag into the team's matchup with Baltimore, but if he fares well in practice Wednesday and while working out early Thursday, he could get the green light to play on a short week. If Tuten suits up, it's conceivable that he handles a lighter workload than normal, after receiving no fewer than 15 touches in any of the Jaguars' first seven contests.

headline: The Jaguars listed Tuten (ankle/foot) as a non-participant in Tuesday's practice.
story: For the second day in a row, Tuten went down as a non-participant on Jacksonville's Week 9 injury report while he nurses a pair of lower-body injuries coming out of this past Sunday's win over the Colts. If Tuten can get back on the field in some capacity Wednesday, it would put him in a good spot to play Thursday against the Ravens. However, if Tuten fails to practice and is ultimately ruled out for Thursday, Chris Rodriguez (hand) -- who has been a limited practice participant so far this week -- would be the top candidate to lead Jacksonville's ground attack in Baltimore.

headline: Tuten (ankle/foot) was not spotted during the portion of Tuesday's practice open to the media, according to Michael DiRocco of ESPN.com.
story: Tuten was listed as a non-participant on Monday's estimated injury report on a day the Jaguars did not practice, and although the Jaguars will return to the field Tuesday, it appears Tuten will not due to the lower-leg injuries. Tuten will not have much time to get any work in this week with the Jaguars facing the Ravens on Thursday, and if he is unable to go the door will be opened for Chris Rodriguez (hand), LeQuint Allen and Ameer Abdullah.

headline: Tuten was a non-participant at Monday's walkthrough due to ankle and foot injuries.
story: Tuten is coming off a sterling performance Sunday against the Colts in which he reeled off 159 yards from scrimmage and two total TDs on 18 touches, but he now has a pair of health concerns in tow. The Jaguars may be exercising caution with their No. 1 RB, but his status -- along with backup Chris Rodriguez (hand), who was listed as limited -- will be watched to get a sense of who may be available to the backfield Thursday at Baltimore.

headline: Michael Florio: Bhayshul Tuten 'an RB1 no matter how you slice it'
story: Michael Florio: Bhayshul Tuten 'an RB1 no matter how you slice it'

headline: Tuten rushed 16 times for 104 yards and a touchdown and brought in both targets for 55 yards and another score in the Jaguars' 42-7 win over the Colts on Sunday.
story: Tuten looked refreshed coming out of the Week 7 bye, breaking out for a new single-game career-high rushing total. Tuten also recorded his third rushing touchdown of the season on a rumbling 39-yard run during the second quarter where he broke several tackles, and he added his third receiving score over the last two games with a 25-yard grab as time expired in the third quarter. Tuten is up to 4.5 yards per carry after averaging a season-best 6.5 yards per tote Sunday, and he's added six total touchdowns heading into a Week 9 road matchup against the Ravens on Thursday night.

headline: Tuten carried the ball 12 times for 39 yards and caught all four of his targets for 48 yards and two touchdowns in Sunday's 34-31 loss to the Texans.
story: While the Houston front seven kept him bottled up on the ground -- Tuten's longest run went for just five yards -- the second-year RB made an impact through the air, turning a dump pass from Trevor Lawrence into a 27-yard score in the second quarter before catching another two-yard TD before halftime. The receiving touchdowns were his first of the season and tied his total from all of 2025, and Tuten topped 80 scrimmage yards for the fourth straight game. The Jaguars will get a bye before facing the Colts in Week 8.

headline: Tuten carried the ball 22 times for 72 yards and caught two of three targets for 24 yards in Sunday's 19-17 win over the Eagles.
story: The second-year back set new season highs in touches and scrimmage yards as he reached 90 in the latter category for a third straight game. Tuten has yet to have a truly huge performance this season, but he's been very steady so far as the Jaguars' No. 1 RB, collecting 349 rushing yards and two TDs on 4.3 yards per carry while adding a 9-78-0 line on 10 targets through five games. Tuten hasn't gotten into the end zone in two straight games, a streak he'll look to snap in Week 6 against the Texans.

headline: Tuten rushed 17 times for 73 yards and brought in both targets for 18 yards in the Jaguars' 22-17 win over the Bengals on Sunday.
story: Tuten filled his usual role as the clear lead option in Jacksonville's ground attack with aplomb, grinding out tough yards on many of his carries and also contributing a 20-yard run. He also recorded multiple receptions for the third consecutive game, and although he saw backfield mate Chris Rodriguez score the Jaguars' only rushing touchdown of the day that came on a breakaway run from 25 yards out as opposed to in close. Tuten has at least 15 carries in three of his first four games heading into a Week 5 showdown against the Eagles in London next Sunday.

headline: Tuten rushed 15 times for 73 yards and a touchdown and brought in both targets for 17 yards in the Jaguars' 35-6 win over the Patriots on Sunday.
story: Serving as the clear lead back once again, Tuten proved himself worthy of the role with a crisp performance that saw him consistently generate useful gains versus a talented Patriots front seven. He capped off his fantasy-friendly effort with his second rushing touchdown of the campaign, a one-yard run with just over eight minutes remaining to close out the scoring on the afternoon. Tuten is averaging an impressive 4.7 yards per carry and a solid 16.0 touches through three games, rendering him an appealing option in all formats heading into a Week 4 road showdown against the Bengals next Sunday.

headline: Tuten rushed 13 times for 65 yards and a touchdown and brought in both targets for minus-3 yards in the Jaguars' 20-13 loss to the Broncos on Sunday.
story: Tuten worked as the Jaguars' clear lead back for the second time in as many games to open the season, even though his rushing workload was relatively modest Sunday. Tuten got into the end zone for the first time this season on a one-yard run early in the second quarter, and he was efficient overall against a high-caliber defense. Tuten figures to remain in the same role for a Week 3 home showdown against the defending AFC champion Patriots next Sunday.

headline: Tuten rushed 15 times for 66 yards and brought in his only target for 22 yards in the Jaguars' 34-10 win over the Browns on Sunday. He also recovered a fumble.
story: Any questions surrounding the potential workload split in the Jaguars' ground attack were definitively answered for the time being Sunday, as Tuten put together an impressively efficient performance and outpaced backfield mate Chris Rodriguez by nine carries despite seeing his day come to an early end due to the lopsided score. Tuten was able to consistently generate productive runs, but he'll have a much stiffer test on the road against the Broncos in a Week 2 matchup next Sunday.

headline: The Jaguars have relayed to inquiring teams that they intend to keep Thomas through Tuesday's trade deadline, Jeremy Fowler of ESPN.com reports.
story: After sending out a first-round pick, two second-round picks, a fifth-round pick and a sixth-round pick Monday in separate deals to bring in defenders Jordan Davis, Jessie Bates and Davon Godchaux, the Jaguars likely could have recouped some of that draft capital if they had opted to move Thomas. Instead, Fowler indicates that the Jaguars plan to keep the rest of their roster intact ahead of the deadline, which will result in Thomas sticking around. Rather than operating as the high-volume target earner he was during his banner 2024 rookie campaign, Thomas looks like he'll continue to serve mainly as a vertical threat who frees up opportunities in the short and intermediate areas for other pass catchers. Thomas has drawn three or fewer targets in six straight games, producing a weak 4-37-2 receiving line during that stretch.

headline: Thomas wasn't targeted in Thursday night's 33-10 win over the Ravens.
story: Thomas played just 19 of 56 offensive snaps and ran only 11 routes on Trevor Lawrence's 26 dropbacks. It's become clear that Thomas is no longer a big part of the offense and needs an injury ahead of him or a trade out of Jacksonville to become relevant in season-long fantasy. He has just one catch for a 12-yard touchdown over his last four games.

headline: Thomas has drawn interest from other teams leading up to the Nov. 10 trade deadline, Ian Rapoport of ESPN reports.
story: Since delivering an 87-1,282-10 receiving line over 17 games as a rookie in 2024, Thomas' production has cratered in the ensuing two seasons. He's been firmly behind Parker Washington and Jakobi Meyers (hamstring/ankle) in terms of snap share through the Jaguars' first seven games and has drawn more than three targets in just one of those contests. Though the vertical threat Thomas presents might make him an appealing target for teams seeking a big-play receiver, it's unclear if the Jaguars have much motivation to move him. Despite his declining role within the Jacksonville offense, Thomas remains under contract through next season at relatively modest cap hits of $4.01 million in 2026 and $4.66 million in 2027.

headline: Thomas caught one of two targets for a 12-yard touchdown in Sunday's 42-7 win over the Colts.
story: Thomas got the scoring started against Indianapolis, securing a red-zone touchdown with 5:30 left in the opening quarter. With the Jaguars throttling the Colts, Trevor Lawrence dropped back just 17 times all afternoon. On 17 pass attempts between Lawrence (14) and Quinn Ewers (three), 11 different Jaguars drew at least one target. Through seven games this season, Thomas has 10 catches for 117 yards and two touchdowns on 22 targets. A low catch rate and diminished snaps have led to Thomas' name being circulated in trade rumors 10 days ahead of the trade deadline.

headline: Thomas didn't haul in either of his two targets during Sunday's 34-31 loss to the Texans in London.
story: Per Michael DiRocco of ESPN.com, Thomas logged 15 offensive snaps in the first half but none after halftime, while all of fellow wideouts Parker Washington (11 targets), Jakobi Meyers (10) and Travis Hunter (four) had major roles in the Jaguars offense. Thomas maintained a regular workload in the first five games of the season, with his snap shares ranging from 35 to 62 percent en route to a 9-105-1 line on 18 targets. Sunday's development could be a sign of things to come for Thomas without the team mentioning any sort of injury during or after Sunday's contest.

headline: Thomas failed to catch any of his three targets in Sunday's 19-17 win over the Eagles.
story: Getting the ball to Parker Washington was once again was the primary focus for Trevor Lawrence, as the fourth-year wideout popped for a 6-124-2 line on nine targets, and Thomas didn't do anything with the little volume he got to prove he should be a bigger part of the game plan. Thomas has gotten three targets ore fewer in four of five games to begin the season, leading to a meager 9-105-1 line on 18 targets, and there's little reason to expect a breakout in Week 6 against the Texans.

headline: Thomas secured both targets for 17 yards and a touchdown in the Jaguars' 22-17 win over the Bengals on Sunday.
story: Thomas was a minimal part of the air attack once again, but that description also applied to fellow wideouts Jakobi Meyers and Parker Washington as the Bengals did an effective job taking away Trevor Lawrence's primary targets. However, Thomas was able to break through with what turned out to be a key score, as he recorded a seven-yard scoring grab late in the first half in a game that was ultimately decided by five points. Thomas still has a modest nine receptions for 105 yards and Sunday's touchdown on 15 targets as the Jaguars head across the pond to face the Eagles in London in Week 5.

headline: Thomas secured his only target for eight yards in the Jaguars' 35-6 win over the Patriots on Sunday.
story: Thomas' minimal role in the Jaguars' air attack was glaring on a day when Trevor Lawrence threw three touchdown passes. All of Jakobi Meyers, Parker Washington, Brenton Strange, Josh Cameron and LeQuint Allen outpaced Thomas with at least one aspect of their receiving lines, and the latter has a modest 7-88-0 line on 12 targets over the first three games of the campaign. Given the complementary role he seems to have fallen into, Thomas' prospects are generally dim heading into a Week 4 road matchup against the Bengals next Sunday.

headline: Thomas brought in three of eight targets for 40 yards in the Jaguars' 20-13 loss to the Broncos on Sunday.
story: Thomas' inefficient afternoon saw him mirror his stat line from Week 1. The 2024 first-round pick's start to the new season has been somewhat worrisome considering he often underwhelmed in 2025 while playing in head coach Liam Coen's offense for the first time. Thomas should continue to see plenty of opportunity, but it remains to be seen how he'll fare against a second straight tough secondary in that of the Patriots during a Week 3 home matchup next Sunday.

headline: Thomas (shoulder) doesn't have an injury designation for Sunday's game at Denver, Ryan O'Halloran of the Florida Times-Union reports.
story: The Jaguars listed Thomas as a limited practice participant all week, after he played just eight snaps on offense after the first quarter of a Week 1 win over Cleveland. He did catch three passes for 40 yards in the opening quarter, and he likely would've played more if the Jaguars hadn't been up by three-plus scores for the entire second half. Still, there's some risk of re-injury, and continued risk of playing behind Parker Washington and Jakobi Meyers in multi-TE formations.

headline: Thomas (shoulder) practiced in a limited capacity Thursday.
story: Thomas now has back-to-back capped sessions under his belt due to a shoulder injury to kick off Week 2 prep, which isn't unexpected after coach Liam Coen told Michael DiRocco of ESPN.com on Monday that the wide receiver would be limited in practice this week. Nevertheless, Thomas now has one more chance to get back to full Friday before the jaguars potentially tag him with a designation for Sunday's game at Denver.

headline: Thomas (shoulder) was limited in Wednesday's practice.
story: This was expected, as coach Liam Coen said Monday that the third-year wideout would be limited this week as he works through a shoulder issue. Coen added that he expects Thomas to be available Week 2, but it will depend on how his shoulder holds up going into the weekend. Of note, fellow wideout Jakobi Meyers (thumb) was also limited Wednesday.

headline: Coach Liam Coen said Monday that Thomas (shoulder) will be limited in practice this week, Michael DiRocco of ESPN.com reports.
story: Thomas was briefly forced from Sunday's win over the Browns but was able to return and finished with three catches for 40 yards on three targets. Coen expects Thomas to play next Sunday against the Broncos despite the shoulder issue, but the matchup will be much tougher on paper. Behind Parker Washington in the pecking order for targets, Thomas is shaping up as a WR4 fantasy bet moving forward.

headline: Thomas brought in all three targets for 40 yards in the Jaguars' 34-10 win over the Browns on Sunday. He also committed a fumble recovered by Jacksonville.
story: Thomas was left out of the fun when it came to Trevor Lawrence's four touchdown passes, but the third-year wideout did finish tied for second in receiving yards and targets on the Jaguars while also serving as the runner-up in receptions. Thomas had an inconsistent first season in head coach Liam Coen's offense a year ago, but his efficient showing Sunday qualifies as an encouraging start for 2026 despite the modest yardage total. Thomas will have a formidable challenge on his hands next Sunday, however, as the Jaguars travel to Denver for a showdown against the stingy Broncos defense.

headline: Thomas (shoulder) returned to Sunday's game against the Browns late in the second quarter, Michael DiRocco of ESPN.com reports.
story: Initially labeled questionable to return after he required a trip to the locker room in the second quarter to have his shoulder examined, Thomas was able to return to the field for the Jaguars' final drive of the first half, which ended in a punt.

headline: Thomas is questionable to return to Sunday's game against the Browns due to a shoulder injury.
story: Thomas reached a major milestone during Sunday's game, becoming the second-youngest player in Jaguars franchise history to surpass 2,000 career receiving yards after reeling in three receptions for 40 yards on three targets. However, Thomas may not be able to build on that total for the rest of the contest, as he headed to the locker room in the second quarter with trainers by his side, per John Shipley of SI.com. He'll get his shoulder examined further before the Jaguars decide if he's able to return.

headline: The Jaguars acquired Godchaux from the Saints on Monday in exchange for a 2028 sixth-round pick, though the selection could turn into a 2027 sixth-round pick if "conditions are met," Jonathan Jones of The Athletic of The Athletic reports.
story: Godchaux was selected by Miami in the fifth round of the 2017 NFL Draft. Since then, he has appeared in 145 regular-season games for the Dolphins, Patriots and Saints, garnering 487 total tackles (224 solo), 5.5 sacks and three forced fumbles. Godchaux's presence will bolster depth at the defensive tackle position for the Jaguars, especially with DaVon Hamilton (knee) done for the remainder of the 2026 campaign.

headline: Godchaux (groin) does not have an injury designation for Sunday's game against the Vikings.
