story: Godchaux tweaked his groin during the Saints' loss to the Falcons in Week 4. He ended Week 5 prep with a full practice Friday, which was enough for the veteran defensive lineman to fade an injury tag for Sunday's home game. Godchaux has 12 tackles (four solo) through the first four games of the regular season.

headline: Godchaux exited Monday night's game against the Falcons with a groin injury.
story: He's officially questionable to return, but the game is already well out of reach for New Orleans. Prior to his injury, Godchaux logged one tackle (zero solo). Colby Wooden and Khristian Boyd are next in line for snaps at defensive tackle.

headline: Williams (coach's decision) is inactive for Sunday's game against the Patriots.
story: Williams will be a healthy scratch for a second consecutive week, and the rookie sixth-rounder's next chance to play is Week 4 against the Bengals on Sunday, Oct. 4. The Jaguars will go with five active wide receivers in Parker Washington, Brian Thomas, Jakobi Meyers, Josh Cameron and Travis Hunter.

headline: Williams (coach's decision) is inactive for Sunday's game against the Broncos, John Oehser of the Jaguars' official site reports.
story: Williams did not record any offensive stats over his 10 snaps in the Jaguars' Week 1 win over the Browns. The wide receiver and reserve returner will now take a back seat as head coach Liam Coen finds other ways to fill Williams' minimal snaps.

headline: Williams didn't record any offensive stats during Sunday's 34-10 win over the Browns.
story: Williams had a quiet outing during his regular-season debut, failing to record any targets across 10 offensive snaps. The rookie sixth-round pick also played six snaps on special teams and will likely continue to see limited usage going forward.

headline: Oluokun recorded seven tackles (six solo), including 1.0 sacks, in Thursday's 33-10 victory over Baltimore.
story: Oluokun tied for his team's lead in stops and notched his second sack of the season when he brought down Joe Fagnano early in the second quarter. Oluokun has been a reliable fantasy IDP asset in 2026 with at least seven tackles in six of his eight games so far. He's tallied 58 total stops, including the 2.0 sacks, along with two interceptions and a forced fumble.

headline: Oluokun recorded nine total tackles (five solo), including 1.0 sacks, during Sunday's 42-7 win against the Colts.
story: Oluokun led the team in takedowns, notching at least eight tackles for the third straight game. The linebacker was also able to get to quarterback Daniel Jones for his first sack of the year in the second quarter, matching his season total from both the 2024 and 2025 campaigns. Oluokun is as steady as it gets from a fantasy perspective, and he has now registered 51 total tackles (31 solo), including 1.0 sacks, while also adding two interceptions and a forced fumble over seven contests to open the regular season.

headline: Oluokun logged eight tackles (four solo) in the Jaguars' 34-31 loss to the Texans in London on Sunday.
story: Oluokun did not have an outstanding game by any metrics but did put up a solid stat line in a close divisional loss. The linebacker played 94 percent of the Jaguars' defensive snaps in the contest while logging an additional 24 percent of the team's snaps on special teams. Oluokun leads the Jaguars with 42 tackles on the season.

headline: Oluokun logged seven tackles (six solo), one interception and one forced fumble during the Jaguars' 22-17 win over the Bengals on Sunday.
story: Oluokun helped the Jaguars preserve their one-score lead by picking off Joe Burrow on the second play of the fourth quarter, stopping the Bengals' offensive drive that was in Jaguars territory. Oluokun is already up to two interceptions through four regular-season games, which is one shy from matching his career high in 2021 as a member of the Falcons. The veteran linebacker is up to 24 total tackles on the season.

headline: Oluokun recorded seven total tackles (five solo) during Sunday's 20-13 loss to the Broncos.
story: Oluokun finished tied for the team lead in takedowns with fellow linebacker Ventrell Miller, building off of a Week 1 performance against Cleveland during which he secured four total tackles (three solo) and an interception. Oluokun has registered at least 108 total tackles in each of his last six seasons, and he figures to remain rather busy this year.

headline: Oluokun (wrist) does not have an injury designation ahead of Sunday's game against the Broncos, Ryan O'Halloran of The Florida Times-Union reports.
story: Oluokun logged limited participation in Wednesday and Thursday's practice sessions before upgrading to full participation Friday. The outside linebacker is officially all set to suit up for Sunday's contest across from Dennis Gardeck in the Jaguars' defense's second level.

headline: Oluokun (wrist) was a limited participant at practice Thursday.
story: It's still unknown exactly when Oluokun picked up the wrist issue, but his availability for Week 2 now seems to be in jeopardy regardless. He'll likely need to practice in full Friday to avoid carrying an injury designation into the weekend.

headline: Oluokun (wrist) participated in a limited capacity during Wednesday's practice.
story: Oluokun likely suffered the wrist injury in the Jaguars' 34-10 win over the Browns on Sunday. The linebacker was dominant in the contest, recording four tackles (three solo) and an interception. Oluokun will need to upgrade to a full participant by Friday's practice to avoid an injury designation ahead of next Sunday's game against the Broncos.

headline: Oluokun recorded four total tackles (three solo) and an interception during Sunday's 34-10 win over Cleveland.
story: Oluokun was uncharacteristically quiet when it comes to takedowns, securing his fewest tackles in a regular-season game since Week 7 of the 2025 campaign. He made his mark in different way Sunday, intercepting a throw from Browns quarterback Deshaun Watson in the first quarter. The linebacker has registered at least 108 total tackles in each of the last six seasons, and he figures to be busier in Week 2 against the Broncos.

headline: Koziol finished Thursday's 33-10 win over Baltimore with two catches for 15 yards on two targets.
story: Koziol was part of a three-tight-end starting unit for Jacksonville alongside Brenton Strange and Nate Boerkircher. Koziol logged the fewest offensive snaps (12) among the trio but matched both in receptions. He entered Thursday with just one catch through five contests, so it's probably not wise to count on him for substantial production moving forward.

headline: Koziol (coach's decision) is inactive for Sunday's game against the Broncos, John Oehser of the Jaguars' official site reports.
story: Koziol is once again a healthy scratch. The tight end is the odd man out in a position room that consists of Brenton Strange, Nate Boerkircher and Quintin Morris.

headline: Koziol (coach's decision) is inactive for Sunday's game against the Browns.
story: Koziol, the Jaguars' fifth-round pick of the 2026 NFL Draft, will be a healthy inactive for Week 1, so his next chance to make his regular-season debut is Week 2 against the Broncos on Sunday, Sept. 20. Brenton Strange, Quintin Morris and rookie second-rounder Nate Boerkircher will be Jacksonville's active tight ends against Cleveland.

headline: Boerkircher hauled in two of three targets for 61 yards in Thursday night's 33-10 win over Baltimore.
story: Boerkircher was tied with Parker Washington for the second-most receiving yards on the team with 61. This game marks the fourth time this season that the rookie has surpassed 30 snaps on offense. Boerkircher has made a name for himself as Jacksonville's No. 2 option at tight end behind Brenton Strange.

headline: Boerkircher caught his lone target for a 31-yard touchdown in Sunday's 42-7 win over the Colts.
story: The rookie tight end converted his long touchdown on a busted coverage, putting the Jaguars up 14-0 in the second quarter. Boerkircher entered Sunday with six grabs for 52 yards and a touchdown on eight targets across six games. He has minimal fantasy appeal outside of single-game DFS slates ahead of Thursday night's date with the Ravens.

headline: Boerkircher caught both of his targets for eight yards and a touchdown during Sunday's 34-31 loss to the Texans.
story: Boerkircher was able to find pay dirt for the first time in his NFL career, reeling in a one-yard touchdown pass from quarterback Trevor Lawrence in the fourth quarter. The 25-year-old now has gathered in six of eight targets for 52 yards and a touchdown over six contests to open the regular season.

headline: Boerkircher (back) does not have any injury designation ahead of Sunday's game against the Texans.
story: Boerkircher upgraded to a full participant in Friday's practice after being limited to start Week 6 prep. The tight end is all set to suit up for Sunday's game as the No. 2 tight end behind Brenton Strange.

headline: Boerkircher (back) was a limited participant at practice Thursday.
story: Boerkircher popped up on Jacksonville's injury report Wednesday with a back issue, and his availability for Week 6 now appears to be in jeopardy. He'll probably need to log a full practice Friday to avoid carrying an injury designation into the weekend.

headline: Boerkircher (back) was a limited participant in Wednesday's practice.
story: Boerkircher appears to have picked up a back injury after the Jaguars' Week 5 win over the Eagles in London. The tight end will likely need to upgrade to a full participant by Friday's practice to avoid any injury designation ahead of Sunday's game against the Texans.

headline: Boerkircher (illness) does not carry an injury designation into Thursday's game against the Bengals.
story: Boerkircher was held out of Thursday's practice due to an illness, but he's past his ailment and will be available to play Sunday. The rookie second-rounder has one catch (on two targets) for nine yards through three regular-season games while serving as the Jaguars' TE2 behind Brenton Strange.

headline: Boerkircher (illness) did not practice Thursday, Michael DiRocco of ESPN.com reports.
story: Boerkircher was added to the injury report due to an illness, though barring a setback, he should be good to go for the Week 4 meeting with the Bengals. The 25-year-old logged 89 offensive snaps combined in the first three weeks of the 2026 campaign, second to Brenton Strange (136) at the tight-end position. However, Boerkircher hasn't been productive, catching one pass (two targets) for nine yards during that span.

headline: Boerkircher caught his only target for nine yards during Sunday's 34-10 win versus the Browns.
story: Boerkircher played 38 of Jacksonville's 57 offensive snaps in his pro debut, good for second most among Jaguars tight ends behind Brenton Strange (39). Boerkircher was billed as more of a blocker than a route runner when he was taken in the second round of the 2026 NFL Draft, and at least in the short term, Strange should be expected to continue to see more targets between the two of them.

headline: Cameron caught his only target for six yards in Thursday night's 33-10 victory over the Ravens.
story: Cameron didn't see the ball until the fourth quarter despite playing the third most snaps at wide receiver (25) for the Jaguars on Thursday, behind only Parker Washington (38) and Jakobi Meyers (38). This marks the third game in a row during which the 23-year-old played as the Jaguars' No. 3 option at receiver, but his limited usage keeps him as a low-priority waiver-wire add.

headline: Cameron did not catch his lone target in a 42-7 rout of the Colts on Sunday. He returned one punt for six yards and one kickoff for 18 yards.
story: Jacksonville didn't need to go to its air-game much given the easy win, and QB Trevor Lawrence threw just 14 passes. None of those went to Cameron -- his only target (which he didn't catch) came from backup signal-caller Quinn Ewers in garbage time. Cameron did log a season-high 52 percent offensive snap share, but game script didn't do him any favors in terms of production. With no catches in three of his seven games this season, Cameron doesn't make for an appealing fantasy asset.

headline: Cameron didn't garner a target and recorded 46 kickoff-return yards during Sunday's 34-31 loss to the Texans.
story: Cameron went without a target for the first time since Week 2, but he did play a season-high 50 percent of the team's offensive snaps. The wide receiver played 19 more snaps on offense than Brian Thomas, and he appears to have officially taken over as the team's No. 3 option behind Parker Washington and Jakobi Meyers at his position. On the year, Cameron has caught eight of 12 targets for 117 yards and two touchdowns while also adding 245 yards as a kick returner over six games.

headline: Cameron caught three of six targets for 43 yards during the Jaguars' 19-17 win over the Eagles on Sunday in London. He also returned one kickoff for 18 yards and added a tackle on special teams.
story: Cameron opened Sunday's game in style, when he took the first kickoff of the contest 90 yards to the house for a touchdown, but that score ended up being nullified by a holding penalty on the Jaguars. The rookie sixth-rounder still managed to contribute offensively and finished third on the Jaguars in catches, targets and receiving yards, including a 32-yard catch early in the third quarter. Cameron's 22 offensive snaps were fourth-most among Jacksonville wide receivers, but his 6-97-1 receiving line (10 targets) over the last three weeks is noticeably better than Brian Thomas (3-25-1 on six targets) in that same span. The Jaguars will stay in London for a Week 6 AFC South showdown against the Texans on Oct. 18.

headline: Cameron hauled in both of his targets for 42 yards during the Jaguars' 22-17 win over the Bengals on Sunday. He also returned two kickoffs for 45 yards.
story: Cameron got on the board in the second quarter with a 29-yard catch before connecting with Trevor Lawrence on a 13-yard pass in the third. The rookie sixth-rounder played 22 of the Jaguars' 61 offensive snaps (36.1 percent), which was fourth most among Jacksonville's wide receivers. Cameron has a 5-74-2 line on six targets through four games, and his scoring floor figures to remain limited unless the Jaguars are without one or more of Parker Washington, Brian Thomas or Jakobi Meyers. Up next for the Jaguars is a Week 5 home game against the Eagles.

headline: Cameron secured one of two targets for a 12-yard touchdown in Sunday's 35-6 win over the Patriots.
story: Cameron got the scoring started early in the second quarter, catching the first of Trevor Lawrence's three touchdown passes. The rookie ended up finishing with 23 offensive snaps against New England, the same amount as Brian Thomas but behind Parker Washington and Jakobi Meyers, who both played 50 snaps on offense. Cameron could be pushing Thomas for the No. 3 receiver role in Jacksonville.

headline: Cameron returned two kickoffs for 50 yards in Sunday's 20-13 loss to the Broncos.
story: Cameron played 10 offensive snaps and 14 special-teams snaps in Sunday's contest. The wide receiver was not targeted in the contest but averaged 25 yards on his two returns.

headline: Cameron caught both of his targets for 20 yards and a touchdown in the Jaguars' 34-10 win over the Browns on Sunday.
story: The sixth-round rookie wideout played well ahead of Travis Hunter, out-snapping him by a 19-4 margin behind the Jaguars' top trio of Parker Washington, Brian Thomas and Jakobi Meyers at wideout. Cameron ended up catching Trevor Lawrence's second touchdown, a four-yard score toward the end of the first quarter. Cameron would appear to have the lead for WR4 duties in Jacksonville.

headline: Abdullah carried the ball seven times for 30 yards and returned one kickoff for 24 yards in Thursday night's 33-10 win over the Ravens.
story: Abdullah recorded the third-most-offensive snaps in the backfield (seven), behind Chris Rodriguez (25) and Bayshul Tuten (20). Should everyone in the backfield remain healthy, Abdullah will likely see a similar workload for the rest of the season.

headline: Abdullah carried the ball three times for 11 yards and caught his only target for two yards during Sunday's 20-13 loss to the Broncos.
story: The 30-year-old was most involved on special teams and saw just six of the Jaguars' 59 offensive snaps, finishing behind Bhayshul Tuten (30), Chris Rodriguez (13) and LeQuint Allen (nine) in the backfield. Abdullah should continue to see a similar workload as long as the RBs ahead of him on the depth chart remain healthy.

headline: Strange caught both of his targets for 22 yards in Thursday night's 33-10 win over the Ravens.
story: The Jaguars keep blowing teams out and aren't being pushed on offense, which is keeping Trevor Lawrence's pass volume low. Strange is still making the most of his few opportunities, totaling four grabs for 77 yards on four targets over the last two weeks, games in which the Jaguars have combined to outscore their opponents 75-17. Strange is a TE1 for fantasy and gets a date with the Titans on Sunday, Nov. 15.

headline: Strange caught both of his targets for 55 yards during Sunday's 42-7 win over Indianapolis.
story: Strange was able to make it seven games in a row with multiple catches to open the 2026 campaign. The tight end tied running back Bhayshul Tuten for the team lead in receiving yards, exceeding 50 yards for the third time in the last four games. Strange has now reeled in 28 of 35 targets for 334 yards and a touchdown over seven contests this season.

headline: Strange caught five of seven targets for 44 yards during Sunday's 34-31 loss to the Texans.
story: Strange finished tied for the team lead in catches with wide receiver Jakobi Meyers, while his seven targets were third behind Meyers (10) and Parker Washington (11). The tight end has now reeled in at least five passes in three straight contests, compiling 207 receiving yards on 19 catches in those games. The Jaguars are off in Week 7, so his next chance to continue his momentum will come Nov. 1 against the Colts.

headline: Strange caught seven of eight targets for 68 yards in Sunday's 19-17 win over the Eagles.
story: After breaking out for a 7-95-0 line last week, Strange tied that season high in catches, although for less yardage. The tight end is re-establishing himself as Trevor Lawrence's preferred safety valve, which should assure him a solid floor for volume. Strange will take a 21-235-1 line on 26 targets through five games into a Week 6 clash with the Texans.

headline: Strange caught seven of eight targets for 95 yards in Sunday's 22-17 win over the Bengals.
story: Cincinnati annually plays bad defense against opposing tight ends, and Strange was able to take advantage of the clean matchup by leading the team in targets, catches and receiving yards Sunday. An every-down tight end in Jacksonville's potent offense, he's a weekly fringe TE1/2 headed into next Sunday's game against the Eagles. On the season, Strange has 14 catches for 167 yards and one touchdown on 18 targets.

headline: Strange caught three of five targets for 32 yards during the Jaguars' 35-6 win over the Patriots on Sunday.
story: Most of Strange's production came on a 23-yard catch midway through the second quarter, which put the Jaguars just outside the red zone and helped lead to a 10-yard touchdown pass from Trevor Lawrence to Jakobi Meyers five plays later. Strange finished Sunday's game tied for the second-most targets and catches and third in receiving yards behind Meyers (64) and Parker Washington (40). Strange is off to a somewhat slow start to the 2026 season, though he's competing against Meyers, Washington and Brian Thomas for targets in the passing game. Strange will take a 7-72-1 line (on 10 targets) into a Week 4 road clash against the Bengals.

headline: Strange caught both of his targets for 17 yards in Sunday's 20-13 loss to the Broncos.
story: Parker Washington (12 targets) and Brian Thomas (eight) saw a combined 20 targets on Trevor Lawrence's 29 pass attempts, leaving very little opportunity for the rest of the Jaguars' pass catchers. Strange still ran 25 routes on 31 dropbacks, proving he's an every-down tight end in one of the league's premier offenses. He'll be a touchdown-dependent TE1/2 next Sunday against the Patriots.

headline: Strange caught two of three targets for 23 yards and a touchdown Sunday in a 34-10 victory versus Cleveland.
story: Strange had a relatively quiet day in terms of targets and yardage, but he finished with a fine fantasy total on the strength of a 14-yard connection with Trevor Lawrence in the second quarter. Strange seems to have carried over the red-zone chemistry with Lawrence that developed late last year, when all three of his scores came over the Jaguars' final six regular-season games. The 2023 second-round draft pick logged a career-best 540 receiving yards last season and is positioned to be Jacksonville's top tight end again in 2026.

headline: Hunter caught his only target for minus-1 yard and lost a fumble in Thursday night's 33-10 win over the Ravens.
story: Hunter played six offensive snaps against Baltimore but turned the ball over on his only touch. After posting a 4-59-1 receiving line against the Texans in London back in Week 6, Hunter has done very little on offense. He needs the Jaguars' opponents to make games closer so the coaching staff feels obligated to utilize Hunter's big-play ability.

headline: Hunter failed to catch his lone target in Sunday's 42-7 win over the Colts. He added five rushing yards on one attempt.
story: With the Jaguars destroying their division rivals, Trevor Lawrence dropped back to pass just 17 times. Hunter's playmaking ability wasn't needed, as he logged just six offensive snaps. He'd likely benefit from a Brian Thomas trade ahead of next week's deadline.

headline: Hunter caught all four of his targets for 59 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 34-31 loss to the Texans in London. He also recorded three tackles and an interception.
story: The two-way player is beginning to flash the talent that made him the second overall pick in the 2025 NFL Draft. Hunter's receiving numbers were by far a season high -- he had only two catches coming into Sunday -- and his day on offense was capped by a seven-yard touchdown reception from Trevor Lawrence in the fourth quarter that brought the Jaguars to within a field goal at 31-28. Hunter then made an impact on the very next possession, picking off a C.J. Stroud pass in the end zone with just under four minutes left on the clock to keep his team in the game. The touchdown and interception were each the second of his career in his 13th NFL game, and Hunter became the first player since 2002 to have one of each in the same game. Jacksonville's receiver room is crowded with Parker Washington, Jakobi Meyers and Brian Thomas at the top of the depth chart, but head coach Liam Coen hinted after the game that Hunter's role on offense could continue to grow following the team's Week 7 bye, per CBS 47 Jacksonville.

headline: Hunter recorded a nine-yard reception and tallied six tackles and a pass breakup in Sunday's 19-17 win over the Eagles in London.
story: After not getting any run on offense in the Jaguars' Week 4 win over the Bengals, Hunter ended up taking the field for six of 72 snaps in Week 5 and was able to come away with his second reception of the season. The two-way player continues to see the overwhelming amount of his playing time on defense, where he was on the field for all 62 snaps. Expect the Jaguars continue to use Hunter almost exclusively at cornerback while sprinkling him into the offensive game plan only occasionally.

headline: Hunter logged four tackles (three solo) and two pass defenses during the Jaguars' 22-17 win over the Bengals on Sunday.
story: After snagging his first NFL interception against the Patriots in Week 3, Hunter demonstrated his defensive prowess in Week 4 with two pass defenses. Notably, for the first time this season, the 2025 second-overall pick did not play a single snap on offense. It appears the Jaguars are comfortable with rookie Josh Cameron serving as the depth wideout behind Parker Washington, Jakobi Meyers and Brian Thomas, so Hunter's playing time figures to be limited to defense. Hunter has 13 tackles (nine solo) and four pass defenses (including one interception) through the first four games of the regular season.

headline: Hunter played five offensive snaps in Sunday's 35-6 win over the Patriots.
story: He failed to see a target in the passing game for the second straight week and is clearly not in the team's plans on that side of the ball with everyone healthy at wideout. Hunter would likely need one or even two injuries ahead of him on the depth chart to see significant snaps on offense. On defense against New England, Hunter logged four tackles (three solo) and one pass breakup, including his first career regular-season interception.

headline: Hunter played six offensive snaps but didn't record a target during the Jaguars' 20-13 loss to the Broncos on Sunday.
story: It was a slight increase from the four offensive snaps Hunter played in Week 1 against the Browns. The second-year pro mostly saw the field on defense Sunday, playing 37 of 62 defensive snaps (59.7 percent) and finishing with four solo tackles and a pass defense. Hunter's involvement on offense figures to be minimal, given the plethora of targets Trevor Lawrence has at his disposal in Parker Washington, Jakobi Meyers, Brian Thomas and Brenton Strange.

headline: Hunter played four offensive snaps in the Jaguars' 34-10 win over the Browns on Sunday.
story: On those four plays, Hunter recorded an eight-yard catch on one target and rushed for three yards on one carry. On defense, Hunter logged 29 snaps and totaled one solo tackle. It's become evident that the Jaguars have no plans to feature Hunter on offense unless the wide-receiver room is struck by a string of injuries. He can be left on the waiver wire in all redraft fantasy formats.

headline: Little made all four of his field-goal attempts and all three of his extra-point tries in a 33-10 win over Baltimore on Thursday.
story: The Jaguars dominated in the victory, but they fell short of the end zone enough times to keep Little busy. He didn't need to fully flex the strength of his leg, as his longest kick was from a modest 47 yards out, but Little extended his run of consecutive successful FG attempts to 10. He's now gone 14-of-16 on field-goal tries this season while converting 25 of 26 point-after attempts.

headline: Little nailed all six extra-point attempts in Sunday's 42-7 win over the Colts.
story: The kicker did not get a field-goal attempt, but he was the beneficiary of an offense that scored six touchdowns. Little has connected on 22 of 23 extra-point tries in 2026, though he has only 12 total field-goal attempts, 10 of which he's made.

headline: Little made his sole field-goal attempt and all four of his PATs in the Jaguars' 34-31 loss to the Texans on Sunday in London.
story: Little made a 60-yard field goal with 1:55 left in the fourth quarter to tie the game, 31-31. The Jaguars' kicker continues to deliver in big moments for the team whenever called upon. Little moves to 10-for-12 on field-goal attempts and 16-for-17 on PATs through six games in 2026.

headline: Little made both of his field goals and went 1-for-2 on extra-point tries during the Jaguars' 19-17 win over the Eagles on Sunday in London.
story: The Jaguars looked dead in the water after Eagles' kicker Jake Elliott connected on a 48-yard field goal to give Philadelphia a 17-16 lead with only eight seconds left in the fourth quarter. However, Ameer Abdullah gave Jacksonville hope with a 53-yard return on the ensuing kickoff, and Little answered the call with a 57-yard field goal to seal the victory for the Jaguars. Little is 9-for-11 on field-goal attempts through five regular-season games, with both of those misses coming from 50-plus yards. The Jaguars will stay in London for Week 6 to face the Texans in an AFC South showdown.

headline: Little went 3-for-3 on field-goal tries and made his only PAT during Sunday's 22-17 win over the Bengals.
story: Little delivered a pair of field-goal makes from 55 and 28 yards in the first half before later adding another 54-yard make in the third quarter. The kicker has now gone 7-for-9 on field-goal tries, including 4-for-6 from 50-plus yards, and he figures to continue to get plenty of opportunities while finishing off the drives of Jacksonville's potent offense.

headline: Little hit all five of his extra-point attempts and missed a 70-yard field-goal try in Sunday's 35-6 win over the Patriots.
story: The Jaguars lined up for what would have been a record-setting field goal just before halftime, but Little missed it wide right. The kicker has failed to connect on only two attempts this season, a 54-yard field-goal try and this 70-yard attempt. The Jaguars have been offering him plenty of scoring opportunities through three games, and it's clear that the team doesn't hesitate to test Little's strong leg.

headline: Little went 2-for-3 on field-goal attempts and made his lone PAT in Sunday's 20-13 loss to the Broncos.
story: With the scored tied 13-13 early in the fourth quarter, Little lined up for a 54-yard field goal but pulled it wide left for his first miss of the season. His makes were from 44 and 23 yards earlier in the contest. Through two games, Little has made four of five field-goal tries and all five PATs. He'll get a date with the Patriots next Sunday.

headline: Little went 2-for-2 on field-goal attempts and made all four of his PATs in Sunday's 34-10 win over the Browns.
story: After finishing as fantasy's K5 overall last regular season, Little picked up right where he left off in Week 1 against Cleveland. His field-goal makes came from 47 and 40 yards Sunday, and he's now 31-for-37 on field goals from 40-plus yards out across 35 career regular-season contests. The big-legged Little is an every-week K1 in this Jacksonville offense.

headline: Lawrence completed 16 of 26 passes for 242 yards with a touchdown and no interceptions while rushing once for minus-1 yard in the Jaguars' 33-16 win over the Ravens on Thursday night.
story: Lawrence unsurprisingly didn't have a high-volume night, as the Jaguars were progressively able to take control of the game with Joe Fagnano under center for the Ravens. The veteran signal-caller hit Parker Washington on a 50-yard catch-and-run touchdown over the middle just before halftime for his one scoring pass, and Lawrence connected with eight different targets overall on the night. The 2021 first overall pick has now thrown for 1,932 yards with an 18:4 TD:INT and added 79 yards on the ground heading into a Week 10 road matchup against the Titans on Sunday, Nov. 15.

headline: Lawrence completed 10 of 14 passes for 210 yards with three touchdowns and no interceptions while rushing three times for 10 yards in the Jaguars' 42-7 win over the Colts on Sunday.
story: Lawrence helped the Jaguars to a commanding 28-0 halftime lead with scoring strikes to Brian Thomas (12 yards) and Nate Boerkircher (31 yards), and he added a 25-yard TD toss to Bhayshul Tuten as time expired in the third quarter. Lawrence eventually gave way to Quinn Ewers late in the blowout win, but not before completing 71.4 percent of his passes and throwing at least three touchdown passes for the fourth time on the campaign. Lawrence now has 1,690 passing yards with a 17:4 TD:INT and has added 80 rushing yards heading into a Week 9 road matchup against the Ravens on Thursday night.

headline: Lawrence completed 24 of 41 passes for 306 yards and four touchdowns with one interception in Sunday's 34-31 loss to the Texans. He added 11 rushing yards on three carries.
story: The Jaguars had to open things up in the second half after falling behind 24-14 following the Texans' first possession of the third quarter, and Lawrence wound up attempting 40-plus passes for the first time this season while tying his 2026 high in TD passes with two scores to Bhayshul Tuten, and one each to Travis Hunter and rookie tight end Nate Boerkircher. He also topped 300 passing yards for a second straight game. Lawrence will take a 14:4 TD:INT into a bye before clashing with the Colts in Week 8.

headline: Lawrence completed 24 of 39 passes for 331 yards and two touchdowns with one interception in Sunday's 19-17 win over the Eagles. He added 25 rushing yards on three carries.
story: Both TDs went to Parker Washington, a 51-yard catch-and-run in the first quarter and then a 27-yard score in the fourth on a spectacular one-handed grab by the wideout. It was the first time this season Lawrence had committed a fumble or committed multiple turnovers in a game, but he compensated with a season high in passing yards. Lawrence will take a 10:3 TD:INT through five contests into a Week 6 clash with the Texans.

headline: Lawrence completed 18 of 23 passes for 227 yards with one touchdown and no interceptions while adding three carries for no gain in the Jaguars' 22-17 win over the Bengals on Sunday.
story: While Lawrence saw opposite number Joe Burrow nearly double his passing production with a gaudy 428-yard total, the former guided his team to victory with a highly efficient and turnover-free effort. Lawrence averaged an impressive 9.9 yards per attempt and weathered a quartet of sacks while connecting with seven different targets. The 2021 first overall pick had to resort to relying heavily on tight end Brenton Strange (7-95-0 on eight targets), as Cincinnati effectively took away Lawrence's wide receivers for most of the afternoon, but the talented signal-caller did hit Brian Thomas from seven yards out in the second quarter for his one touchdown toss. Lawrence looks to be hitting on all cylinders to open his second season in Liam Coen's offense, taking a 69.2 percent completion rate, 843 passing yards and an 8:2 TD:INT into a Week 5 London showdown against the Eagles next Sunday.

headline: Lawrence completed 19 of 29 passes for 182 yards with three touchdowns and one interception while adding four rushes for 25 yards in the Jaguars' 35-6 win over the Patriots on Sunday.
story: Lawrence's passing yardage continued its downward trend for the second straight game, but the 2021 first overall pick threw multiple touchdown passes for the second time to open the season. He connected with Josh Cameron (12 yards), Jakobi Meyers (10 yards) and Parker Washington (17 yards) for his trio of scoring tosses, and he offered solid supplemental fantasy production with his legs. Lawrence will take 616 passing yards and a 7:2 TD:INT into a Week 4 road showdown against Joe Burrow and the Bengals next Sunday.

headline: Washington secured two of seven targets for 61 yards and a touchdown in the Jaguars' 33-10 win over the Ravens on Thursday night. He also returned one punt for 11 yards.
story: Washington led the Jaguars in targets while tying for second in receptions and receiving yards on the night. The fourth-year receiver snapped a two-game touchdown drought, crossing the goal line from 50 yards out on a catch and run over the middle with under a minute remaining in the first half. Washington has eclipsed 60 receiving yards in three of the past four games heading into a Week 10 road matchup against the Titans on Sunday, Nov. 15.

headline: Washington brought in one of two targets for 16 yards and rushed once for 10 yards in the Jaguars' 42-7 win over the Colts on Sunday.
story: The Jaguars had little need to be aggressive through the air with the Colts non-competitive throughout the afternoon. Trevor Lawrence ultimately put up only 14 pass attempts and Quinn Ewers added another three in mop-up duty, leaving little for Washington and the rest of the air attack to produce with. Washington has a 27-432-4 receiving line on 48 targets through seven games heading into a Week 9 road matchup against the reeling Ravens on Thursday night.

headline: Washington caught four of 11 targets for 64 yards in Sunday's 34-31 loss to the Texans.
story: Despite leading the Jaguars in targets, Washington finished second to Jakobi Meyers in both catches and receiving yards, and he wasn't on the other end of any of Trevor Lawrence's four TDs. It's the third time in the last four games that Washington has failed to reach five grabs or 70 yards, but the fourth contest featured a 6-124-2 line from the fourth-year wideout. Washington will take a 26-416-4 line on 46 targets into a bye before facing the Colts in Week 8.

headline: Washington caught six of nine targets for 124 yards and two touchdowns in Sunday's 19-17 win over the Eagles.
story: The fourth-year wideout accounted for both of the Jaguars' TDs on the day, breaking free for a 51-yard score in the first quarter and then beating blanket coverage from Riq Woolen for a spectacular one-handed grab in the fourth quarter from 27 yards out. Washington was apparently just scratching the surface of his potential in 2025, and through five games this season he's posted a 22-352-4 line on 35 targets as Trevor Lawrence's top downfield option. Washington will look to keep rolling in Week 6 against a Texans defense that has unexpectedly struggled so far in 2026.

headline: Washington secured one of three targets for seven yards, rushed once for three yards and returned one punt for three yards in the Jaguars' 22-17 win over the Bengals on Sunday.
story: Washington had been Trevor Lawrence's top target by a comfortable margin over the first three games of the season, but the Bengals effectively shut down the bulk of Jacksonville's wide-receiver production Sunday. Washington saw the biggest downturn, making it a forgettable fantasy afternoon overall despite the team-level success the Jaguars enjoyed. Washington figures to have an uphill battle in terms of a potential Week 5 resurgence as well, considering the Jaguars will face off with a talented Eagles defense in a Week 5 matchup in London next Sunday.

headline: Washington secured three of five targets for 40 yards and a touchdown in the Jaguars' 35-6 win over the Patriots on Sunday.
story: The dynamic slot receiver tied for second in receptions and targets on the afternoon for Jacksonville while also finishing as the runner-up in receiving yards. Washington was on the receiving end of one of Trevor Lawrence's three touchdown passes of the day, recording a 17-yard scoring grab late in the third quarter. Washington's totals Sunday were season lows across the board, but he's off to a hot start with a 15-221-2 receiving line over the first three games heading into a Week 4 road showdown against the Bengals next Sunday.

headline: Washington brought in seven of 12 targets for 98 yards in the Jaguars' 20-13 loss to the Broncos on Sunday. He also returned two punts for 12 yards and fumbled once but recovered.
story: Washington led the Jaguars across the board in receptions, receiving yards and targets while also posting a game-high 32-yard catch. The fourth-year wideout has picked up right where he left off during his breakout stretch run and postseason in 2025, as he's quickly put together a 12-181-1 line on 18 targets over his first two games. Washington will remain a focal point of the Jaguars' air attack in a second consecutive marquee matchup in Week 3 at home against the defending AFC champion Patriots.

headline: Washington secured five of six targets for 83 yards and a touchdown in the Jaguars' 34-10 win over the Browns on Sunday. He also returned one punt for minus-5 yards.
story: Washington led the Jaguars in all of receptions, receiving yards and targets, and his impressive 30-yard touchdown grab in the first quarter kicked off a prolific afternoon for Jacksonville's offense. Washington, whose late-season surge in 2025 has put him in line for an extension, certainly benefits from the strong start to the new season in that regard, and he should remain a focal point despite a tough Week 2 road matchup against the Broncos next Sunday.

headline: Jones recorded four tackles (two solo), including 2.0 sacks, and a pass breakup in Sunday's 35-12 win over the Jets.
story: The 32-year-old defensive lineman had gotten off to a slow start to begin the 2026 season, his 11th in the league. Prior to Sunday, he'd recorded just 0.5 sacks across the first seven games, so his 2.0 sacks were his first full ones of the campaign. Jones is now up to 17 tackles (eight solo), including 2.5 sacks, three pass breakups and a fumble recovery on 72 percent of the defensive snaps.

headline: Jones (calf) is active for Sunday's game against the Colts.
story: Jones has been given the green light to play Sunday after working through a calf injury throughout the week. Even though he'll suit up, the veteran defensive lineman may operate on a limited snap count, which would result in Peter Woods, Bryson Eason and Khyiris Tonga all operating in elevated roles.

headline: Jones (calf) is expected to play against the Colts on Sunday, Ian Rapoport of NFL Network reports.
story: Jones was limited by a calf injury all week and drew the questionable tag for Sunday's home tilt, but the veteran defensive lineman is on track to be active against Indianapolis. He could operate under a limited snap count, which would result in more playing time for Khyiris Tonga, Peter Woods and Bryson Eason.

headline: Jones (calf) is officially listed as questionable for Sunday's game versus the Colts, Matt McMullen of the Chiefs' official site reports.
story: Jones was limited at practice all week because of a nagging calf issue, but the same applied throughout Week 1 prep before he ultimately played through the issue in Monday night's win over the Broncos. If Jones can't do the same Sunday, rookie first-rounder Peter Woods would stand to benefit in terms of defensive snaps.

headline: Jones (calf) was a limited participant at practice Wednesday.
story: Jones was able to play through the tension in his calf in Monday's win versus the Broncos, so it's unlikely his availability for Week 2 is in any true jeopardy. A full practice Thursday or Friday would clear up any lingering doubt going into the weekend.

headline: Karlaftis recorded six tackles (four solo), including 2.0 sacks, and a pass breakup in Sunday's 35-12 win over the Jets.
story: After starting the season without a sack in his first four games, Karlaftis has 4.0 sacks over his last four contests. For the season, the 25-year-old edge rusher is up to 32 tackles (16 solo), including the 4.0 sacks, a career-high nine pass breakups, including his first career interception, and a forced fumble across eight games. He's on pace to shatter his previous career high of 48 tackles, which was set last season.

headline: Karlaftis registered six total tackles, a sack and two pass breakups in Sunday's 22-6 win over the Chargers.
story: Though Sunday's contest marked the first time all season that he notched a sack, Karlaftis has been making life difficult on quarterbacks throughout the campaign. Per Pro Football Focus, Karlaftis ranks seventh in the NFL with 27 total quarterback pressures, including 19 over the Chiefs' past two games. Karlaftis has also tallied 21 tackles, four pass breakups and an interception through five appearances.

headline: Bolton recorded 12 tackles (five solo) and a forced fumble in Sunday's 35-12 win over the Jets.
story: Bolton doesn't do much in the box scores other than rack up tackles, but he's good at that and now has five double-digit tackles games through eight contests to begin the 2026 campaign. For the season, Bolton is up to 80 tackles (39 solo), two pass breakups and a forced fumble on 99 percent of the Chiefs' defensive snaps.

headline: Bolton registered 11 tackles (six solo) during the Chiefs' 20-3 loss to the Seahawks on Sunday.
story: Bolton played all but one of the Chiefs' 69 defensive snaps during Sunday's loss, and he finished second on the team in tackles behind Drue Tranquill (12). Bolton has recorded double-digit stops in four of six regular-season games and is up to 59 tackles (29 solo) and two pass defenses on the year.

headline: Bolton recorded 11 total tackles (three solo) during Sunday's 22-6 win over the Chargers.
story: Bolton led the team in takedowns, notching double-digit tackles in a game for the third time this season. The linebacker has now registered 48 total tackles (23 solo) and two passes defensed over five contests to open the 2026 campaign.

headline: Bolton posted nine tackles (four solo) during the Chiefs' 30-27 win over the Raiders on Sunday.
story: Bolton played every single defensive snap during Sunday's win and finished as the Chiefs' second-leading tackler behind rookie corner Mansoor Delane (10). Through four regular-season games and heading into the Chiefs' Week 5 bye, Bolton leads the team with 37 combined tackles, which is tied with Akeem Davis-Gaither and Jihaad Campbell for sixth-most in the NFL.

headline: Bolton recorded 11 tackles (eight solo) and a pass breakup in Sunday's 24-10 win over the Dolphins.
story: Bolton has now posted double-digit tackles in back-to-back games. He has 100-plus tackles in four of the last five seasons and appears to be well on his way to another triple-digit campaign. Bolton has 28 tackles (16 solo) and a pair of pass breakups through three games to begin the 2026 season.

headline: Bolton registered 13 tackles (six solo) during the Chiefs' 33-30 overtime win over the Colts on Sunday.
story: Bolton was one of four Chiefs players to play all 65 defensive snaps during Sunday's OT win, with the sixth-year pro also playing seven snaps on special teams. It was the 24th time in Bolton's NFL career that he recorded double-digit tackles, and his 13 takedowns were his most in a game since Week 3 of the 2025 season against the Giants (14). Bolton is up to 17 combined tackles through two regular-season games and will look to stay busy in a Week 3 road tilt against the Dolphins on Sept. 27.

headline: Bolton posted four tackles (two solo) and a pass defense during the Chiefs' 31-10 win over the Broncos on Sunday.
story: Bolton's four tackles would have been his second-lowest total of the 2025 regular season (two in Week 7 against the Raiders), though he still finished tied for the third-most tackles on the Chiefs behind L'Jarius Sneed (eight) and Drue Tranquill (seven). Even with Kansas City holding a commanding lead in the fourth quarter, Bolton still played all 51 defensive snaps, so he should have plenty of opportunities to put up larger numbers in the box score this season. He's logged at least 100 tackles in four of his six years in the NFL, and he finished the 2025 campaign with 154 tackles (73 solo), including 1.0 sacks, six pass defenses (including an interception) and one forced fumble across 17 regular-season games.

headline: Tranquill collected 13 tackles (seven solo) in Sunday's 35-12 win over the Jets.
story: It was Tranquill's second double-digit tackles game of the season, and both have come over the last three weeks. The veteran linebacker has piled up 66 tackles (33 solo), two pass breakups and one fumble recovery on 88 percent of the defensive snaps across eight games this season.

headline: Tranquill finished Sunday's 20-3 loss to the Seahawks with 12 tackles (four solo).
story: Tranquil led the Chiefs in combined tackles Sunday, and he was one of three Kansas City defenders to reach double-digit stops. He's logged at least seven tackles in each of the first six games of the regular season and is up to 48 tackles (22 solo), two pass defenses and one fumble recovery in 2026.

headline: Delane (shoulder) was a full participant in Wednesday's practice.
story: The first-round rookie cornerback appears set to return to the lineup Sunday against the Falcons after missing the previous two contests. Delane has been dealing with the shoulder issue since initially injuring it during the offseason program. Across five games this season, Delane has 27 tackles (17 solo) and five pass breakups, including an interception.

headline: Chiefs head coach Andy Reid said Friday that Delane (shoulder) will not play Sunday against the Jets, Nate Taylor of ESPN.com reports.
story: Reid added that the rookie Delane is "making progress" but isn't quite ready to make his return, marking the second straight game the 22-year-old will miss. Delane has 27 tackles (17 solo), five pass deflections and one interception in five games this season.

headline: Delane (shoulder) has been downgraded from questionable to out for Sunday's game against the Broncos.
story: Delane was initially given the questionable tag for Week 8 despite not practicing both Thursday and Friday. The Chiefs will now be without their rookie first-round corner and veteran defensive back L'Jarius Sneed (knee), the latter of whom was placed on injured reserve Saturday. Their absences for Sunday's AFC West tilt means more defensive snaps are available for the likes of Kristian Fulton, Jadon Canady, Christian Roland-Wallace and Jaden Hicks. Delane's next opportunity to play is Week 9 against the Jets on Sunday, Nov. 8.

headline: Delane (shoulder) is listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the Broncos.
story: Delane missed each of the last two practices of Week 8 prep due to a shoulder issue, suggesting that the rookie first-rounder picked up the injury during Wednesday's session. The Chiefs have not ruled out Delane despite the missed practices, but if he's unable to play Sunday, then Kristian Fulton and Christian Roland-Wallace would be the top candidates to start opposite Nohl Williams at outside corner.

headline: Delane (shoulder) did not practice Thursday.
story: Delane practiced Wednesday, though after missing Thursday's session, he is now listed on the injury report ahead of Sunday's divisional clash with the Broncos. The 22-year-old rookie dealt with the shoulder issue during training camp, and while he managed to suit up in Week 1 against Denver, he aggravated the injury during the contest and missed the Week 2 overtime victory over the Colts. He has had a sound inaugural campaign in 2025, amassing 27 total tackles (17 solo), one interception and four additional passes defended. If Delane can't play in Week 8, Christian Roland-Wallace and Kristian Fulton would be in line for more snaps.

headline: Delane tallied 10 tackles (seven solo) and one pass defense during the Chiefs' 30-27 win over the Raiders on Sunday.
story: The rookie first-rounder played 78 of 84 defensive snaps Sunday (92.9 percent) and was the only Chiefs player to log double-digit tackles. He's reached that mark in back-to-back games and is up to 20 tackles (14 solo) and three pass defenses (including one interception) through the first three games of his NFL career. Up next for the Chiefs is a Week 6 home game Sunday, Oct. 18 against the Chargers, whose offense has struggled with Justin Herbert under center.

headline: Delane recorded 10 tackles (seven solo) and a pass breakup in Sunday's 24-10 win over the Dolphins.
story: Delane picked off a pass in his regular-season NFL debut in Week 1 against the Broncos but injured his shoulder after playing just three defensive snaps. He was cleared for Week 2 versus Indianapolis but was ultimately held out to rest his shoulder. Delane played 98.6 percent of the defensive snaps against Miami and appears to be past the issue.

headline: Delane (shoulder) is active for Sunday's game against the Colts.
story: Delane suffered a shoulder injury during the Chiefs' Week 1 win over the Broncos, but he did enough during the week and Sunday's pregame warmups to be cleared to play against Indianapolis. If Delane suffers a setback against Indianapolis, then Kristian Fulton would likely enter the game at outside corner.

headline: Delane (shoulder) is officially listed as questionable for Sunday's game versus the Colts, Matt McMullen of the Chiefs' official site reports.
story: Delane was limited at practice Friday after practicing in full Wednesday and Thursday, suggesting he suffered some sort of setback during the week. If he can't suit up in Week 2, it could mean increased reps at corner for Kristian Fulton.

headline: Delane (shoulder) was a full participant at practice Wednesday.
story: Delane left Monday's win versus the Broncos early after injuring his shoulder, but it looks like that will be the extent of his absence. He intercepted a pass on his third regular-season snap as a pro in Week 1, and he'll be looking to keep the momentum up Sunday versus the Colts.

headline: Delane (shoulder) should only miss minimal time as he recovers from the injury he suffered in Monday's 31-10 win over the Broncos, Ian Rapoport of NFL Network reported Tuesday.
story: Delane picked off Bo Nix on Denver's opening drive. The cornerback's "Welcome to the NFL" moment was kinder than most, but it quickly flipped the other way as he was forced out of the game early with a shoulder issue. If the first-round rookie cannot heal enough to suit up for Sunday's game against the Colts, Nohl Williams and Kristian Fulton will likely start at outside cornerback for the Chiefs.

headline: Delane (shoulder) has been ruled out for the remainder of Monday night's game against the Broncos.
story: Delane kick-started his NFL debut by intercepting Bo Nix on the Broncos' opening possession. The cornerback's injury may be a flare-up of an existing issue he struggled with throughout OTAs. With the first-round rookie ruled out, Nohl Williams will likely see more snaps at outside cornerback.

headline: Delane has a shoulder injury and is questionable to return to Monday's matchup with the Broncos.
story: The rookie first-round pick intercepted a Bo Nix pass on Denver's first possession of the game, leading to a Kansas City touchdown. Delane was dealing with a shoulder injury during OTAs and was limited to start training camp as a result of the issue. Kristian Fulton, Nohl Williams and Christian Roland-Wallace could see more snaps in his absence.

headline: Mahomes (right elbow/knee) was a full participant in Wednesday's practice.
story: As were Rashee Rice (knee) as well as Xavier Worthy (hamstring), and with Chiefs having added Josh Downs (who is not on the injury report) via a trade with the Colts, the team heads into Sunday's game against the Falcons with its franchise QB and top three WRs presumably available for Week 10 action. Mahomes clearly endured some elbow discomfort during the Chiefs' Week 9 win over the Jets, but the issue is something he'll continue to play through.

headline: Chiefs coach Andy Reid said that he expects full practice participation by Mahomes (elbow) on Wednesday, Charles Goldman of AtoZSports.com reports.
story: Mahomes played through some elbow discomfort during the Chiefs' Week 9 win over the Jets, but Reid indicated Monday that the star QB was considered day-to-day as this Sunday's game against the Falcons approaches, per Sam McDowell of The Kansas City Star. Assuming Mahomes indeed logs a full session Wednesday, he'll be in line to play this weekend, and if so, will be working with a WR corps bolstered by Tuesday's trade deadline acquisition of Josh Downs from the Colts.

headline: Chiefs coach Andy Reid said Monday that Mahomes (elbow) is considered day-to-day as this Sunday's game against the Falcons approaches, Sam McDowell of The Kansas City Star reports.
story: Mahomes emerged from Week 9 action with what Ian Rapoport of NFL Network described earlier Monday as an elbow "strain/sprain" to his throwing arm following an MRI on Sunday. For his part, Reid also noted with regard to the star QB's exam results that "it was more positive news than negative news. It looks like it's just a matter of rehabbing and getting rid of some of the soreness." As a result, look for Mahomes' practice participation to be managed this week, which could lead to his top backup Justin Fields logging some added reps in the coming days.

headline: Mahomes was diagnosed with an "elbow strain/sprain" on his throwing arm following an MRI on Sunday, and he'll "continue to be monitored" leading up to the Chiefs' Week 10 game in Atlanta, Ian Rapoport of NFL Network reports.
story: Though his MRI didn't reveal any major injury, Mahomes could have his practice activity managed carefully in Week 10 while he tends to the elbow issue. Mahomes sustained the right elbow injury at the two-minute mark in the second quarter Sunday, when the Jets' David Bailey took him down on a strip-sack. The Chiefs recovered the fumble, and after tossing a few warmup passes, Mahomes was able to stay in the game and finished with 23 completions on 31 attempts for 242 yards and two touchdowns in a 35-12 victory.

headline: Mahomes (elbow) underwent an MRI after Sunday's 35-12 win over the Jets, and the tests did not reveal a major injury, Ian Rapoport of NFL Network reports.
story: Mahomes returned to Sunday's win after hurting his elbow late in the first half, and the initial MRI result offers some early optimism regarding the star quarterback's status for Week 10 against the Falcons. His participation level in practice will bear monitoring over the coming days, but all signs point to Mahomes having avoided a significant injury.

headline: What kind of fantasy QB is Patrick Mahomes right now?
story: What kind of fantasy QB is Patrick Mahomes right now?

headline: Coach Andy Reid acknowledged after Sunday's 35-12 win over the Jets that Mahomes will likely be sore Monday after suffering an apparent elbow injury during the contest, Lindsey Thiry of ESPN reports.
story: Despite dealing with the elbow issue, Mahomes was able to finish Sunday's game, en route to completing 23 of his 31 pass attempts for 242 yards and a pair of TDs. In terms of his status as next Sunday's contest against the Falcons goes, Pete Sweeney of The Kansas City Star relays that Mahomes said, "if I'm able to play then I'm going to play." In the event that Mahomes' practice participation is impacted all in the coming days, Justin Fields would be next up for the Chiefs' first-team QB reps in that scenario.

headline: Mahomes completed 30 of 41 passes for 321 yards and three touchdowns in Sunday's 28-24 loss to the Broncos. He added six rushing yards on two carries.
story: The two-time MVP threw a TD in each of the first three quarters, including a four-yard toss to Noah Gray in the third that gave Kansas City a 24-13 lead, but Mahomes got shut out of the end zone over the final 15 minutes as Denver staged a comeback. It was the second three-touchdown performance of the season for Mahomes as well as his second 300-yard effort, after he threw for 382 yards and three scores against the Colts in Week 2. He'll look to keep rolling in Week 9 against a Jets defense that's allowed three straight quarterbacks to produce at least three TDs against it.

headline: Mahomes completed 19 of 33 passes for 165 yards, no touchdowns and one interception in Sunday's 20-3 loss to the Seahawks. He added two rushing attempts for 14 yards.
story: Mahomes was picked off in the second quarter and remarkably recovered his own fumble in a pile of bodies to avoid a second turnover in the third quarter, setting up a Harrison Butker field goal on the next play for the Chiefs' only points of the night. This was the first start in Mahomes' career during which Kansas City failed to reach the red zone, and he hasn't thrown a touchdown pass in two games since KC's Week 5 bye. Seattle's defense dominated while Kansas City struggled to move the ball in the absence of No. 1 WR Rashee Rice (hamstring/knee), whom the Chiefs will hope to get back for a Week 8 road game against the Broncos.

headline: Mahomes completed 23 of 30 passes for 272 yards, no touchdowns and one interception and rushed five times for 16 yards during Sunday's 22-6 win versus the Chargers.
story: The Chiefs offense continues to be the Kenneth Walker show, as the No. 1 RB reeled off 100-plus rushing yards for the fourth time in five appearances to begin his tenure with the team. Meanwhile, Mahomes failed to record a touchdown pass for the first time this season after tossing multiple TDs in each of the first four contests. Considering Kansas City's receiving corps is particularly ravaged by injuries at the moment, the offense may continue to lean more on Walker's legs than Mahomes' right arm next Sunday at Seattle.

headline: Mahomes completed 15 of 30 passes for 225 yards and two touchdowns in Sunday's 30-27 win over the Raiders. He also rushed twice for no gain.
story: Mahomes threw touchdown passes of two yards and eight yards to Tyquan Thornton, who exited the game in the fourth quarter due to an ankle injury suffered at the end of a 55-yard catch. The Chiefs also lost Rashee Rice (hamstring) in the first half. Thornton is likely looking at a lengthy absence, but Rice has a chance to recover during Kansas City's Week 5 bye before facing the Chargers in Week 6. Mahomes has led the Chiefs to a 4-0 record while posting a 9:2 TD:INT, but the team is down to Xavier Worthy, Cyrus Allen, Jalen Royals and Nikko Remigio at wide receiver at the moment.

headline: Worthy (hamstring) was a full participant in Wednesday's practice for Kansas City.
story: Worthy was considered day-to-day after exiting Sunday's 35-12 win over the Jets in the fourth quarter. A quick return to full practice participation suggests Worthy will be fine for the upcoming matchup with Atlanta on Sunday, but his target share may decline in the second half of the season after Kansas City traded for WR Josh Downs.

headline: Worthy (hamstring) is slated to practice Wednesday, " Pete Sweeney of The Kansas City Star reports.
story: Worthy exited this past Sunday's win over the Jets with a hamstring injury, and Monday he was was deemed day-to-day by coach Andy Reid, per Matt McMullen of the Chiefs' official site. In terms of how things have progressed since then, Reid said Wednesday that Worthy is "actually feeling pretty good," which is a notion that's supported by the wideout's anticipated practice participation.

headline: Coach Andy Reid said Monday that Worthy (hamstring) is considered day-to-day in advance of Sunday's game against the Falcons, Matt McMullen of the Chiefs' official site reports.
story: The same applies to QB Patrick Mahomes (elbow), with the status of both key Kansas City skill players worth monitoring closely in the coming days. If Worthy is limited or out this weekend, added reps behind top WR Rashee Rice will be available for some combination of Cyrus Allen, Jalen Royals and Andrew Armstrong.

headline: Worthy (hamstring) won't return to Sunday's game against the Jets.
story: Matt Derrick of ChiefsDigest.com previously noted that Worthy immediately grabbed his hamstring and was unable to put weight on his leg after sustaining his injury Sunday. That Worthy was so quickly ruled out for the remainder of the contest is certainly concerning in terms of his status for next week's game against the Falcons. In his absence versus the Jets, Cyrus Allen, Jalen Royals, Andrew Armstrong and Nikko Remigio are available to work behind top WR Rashee Rice.

headline: Worthy left Sunday's game against the Jets with an apparent leg injury, Mike Garafolo of NFL Network reports.
story: Per Matt Derrick of ChiefsDigest.com, Worthy immediately grabbed his hamstring and was unable to put weight on his leg before heading to the blue medical tent to get checked out. Prior to his exit from the contest, Worthy caught all six of his targets for 48 yards.

headline: Worthy caught three of six targets for 13 yards during Sunday's 28-24 loss to the Broncos.
story: Worthy put together another disappointing performance, reeling in three passes while failing to exceed 15 receiving yards for the second straight game. The wide receiver operated in a more prominent role for a couple weeks with Rashee Rice sidelined with a hamstring injury, but Rice returned to action Sunday and caught seven of eight targets for 53 yards. Worthy will continue to be an unappealing fantasy option ahead of the team's Week 9 matchup with the Jets.

headline: Rashee Rice (knee/hamstring) has no injury designation for Sunday's game against the Broncos, so Worthy will move back into his WR2 role for Week 8.
story: Rice injured his hamstring and knee against the Raiders in Week 4 and missed both of the Chiefs' two games following the Week 5 bye. During that two-game absence, Worthy turned 13 targets into 10 catches for 84 yards, but the return of Rice may give the former more space to operate in the passing game, seeing as the Broncos defense also will have to account for the returning Rice and veteran tight end Travis Kelce.

headline: Worthy caught three of six targets for 11 yards in Sunday's 20-3 loss to the Seahawks.
story: Seattle successfully limited Worthy's output in the absence of Rashee Rice (hamstring/knee), with the versatile Nick Emmanwori running stride for stride with the speedy Worthy on a couple of downfield misconnections. Worthy finished second behind Travis Kelce (eight) in targets but sixth on the Chiefs in receiving yards Sunday. Heading into a Week 8 road game against the Broncos, Worthy has drawn at least six targets in five of six games this season. He has reached 70 yards twice and failed to eclipse 25 yards in any of the other four games.

headline: Worthy will once again operate as the Chiefs' top wide receiver after Rashee Rice (hamstring/knee) was ruled out ahead of Sunday's game against the Seahawks, Pete Sweeney of The Kansas City Star reports.
story: It'll be the second consecutive game that Rice will be sidelined due to hamstring and knee injuries that he sustained in Week 4 against the Raiders. Worthy paced the Chiefs with seven catches on as many targets for 73 yards in a Week 6 win against the Chargers, and the third-year wideout once again will lead Kansas City's wide receiver group for Week 7, with Jalen Royals and rookie Cyrus Allen also in the mix for larger roles.

headline: Worthy totaled seven catches on as many targets for 73 yards during Sunday's 22-6 victory versus the Chargers.
story: Worthy served as the Chiefs' No. 1 WR in Week 6 with Rashee Rice (hamstring/knee) on the pine, and the former paced the team in all receiving categories on an afternoon in which QB Patrick Mahomes didn't record a touchdown pass. There are bound to be weeks like Sunday in which a ground game led by RB Kenneth Walker keeps Kansas City's offense humming along, but if Rice continues to miss time, Worthy figures to be among the team's leading pass catchers on a weekly basis.

headline: Worthy will be the Chiefs' top wideout against the Chargers on Sunday due to the absence of Rashee Rice (hamstring/knee).
story: Rice sustained his injuries during the Chiefs' Week 4 win against the Raiders, and the extra rest courtesy of the Week 5 bye was not enough for him to be cleared to play Sunday. Worthy finished that Week 4 contest with four catches (on seven targets) for 70 yards, and with Rice sidelined, quarterback Patrick Mahomes will rely more heavily on Worthy and veteran tight end Travis Kelce in the passing game, with Jalen Royals and rookie Cyrus Allen also in line for more playing time on offense.

headline: Worthy caught four of seven targets for 70 yards in Sunday's 30-27 win over the Raiders.
story: Worthy finished second on the team in targets and receiving yards behind Tyquan Thornton, who caught five of eight targets for 111 yards and two touchdowns prior to suffering an ankle injury in the fourth quarter. Rashee Rice (hamstring) exited the game in the first quarter, so Worthy is the top healthy wide receiver for Kansas City, though Rice will have a chance to heal during the Week 5 bye before the Chargers come to town in Week 6.

headline: Worthy caught both of his targets for 20 yards during Sunday's 24-10 win over the Dolphins.
story: Worthy entered Sunday's game on the heels of a 5-25-1 performance (on seven targets) during the Chiefs' Week 2 overtime win over the Colts. He didn't see any targets in the red zone Sunday compared to the three he had against Indianapolis, though he did lead all Chiefs wide receivers with 43 offensive snaps. His speed makes him a boom-or-bust candidate every week, though Worthy and the Chiefs pass catchers could thrive in a Week 4 road tilt against the Raiders if Las Vegas' rookie safety Treydan Stukes (concussion) is unable to play.

headline: Worthy brought in five of seven targets for 25 yards and a touchdown in the Chiefs' 33-30 overtime win over the Colts on Sunday night.
story: Worthy finished third in receptions and targets on the night for the Chiefs, but he was fifth in receiving yards and well behind fourth-place Kenneth Walker's 61 yards. However, Worthy was able to salvage his fantasy line against Indianapolis with a one-yard touchdown reception late in the second quarter. The speedster saw Tyquan Thornton vulture some downfield targets Sunday night, and Worthy is now averaging a tiny 5.4 yards per catch over his first eight receptions of the new season. The 2024 first-round pick will look to break through downfield in a Week 3 road matchup against the Dolphins' vulnerable defense.

headline: Worthy secured three of six targets for 18 yards in the Chiefs' 31-10 win over the Broncos on Monday night.
story: Worthy was on the receiving end of Patrick Mahomes' first completion of the season, which went for nine yards and took the Chiefs down to the Broncos' 26-yard line on an opening drive that culminated in a 15-yard touchdown run by the returning signal-caller. Worthy produced modest gains on his other pair of grabs, but Mahomes recorded just five completions overall to wide receivers in the season-opening victory. Worthy boasts the potential for much better production, and he could have a good opportunity to deliver on that upside in a favorable Week 2 home matchup against the Colts on Sunday night.

headline: Butker will remain Kansas City's kicker ahead of Sunday's game against the Falcons, Sam McDowell of The Kansas City Star reports.
story: On that topic, coach Andy Reid said Wednesday, "I'm gonna stick with Butker this week." While the veteran kicker has held on to the top job through the Chiefs' first eight games, he's had accuracy issues this season, having converted 12 of his 19 field-goal attempts and making 22 of his 23 extra-point tries in that span. Reid's comment about Butker on Wednesday implies that the team's kicking situation is being evaluated on a weekly basis. Justin Tucker is on Kansas City's practice squad, and he remains an option should Reid decide that a switch is in order down the road.

headline: Butker missed his only field-goal attempt and made all five of his PATs during Sunday's 35-12 win over the Jets.
story: Butker pushed his only field-goal try wide right from 51 yards out in the final moments of the first half. The kicker has now gone 12-for-19 on field-goal attempts this season, and head coach Andy Reid was asked about Butker's future following the game, stating that he'll "address that" as the team prepares for Week 10, per Sam McDowell of The Kansas City Star. The team signed veteran Justin Tucker to the practice squad in late October, and Tucker could get a shot with the active roster in Butker's place.

headline: Head coach Andy Reid said that Butker will remain the Chiefs' kicker for Sunday's game against the Jets, Nate Taylor of ESPN.com reports.
story: Butker -- who has made 12 of his 18 field-goal attempts in seven games this season -- converted one of his two tries along with with all three point-after attempts in the Chiefs' Week 8 loss to the Broncos. Despite his recent accuracy issues, Butker will retain his kicking role this weekend, even though the Chiefs recently signed Justin Tucker to the practice squad.

headline: Butker made one of his two field-goal attempts and converted all three PATs in the Chiefs' 28-24 loss to the Broncos on Sunday.
story: Butker converted a 45-yard field goal in the second quarter but missed a 54-yarder with 2:36 left in the fourth quarter that would have put the Chiefs up 27-21. The Broncos ended up winning by stopping a Chiefs touchdown attempt as time expired, something that could have been avoided had Butker converted on the prior drive. Butker has now gone 2-for-5 on field-goal attempts in the past two weeks and moves to 12-for-18 on the season.

headline: Head coach Andy Reid said Wednesday that Butker will "probably" serve as the Chiefs' kicker in Sunday's game against the Broncos, Sam McDowell of The Kansas City Star reports.
story: The Chiefs signed veteran kicker Justin Tucker to their practice squad Wednesday, with the move seemingly calling into question Butker's job security. Though he didn't give Butker the strongest endorsement, Reid noted that the Chiefs believe that a technique problem rather than any physical ailment has contributed to Butker missing five field-goal and one extra-point attempt through the team's first six games, per Matt Derrick of ChiefsDigest.com. The Chiefs are planning for Butker to get the bulk of the kicking reps in practice this week, and if he can assuage some of the concern about his technique, he'll suit up Sunday and look to solidify his standing atop the depth chart.

headline: Butker went 1-for-3 on field-goal attempts during Sunday night's 20-3 loss to Seattle.
story: Butker was off his game again in Week 7, leaving a 58-yard attempt short as time expired in the first half before later missing a 45-yard try wide right in the fourth quarter. The kicker was able to convert one field-goal attempt Sunday, nailing a 50-yarder in the third quarter. Butker has now gone 11-for-16 on field-goal attempts, including 2-for-6 from 50-plus yards, over the first six contests of the 2026 campaign.

headline: Butker made three of his four field-goal attempts and one of two PATs in the Chiefs' 22-6 win over the Chargers on Sunday.
story: Butker made field goals from 30, 44 and 50 yards while missing an attempt from 52 yards early in the fourth quarter. The kicker moves to 10-for-13 on field-goal attempts and 14-for-15 on PATs through five regular-season games so far in 2026.

headline: Butker converted his only field-goal attempt and all three of his PATs during Sunday's 30-27 win over the Raiders.
story: Butker made a 28-yard field-goal try in the second quarter, but he was limited to just one field-goal make for the third time over four contests this season. The kicker has gone 7-for-9 on field-goal attempts, including 0-for-2 from 50-plus yards, to this point in the 2026 campaign.

headline: Butker went 1-for-2 on field-goal tries and 3-for-3 on extra-point attempts in Sunday's 24-10 win over the Dolphins.
story: The kicker missed from 50 yards out late in the fourth quarter when the game was well in hand. Butker is 6-of-8 on field-goal tries and 10-of-10 on extra-point attempts in 2026. He is getting enough opportunities in the Chiefs' new-look offense to average double-digit points in fantasy.

headline: Butker went 4-for-5 on field-goal attempts and made all three of his PATs in Sunday night's 33-30 overtime win against the Colts.
story: Butker was a busy man versus Indianapolis, making field-goal tries from 46, 28, 31 and 40 yards in the victory, the last of which was a game-winner in overtime. The kicker's lone miss of the day came in the second quarter when he pushed a 51-yard attempt wide left. Through two contests, Butker has looked as good as always, converting five of six field-goal attempts, and he'll look to add his first make from 50-plus yards in Week 3 versus Miami.

headline: Butker connected on his lone field-goal attempt and all four of his extra-point tries during Kansas City's 31-10 win over the Broncos on Monday.
story: Butker's lone field goal was a 28-yard chip shot late in the third quarter, but most of his work came on PATs and kickoffs in Monday's regular-season opener. The offense under Patrick Mahomes and coordinator Eric Bieniemy looked promising in Week 1, so Butker's scoring ceiling figures to be higher this year than it was in 2025. Kansas City will stay at home for a Week 2 tilt against Indianapolis on Sunday.

headline: Fields carried twice for minus-one yard and lost a fumble while logging five snaps on offense in Sunday's 35-12 win over the Jets.
story: The Chiefs' backup quarterback saw the field for just the second time this season, after he had previously played one snap in a Week 1 win over the Broncos. Due to head coach Andy Reid's reluctance to use starter Patrick Mahomes on quarterback sneaks, Fields subbed into the game for a third-and-1 play in the first quarter. Fields ended up coughing the football, with the Jets making the recovery. The Chiefs went on to build enough of a lead to rest Mahomes for the final possession of the game with just over two minutes left in the fourth quarter, when Fields proceeded to hand the ball off three times before kneeling to run out the clock.

headline: Royals caught both of his targets for 18 yards Sunday in a 35-12 rout of the Jets.
story: Royals ranked fourth among KC wideouts in offensive snaps (21), trailing Xavier Worthy (49), Rashee Rice (38) and Andrew Armstrong (22). Royals matched his season high with two catches, and the 18 receiving yards were his second-most in a game this season. That speaks to the minimal production he's provided thus far, and Royals' role could be further reduced with the Chiefs' acquisition of Josh Downs on Tuesday.

headline: Royals caught two of his four targets for 24 yards during Kansas City's win over the Chargers on Sunday.
story: Royals saw increased playing time with Rashee Rice out due to a hamstring injury and ended up amassing a season-high 24 receiving yards. The 2025 fourth-round pick has now caught five passes for 41 yards and a touchdown across five games this season and could once again serve as the team's No. 2 receiver should Rice remain sidelined for the Week 7 matchup against the Seahawks.

headline: Royals caught both of his targets for six yards and a touchdown while logging two tackles on kick coverage in Sunday's 33-30 overtime win against the Colts.
story: Royals made an impact on his 12 offensive snaps and seven special-teams snaps. The wide receiver scored the Chiefs' last touchdown of the game midway through the third quarter on a 1-yard pass. The fourth-round rookie may see an uptick in usage if coach Andy Reid finds new ways to use the speedy young player as the season develops.

headline: Woods (neck) has been ruled out ahead of Sunday's game against the Jets, Nate Taylor of ESPN.com reports.
story: Woods will not play in Sunday's game as he continues to deal with a neck injury he sustained in the Chiefs' Week 8 loss to the Broncos. The rookie first-rounder is continuing to make progress in his recovery.

headline: Woods (neck) has been ruled out for the rest of Sunday's contest against the Broncos.
story: Woods went down with a neck injury early in the contest, and his night has now officially come to a premature end. Woods will now shift his focus toward being ready to go for the team's Week 9 matchup with the Jets.

headline: Woods (neck) is questionable to return to Sunday's contest against the Broncos.
story: Woods suffered a neck injury in the first quarter, and his status for the rest of the game is now uncertain. In his absence, Chris Jones and Khyiris Tonga will continue to operate as the Chiefs' top options at defensive tackle.

headline: Gray caught his only target for 11 yards Sunday in a 35-12 win against the Jets.
