story: McConkey attempted to play through a foot injury in Week 4, but when he exited this past Sunday's loss at Seattle in the third quarter, he had no catches among his two targets. Coach Jim Harbaugh told Alex Insdorf of BoltBeat.com on Monday that McConkey is "week-to-week," so his lack of activity to begin Week 5 prep lines up with that assessment. Friday's injury report ultimately may provide clarity on McConkey's status for Sunday's game against the Broncos.

headline: Chargers head coach Jim Harbaugh said that McConkey (foot) is expected to be at practice Wednesday, Kris Rhim of ESPN.com reports.
story: Harbaugh didn't reveal what the extent of McConkey's participation might be, and it's possible that the wideout is limited to rehab work off to the side. McConkey has battled through a couple of injuries this season, the most recent being a foot issue that flared up in the third quarter of Sunday's loss to the Seahawks. The -0-4 Chargers have a critical game this weekend at home against the Broncos.

headline: McConkey (foot), per head coach Jim Harbaugh, is "week-to-week," Alex Insdorf of BoltBeat.com reports.
story: McConkey suited up for Sunday's loss to the Seahawks despite dealing with a foot injury throughout the week, but he was forced from the game with the same issue, and Harbaugh's comment Monday indicates he could miss some time. Another report -- via Kris Rhim of ESPN.com -- indicates McConkey may be more "day-to-day" than "week-to-week," but one way or another more will be known about McConkey's status when the Chargers next release an official injury report Wednesday. Should McConkey wind up sidelined, Quentin Johnston and Tre' Harris would presumably be Justin Herbert's clear top two options at the wideout spots.

headline: McConkey won't return to Sunday's contest at Seattle due to a foot injury.
story: McConkey may have aggravated the foot issue he tended to in advance of this game, but in any case he had no catches (on two targets) at the point of his departure in the third quarter. With the third-year pro ruled out Sunday, Quentin Johnston, Tre' Harris, Marquez Valdes-Scantling and Derius Davis represent the Chargers' healthy available wide receivers for the rest of Week 4 action.

headline: McConkey (foot) is active for Sunday's game at Seattle, Eric Smith of the Chargers' official site reports.
story: McConkey had an interesting week, to say the least, which included sitting out Thursday's practice due to a foot injury and then being spotted with a visible limp afterward, according to Kris Rhim of ESPN.com. The third-year wide receiver sandwiched limited sessions around that absence, and after he entered the weekend as questionable for Week 4 action, Ian Rapoport of NFL Network reported Sunday morning that McConkey was likely to play this weekend. Now that that's been confirmed, McConkey will look to build upon his 12-183-1 line on 15 targets in three contests to begin the campaign.

headline: McConkey (foot), who is listed as questionable for Sunday's game at Seattle, is likely to suit up, Ian Rapoport of NFL Network reports.
story: McConkey was limited at Wednesday's session due to a foot injury and then didn't practice at Thursday, after which he was seen exhibiting a limp, per Kris Rhim of ESPN.com. McConkey again was limited Friday before drawing a questionable tag for Week 4 action. The current health concern isn't considered as serious as the rib issue he dealt with earlier this season, per Rapoport, so he should be good for his usual No. 1 WR role in the Chargers offense Sunday, assuming he's active.

headline: McConkey (foot) is questionable for Sunday's game against Seattle, Kris Rhim of ESPN.com reports.
story: McConkey missed practice Thursday but returned for Friday's light session, giving him a chance to suit up versus Seattle. With the Chargers still looking for their first win, having McConkey available would give them significantly better odds of beating the Seahawks. Playing through injuries already to begin the season, McConkey has 12 catches for 183 yards and one touchdown on a disappointing 15 targets. He's a fantasy WR2/3 at less than 100 percent in a struggling offense.

headline: McConkey (foot) is at practice Friday, Kris Rhim of ESPN reports.
story: After failing to practice Thursday and being seen leaving the locker room with a limp, McConkey's presence Friday is a positive sign for his chances of suiting up Sunday against the Seahawks. It's been a disappointing season for the Los Angeles offenses as a whole, and that includes McConkey, who has already dealt with rib and foot issues four weeks into the campaign.

headline: McConkey (foot) was seen walking out of the locker room with a limp after not taking part in Thursday's practice, Kris Rhim of ESPN reports.
story: McConkey showed up on the Chargers' first Week 4 injury report Wednesday as limited due to a foot injury. His downgrade to DNP one day later was potentially an ominous sign of things to come, and the aforementioned limp adds fuel to the fire that he may be in danger of sitting out Sunday's game at Seattle. Ultimately, the team may clarify McConkey's status when it posts its final practice report of the week Friday.

headline: McConkey (foot) was a non-participant in Thursday's practice.
story: McConkey opened Week 4 prep Wednesday as a limited participant, so his downgrade in activity a day later is somewhat concerning with regard to his status for Sunday's game against the Seahawks. The Chargers will see what, if anything, McConkey is able to do during their final practice of the week Friday before deciding whether he'll carry a designation into the weekend. If Los Angeles' top wideout ends up being sidelined Sunday, more opportunities in the passing game would open up for wideouts Quentin Johnston and Tre' Harris and tight end Oronde Gadsden.

headline: McConkey (foot) wasn't spotted at Thursday's practice and appears likely to be listed as a limited participant, Kris Rhim of ESPN.com reports.
story: McConkey had previously been managing a rib issue, but the wideout is tending to a new health concern this week that could threaten his availability for Sunday's game at Seattle. After the foot injury resulted in him being a limited participant in Wednesday's practice, McConkey looks like he'll take a step back in terms of activity Thursday. The Chargers could provide more clarity on the extent of McConkey's injury once Thursday's practice concludes.

headline: McConkey was limited at Wednesday's practice due to a foot injury.
story: McConkey previously dealt with a rib issue this season, but he's been able to suit up for all three contests en route to a 12-183-1 line on 15 targets. He'll have two more chances this week to get back to full participation, and Friday's practice report ultimately will unveil whether or not he enters the weekend with a designation for Sunday's game at Seattle.

headline: McConkey secured four of five targets for 66 yards in the Chargers' 24-16 loss to the Bills on Sunday.
story: Justin Herbert's top target turned in a solid stat line in the Chargers' third straight loss to open the season, yet it still wasn't enough to net Los Angeles its first win. McConkey finished second in receptions and receiving yards while slotting in third in targets on the afternoon for the Bolts, but through three contests, he sports a modest 12-183-1 line on 15 targets. It doesn't get any easier for the Chargers in Week 4, as they pay a visit to the defending champion Seahawks next Sunday afternoon.

headline: McConkey (ribs) secured all three targets for 35 yards in the Chargers' 26-14 loss to the Raiders on Sunday.
story: McConkey gained clearance from his questionable tag due to a rib injury to suit up, and the third-year wideout tied for the team lead in receptions while finishing second in receiving yards. However, it was a lackluster and mistake-filled day overall for the Chargers passing attack, so McConkey's numbers should also be viewed in that context. McConkey should play a critical role as Los Angeles looks to avoid what would be an alarming third straight loss to open the season in a Week 3 road showdown against the Bills next Sunday.

headline: McConkey (ribs) is listed as active for Sunday's game against the Raiders, Kris Rhim of ESPN.com reports.
story: Separate reports leading up to the game indicated that McConkey intended to play, and he will indeed suit up for Week 2. McConkey is apparently playing through a cracked rib and will sport a flak jacket, so while he will be out there, it's unclear if he will fill his usual role.

headline: McConkey (ribs), who is listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the Raiders, is "trending in the right direction" ahead of the 4:05 p.m. ET kickoff, Adam Schefter of ESPN reports.
story: Official word on McConkey's status will arrive when the Chargers post their inactive list 90 minutes prior to kickoff, but unless he experiences a setback with his cracked rib while warming up Sunday, the third-year wideout is on track to suit up. Schefter relayed earlier Sunday that McConkey will wear a flak jacket to protect his injured rib if he does wind up playing.

headline: McConkey (ribs), who is listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the Raiders, "has made rapid progress" and "has every intention of playing," Tom Pelissero of Netflix reports.
story: After sitting out practice the first two days of the week, McConkey was able to sneak in a limited session Friday. Though Pelissero relays that a final decision on McConkey's status won't be made until later Sunday, fantasy managers can expect him to avoid the Chargers' inactive list, which will be released 90 minutes prior to the game's 4:05 p.m. ET kickoff. According to Ian Rapoport of NFL Network, McConkey is working his way back from a cracked rib and has improved more steadily than anticipated since suffering the injury in last weekend's season-opening loss to the Cardinals. McConkey is expected to wear a flak jacket to offer further protection for the rib Sunday, assuming he gets the green light to play, per Adam Schefter of ESPN.

headline: McConkey (rib) is listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the Raiders, ESPN's Kris Rhim reports.
story: McConkey missed the fourth quarter of last week's game and didn't practice Wednesday or Thursday, but a return to practice Friday gives him a shot to play this Sunday. If it comes down to a game-time decision, fantasy managers should have an alternative ready from the late-afternoon games or primetime contests (the Chargers are scheduled for a 4:05 p.m. ET kickoff). Quentin Johnston and Tre' Harris will both get plenty of snaps at wide receiver if McConkey ends up on the inactive list.

headline: The Chargers signed Wease off the practice squad to the active roster Saturday.
story: The Chargers are thin at wide receiver ahead of Sunday's game against the Broncos, given that both Quentin Johnston (chest) and Brenen Thompson (quadriceps) are ruled out while Ladd McConkey (foot) is listed as questionable despite not practicing all week. If McConkey is not cleared to play, then Wease would step into the WR4 role behind Tre' Harris, Marquez Valdes-Scantling and Derius Davis. Wease joined the Chargers' practice squad in early September after failing to make the Dolphins' 53-man roster at the end of training camp in late August.

headline: Dicker went 3-for-3 on field-goal attempts and made his only PAT during Sunday's 44-22 loss to Houston.
story: Dicker was able to make multiple field-goal tries for the third straight game and fifth time this season. The kicker did all his damage in the first half, converting field goals from 52, 33 and 43 yards before the break. Dicker has now gone 15-for-17 on field-goal attempts, including 1-for-2 from 50-plus yards, over eight contests so far during the 2026 campaign.

headline: Dicker made all three of his field-goal attempts during Sunday's 24-9 loss against the Rams. He did not kick any extra-point tries.
story: The Chargers offense put forth another poor effort in Week 8, with four of their 11 drives ending in punts and another three ending with turnovers. Dicker has mostly been efficient through his first seven games of the season, making 12 of his 14 field-goal attempts, but until the offense demonstrates it can consistently move the ball down the field, he'll be hard to trust as a fantasy option.

headline: Dicker made both of his field-goal attempts in the Chargers' 22-6 loss to the Chiefs on Sunday.
story: Dicker's 23-yard and 30-yard field goals were the only points scored by the Chargers in the team's blowout loss. While the offense could not get going, as has been the theme all season, Dicker remained reliable. The 26-year-old moves to 9-for-11 on field-goal attempts and a perfect 9-for-9 on extra-point attempts over six regular-season games in 2026.

headline: Dicker made his lone field-goal attempt and both of his extra-point tries during the Chargers' 23-17 loss to the Broncos on Sunday.
story: Dicker got the Chargers on the board with a 42-yard field goal in the second quarter before adding two PATs in the second half. Dicker has attempted one field goal or zero in three of the first five games of the regular season and has yet to make a field goal from 50-plus yards. He's 7-for-9 on field-goal attempts and 9-for-9 on extra-point tries heading into a Week 6 road matchup Oct. 18 against the Chiefs, who are coming off a bye.

headline: Dicker went 3-for-3 on field-goal attempts and made both of his PATs during Sunday's 30-23 loss to Seattle.
story: Dicker made field goals from 40 and 39 yards in the first half before converting a 36-yarder late in the fourth quarter. The kicker had missed a field-goal try in each of the last two games entering Week 4, but he was able to get back on track against the Seahawks. Dicker has now gone 6-for-8 on field-goal attempts while making all seven of his extra-point tries over four contests this year.

headline: Dicker went 3-for-4 on field-goal attempts and made his lone extra-point try during the Chargers' 24-16 loss to the Bills on Sunday.
story: Dicker's made field goals came from 33, 21 and 33 yards, with his miss early in the second quarter coming from 45 yards. Dicker has missed two of his five field-goal attempts through the first three games of the regular season, well below the 90 percent success rate he enjoyed in each of the first four years of his NFL career.

headline: Dicker missed his lone field-goal attempt but made both PATs in Sunday's 26-14 loss to the Raiders.
story: The Chargers lost by the score of 26-14 for the second straight week, and both were upsets at home. The day started off on the wrong foot, as Dicker hit the right upright from 58 yards out to end Los Angeles' opening drive. Through two games, he's still looking for his first made field goal after not attempting any against Arizona in Week 1. Things won't get any easier next Sunday on the road outdoors against the Bills.

headline: Dicker converted both of his point-after tries in Sunday's 26-14 loss to the Cardinals.
story: It was a stunning loss by the Chargers after they were installed as double-digit favorites at home against Arizona. Still the most accurate kicker in NFL history with a 93.5 percent success rate on field goals, Dicker was fantasy's No. 5 overall kicker in points per game last season, as he made 38 of 41 field-goal tries and 34 of 35 PATs. The Chargers will try to right the ship next Sunday at home against the Raiders.

headline: Uiagalelei completed two of seven passes for 27 yards and a touchdown after replacing Justin Herbert (finger) in the fourth quarter of Sunday's 44-22 loss to the Texans, and head coach Jim Harbaugh said after the game that Herbert could have a fractured finger, Alex Insdorf of BoltBeat.com reports.
story: Uiagalelei was inaccurate in his first taste of regular-season NFL action but threw a 15-yard touchdown pass to Derius Davis. If Herbert isn't available to face the Ravens on MNF in Week 10 and Trey Lance (groin) isn't ready to return from injured reserve, Uiagalelei would presumably be tabbed for the first regular-season start of the latter's career.

headline: Uiagalelei (coach's decision) is inactive for Sunday's game versus Seattle, though he is listed as the team's emergency quarterback.
story: Trey Lance (groin) is available to suit up in Week 4, meaning Uiagalelei will be a healthy scratch. However, if Lance and Justin Herbert exit the contest due to injury, illness or ejection, Uiagalelei will serve as the team's emergency signal-caller.

headline: Uiagalelei (coach's decision) is inactive but will serve as the emergency third quarterback against the Bills on Sunday, Eric Smith of the Chargers' official site reports.
story: The Chargers signed Uiagalelei to the active roster Saturday to provide depth at quarterback due to the uncertainty around the status of Trey Lance (groin). Lance has been cleared to play Week 3 and will be Justin Herbert's backup. As the emergency QB3, Uiagalelei is prohibited from playing Sunday unless both Herbert and Lance were to leave the game due to injury, illness or ejection.

headline: The Chargers signed Uiagalelei from the practice squad to the active roster Saturday.
story: With backup quarterback Trey Lance (groin) still nursing a lingering injury, Uiagalelei could serve as the backup quarterback to Justin Herbert for Sunday's game against the Bills. Uiagalelei is set to suit up for his first game of the 2026 regular season, though he will likely not see any snaps unless Herbert is forced to exit the contest due to injury.

headline: Johnston caught one of four targets for a 58-yard touchdown in Sunday's 44-22 loss to the Texans.
story: Johnston's long touchdown catch cut the deficit to 38-15 in the fourth quarter. That was the final pass Justin Herbert (finger) completed before exiting the game. If Herbert can't play against the Ravens in Week 10, Johnston would likely find himself catching passes from DJ Uiagalelei. Johnston's 58 receiving yards set a new season high, surpassing his one-catch, 57-yard effort in Week 6, and Sunday's TD was his first of the season.

headline: Johnston caught all four of his targets for 37 yards in Sunday's 24-9 loss to the Rams.
story: Johnston's four grabs marked a new personal single-game high through six games this season. One of the least efficient wideouts in the league, Johnston entered Sunday with just eight grabs for 165 yards on 22 targets. He hasn't been playable in fantasy football for weeks and will square off with a stingy Houston secondary in Week 9.

headline: Johnston's role in the passing game will shrink slightly in Week 8 against the Rams given that both Ladd McConkey (concussion) and Tre' Harris (hamstring) have been cleared to play, Eric Smith of the Chargers' official site reports.
story: Both Johnston and McConkey were sidelined for Week 5, but the latter entered the league's concussion protocol during the Chargers' Week 6 loss to the Chiefs. Johnston logged 17 targets through his first three games of the regular season, although he's seen only five passes from Justin Herbert over his last two outings, which Johnston turned into two catches for 101 yards. The Chargers are averaging only 168.2 passing yards per game this season -- which ranks 28th in the NFL -- and they face a Rams defense that boasts the fourth-best pass defense in the league (186.3 passing yards allowed per game).

headline: Johnston caught one of three targets for 57 yards in Sunday's 22-6 loss to the Chiefs.
story: Johnston needed just one catch to set a season high in receiving yards, but he was tackled at the 1-yard line to keep him without a touchdown this season after consecutive eight-touchdown regular seasons. The Chargers proceeded to back up 11 yards from there and settled for a field goal. Johnston has caught a deep pass in each of the past two games, securing a 44-yard catch in the Week 5 loss to Seattle prior to the 57-yard catch against the Chiefs. The 2023 first-round pick has just eight catches through five appearances heading into LA's Week 7 bye.

headline: Johnston (chest) doesn't have an injury designation for Sunday's game against the Chiefs, Noah Furtado of The Athletic reports.
story: Ladd McConkey (foot) has also been cleared to play, while Tre' Harris (hamstring) has been ruled out. Harris seemed to be threatening Johnston for the No. 2 receiver job, but for now it'll likely be Johnston's role.

headline: Johnston (chest) was a limited participant in Thursday's practice.
story: Johnston practiced in a limited fashion for the second day in a row, which offers hope that he'll be able to put an end to a one-game absence and return to action Sunday in Kansas City. In order to avoid carrying a designation into the weekend, however, Johnston may need to upgrade to full participation during Friday's practice.

headline: Johnston (chest) was listed as a limited participant on Wednesday's injury report.
story: A chest injury kept Johnston off the field for Week 5, but he was able to get some work in Wednesday. Fellow pass catchers Ladd McConkey (foot) and Tre' Harris (hamstring) are also banged up -- the latter did not practice Wednesday -- so it remains to be seen what the Los Angeles receiver room will look like Sunday against the Chiefs.

headline: Johnston (chest) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against Denver.
story: With Johnston sidelined and Ladd McConkey (foot) listed as questionable, Tre' Harris may end up being the No. 1 wide receiver for Justin Herbert on Sunday. There was no hint earlier this week of Johnston's chest injury being serious, but he'll apparently miss at least one game.

headline: Johnston (chest) wasn't practicing during the portion of Friday's session open to the media, Noah Furtado of The Athletic reports.
story: With Johnston having been limited Wednesday and Thursday, this could be more of a rest day for the wideout. The winless Chargers appear set to head into Sunday's game against the Broncos without Ladd McConkey (foot) after he missed practice all week, so Johnston is going to be needed alongside Tre' Harris at wide receiver.

headline: Johnston (chest) was a limited participant at Thursday's practice.
story: A chest injury has resulted in back-to-back capped sessions for Johnston to kick off Week 5 prep, giving him just one more opportunity to get back to full Friday before the Chargers potentially tag him with a designation for Sunday's game against the Broncos. With Ladd McConkey (foot) not practicing Wednesday or Thursday and potentially trending toward an absence, an active Johnston likely will be the top pass catcher available to QB Justin Herbert this weekend.

headline: Johnston was limited at Wednesday's practice due to a chest injury.
story: The Chargers' receiving corps is banged up at the moment, with all of WR Ladd McConkey (foot, DNP on Wednesday), WR Brenen Thompson (quadriceps, LP) and TE Charlie Kolar (forearm, LP) dealing with health concerns, and WR KeAndre Lambert-Smith (hamstring) and TE David Njoku (fibula) on IR. Johnston has had every opportunity to produce this season, with at least a 75 percent snap share in all four games, but he so far has just nine touches for 111 yards from scrimmage and no TDs. Assuming McConkey isn't able to play Sunday versus the Broncos and Johnston suits up, the latter could be the unquestioned No. 1 pass catcher for QB Justin Herbert.

headline: Johnston caught one of two targets for 44 yards in Sunday's 30-23 loss to the Seahawks. He added one carry for minus-4 yards.
story: Despite Ladd McConkey (foot) playing just 24 of 71 offensive snaps, including zero in the second half, Johnston was a ghost most of the afternoon before hauling in a deep ball in the fourth quarter. Johnston continues to pace the team in snaps and routes at wide receiver, but he has little to show for it this season, posting just seven catches for 108 yards and no touchdowns on 19 targets. Johnston won't be a recommended fantasy play next Sunday against the Broncos, even if Patrick Surtain (ankle) and Riley Moss (ribs) are still banged up.

headline: Johnston caught three of six targets for 40 yards during Sunday's 24-16 loss to the Bills.
story: Johnston finished second on the team in targets, and his 40 receiving yards were nearly double his previous season total of 24 yards. He and the rest of the Chargers offense have yet to find their stride in 2026, making him hard to trust as a fantasy asset. The wide receiver will look to get back on track in a tough matchup in Week 4 against the Seahawks.

headline: Johnston caught one of five targets for seven yards in Sunday's 26-14 loss to the Raiders.
story: Johnston finished with a team-high five targets, but he failed to capitalize versus Las Vegas. The wide receiver has caught three of 11 targets for 24 yards over two games to open the 2026 campaign, and his next chance to get on track will come Week 3 against the Bills.

headline: Johnston caught two of his six targets for 17 yards in Sunday's 26-14 loss to the Cardinals.
story: Johnston was unable to capture more than half of his targets, failing to show up even after No. 1 wide receiver Ladd McConkey (chest) exited the game with a chest injury. Johnston also committed a costly false-start penalty in the fourth quarter, which cannot be good for the wide receiver's chemistry with quarterback Justin Herbert.

headline: Mitchell rushed seven times for 33 yards and caught three of four targets for 34 yards in Sunday's 44-22 loss to the Texans. He also lost a fumble.
story: Mitchell led LA's three-man backfield rotation with 67 scrimmage yards, while Omarion Hampton had 60 and Kimani Vidal contributed 36. Mitchell's fumble came late in the third quarter, with the Chargers already trailing 31-9 at the time. The winless Chargers are averaging a league-low 15.1 points per game heading into a Week 10 trip to Baltimore, and things could get even worse if QB Justin Herbert (finger) has to miss time after getting injured in the fourth quarter.

headline: Mitchell rushed four times for six yards and caught all three of his targets for 17 yards in Sunday's 24-9 loss to the Rams.
story: Handpicked by first-year OC Mike McDaniel as a free-agent signing in the offseason, Mitchell has been a total non-factor for much of the first half of the season. With a career 5.7 yards per carry average, Mitchell is averaging just 3.7 yards per rush this season. Involved in a three-way backfield committee with Omarion Hampton and Kimani Vidal, Mitchell is waiver-wire fodder in normal-sized 12-team fantasy leagues.

headline: Mitchell turned two carries into four yards, failed to haul in his lone target and returned four kickoffs for 87 yards during Sunday's 22-6 loss to the Chiefs.
story: Week 6 was the lowest usage Mitchell has seen this season, and his 17 snaps on offense were third most among Chargers running backs behind Omarion Hampton (34) and Kimani Vidal (25). Through six regular-season games, Mitchell has turned 35 carries into 139 yards and added 12 catches (on 15 targets) for 52 yards and a score, but it's hard to put much trust into any of the Chargers' skill-position players given the team's poor start to the season. Perhaps the Week 7 bye will help the Chargers right the ship, with their next game taking place in Week 8 against the Rams on Sunday, Nov. 1.

headline: Mitchell took six carries for 11 yards and caught three of four targets for 18 yards during Sunday's 23-17 loss versus the Broncos.
story: From scrimmage, Sunday was Mitchell's least productive game since Week 1, when he played just 17 offensive snaps. His nine touches in Week 5 tied with 2024 sixth-rounder Kimani Vidal, who managed 56 yards and a touchdown by comparison. Both were outpaced in the touches department by starter Omarion Hampton (15), though both Vidal and Mitchell should continue to be somewhat involved until Hampton is able to demonstrate some explosiveness out of the backfield.

headline: Mitchell tallied 10 carries for 39 yards and five catches (on six targets) for 24 yards during Sunday's 30-23 defeat at Seattle.
story: Mitchell surprisingly led the Chargers backfield in touches with 15, ahead of Omarion Hampton's 11 and Kimani Vidal's seven, but unlike his position mates he didn't reach the end zone. Because Mitchell's touch count has increased in each successive week this season, he's trending in a positive direction, but until one of the trio is handling most of the RB reps, it'll be difficult to trust any of them for fantasy purposes on a weekly basis. He next takes the field next Sunday against the Broncos.

headline: Mitchell (ankle) was a full participant in Friday's practice and does not have an injury designation for Sunday's game against the Seahawks, Kris Rhim of ESPN.com reports.
story: After being limited Wednesday and Thursday and wearing a walking boot earlier in the week, Mitchell's good to go against Seattle. At less than 100 percent and facing a stout defense, Mitchell is tough to get behind for fantasy lineups, even after he closed the snaps and touches gap on Omarion Hampton in last Sunday's loss to the Bills. Neither is an overly exciting Week 4 fantasy bet.

headline: Mitchell (ankle) was a limited participant in Thursday's practice.
story: For the second day in a row, Mitchell had his reps capped while he manages a left ankle injury. So long as he doesn't take a step back in activity during the Chargers' final practice of the week Friday, Mitchell should still be on track to suit up Sunday against the Seahawks. Through the team's first three games, Mitchell has carried 17 times for 85 yards (5.0 YPC) while adding four receptions for 10 yards and a touchdown in a complementary role behind lead back Omarion Hampton.

headline: Mitchell (ankle) was a limited participant at the Chargers' practice Wednesday, Kris Rhim of ESPN.com reports.
story: Mitchell was spotted with a walking boot on his left leg, and the Chargers updated their injury report to reflect the running back as limited Wednesday. He may have suffered the left ankle injury during Wednesday's session, but he didn't express much concern about the injury, and the running back will have two more chances this week to log a full practice before Sunday's matchup with the Seahawks. If Mitchell is unavailable for Week 4, Kimani Vidal would serve as the top reserve option behind starter Omarion Hampton.

headline: Mitchell rushed eight times for 52 yards and caught all three of his targets for minus-5 yards and a touchdown during Sunday's 24-16 loss to the Bills.
story: Mitchell found himself far move involved on offense in Week 3, nearly matching his previous season total of nine carries while the three targets matched a career high. The running back reached paydirt in the first quarter, reeling in a one-yard pass from quarterback Justin Herbert. Mitchell remained the team's second option out of the backfield behind starter Omarion Hampton, but he proved that he could have standalone fantasy value if he gets more consistent touches moving forward.

headline: Mitchell rushed five times for 24 yards and caught his only target for 15 yards during Sunday's 26-14 loss to the Raiders.
story: Mitchell operated as a distant No. 2 option in the backfield, logging 17 snaps on offense while starter Omarion Hampton was on the field for 43 of the team's 68 offensive snaps. Mitchell was able to make the most of his opportunities, averaging 4.8 YPC while reeling in his first catch of the season. The running back also added 47 yards on two kickoff returns in the contest. Mitchell has shown enough to be worth a stash in deeper fantasy leagues, but he will continue to have a limited ceiling as long as Hampton is active.

headline: Mitchell rushed four times for nine yards in a Week 1 loss to Arizona on Sunday. He added 47 yards on two kickoff returns.
story: Mitchell had a long rush of eight yards but combined for just three yards on his other three carries. While he also contributed in the return game, it was a bland Chargers debut for the 24-year-old, who joined Los Angeles as a free agent in March. The Chargers' run game as a whole was largely stifled Sunday, as Omarion Hampton -- the only other RB on the team to log a carry -- finished with a mediocre 43 yards on 12 carries, though he did score a touchdown. Mitchell will look to make more of an impression in Week 2 versus Las Vegas next Sunday.

headline: Hampton rushed 13 times for 60 yards and wasn't targeted in Sunday's 44-22 loss to the Texans.
story: Hampton worked as the Chargers' primary rushing option ahead of Keaton Mitchell and Kimani Vidal, who recorded seven carries apiece. The 0-8 Chargers unsurprisingly faced another negative game script, though, and Hampton wasn't involved in the passing game. The 2025 first-round pick continues to disappoint on a surprisingly awful offense that could get even worse should QB Justin Herbert (finger) miss any additional action after exiting in the fourth quarter. Hampton will try to snap a four-game touchdown drought in Week 10 against the Ravens.

headline: Hampton rushed nine times for 20 yards and brought in two of three targets for seven yards in the Chargers' 24-9 loss to the Rams on Sunday.
story: Hampton logged just one more carry than Kimani Vidal and five more than Keaton Mitchell, as the Chargers' ground game continued to resemble a committee scenario. Hampton now has 45 rushing yards or fewer in four straight games, and he's logged single-digit carries in three of those contests. The second-year back is averaging just 3.5 yards per carry behind an injury-hampered offensive line as well, leaving his outlook bleak for a Week 9 home matchup against an aggressive Texans defense next Sunday.

headline: Hampton rushed seven times for 18 yards and caught all four of his targets for 21 yards in Sunday's 22-6 loss to the Chiefs.
story: The Chargers continued to deloy an ineffective backfield rotation, as Hampton got 11 touches compared to 10 for Kimani Vidal and two for Keaton Mitchell. None of the three running backs exceeded 3.0 yards per carry while QB Justin Herbert led the team with 26 rushing yards. Hampton has been trending in the wrong direction, with his rushing yardage dropping with each subsequent game since a 94-yard performance on the ground in Week 2 against the Raiders. He'll look to reverse that trend in Week 8 against the Rams following a Week 7 bye.

headline: Hampton turned 14 carries into 33 yards and one target into a six-yard catch during Sunday's 23-17 loss to the Broncos.
story: Hampton has found room to run in the Chargers' mostly stagnant offense difficult to come by so far this season, averaging 3.7 YPC through five games after going for 4.4 as a rookie in 2025. On Sunday in particular, he had to contend with fellow RBs Kimani Vidal (nine touches) and Keaton Mitchell (six) mixing into the action a decent amount. Due to ceding those reps to his backfield mates, Hampton's weekly ceiling doesn't appear to be as high as it may have seemed heading into the campaign.

headline: Hampton had nine carries for 45 yards and one touchdown and two catches (on two targets) for eight yards during Sunday's 30-23 loss at Seattle.
story: Hampton failed to reach 10 rushes in a game for the first time in four opportunities this season, and he ceded a number of backfield reps to position mates Keaton Mitchell (15 touches for 63 yards) and Kimani Vidal (seven touches, 36 yards and one TD). It's unclear if the Chargers intend to keep up more of a timeshare between the trio moving forward, but Hampton's lack of targets (five) so far in 2026 inhibit his overall value if he isn't taking on a majority of the rushing workload. His next chance to take the field arrives next Sunday versus the Broncos.

headline: Hampton rushed 15 times for 56 yards and failed to bring in his only target in the Chargers' 24-16 loss to the Bills on Sunday.
story: The Chargers' No. 1 back got seven more carries than change-of-pace option Keaton Mitchell, but he was able to outpace the latter by only four yards. It was a disappointing downturn for Hampton, who'd broken out with 94 rushing yards and a touchdown while adding a 2-21-0 receiving line against the Raiders in Week 2. The Chargers are now alarmingly 0-3 heading into a daunting Week 4 road matchup against the Seahawks, but Hampton figures to remain in a clear-cut lead role for that contest.

headline: Hampton rushed 23 times for 94 yards and a touchdown and brought in both targets for 21 yards in the Chargers' 26-14 loss to the Raiders on Sunday. He also lost a fumble.
story: Hampton put together a perfectly useful fantasy performance in the Chargers' alarming upset loss, spearheading Los Angeles' ground attack while handling a workhorse role. Hampton added a one-yard touchdown run in the second quarter, but his lost fumble in Raiders territory with 3:52 remaining in the game and the Bolts trying to erase a three-point deficit was a back-breaker, as it led to Las Vegas' game-clinching touchdown. Hampton has a rushing touchdown in each of the first two games of the new season but has a pair of lost fumbles as well. Nevertheless, the talented back will remain in the lead role for a Week 3 road showdown against the Bills next Sunday, a critical early-season contest for Jim Harbaugh's squad.

headline: Hampton rushed 12 times for 43 yards and a touchdown and lost a fumble in the Chargers' 26-14 loss to the Cardinals on Sunday.
story: Hampton and the Chargers looked ready to roll early in the alarming loss, as the second-year back answered Arizona's opening-drive touchdown with a hard-charging eight-yard scoring run with 4:22 remaining in the first quarter. He was very quiet from that point forward, however, and his lost fumble at Arizona's 34-yard line on the following possession cost Los Angeles both a potential scoring opportunity and led to a Cardinals field goal. Hampton also was surprisingly shut out of any pass-catching opportunities, but he should have a good chance at a larger workload in a Week 2 divisional home clash against the Raiders next Sunday.

headline: Davis caught one of two targets for a 15-yard touchdown in Sunday's 44-22 loss to the Texans.
story: With Justin Herbert (finger) out of the game and the score out of hand already, Davis caught a 15-yard touchdown from backup DJ Uiagalelei in the fourth quarter. Davis has no fantasy value as a reserve wideout in one of the league's worst offenses.

headline: Davis (undisclosed) was a full participant in Wednesday's practice.
story: Davis sustained an unspecified injury during the Chargers' 26-14 loss to the Cardinals in Week 1, but his full practice participation Wednesday puts the 2023 fourth-rounder on track to play against the Raiders on Sunday. Davis returned two kickoffs for 33 yards and recorded a tackle prior to his exit against Arizona.

headline: Davis (undisclosed) is day-to-day with an injury he suffered during Sunday's 26-14 loss to the Cardinals.
story: Davis appears to have been injured on Justin Herbert's fourth-quarter interception, as he took a significant hit from safety Andrew Wingard. The wide receiver's status for Sunday's game against the Raiders will depend on his practice participation throughout Week 2 prep.

headline: Hart (ankle) is questionable to return to Sunday's game against the Texans.
story: Hart exited the third quarter of Sunday's game with an ankle injury. Rodney Shelley will play outside cornerback opposite Donte Jackson while Hart undergoes further evaluation.

headline: Waxter (ankle) has been ruled out for the remainder of Sunday's game against the Texans.
story: The special-teamer will not return to Sunday's contest after exiting in the first quarter. A number of players could step up to contribute on special teams in Waxter's absence.

headline: Waxter (ankle) is questionable to return  to Sunday's game against the Texans.
story: Waxter exited the first quarter of Sunday's contest with an ankle injury. Another wide receiver or defensive back will need to absorb the cornerback's special-teams snaps while he is absent.

headline: Eboigbe is questionable to return to Sunday's game against Houston due to an ankle injury, Noah Furtado of The Athletic reports.
story: Eboigbe was hurt in the first quarter, and his return is uncertain. Nick Barrett will likely pick up more defensive snaps for as long as Eboigbe remains sidelined.

headline: Perryman (undisclosed) was not activated ahead of Sunday's game against the Texans, per the NFL's transaction log.
story: Perryman logged a pair of limited sessions during Week 9 prep but is not quite ready to return to the Chargers' 53-man roster. The inside linebacker will continue his recovery during Week 10 prep in the hopes of making his 2026 regular-season debut soon.

headline: Perryman (undisclosed) has been deemed doubtful to suit up against Houston on Sunday.
story: Perryman has been on IR all season due to an undisclosed issue. He was designated to return to practice Wednesday, and the veteran linebacker ended up logging a trio of limited sessions. However, it appears he's not quite ready to return to game action. In order for Perryman to have any chance to play Sunday, he'll need to be activated from IR on Saturday.

headline: The Chargers designated Perryman (undisclosed) for return to practice from their injured reserve list Wednesday, Noah Furtado of The Athletic reports.
story: Perryman has spent the entire regular season up to this point on IR with an undisclosed injury, but it now looks like he's nearing a return to game action. His activity at practice during the week will be worth keeping an eye on ahead of Sunday's game versus the Texans.

headline: Head coach Jim Harbaugh said Wednesday that Perryman (undisclosed) is "close" to returning from injured reserve, Alex Insdorf of BoltBeat.com reports.
story: Harbaugh added that Perryman isn't quite ready to return to practice, and given that the veteran linebacker's 21-day practice window has yet to open, he's probably not available for Sunday's game against the Rams. Perryman landed on IR on Sept. 1 due to an undisclosed injury that he may have picked up toward the tail end of training camp.

headline: Chargers head coach Jim Harbaugh said Wednesday that Perryman (undisclosed) won't be reinstated from injured reserve ahead of Sunday's game against the Chiefs, Alex Insdorf of BoltBeat.com reports.
story: Per Ricardo Sandoval of USA Today, Harbaugh said back on Sept. 1 that he expected Perryman to spend the minimum four games on IR due to his unspecified injury, but the veteran linebacker will now be sidelined for a sixth straight game to begin the campaign. The 33-year-old appeared in 10 games for the Chargers in 2025, logging 47 tackles and three pass breakups.

headline: Njoku (fibula) wasn't activated from IR-designated to return ahead of Sunday's game against the Texans, per the NFL's official transaction log.
story: Njoku returned to practice this week but was limited all three days before being deemed doubtful for Week 9 action. The TE's next chance to play will arrive Monday, Nov. 16, when the Chargers face the Ravens.

headline: Njoku (fibula) is listed as doubtful for Sunday's game against the Texans.
story: Njoku returned to practice this week but never advanced from limited participation to full. He could have a real shot next week when the Chargers face the Ravens. In the meantime, Charlie Kolar and Oronde Gadsden will get most of the TE snaps for Los Angeles.

headline: Njoku (fibula) was limited in Thursday's practice.
story: Njoku had his 21-day practice window opener Wednesday, and he's logged back-to-back limited practice sessions to begin Week 9 work. He's been on the shelf since going down with the lower leg injury in Week 2.

headline: Chargers head coach Jim Harbaugh said Wednesday that Njoku (fibula) has been designated for return from injured reserve, Alex Insdorf of BoltBeat.com reports.
story: The transaction opens up a 21-day window wherein Njoku can be evaluated for a return to the 53-man roster. The veteran tight end has been out of action since sustaining the fibula injury Week 2, but if he's able to turn in a full practice at some point over the next three days, he could have a chance at being activated from IR ahead of Sunday's game against the Texans. Once he's back in the fold, Njoku could push Charlie Kolar and Oronde Gadsden for snaps at tight end.

headline: Coach Jim Harbaugh said Monday that the Chargers likely will open the 21-day window for Njoku (fibula) this week, Alex Insdorf of BoltBeat.com reports.
story: Njoku landed on IR after sustaining a fibula injury in Week 2, but the tight end's looming return to practice should provide a nice boost to a Chargers' TE corps that also includes Oronde Gadsden and Charlie Kolar. In his only full game with the team (Week 1 versus the Cardinals), Njoku recorded a 55 percent snap share en route to catching all five of his targets for 58 yards. If he can approach that level of production once he's back in the lineup, Njoku could resurface as a fantasy option as the season rolls along.

headline: The Chargers placed Njoku (fibula) on injured reserve Wednesday.
story: Njoku will be sidelined for at least the Chargers' next four games after sustaining a fibula injury in Sunday's 26-14 loss to the Raiders. Fellow tight end Charlie Kolar (forearm) was able to avoid placement on IR but has already been ruled out for the Chargers' Week 3 contest in Buffalo, leaving Oronde Gadsden as the top option on the depth chart heading into that game.

headline: Head coach Jim Harbaugh told reporters Monday that Njoku (fibula) and Charlie Kolar (forearm) will both go on injured reserve, Kris Rhim of ESPN.com reports.
story: Both Njoku and Kolar sustained their injuries during Sunday's 26-14 loss to the Raiders, with the former being carted off the field during the second quarter. Both tight ends will be required to miss at least the next four games, so the earliest Njoku can return is Week 8 against the Rams on Sunday, Nov. 1. For the time being, second-year pro Oronde Gadsden, who posted a 49-664-3 line on 69 targets across 15 regular-season games last year, is the only healthy tight end on the Chargers' active roster.

headline: Njoku (knee) won't return to Sunday's game against the Raiders.
story: Njoku was carted off the field in the second quarter due to a knee injury, which initially left him questionable to reenter this Week 2 contest. Now that he's ruled out, he'll end it with one catch (on three targets) for nine yards. Charlie Kolar and Oronde Gadsden will man tight end for the rest of Sunday's outing.

headline: Njoku (knee) is questionable to return to Sunday's game against the Raiders.
story: Njoku had to be carted off the field after sustaining a knee injury early in the second quarter, and the veteran tight end is in the locker room undergoing further tests to determine the severity of the injury. Second-year pro Oronde Gadsden should see an uptick in offensive snaps for as long as Njoku is out of the game.

headline: Njoku caught five passes on as many targets for 58 yards during the Chargers' 26-14 loss to the Cardinals on Sunday.
story: Njoku's 30 snaps on offense were tied with Charlie Kolar for most among Chargers tight ends, yet it was the former that was more heavily involved in the passing game, co-leading the team in catches while finishing second in both targets and yards behind wideout Ladd McConkey (ribs). Four of Njoku's five catches went for 10-plus yards, with three of those receptions resulting in first downs. Njoku's role in the Chargers' passing attack could expand for Week 2 against the Raiders this Sunday if McConkey isn't cleared to play.

headline: Shelley (ankle) has no designation for Sunday's tilt against the Texans.
story: Shelley missed each of Los Angeles' past three games while tending to an ankle injury. However, he followed two limited practices to begin this week with a full session Friday to position himself for a return Sunday. Shelley has played a rotational role in the secondary when active this season while also contributing on special teams.

headline: Shelley (ankle) is inactive for Sunday's game against the Rams.
story: Shelley will miss another contest Sunday, so his next opportunity to get back on the field will come in Week 9 against the Texans. With Donte Jackson (hamstring) ruled out, Tarheeb Still could be more involved.

headline: Shelley (hamstring) won't suit up for Sunday's game against the Chiefs.
story: Shelly didn't play in Week 5 against the Broncos. He was listed as doubtful heading into the meeting with Kansas City but will now miss his second consecutive contest. With Donte Jackson (hamstring) also sidelined, Deane Leonard is the favorite to start opposite Cam Hart at corner.

headline: Shelley (hamstring) is listed as doubtful for Sunday's game against the Chiefs.
story: It looks like Shelley will miss a second consecutive game due to a hamstring injury, which he has worked through for most of the regular season. With Donte Jackson (hamstring) already ruled out, Deane Leonard figures to start opposite Cam Hart at outside cornerback, assuming Shelley is also inactive.

headline: Shelley (hamstring) is inactive for Sunday's game versus the Broncos, Eric Smith of the team's official site reports.
story: Shelley has been dealing with the hamstring injury for at least a few weeks. After suiting up in the Chargers' first four games of the 2026 campaign, he will finally sit out in Week 5 against Denver.

headline: Shelley (hamstring) is active Week 3 against the Bills.
story: Shelley was at risk of missing his first game of the season after sitting out practice Thursday, but he returned on a limited basis Friday and ended up getting cleared to play. The undrafted free agent has primarily served on special teams to start his career, and he did pick up his first two career tackles in Week 2 against the Raiders. He'll be slotted for a similar role this week in Buffalo.

headline: Jackson (hamstring) does not have a designation for Sunday's tilt against the Texans.
story: Jackson missed each of the Chargers' past three games due to a hamstring injury, but he was able to log a full practice session Friday and is set to return to action versus Houston. Before getting hurt, he started in three of his four appearances to begin the season, so he'll likely return to that role Sunday, especially since fellow cornerback Deane Leonard (concussion) has been ruled out.

headline: Jackson (hamstring) is inactive for Sunday's game against the Rams.
story: Jackson will miss his third consecutive game Sunday, meaning his next opportunity to play will come in Week 9 versus the Texans. With Rodney Shelley (ankle) also sidelined, Tarheeb Still is projected to be more involved.

headline: Jackson (hamstring) is listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the Rams, Eric Smith of the Chargers' official site reports.
story: A hamstring injury prevented Jackson from playing in the Chargers' two games prior to the Week 7 bye. He was a limited participant in all three practices during Week 8 prep, but if he cannot play, then Rodney Shelley (hamstring) and Tarheeb Still would be candidates to start opposite Cam Hart at outside cornerback.

headline: Jackson (hamstring) was limited in Thursday's practice.
story: Jackson suffered a hamstring strain in the Week 4 meeting with Seattle. As a result, he didn't play in Week 5 versus Denver and Week 6 against Kansas City while also missing practice during that span. With the Chargers coming off a bye, it appears Jackson is trending in a favorable direction regarding his availability for Sunday's game against the Rams, though he likely has some more boxes to check before getting the green light.

headline: Jackson (hamstring) has been ruled out ahead of Sunday's game against the Chiefs.
story: Jackson will end up missing a second consecutive game due to a hamstring injury he sustained in Week 4 against the Seahawks. He hasn't been cleared to return to practice since sustaining the injury, but with the Chargers on a bye for Week 7, Jackson will have additional time to rest before Week 8 against the Rams on Sunday, Nov. 1. With Rodney Shelley (hamstring) listed as doubtful, Deane Leonard will likely start at outside cornerback in Jackson's absence.

headline: Jackson (hamstring) did not practice Thursday.
story: Jackson didn't play in Sunday's loss to the Broncos and missed his second consecutive practice Thursday. Therefore, it doesn't appear he's moving in the right direction with respect to suiting up in Week 6 versus the Chiefs, although Friday's practice should offer further insight on his status.

headline: Jackson (hamstring) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Broncos.
story: Jackson was held out of practice all week due to a hamstring injury, which he picked up during the Chargers' Week 4 loss to the Seahawks. His next chance to play is Week 6 against the Chiefs, but in his absence, Deane Leonard and Rodney Shelley are the top candidates to start at outside cornerback opposite Cam Hart.

headline: Jackson (hamstring) did not practice Wednesday, Kris Rhim of ESPN.com reports.
story: Jackson was in concussion protocol and listed as questionable ahead of the Week 4 meeting with Seattle. While he managed to get on the field, he exited the contest due to a hamstring issue and didn't return. It's possible Jackson didn't practice Wednesday as a precaution, so he'll have a few more chances to get out there. For now, the 30-year-old should at least be considered questionable for the Week 5 matchup with Denver.

headline: Jackson (hamstring) is questionable to return to Sunday's game against Seattle.
story: Jackson was listed as questionable heading into this contest due to a concussion. While he was cleared to suit up, a hamstring injury could keep him off the field for the remainder of Sunday's game.

headline: Jackson (concussion) is available for Sunday's game against Seattle.
story: Jackson was in the league's concussion protocol. However, after practicing in full Friday, he will suit up for the Week 4 meeting with the Seahawks.

headline: Jackson (concussion) is listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the Seahawks.
story: Jackson entered the league's concussion protocol during the Chargers' Week 3 loss to the Bills. He progressively increased his practice participation this past week, culminating in a full session Friday, but Jackson will need to pass an evaluation by an independent neurologist in order to be cleared to play against Seattle.

headline: Jackson (concussion) was a limited participant at the Chargers' practice Thursday.
story: Jackson suffered a concussion in the team's 24-16 loss to the Bills in Week 3, and he was considered a non-participant at Wednesday's practice. His ability to return to practice Thursday is a step in the right direction, but he still has to clear concussion protocol before he'd be eligible to play Sunday versus Seattle.

headline: Jackson (concussion) won't return to Sunday's game versus the Bills.
story: Jackson suffered a head injury and exited the game for an evaluation. Now that a concussion is confirmed, it could mean an extended absence is on the horizon. With Jackson done for the remainder of Week 3, Cam Hart and Tarheeb Still are candidates to see more action.

headline: Jackson is being evaluated for a head injury and is questionable to return.
story: Jackson has been taken to the locker room to be evaluated by medical staff after initially being looked at in the blue medical tent. Rodney Shelley is in line for more work on defense for as long as Jackson is out of the game.

headline: Landman recorded seven tackles (three solo), one pass breakup and a forced fumble in Sunday's 20-13 win over the Commanders.
story: Much like last season, when Landman set a career high with 132 tackles across 17 starts, he's racking up the tackles through eight games in 2026. The middle linebacker is up to 66 tackles (37 solo), three forced fumbles and two pass breakups on 86 percent of the defensive snaps. Interestingly, Landman's snaps have been cut some since returning from a concussion in Week 8. Over the last two weeks, he's played less than 70 percent of the defensive snaps after being over 90 percent across Weeks 1 through 6.

headline: Landman (concussion) does not carry an injury designation into Sunday's game against the Chargers, Adam Caplan of SiriusXM NFL Radio reports.
story: Landman strung together a trio of full practices, and after passing an evaluation by an independent neurologist, he has been cleared to play in Sunday's contest. The fifth-year pro has 51 tackles (27 solo), one pass defense and two forced fumbles through six regular-season games.

headline: Landman (concussion) was a full participant in Wednesday's practice, Stu Jackson of the Rams' official site reports.
story: Landman returned to practice as a full participant but has not yet officially cleared the NFL's five-step concussion protocol. With Landman returning to full practice, the announcement that he is all set to suit up for Sunday's game against the Chargers should come soon. If Landman is ready to play, Grant Stuard and Shaun Dolac should see less action in Week 8.

headline: Landman (concussion) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Raiders, Gary Klein of the Los Angeles Times reports.
story: Landman entered the league's concussion protocol following the Rams' Week 6 loss to the Cardinals, and he was unable to practice all week. His next chance to play is Week 8 against the Chiefs on Sunday, Nov. 1, though he would have to return to practice in at least a limited capacity to have a realistic shot at playing in that contest. The Rams may turn to Grant Stuard, Shaun Dolac or practice squad linebacker Eric Kendricks in Landman's absence.

headline: Landman (concussion) did not participate in Wednesday's practice, Adam Grosbard of The Orange County Register reports.
story: Landman likely sustained his concussion in the Rams' Week 6 loss to the Cardinals. The linebacker has enterted the NFL's five-step concussion protocol and will need to upgrade his practice participation with the approval of an independent neurologist before being cleared for game-day activities. If Landman cannot clear the league's protocol by Sunday's game against the Raiders, veteran linebacker Eric Kendricks could be called up to the active roster in his place.

headline: Landman recorded 10 tackles (six solo) during the Rams' 18-16 loss to the Cardinals on Sunday.
story: Landman led the Rams in total tackles Sunday, and it was his third consecutive game with double-digit stops. He's up to 51 combined tackles through six regular-season games, which leads the Rams and is 12th-most in the NFL. He's well on track to crack 100-plus tackles for a second-straight year and for the third time in his five-year NFL career.

headline: Landman (wrist/shoulder) does not carry an injury designation into Sunday's game against the Cardinals, Stu Jackson of the Rams' official site reports.
story: Landman was diagnosed with a wrist injury following the Rams' loss to the Bills in Week 5. He was also working through a shoulder issue during Week 6 prep, but his full practice Friday was enough for him to avoid an injury designation for Sunday's contest. Landman has accumulated 41 tackles (21 solo), one pass defense and two forced fumbles through five regular-season games.

headline: Landman (wrist) was listed as a limited participant on the Rams' estimated injury report Wednesday, Sarah Barshop of ESPN.com reports.
story: Landman compiled a season-high 13 total tackles (eight solo) and a pair of forced fumbles during Monday night's 37-34 overtime loss to the Bills, and he may have picked up a wrist injury during the contest. The linebacker's ability to be considered limited Wednesday is a sign that the injury may not be serious. Landman will have two more opportunities to officially practice before Sunday's contest against the Cardinals.

headline: Landman (shoulder) does not carry an injury designation into Monday night's game against the Bills, Sarah Barshop of ESPN.com reports.
story: Landman had his practice reps limited due to a shoulder issue, but he avoided an injury tag for MNF after logging a full practice Saturday. The fifth-year pro has 28 tackles (13 solo) and one pass defense through the first four games of the regular season.

headline: Landman (shoulder) was a limited participant in Friday's practice, Sarah Barshop of ESPN.com reports.
story: Landman was held out of Thursday's practice due to a shoulder injury, but he was back on the field Friday in a limited capacity. A full practice Saturday would probably be enough for him to avoid an injury tag for Monday's interconference game against the Bills.

headline: Landman (shoulder) did not participate at practice Thursday, Sarah Barshop of ESPN.com reports.
story: Landman played 57 of the Rams' 61 defensive snaps in Sunday's game at Philadelphia, so it's not clear when he hurt his shoulder. He'll probably need to return to practice Friday or Saturday to have a shot at suiting up Monday versus the Bills.

headline: Landman recorded 10 tackles (four solo) during Sunday's 24-20 win at Philadelphia.
story: The Eagles did not go away from their ground game in Week 4 despite losing running back Saquon Barkley to a hamstring injury early in the contest, and Landman saw plenty of opportunities to tackle ballcarriers as a result. He's a high-floor IDP consideration in some formats heading into a Week 5 contest versus the Bills.

headline: Landman (shoulder) does not have any injury designation ahead of Sunday's game against the Eagles.
story: Landman logged consecutive limited practices on Wednesday and Thursday before upgrading to full participation for Friday's session. The inside linebacker is all set to suit up next to Omar Speights for Sunday's NFC showdown against the Eagles. Landman worked through his shoulder issue for the Rams' Week 3 loss to the Broncos as well, playing 88 percent of the team's defensive snaps in the game.

headline: Landman (shoulder) was a limited participant at practice Wednesday, Adam Caplan of SiriusXM NFL Radio reports.
story: Landman was able to play through the shoulder injury during Sunday's game at Denver, but he's apparently still not back at full strength. Barring any setbacks, however, there's still a good chance he'll suit up in Week 4 at Philadelphia.

headline: Landman (shoulder) does not carry an injury designation ahead of Sunday's game against the Broncos, Sarah Barshop of ESPN.com reports.
story: Landman tied for a team-high seven tackles in Monday's 28-6 victory over the Giants. He was limited in practice throughout the week because of a shoulder injury, though that doesn't appear to be enough to keep him off the field in Week 3.

headline: Landman (shoulder) was a limited participant in Wednesday's estimated practice, Nate Atkins of The Athletic reports.
story: Landman logged limited sessions in the lead-up to the Rams' Week 2 win over the Giants. The linebacker was able to play through a shoulder injury in the contest, logging seven tackles (three solo) over 49 defensive snaps. Landman has started Week 3 prep in similar fashion, and it remains to be seen if he'll ultimately mirror his Week 2 regimen and suit up for Sunday night's game against the Broncos.

headline: Landman recorded seven tackles (three solo) in Monday night's win over the Giants.
story: Landman dealt with a shoulder injury during the practice week but ended up having no designation headed into the Week 2 contest. He logged 84.5 percent of the Rams' defensive snaps and now has 15 tackles (eight solo), including one TFL, one QB hit and a pass breakup through two games to begin the 2026 campaign.

headline: Landman (shoulder) does not have any injury designation ahead of Monday night's game against the Giants, Benjamin Royer of The Orange County Register reports.
story: Landman will suit up for Monday night's game despite not logging a single full practice throughout Week 2. The linebacker was likely just resting his shoulder injury in anticipation of game day and will be all set to play nearly all of the Rams' defensive snaps, as he saw 98 percent in Week 1 against the 49ers.

headline: Landman (shoulder) will be a limited participant in Saturday's practice, Stu Jackson of the Rams' official site reports.
story: Landman has been limited in every practice of Week 2. The inside linebacker appears to be able to navigate his shoulder issue, but it remains unclear whether he is capable of sustaining NFL contact with the injury. If Landman cannot suit up, Shaun Dolac will likely start at inside linebacker next to Omar Speights (hip) for Monday's game against the Giants.

headline: Landman (shoulder) was a limited participant at practice Thursday, Sarah Barshop of ESPN.com reports.
story: The expectation earlier in the week was that Landman was on track to play in Week 2 versus the Giants, and a limited practice Thursday keeps that door open. He'll have two more chances to practice in full before the Rams publish their final injury report of the week Saturday.

headline: Landman (shoulder/thumb) is expected to be ready for next Monday night's game against the Giants, Rick Stroud of the Tampa Bay Times reports.
story: Landman picked up two injuries in the Rams' Week 1 loss to the 49ers. The inside linebacker made eight tackles in the contest, making it a strong start to the veteran's fifth NFL campaign. The 27-year-old will likely start the week as a limited participant in practice, hopefully working his way up to full participation by Saturday to be cleared of any injury designation ahead of the Week 2 matchup against the Giants.

headline: Lake recorded seven tackles (three solo) and a forced fumble in Sunday's 20-13 win over the Commanders.
story: Lake was credited with a forced fumble on the final play of the game, where Washington was trying to lateral the football down the field. Byron Young made the recovery for the Rams to clinch the win. For the season, Lake has recorded 63 tackles (37 solo) and has already set career highs in pass breakups (11), interceptions (three) and forced fumbles (two). He's also on pace to set a new career high in tackles.

headline: Lake recorded seven total tackles (two solo) and two passes defensed, including an interception, during Sunday's 24-9 win over the Chargers.
story: Lake was able to secure exactly seven takedowns for the third straight week, as he has now registered six or more tackles in every game this season. The 27-year-old's biggest moment of the contest came in the first quarter, when he jumped in front of a short pass from Chargers quarterback Justin Herbert for his third interception of the year. Lake has now compiled 56 total tackles (34 solo), a forced fumble, and 11 passes defensed, three of which are interceptions, over eight games so far in the regular season.

headline: Lake finished Sunday's 35-21 win over the Raiders with seven tackles (four solo).
story: Lake ended up leading the Rams in tackles Sunday, and he's posted at least six stops in each of the first seven games of the regular season. The fifth-year defensive back is up to 49 tackles (32 solo), nine pass defenses (including two interceptions) and one forced fumble in 2026.

headline: Lake registered seven tackles (six solo) and an interception during the Rams' 18-16 loss to the Cardinals on Sunday.
story: Lake picked off Jacoby Brissett early in the first quarter on a pass intended for Trey McBride, which the Rams offense converted into a 44-yard field goal six plays later. It was Lake's second interception of the season, which is already a career high for the 2022 sixth-rounder. He's also up to eight pass defenses through six regular-season games, which is tied for second-most in the NFL behind Jacob Parrish (nine).

headline: Lake (hip) is active for Monday's game against the Bills, Nate Atkins of The Athletic reports.
story: Lake has been cleared to play through a hip injury after going through pregame warmups. The fifth-year pro has played every single defensive snap through Rams' first four games of the regular season, accumulating 29 tackles (18 solo), seven pass defenses (one interception) and one forced fumble in that span.

headline: Lake (hip) is listed as questionable for Monday's game against the Bills, Stu Jackson of the Rams' official site reports.
story: Lake earned the questionable tag after logging a limited session Saturday, but head coach Sean McVay told reporters after practice that the fifth-year safety is "trending in the right direction" for Monday night's game. Emmanuel Forbes and Josh Wallace would see more defensive snaps in the event that Lake is not cleared to play against Buffalo.

headline: Lake (hip) did not participate at practice Thursday, Sarah Barshop of ESPN.com reports.
story: Lake was on the field for all 61 of the Rams' defensive snaps in Week 4, so it's not clear when he picked up the injury. He'll likely have to get back on the practice field Friday or Saturday to put himself on pace to play Monday versus the Bills.

headline: Lake recorded seven tackles (six solo), three pass breakups and a forced fumble in Monday night's 28-6 win over the Giants.
story: With the Giants forced to pass much of the night, there were plenty of opportunities to make plays on the ball in the air for the Rams. Lake has now posted back-to-back games of three pass breakups, and he's logged 17 tackles (13 solo) with one interception.

headline: Head coach Sean McVay said Wednesday that Nacua (knee/toe) won't be placed on injured reserve right now "just because of some semantics with the roster," Greg Beacham of the Associated Press reports. "He's still going to be out for a significant period of time," McVay added.
story: In particular, the Rams already have used up three of their possible eight activations from reserve lists, and they currently have 12 players on IR. Nacua suffered PCL and MCL sprains and also a turf-toe injury on the team's final offensive snap of this past Sunday's win at Washington. Dan Graziano of ESPN.com reported Wednesday that Los Angeles is optimistic Nacua will be able to return in Week 14 or 15, which would mean three or four games out of commission, as opposed to the required four contests if he's moved to injured reserve. As a result, the roster crunch combined with Nacua's possible recovery timeline means he may not officially go on IR.

headline: The Rams are optimistic that Nacua (knee/toe) will be able to return to action Week 14 versus the 49ers or Week 15 versus the Cowboys, Dan Graziano of ESPN.com reports.
story: While the Rams have yet to officially rule Nacua out for their Week 10 game at Arizona, head coach Sean McVay acknowledged Monday that the wideout was likely to land on injured reserve. It's unclear if the Rams are still planning on deactivating Nacua, however; they placed fellow receiver Jordan Whittington (back) on IR on Tuesday, while Nacua remained a member of the 53-man roster. With a bye on tap Week 11, the Rams could be compelled to keep Nacua off IR if they believe he can play Week 14, which would mean that he misses three games rather than the four required for an IR stint. Whatever the case, the Rams will have to get by with a depleted pass-catching group in the short term, as Nacua, Whittington, Davante Adams (hamstring) and Terrance Ferguson (hamstring) are all sidelined with injuries.

headline: The Rams are expected to place Nacua (knee/toe) on injured reserve in the coming days due to injuries that will likely sideline him for at least one month, Sarah Barshop of ESPN.com reports.
story: Though head coach Sean McVay wasn't willing to commit to a timeline for Nacua's recovery when he addressed the matter Monday, the wideout looks as though he'll get the next four games off, at a minimum, while he contends with an MCL and PCL sprain in his right knee as well as turf toe. Los Angeles will likely make Nacua's move to IR official at some point prior to Sunday's game in Arizona, leaving the Rams without their top two wideouts for at least one contest since Davante Adams (hamstring) isn't projected to be activated from IR until at least Week 11. Given the lack of healthy dependable options in the receiver room, the Rams could be actively looking to acquire an established wideout prior to Tuesday's trade deadline.

headline: Rams head coach Sean McVay said Monday that Nacua (knee) is likely headed to injured reserve due to a PCL/MCL sprain in his knee as well as turf toe, Adam Grosbard of The Orange County Register reports.
story: With Davante Adams (hamstring) already on IR, Nacua's injury situation represents another huge blow to the Rams offense. Tutu Atwell, Konata Mumpfield, Jordan Whittington and CJ Daniels are the team's remaining healthy receivers, but a trade to bolster the position seems imperative ahead of Tuesday's deadline.

headline: Nacua suffered a knee injury during Sunday's 20-13 win at Washington and will undergo an MRI on Monday to determine its extent, Mike Garafolo of NFL Network reports.
story: The Rams already are without WR Davante Adams for a few more weeks after he underwent surgery on his left hamstring, and the team now may be sans Nacua if the results of Monday's testing go a certain way. L.A. doesn't believe that Nacua sustained a torn ACL, but the MRI will reveal what type of damage he incurred. Before picking up the injury on the Rams' final offensive snap, Nacua gathered in 14 of 19 targets for 150 yards and one touchdown and took two carries for 20 yards.

headline: Nacua returned to Sunday's game against the Commanders after visiting the medical tent, Stu Jackson of the Rams' official site reports.
story: Nacua was evaluated after sustaining an unspecified injury, but his absence wound up being brief. Barring another issue, he appears to be good to go for the remainder of Sunday's contest.

headline: Nacua secured 11 of 12 targets for 80 yards and a touchdown in the Rams' 24-9 win over the Chargers on Sunday.
story: Nacua unsurprisingly led the Rams across the board in receptions, receiving yards and targets and did so by a wide margin. With Davante Adams (IR, hamstring) unavailable for the last two games, Nacua has drawn 22 total targets and scored twice, with Sunday's touchdown coming on an 18-yard catch-and-run in the latter portion of the third quarter. Nacua is being used in a shorter-area role than past seasons -- he's averaging a career-low 10.1 yards per catch -- but he'll remain an elite fantasy option in a Week 9 road matchup against the Commanders next Sunday.

headline: Nacua brought in eight of 10 targets for 68 yards and a touchdown and rushed twice for 10 yards in the Rams' 35-21 win over the Raiders on Sunday.
story: Nacua led the Rams in receptions, receiving yards and targets on the afternoon, playing through his calf injury without issue while also helping make up for the absence of Davante Adams (IR, hamstring). Nacua rounded out his busy day with his second touchdown catch of the season, which came from 11 yards out with just over four minutes remaining in the second quarter. Nacua figures to be even more involved than usual while Adams is sidelined, and he'll take a 45-485-2 line into a Week 8 home matchup against the Chargers next Sunday.

headline: Nacua (calf) is active for Sunday's game at Las Vegas, Sarah Barshop of ESPN.com reports.
story: Nacua's addition to the practice report Thursday due to a calf issue was more cause for concern for a roster riddled with injuries. While Nacua didn't practice Friday and was listed as questionable for Week 7, Adam Schefter of ESPN reported Sunday morning that Rams are optimistic about Nacua's ability to play, and that now has been confirmed. Nacua could have his workload capped somewhat, but he'll be needed to power an air attack without Davante Adams (hamstring) for at least the next four contests. In his four appearances this season, Nacua has put together a 37-417-1 line on 52 targets.

headline: The Rams are optimistic that Nacua (calf), who is listed as questionable for Week 7, will play in Sunday's game at Las Vegas, Adam Schefter of ESPN reports.
story: The injury-plagued Rams endured another scare this week when Nacua made an early exit from Thursday's practice due to a calf injury. Ian Rapoport of NFL Network reported Friday that Nacua's new health concern is believed to be "more minor than anything else" and "not significant," but the wide receiver sat out the team's last Week 7 session and was listed as questionable ahead of the weekend. Nacua likely is poised for a pregame workout before L.A. makes a call on his status about 90 minutes before Sunday's 4:25 p.m. ET kickoff.

headline: Nacua (calf) won't practice Friday and will be listed as questionable for Sunday's game at Las Vegas, Sarah Barshop of ESPN.com reports.
story: Nacua made an early exit from Thursday's practice due to a calf injury and officially went down as a limited participant. Ian Rapoport of NFL Network reported Friday morning that Nacua's new health concern is "more minor than anything else" and "not significant." Nevertheless, Nacua is set for a pregame workout before the Rams make a decision on his status about 90 minutes before Sunday's 4:25 p.m. ET kickoff, per Barshop.

headline: The calf injury Nacua sustained Thursday is believed to be "more minor than anything else" and "not significant," Ian Rapoport of NFL Network reports.
story: Nacua left Thursday's practice with the calf issue, and tests performed afterward appear to have indicated that the wideout did not sustain a serious injury. The report notes that Nacua's availability for Week 7 remains uncertain, but the Rams will presumably provide an official update on both his short- and long-term status at some point Friday.

headline: Nacua suffered a calf injury during Thursday's practice and went down as a limited participant, Adam Grosbard of The Orange County Register reports.
story: Nacua already has dealt with psoas soreness (in August) and discomfort in his groin (in September), the latter of which cost him Weeks 2 and 3. With a new health concern in tow, it remains to be seen if he's in any danger of missing Sunday's contest at Las Vegas. Head coach Sean McVay likely will touch on Nacua's new health concern Friday, at which point the wide receiver may be tagged with a Week 7 game designation.

headline: Nacua hauled in six of seven targets for 80 yards during Sunday's 18-16 loss to the Cardinals
story: The modest stat line for Nacua may indicate otherwise, but it was a subpar performance aside from the 43-yard connection he made with QB Matthew Stafford just before the two-minute warning in the fourth quarter. As for his five other grabs, Nacua averaged just 7.4 YPC. It was a far cry from the 17-138-1 line on 24 targets that he put up during last Monday's overtime loss to the Bills, but he's still sitting on a healthy 37-417-1 line on 52 targets through his four appearances this season. Nacua and the 2-4 Rams will look to right the ship next Sunday at Las Vegas.

headline: Nacua brought in 17 of 24 targets for 138 yards and a touchdown and rushed twice for nine yards in the Rams' 37-34 overtime loss to the Bills on Monday night.
story: Nacua's jaw-dropping stat line included new career highs in receptions and targets, as well as a team-high figure in receiving yards.
