headline: The Vikings activated Mason (thumb) from injured reserve Saturday, and he does not carry an injury designation into Sunday's game against the Colts.
story: Mason has spent the four-game minimum on IR while recovering from a thumb injury, and the veteran running back has been given the green light to return for Week 7. He'll rejoin Aaron Jones in the backfield for Sunday's game, and the veteran duo figures to operate in a timeshare as was the case last season, per Kevin Seifert of ESPN.com.

headline: Head coach Kevin O'Connell said Friday that Mason (thumb) is listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the Colts after practicing fully all week, Alec Lewis of The Athletic reports.
story: Since he was designated to return from injured reserve Monday, Mason has been listed as full on three straight practice reports, but the Vikings will err on the side of caution, especially because they still must activate him by Saturday afternoon for the running back to have a chance to play Sunday. Assuming that comes to pass, Mason will rejoin Aaron Jones in the backfield, likely in a timeshare as they did in 2025 and in Week 1 before the former suffered a small fracture in his thumb that required surgery.

headline: Mason (thumb) practiced fully Thursday.
story: With back-to-back uncapped sessions under his belt so far this week, Mason appears to be putting himself in a position to be activated from injured reserve ahead of Sunday's contest versus the Colts. He's seeking his first game action since Week 1, when he suffered a small fracture in his thumb that required surgery. If he's able to return this weekend, Mason likely will resume a timeshare with Aaron Jones out of the Vikings backfield.

headline: Mason (thumb), who remains on injured reserve, practiced in full Wednesday.
story: The Vikings designated Mason for return from IR on Monday, and two days later he was uninhibited on the practice field. He's seeking his first game action since Week 1, after which he underwent surgery on a small fracture in his thumb. The team will need to activate Mason by Saturday afternoon in order for him to have a chance to play Sunday against the Colts, but a full practice Wednesday puts him on pace to be involved in such a transaction.

headline: Head coach Kevin O'Connell said that Mason (thumb) is expected to practice Wednesday, Alec Lewis of The Athletic reports.
story: The Vikings designated Mason to return from injured reserve Monday after he missed the team's previous four games due to a small fracture in his thumb that required surgery. His activity level Wednesday will serve as his baseline for Week 7 prep, but per Kevin Seifert of ESPN.com, the team is optimistic that Mason will do enough this week to be activated ahead of Sunday's contest against the Colts.

headline: The Vikings designated Mason (thumb) for return from injured reserve Monday.
story: Minnesota will open Mason's 21-day practice window Monday after the running back missed the team's last four games while recovering from thumb surgery. Per Kevin Seifert of ESPN.com, the Vikings have optimism that Mason will be able to play Sunday against the Colts, though his availability may hinge on how he looks from a conditioning standpoint during practices after a month-long layoff from action. Once he's fully ramped up, Mason should settle back in as the Vikings' top ball carrier on earlier downs, allowing Aaron Jones to slide back into more of a change-of-pace role.

headline: The Vikings are hopeful that Mason (thumb) will be ready to return from injured reserve for their Week 7 game versus the Colts, Jeremy Fowler of ESPN.com reports.
story: Mason has already missed the required four games after landing on injured reserve following the Vikings' season-opening win over the Packers, and he'll get additional time to recover from thumb surgery while the team is on bye Week 6. Assuming that Mason's thumb has healed as expected following the five-week absence, he'll likely be designated for return from IR and resume practicing coming out of the bye. Aaron Jones has shouldered the load out of the Minnesota backfield over the past four games, but Mason should reclaim the bulk of the snaps on early downs once he's reinstated from IR.

headline: Coach Kevin O'Connell said Wednesday that Mason has a small fracture in his thumb that underwent surgery, and the running back will be placed on injured reserve, Alec Lewis of The Athletic reports.
story: Mason emerged from the Vikings' Week 1 win against the Packers with a sore thumb, but the severity of the issue didn't become clear until O'Connell spoke to the media Wednesday. With Mason out for at least the next four games, Aaron Jones is set to lead the Vikings backfield for the foreseeable future, with Demond Claiborne, DeeJay Dallas and practice-squad member Jerome Ford all candidates for reps that don't go to Jones.

headline: Vikings head coach Kevin O'Connell said Monday that Mason is being further evaluated after experiencing thumb soreness coming out of Sunday's 39-22 win over the Packers, Alec Lewis of The Athletic reports.
story: Mason (30 of 65 offensive snaps) and Aaron Jones (29 snaps) had a near-even split of the backfield reps Week 1, with the former leading the ground attack with 59 yards and a touchdown on 15 carries while going without a target. The 27-year-old apparently hurt his thumb at some point during the contest, but the Vikings haven't yet indicated that the injury is anything more than a day-to-day concern. Mason will likely be put through more tests before the Vikings have a clearer picture of his status heading into a Week 2 matchup with the Bears.

headline: Mason rushed 15 times for 59 yards and a touchdown but wasn't targeted in Sunday's 39-22 win over the Packers.
story: Mason had three more carries than Aaron Jones, and neither of Minnesota's top two running backs recorded a catch. Jones and Mason each had a short touchdown run as the Vikings compiled 22 unanswered fourth-quarter points, with Mason's coming on a one-yard run with 4:48 to play. Mason set a career high with six rushing touchdowns during the 2025 regular season while rushing for 758 yards in his first year with the Vikings following a three-year stint in San Francisco. Jones and Mason are expected to split carries again in Week 2 at Chicago.

headline: Ingram-Dawkins exited Monday night's game against the Bills with an ankle injury and is questionable to return.
story: Levi Drake Rodriguez, Elijah Williams and Jalen Redmond will handle more of the defensive-line duties with Ingram-Dawkins sidelined.

headline: Ingram-Dawkins (oblique) was a full participant in Thursday's practice.
story: Ingram-Dawkins was limited Wednesday to begin the practice week, though after being upgraded Thursday, it seems as if he will be good to go Sunday versus Tampa Bay. The 23-year-old finished his rookie campaign in 2025 with 12 total tackles (six solo), including 1.0 sacks, and one pass defended.

headline: Coach Kevin O'Connell said Monday that Ingram-Dawkins is "day-to-day" after injuring his hip in Week 2 at Chicago, Alec Lewis of The Athletic reports.
story: Ingram-Dawkins left in the first quarter of the Vikings' victory in Week 2 after suffering a hip injury, but it seems like he avoided anything too severe. His status will be worth keeping an eye on when Minnesota releases its first official injury report of the week Wednesday.

headline: Ingram-Dawkins (hip) is questionable to return to Sunday's game against the Bears.
story: Ingram-Dawkins appeared to sustain the injury late in the first quarter, and he'll continue to be monitored by medical staff to determine whether he can return to Sunday's game. Elijah Williams (coach's decision) is inactive, so Domonique Orange figures to see a bump in rotational snaps on the defensive line in Williams' absence.

headline: The Vikings placed Claiborne (knee) on injured reserve Monday.
story: Claiborne suffered a knee injury during a recent practice. While head coach Kevin O'Connell stated he doesn't believe Claiborne will require surgery, the injury is severe enough to keep him off the field for at least four games. The 23-year-old hasn't done much from a statistical standpoint throughout the 2026 campaign, amassing just 13 yards off six carries while garnering two catches for eight yards.

headline: Claiborne (knee) has been ruled out for Monday's battle against Buffalo, Craig Peters of the Vikings' official site reports.
story: Claiborne didn't practice Friday or Saturday after suffering a knee injury in practice Wednesday. Head coach Kevin O'Connell said he doesn't think Claiborne will need surgery but added that the team is still evaluating the injury. The running back has played sparingly this season, logging 18 offensive snaps through four games and tallying 13 yards on six carries along with eight yards on two receptions.

headline: Claiborne (knee) did not participate in Friday's practice.
story: It is unclear when Claiborne sustained his knee injury, but the running back has downgraded to a DNP after being limited in Thursday's practice. The sixth-round rookie has been a healthy scratch since Jordan Mason returned from IR in Week 7 and will likely meet a similar fate in Week 9 regardless of any injury designation.

headline: Claiborne (coach's decision) is inactive for Sunday's game against the Colts.
story: Claiborne is a healthy scratch for Week 7 due to the return of Jordan Mason, who's been activated from injured reserve after completing his recovery from a thumb injury. Clairborne may have an uphill battle for active status moving forward as long as both Jones and Mason are available.

headline: Claiborne carried the ball three times for 12 yards during Minnesota's win over the Dolphins on Sunday.
story: Claiborne continued to serve a limited role behind Aaron Jones even with Jordan Mason (thumb) on injured reserve. Claiborne will look to be more involved offensively during next week's matchup versus the Saints.

headline: Claiborne caught his sole target for two yards in Sunday's 9-3 win over the Bears.
story: Claiborne is the No. 2 running back behind Aaron Jones while Jordan Mason (thumb) recovers on IR. The 22-year-old saw just two offensive snaps in Sunday's game, meaning DeeJay Dallas could have a shot at claiming the backup role from the sixth-rounder in the future.

headline: Claiborne was a healthy scratch for the Vikings' Week 1 win over the Packers, but he's in line for a larger role for at least the next four games after Jordan Mason (thumb) was placed on injured reserve, Alec Lewis of The Athletic reports.
story: Mason, Aaron Jones and DeeJay Dallas were Minnesota's three active running backs for Sunday's 39-22 win over Green Bay, with Claiborne observing the game in street clothes. Mason's injury means Jones is the clear RB1 on the roster while the former is sidelined, but Claiborne will be in the mix for backup duties, with Dallas -- who was signed to the Vikings' active roster from the practice squad Wednesday -- being the rookie sixth-rounder's main competition. The Vikings hit the road for a Week 2 NFC North tilt this Sunday against the Bears, whose defense gave up 478 total yards -- including 125 rushing yards -- to the Panthers in a 59-37 Week 1 win for Chicago.

headline: Claiborne (coach's decision) is inactive for Sunday's game against the Packers, Craig Peters of the Vikings' official site reports.
story: Claiborne, a sixth-round selection of the Vikings in the 2026 NFL Draft, will have to wait until Week 2 against the Bears on Sunday, Sept. 20, to make his regular-season debut. With Claiborne inactive for Week 1, DeeJay Dallas will serve as the Vikings' RB3 behind Aaron Jones and Jordan Mason.

headline: Jackson (quadriceps) is active for Monday's game against Buffalo, Craig Peters of the team's official site reports.
story: Jackson did not practice Thursday and Friday. While he practiced in a limited capacity Saturday, it still wasn't enough to avoid a questionable designation. However, Jackson has since been upgraded and is ready to go versus the Bills.

headline: Jackson (quadriceps) has been ruled out for the rest of Sunday's game against the Lions.
story: Jackson sustained a quadriceps injury right before halftime, and medical staff have determined that he cannot return to Sunday's game. Harrison Smith should see more work on early downs in Jackson's stead.

headline: Van Ginkel (chest) doesn't have a designation for Monday's matchup against the Bills, Craig Peters of the Vikings' official site reports.
story: Van Ginkel was limited in practice Wednesday and Thursday but was able to upgrade to full participation Saturday. He's thus clear to suit up on Monday Night Football against the Bills. That's a big deal for the Vikings in their quest to slow down Josh Allen, as Van Ginkel leads the team with 6.5 sacks through seven games.

headline: Van Ginkel (chest) was limited in Thursday's practice.
story: Van Ginkel played through the issue last week against the Lions and piled up 2.5 sacks in the loss. The veteran edge rusher has 21 tackles (11 solo), including 6.5 sacks, one interception, one forced fumble and a fumble recovery across seven games this season.

headline: Van Ginkel logged four tackles, including 2.5 sacks, in Sunday's loss to the Lions.
story: The Vikings lost their first game of the campaign, but their defense continued to be ferocious. That was largely due to Van Ginkel, who brought down Jared Goff three times -- two solo and one assisted -- in the first half. That pushed the veteran pass rusher up to 6.5 sacks on the season, tied for fifth-most in the NFL.

headline: Van Ginkel (chest) does not have any injury designation ahead of Sunday's game against the Bears, Craig Peters of the Vikings' official site reports.
story: Van Ginkel was a limited participant in the Vikings' Wednesday and Thursday practices before returning to full participation Friday. The linebacker has recovered from his chest issue enough to be cleared and is all set to suit up for Sunday's divisional contest against the Bears. Van Ginkel logged 1.5 sacks in last Sunday's divisional win over the Packers, putting the 31-year-old on pace to best his single-season record of 11.5 sacks set in the 2024 regular season.

headline: Van Ginkel (chest) was a limited participant in Wednesday's practice.
story: The Vikings' starting weakside linebacker logged 1.5 sacks over 55 defensive snaps in last Sunday's 39-22 win over the Packers. While Van Ginkel had a strong showing, the linebacker likely suffered his chest injury during the game. The 31-year-old will need to upgrade to full practice participation by Friday to avoid an injury designation ahead of next Sunday's game against the Bears.

headline: Gonzalez logged 10 tackles (nine solo) and one pass defense during the Patriots' 45-27 loss to the Packers in Week 9.
story: Gonzalez's 10 stops were a season high, but the larger concern was his poor performance in coverage. Per Pro Football Focus, Gonzalez on coverage for 11 catches for 192 yards and two touchdowns, and quarterback Jordan Love had a 158.3 passing rating while targeting the fourth-year defensive back. It wasn't the performance that the Patriots were expecting after signing Gonzalez to a lucrative four-year, $135 million contract extension in September. Things won't get easier for him nor the Patriots' secondary, as they travel to Munich for Week 10 against the Lions, whose offense ranks fourth in the NFL in yards per game (379.8).

headline: Gonzalez (illness) is listed as active for Thursday night's game against the Bears.
story: Gonzalez was a late addition to the Patriots' injury report ahead of Thursday's kickoff, but he subsequently participated in warmups and is in line to be able to play through his illness after all. In four games thus far, the star cornerback, who anchors New England's secondary, has recorded 14 tackles and five passes defended.

headline: Gonzalez is now listed as questionable for Thursday night's game against the Bears due to an illness.
story: Per Andrew Callahan of the Boston Herald, Gonzalez is a late addition to the injury report, though he was spotted on the field prior to the contest going through light drills. In any case, the star cornerback's Week 7 availability will be confirmed one way or another when the Patriots' inactives are posted ahead of the team's 8:15 ET kickoff.

headline: Gonzalez (shoulder) was a full participant in Thursday's practice.
story: Gonzalez missed the Patriots' last two games. He practiced in a limited capacity Wednesday. However, after being upgraded to a full participant Thursday, Gonzalez has the green light to suit up for the AFC East clash with the Jets on Sunday.

headline: Gonzalez (shoulder) was a limited participant in Wednesday's practice.
story: Gonzalez had not practiced since sustaining a shoulder injury in the Patriots' Week 3 loss to the Jaguars. The cornerback's upgrade to limited participation is a huge step forward, and the star could be back as soon as Week 6 against the Jets.

headline: Gonzalez (shoulder) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against Las Vegas.
story: Gonzalez will be held out for a second straight week due to a shoulder injury, which prevented him from practicing during Week 5 prep. Carlton Davis (neck), Karon Prunty (hamstring) and Channing Canada (hamstring) have also been ruled out, so the Patriots may have to start Charles Woods (shouler) and Marcus Jones at outside cornerback against the Raiders on Sunday.

headline: Gonzalez (shoulder) did not participate at the Patriots' practice Thursday.
story: Gonzalez missed his fifth straight practice as he continues to work his way back from a shoulder injury that he suffered Week 3 against Jacksonville. The cornerback seems likely to miss a second straight contest in Week 5, setting up Charles Woods (shoulder) and Karon Prunty (hamstring) to potentially operate in more substantial roles again Sunday versus Las Vegas.

headline: Gonzalez (shoulder) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Bills, Mike Reiss of ESPN.com reports.
story: Gonzalez was absent from his third straight day of practice Friday due to a shoulder injury likely suffered in the Patriots' loss to the Jaguars in Week 3. With the starting cornerback out, Charles Woods and fifth-round rookie Karon Prunty will likely get more reps.

headline: Gonzalez (shoulder) did not practice Wednesday.
story: Gonzalez likely picked up the injury during the Patriots' 35-6 loss to the Jaguars in Week 3, when he recorded two solo tackles and a pass defense while failing to play every single defensive snap for the first time this season. He'll have two more chances to return to practice this week, but if he cannot play against the Bills this Sunday, then Charles Woods figures to be the top candidate to start at outside cornerback opposite Carlton Davis.

headline: Woods (hamstring) was a limited practice participant Wednesday.
story: Woods was unable to play against the Packers in Week 9 due to a hamstring injury. He's opened Week 10 prep with a limited practice, and if he's cleared to play Sunday against the Lions in Munich, then he would be a candidate for more work in the secondary due to the absence of Carlton Davis (knee).

headline: Woods (hamstring) is listed as questionable ahead of Sunday's game against the Packers.
story: Woods suffered a hamstring injury during pregame warmups and has been downgraded to questionable ahead of Sunday's contest. There is a good chance the cornerback will be sidelined for the game due to the new injury.

headline: Woods (shoulder) does not have an injury designation for Sunday's game against the Jets.
story: Woods aggravated a shoulder injury in Week 5 against the Raiders, but he's been cleared to play Sunday after logging a full practice Friday. He has 22 tackles (16 solo) and three pass defenses through the first five games of the regular season.

headline: Woods (shoulder) was a limited participant in Wednesday's practice.
story: Woods exited the Patriots' Week 5 win over the Raiders early with a shoulder injury and did not return. The cornerback likely aggravated a pre-existing issue in the contest but was still able to suit up for practice Wednesday. Woods played through the injury to start the Week 5 contest and will likely do the same for Week 6 against the Jets unless Carlton Davis (neck) and Christian Gonzalez (shoulder) are healthy enough to reclaim their starting spots at outside cornerback.

headline: Woods (shoulder) is questionable to return to Sunday's game against the Raiders.
story: Woods overcame a shoulder injury to play in Sunday's contest. The cornerback may have aggravated the injury during the course of the game, making it uncertain how significant the injury remains. Fourth-string defensive back Elliott Davison is set to operate opposite third-string option Kindle Vildor at outside cornerback due to the injuries to the Patriots' secondary.

headline: Woods (shoulder) is active Week 5 against the Raiders.
story: Woods suiting up was essentially a necessity for New England, who has four cornerbacks listed on the inactive list Sunday. The third-year defensive back -- who has 18 combined tackles through the first four weeks -- should be in line for a heavy snap count.

headline: Woods (shoulder) is listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the Raiders.
story: The Patriots' secondary is already without starting outside corners Christian Gonzalez (shoulder) and Carlton Davis (neck), so having Woods available for Sunday's game would be a big help for New England. Woods has 18 tackles (14 solo) and one pass defense through four regular-season games.

headline: Woods (shoulder) exited Sunday's 29-26 win over the Bills. He finished with two tackles (one solo).
story: Ethan Hurwitz of Patriots on SI reported Woods suffered a stinger, though the 24-year-old stated, "he's feeling great." However, despite the positive update, he could carry an injury designation heading into the Week 5 meeting with the Raiders. Woods had 16 total tackles (13 solo) and one pass defended in the first three games of the 2026 campaign.

headline: Woods logged 10 tackles (eight solo) and defensed one pass in Sunday's 20-3 win over the Steelers.
story: Woods played 86 percent of the Patriots' defensive snaps in Sunday's contest. The cornerback started in place of Carlton Davis (neck), and he'll likely do so again in Week 3 against the Jaguars if the latter remains absent.

headline: Brown (knee) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Lions in Munich, Evan Lazar of the Patriots' official site reports.
story: Brown tweaked his knee against the Packers in Week 9, and the injury is severe enough for him to not travel with the team to Munich. In his absence, Walter Rouse is expected to serve as the Patriots' starter at left guard. Since the Patriots are on a bye for Week 11, Brown's next chance to suit up is Week 12 against the Chargers on Sunday, Nov. 29.

headline: Coach Mike Vrabel said Monday that Brown (knee) likely won't play in Sunday's game versus the Lions, Evan Lazar of the Patriots' official site reports.
story: Brown injured his knee during the first half of New England's loss versus the Packers in Week 9, and it appears he's trending towards being sidelined in Week 10. Should that be the case, 2024 sixth-rounder Walter Rouse projects to start at left guard Sunday.

headline: Brown (knee) has been ruled out for the rest of Sunday's contest against the Packers.
story: Brown sustained a knee injury in the first half, and he will not return to the contest. If he is forced to miss any action moving forward, Walter Rouse is a top candidate to start in Brown's place at offensive guard.

headline: Brown (knee) is questionable to return to Sunday's contest against the Packers, Mark Daniels of MassLive.com reports.
story: Brown suffered a knee injury late in the first half, and his availability for the rest of the game is now up in the air. In his absence, Walter Rouse has taken over at left guard versus Green Bay.

headline: Brown (knee) does not have an injury designation for Sunday's game against the Dolphins, David Furones of the South Florida Sun Sentinel reports.
story: Brown was unable play against the Bears in Week 7 due to a knee injury. He's faded an injury tag for Sunday's game after logging a full practice Friday, and he should reclaim his starting spot at right guard.

headline: Brown (knee) has been ruled out for Thursday's game against the Bears.
story: Brown injured his knee during the fourth quarter of Sunday's 26-19 win over the Jets. He was held out of all three practices during Week 7 prep, and with both Brown and Alijah Vera-Tucker (hamstring) sidelined Thursday, the Patriots will likely turn to Matt Pryor and Walter Rouse to serve as the starting guards against Chicago. Brown will aim to recover enough to return for Week 8 against Miami on Sunday, Nov. 1.

headline: Coach Mike Vrabel said Tuesday that Brown (knee) probably won't be available for Thursday's game against the Bears, Mike Reiss of ESPN.com reports.
story: Vrabel stopped short of ruling out Brown completely, but it seems like it will be an uphill battle for him to try to be ready to play in Week 7. With regular starting left guard Alijah Vera-Tucker (hamstring) also trending in the wrong direction ahead of Thursday's contest, 2024 sixth-rounder Walter Rouse and veteran Matt Pryor might both be called on to start against a defense that has flashed at times so far this year.

headline: Brown (knee) won't return to Sunday's game against the Jets.
story: Brown suffered a knee injury in the fourth quarter and has since been downgraded to out. Walter Rouse entered the contest and will presumably fill the void for the remainder of the game.

headline: Brown (knee) is active for Sunday's game against the Steelers.
story: Brown did not play in the Patriots' Week 1 loss to the Seahawks due to a knee injury. He was limited in practice in all three sessions during Week 2 prep to draw the questionable tag, but the Ole Miss product has been given the green light to play Sunday.

headline: Campbell (knee) was a full participant in Wednesday's practice.
story: Campbell suffered a knee injury against the Packers in Week 9, but he was cleared to practice in full Wednesday. Given his full practice reps, Campbell should start at left tackle Sunday against the Lions in Munich.

headline: Campbell (knee) is questionable to return to Sunday's contest against the Packers.
story: Campbell suffered a knee injury in the second half, and he seems unlikely to be able to return before the conclusion of the team's Week 9 contest. In his absence, Caleb Lomu has taken over at left tackle versus Green Bay.

headline: Campbell (knee) is active for Sunday's game against the Jets.
story: Campbell sprained his right MCL in the Patriots' Week 5 win over the Raiders. The offensive tackle logged three limited practices during Week 6 prep and will attempt to play through the injury in Sunday's game.

headline: Campbell (knee), who is listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the Jets, is expected to play, Ian Rapoport of NFL Network reports.
story: After being diagnosed with an MCL sprain in his right knee following this past Sunday's win over the Raiders, Campbell appeared to be in danger of missing multiple games. Improbably, he was able to practice on a limited basis throughout the week and now appears likely to try and play through the injury Week 6. Campbell's status will be confirmed when the Patriots release their inactive list 90 minutes prior to the game's 1 p.m. ET kickoff.

headline: Campbell (knee) is questionable for Sunday's game against the Jets.
story: Campbell was limited in practice all week by an MCL sprain in his right knee, which he sustained against the Raiders in Week 5. If he cannot play Sunday, then Caleb Lomu would likely start at left tackle.

headline: Campbell (knee) was a limited participant at practice Thursday.
story: Campbell sustained a sprained right knee in Week 5 versus the Raiders, and his availability for Week 6 is in serious doubt. Unless he's able to upgrade to a full practice Friday, he'll probably end up carrying an injury designation into the weekend.

headline: Campbell is expected to miss game action after spraining his right knee during Sunday's game versus the Raiders, Cameron Wolfe of NFL Network reports.
story: Per Wolfe, the injury isn't believed to be as bad as the MCL tear Campbell sustained back in November of last year, and he hasn't been placed on the Patriots' injured reserve list as of Tuesday. Until he's back in football shape, rookie first-rounder Caleb Lomu projects to step in at left tackle.

headline: Campbell is believed to have suffered a sprained knee during Sunday's 45-17 win over Las Vegas, Ian Rapoport of NFL Network reports.
story: Campbell sustained the injury in the first half and will undergo an MRI on Monday to confirm the diagnosis. The 22-year-old will likely miss action moving forward, and, in his absence, Caleb Lomu is a top candidate to fill in as the team's starting left tackle.

headline: Campbell (knee) has been ruled out for the remainder of Sunday's game against the Raiders.
story: Campbell exited the first half of Sunday's contest with a knee injury. Caleb Lomu will finish the game at left tackle as Campbell looks to recover from what could be a significant knee injury.

headline: Campbell (knee) is questionable to return to Sunday's game against the Raiders.
story: The Patriots' training staff is evaluating the extent of Campbell's knee injury, and it remains unclear how severe it is. Rookie offensive lineman Caleb Lomu has replaced Campbell at left tackle.

headline: Davis (knee) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Lions in Munich, Evan Lazar of the Patriots' official site reports.
story: Davis suffered a knee injury during the Patriots' loss to the Packers this past Sunday. New England already ruled out the veteran defensive back for Week 10, so Charles Woods (hamstring), Channing Canada and Karon Prunty figure to be the top candidates to start opposite Christian Gonzalez at outside cornerback. The Patriots are on a bye for Week 11, so Davis will have more time to recover for Week 12 against the Chargers on Sunday, Nov. 29.

headline: Davis (knee) is questionable to return to New England's matchup Sunday versus the Packers.
story: Davis is in danger of missing the remainder of the game after suffering a knee injury in the second half. Channing Canada and Karon Prunty could be in line for an uptick in playing time if Davis is unable to return to the matchup.

headline: Davis (neck) is active against the Dolphins on Sunday.
story: Davis has been cleared to return form a three-game absence due to a neck injury he picked up in Week 4 against the Bills. He'll resume his starting role at outside cornerback opposite Christian Gonzalez while Charles Woods provides depth at the position.

headline: Davis (neck) is questionable for Sunday's Week 8 contest in Miami.
story: Davis hasn't played since Week 4 because of a neck injury. It's promising that he logged a trio of full practices this week, but New England isn't yet committing to him returning to action against the Dolphins. Should Davis end up missing the matchup, Charles Woods would likely draw another start.

headline: Davis (neck) was a full participant in Wednesday's practice.
story: Davis has finally returned to full participation after missing three consecutive games with a neck injury. The starting cornerback should be able to avoid any injury designation ahead of Sunday's game against the Dolphins as long as he maintains full participation through Friday's practice session.

headline: Davis (neck) has been ruled out ahead of Thursday night's game against the Bears.
story: Davis did not participate in Monday's practice but ended the Patriots' short Week 7 prep with back-to-back limited sessions. Despite the upgrade in practice participation, the cornerback is not quite ready to return to the field and will miss his third consecutive game with a neck injury. Charles Woods should once again start opposite Christian Gonzalez at outside cornerback.

headline: Davis (neck) was a limited participant in Tuesday's practice.
story: Davis has missed the Patriots' last two games due to a neck injury, but it was a promising sign to see him on the field for Tuesday's practice, even in a limited capacity. The Patriots will announce injury designations following Wednesday's practice, at which point Davis' status for Thursday's game against the Bears will be clearer. If he's not cleared to return, then Charles Woods likely will remain the Patriots' second starting outside cornerback opposite Christian Gonzalez.

headline: Davis (neck) did not participate in Monday's estimated practice.
story: Davis has not practiced since sustaining his neck injury, and that remained the case to start Week 7 prep. If the cornerback cannot get on the practice field by Wednesday's session, he'll have almost no chance of suiting up for the Patriots' Thursday night game against the Bears.

headline: Davis (neck) has been ruled out ahead of Sunday's game against the Jets.
story: Davis has not practiced since aggravating a neck injury in the Patriots' Week 4 win over the Bills. The cornerback remains without a set return timeline, and it is unclear how much longer he will be unable to practice.

headline: Davis (neck) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Raiders.
story: Davis was held out of practice all week due to a neck injury, slimming down a Patriots secondary that will also be without Christian Gonzalez (shoulder), Channing Canada (hamstring) and rookie Karon Prunty (hamstring), with Charles Woods (shoulder) and Craig Woodson (shoulder) listed as questionable. Woods would presumably be one of the starting outside cornerbacks if cleared to play Sunday, but with Davis and Gonzalez both sidelined, the Patriots may have to turn to Marcus Jones, Mike Brown, Jaylen Reed or another defensive back from the practice squad to fill in the second starting spot. Davis' next opportunity to play is Week 6 against the Jets on Sunday, Oct. 18.

headline: Davis (neck) did not participate at the Patriots' practice Thursday.
story: Davis has missed back-to-back practices to open the week with a neck injury that he may have suffered in Week 4 versus Buffalo. The cornerback will have one more chance to return to practice Friday before Sunday's matchup with the Raiders.

headline: Davis (neck) was a full participant at practice Wednesday.
story: Davis was unavailable for the team's Week 2 win over the Steelers as a result of a neck injury, but he now appears to be healthy ahead of Sunday's contest against the Jaguars. The 29-year-old will slot in as a starting cornerback versus Jacksonville.

headline: Davis (neck) has been ruled out ahead of Sunday's game against the Steelers.
story: Davis was listed as questionable after Friday's practice. The cornerback was unable to practice at all in Week 2, making it unsurprising that he will be incapable of suiting up for Sunday's contest. Mike Reiss of ESPN.com reports that Charles Woods is likely the next man up at outside cornerback.

headline: Davis (neck) is questionable for Sunday's game versus the Steelers, Evan Lazar of the Patriots' official site reports.
story: Davis played on all but one of the Patriots' defensive snaps in the 13-10 loss to the Seahawks in Week 1. However, he hasn't practiced all week due to a neck injury, casting doubt about his availability against Pittsburgh. If Davis can't suit up in Week 2, Charles Woods, Karon Prunty and Channing Canada could each see more action.

headline: Davis (neck) did not participate in Wednesday's practice.
story: Davis missed just one defensive snap of the Patriots' 13-10 loss to the Seahawks last Wednesday, playing the other 49 and logging three tackles (two solo). The cornerback is dealing with a neck injury, and if he cannot upgrade to at least limited practice participation by Thursday, he will likely miss next Sunday's game against the Steelers.

headline: Byard (chest) was a limited participant in Wednesday's practice.
story: Byard was working through a chest injury in October, but it's unclear whether he's dealing with the same issue for the start of Week 10 prep. The veteran safety will have two more chances to increase his practice participation before the Patriots travel to Munich to face the Lions on Sunday. Byard has 43 tackles (23 solo) and three pass defenses (including one interception) through the first nine games of the regular season.

headline: Byard (chest) is officially active for Thursday's game at Chicago.
story: Byard dealt with a minor chest issue during the week that stuck him with a 'questionable' tag Wednesday, but as expected, he'll be available for Week 7. He figures to play a near-every down role against a run-heavy Chicago offense.

headline: Byard (chest) is listed as questionable for Thursday night's game against the Bears.
story: Byard logged three consecutive full practices during Week 7 prep while dealing with a chest injury. The safety will almost certainly suit up for Thursday's contest and play through what appears to be a minor issue.

headline: Moses (foot) is officially active for Thursday's game at Chicago.
story: Moses was forced out of the Patriots' contest in Week 6 versus the Jets due to a foot injury after just nine snaps, and he was seen wearing a walking boot after that game. Now, despite a short turnaround and having been limited at practice all week, he's in line to play Thursday. He should start at right tackle in Week 7.

headline: Moses (foot) is questionable to play Thursday versus the Bears.
story: Moses has remained limited all week as he nurses a foot injury that he suffered in Week 6 against the Jets, and his status for Week 7 is uncertain as a result. If he is ultimately unable to go, Caleb Lomu would stand to draw the start at right tackle against Chicago on Thursday Night Football.

headline: Moses (ankle) was a limited participant at the Patriots' practice Tuesday.
story: Moses sustained an ankle injury during the team's Week 6 win against the Jets and has now opened the week with back-to-back limited sessions. The offensive lineman will have one more chance to log a full practice before the team travels to face the Bears on Thursday Night Football.

headline: Moses (ankle) was spotted wearing a walking boot after Sunday's 26-19 win over the Jets, Andrew Callahan of the Boston Herald reports.
story: After suffering an ankle injury in Sunday's meeting with the Jets, Moses didn't return. With the short turnaround for the Patriots ahead of Thursday's game against the Bears, the 35-year-old may not have time to recover and play. For now, Moses should at least be considered questionable, but if he can't suit up, Caleb Lomu may operate in his place.

headline: Moses (ankle) has been ruled out for the remainder of Sunday's game against the Jets.
story: Moses suffered an ankle injury in the first half of Sunday's game. Caleb Lomu will likely maintain his spot at right tackle for the remainder of the contest.

headline: Moses (ankle) is questionable to return to Sunday's game versus the Jets.
story: Moses suffered an ankle injury in the first half of the divisional clash against New York. With Moses uncertain to return in Week 6, Caleb Lomu may be on the field more than projected the rest of the way.

headline: Henderson (illness) didn't practice Wednesday and is listed as out for Sunday's game against the Lions in Munich.
story: Henderson was one of three players listed as out for this weekend's contest, signaling that they are not in line to make the trip to Germany. With Rhamondre Stevenson (knee) not practicing Wednesday and reportedly on track to miss some time, it looks like Corey Kiner is trending toward leading New England's Week 10 backfield, with Lan Larison also in the mix and Terrell Jennings a potential practice-squad elevation. New England has a bye in Week 11, so Nov. 29 against the Chargers is Henderson's soonest possible return date.

headline: Henderson (illness) was absent from Wednesday's practice, Evan Lazar of the Patriots' official site reports.
story: With Henderson and Rhamondre Stevenson (knee) both absent, Corey Kiner and Lan Larison are left as New England's top running backs ahead of a Week 10 matchup in Munich against the Lions on Sunday. After that, the Patriots have a Week 11 bye, and it's still unclear when Henderson might be available again.

headline: Henderson (illness) won't play Sunday against the Packers, Evan Lazar of the Patriots' official site reports.
story: Per Mark Daniels of MassLive.com, Mike Vrabel said that the Patriots won't put a timeline on Henderson's return, while adding, per Lazar, that the team is "just trying to make sure that TreVeyon is cared for and his recovery plan is intact and he's comfortable with it." In the absence of Henderson -- who recently experienced "an unexpected and unusual medical emergency involving a series of unexplained neurological symptoms" -- Rhamondre Stevenson will pace New England's backfield, with Corey Kiner and Lan Larison also mixing in.

headline: In a statement posted to social media Friday, Henderson -- who hasn't practiced since last Wednesday -- noted that he recently experienced "an unexpected and unusual medical emergency involving a series of unexplained neurological symptoms," Mike Reiss of ESPN.com reports.
story: Henderson was unavailable for New England's Week 8 win over Miami due to an undisclosed illness, and he's now indicated that tests have "come back positive and reassuring," adding "I will continue working closely with specialists and physical therapists to focus on my recovery, as these symptoms have affected my strength, coordination, and some of my physical functions." The running back noted that for now he is "committed to doing everything necessary to return to full health" and that his "health and long-term well-being" are his foremost priorities. In six games this season while working in a Patriots backfield that also includes Rhamondre Stevenson, Corey Kiner and Lan Larison, Henderson has carried 52 times for 203 yards a touchdown, while adding five receptions for 45 yards.

headline: Henderson (illness) was listed as a non-participant in Thursday's practice, ESPN's Rob Demovsky reports.
story: Henderson officially goes down as a non-participant for a second consecutive Week 9 practice and has now missed a full week due to this illness. His participation level will be worth monitoring Friday, though it looks likely at this point that Henderson will carry an injury designation into Sunday's game against the Packers. Corey Kiner would be in line to maintain an expanded role alongside Rhamondre Stevenson if Henderson sits again Sunday.

headline: Henderson (illness) was not seen at Thursday's practice, Evan Lazar of the Patriots' official site reports.
story: Henderson hasn't practiced since last Wednesday as he deals with an illness. Unless he returns to drills Thursday and/or Friday this week, he may be in danger of missing a second game in a row Sunday against the Packers. Thursday's injury report will reveal Henderson's activity level.

headline: Patriots head coach Mike Vrabel said that Henderson (illness) won't practice Wednesday, Doug Kyed of the Boston Herald reports.
story: Henderson also didn't practice this past Thursday and Friday, and then missed the Patriots' Week 8 win over the Dolphins. The running back's absence to begin Week 9 prep suggests that he's no lock to play Sunday against the Packers, but Henderson's outlook on that front would no doubt improve with a return to the field within the next couple of days. While Henderson was sidelined in Miami, Rhamondre Stevenson paced New England's rushing attack, and Corey Kiner and Lan Larison mixed in behind him.

headline: Henderson (illness) has been downgraded from questionable to out for Sunday's game against the Dolphins, Ian Rapoport of ESPN and NFL Network reports.
story: Henderson was given the questionable tag for Week 8 despite missing the last two practices due to an illness. He won't travel with the team to Miami, so the Patriots' backfield will be led by Rhamondre Stevenson while Corey Kiner provides depth. Henderson's next opportunity to suit up is Week 9 against the Packers on Sunday, Nov. 8.

headline: Henderson (illness) is questionable for Sunday's game against the Dolphins.
story: Henderson logged DNPs on Thursday and Friday and appears to be in danger of missing Sunday's juicy matchup with Miami. His role has been shrinking of late anyway, and if Henderson misses this week's game, Rhamondre Stevenson and Corey Kiner will handle the backfield work for New England.

headline: Henderson (illness) isn't practicing Friday, Mike Reiss of ESPN.com reports.
story: After missing back-to-back practices, Henderson has two days to get healthy before the Patriots face the Dolphins on Sunday at 1:00 p.m. ET. An absence would improve the workload projections for Rhamondre Stevenson and Corey Kiner in a favorable matchup, though Henderson got just five touches in a 30-24 loss to the Bears last week.

headline: Henderson (illness) did not practice Thursday, David Furones of the South Florida Sun Sentinel reports.
story: Henderson will try to shed his illness and return to practice Friday. If he's unable to practice without limitations Friday, the 2025 second-round pick would likely take an injury designation into Sunday's game against the Dolphins. Henderson has struggled to earn playing time in recent weeks, splitting change-of-pace work behind Rhamondre Stevenson with Corey Kiner.

headline: Henderson (undisclosed) wasn't on the field for Thursday's practice, Doug Kyed of the Boston Herald reports.
story: Though the Patriots left him off their initial Week 8 injury report released Wednesday, Henderson may be dealing with an aggravation of the ankle he previously sprained in a Week 5 win over the Raiders. Since then, Henderson has been able to suit up in both of the team's last two contests, but he's played limited snaps behind starter Rhamondre Stevenson. In an effort to get the ball in Henderson's hands more frequently, head coach Mike Vrabel told Kyed on Tuesday that the second-year back could get more involved on kickoff returns, though that plan could be put on hold if Henderson is nursing an injury.

headline: Henderson rushed three times for nine yards and secured both targets for 14 yards in the Patriots' 30-24 loss to the Bears on Thursday.
story: Henderson's modest numbers underscore how modest a role he filled in the high-scoring loss. Rhamondre Stevenson had just six carries in his own right, but he also recorded a team-high 93 receiving yards on five catches. Henderson's rush attempts and rushing yards were both season lows, and the second-year back will look to bounce back in a Week 8 road matchup against the Dolphins on Sunday, Nov. 1.

headline: Henderson (ankle) rushed seven times for 31 yards and brought in his only target for nine yards in the Patriots' 26-19 win over the Jets on Sunday. He also lost a fumble.
story: Henderson beat the odds by suiting up for Sunday's contest despite what has been reported to be a high-ankle sprain. He was just five yards short of backfield mate Rhamondre Stevenson's rushing total despite seeing half the carries, but Henderson's mid-third-quarter fumble did lead to a Jets field goal. Henderson now has a quick turnaround for a Week 7 road matchup against the Bears on Thursday night, so it appears likely he slots into a complementary role again for that contest.

headline: Henderson (ankle) is active for Sunday's game against the Jets.
story: Henderson emerged from a Week 5 win versus the Raiders with an apparent right high-ankle sprain, which typically requires a multi-week recovery. For this particular injury, though, he was able to log three consecutive limited practices this week, receive a questionable designation and then tell Doug Kyed of the Boston Herald on Friday that he's "hoping to play." Ian Rapoport of NFL Network then reported Sunday morning that Henderson was likely to suit up, which now has been confirmed. Even though he's active, the Patriots could lean more on Rhamondre Stevenson and Corey Kiner as the healthier options out of the backfield, but Henderson nonetheless has averaged 11 touches per game in his four appearances this season.

headline: Henderson (ankle), who is listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the Jets, is likely to suit up, Ian Rapoport of NFL Network reports.
story: Henderson has gone from likely to miss multiple games to having a chance to play just one week removed from suffering an apparent right high-ankle sprain last Sunday against the Raiders. Via the running back himself Friday, he is "hoping to play" in Week 6, per Doug Kyed of the Boston Herald, but Henderson likely will be subject to a pregame workout Sunday before a decision is made ahead of the Patriots dropping their inactive list at 11:30 a.m. ET. If Henderson is active, he'll join Rhamondre Stevenson and Corey Kiner out of the Patriots backfield, though in what capacity remains to be seen.

headline: Henderson said Friday that an MRI revealed he sustained a high-ankle sprain but that he is "hoping to play" Sunday against the Jets, Doug Kyed of the Boston Herald reports.
story: It was reported earlier in the week that Henderson was facing a multi-week absence due to a high-ankle sprain, and while he was indeed diagnosed with the more severe ankle issue, he was able to practice this week and will have a chance to take the field in Week 6.

headline: Henderson (ankle) is practicing Friday, Mark Daniels of MassLive.com reports.
story: After opening Week 6 prep with back-to-back limited sessions, Henderson is participating for a third straight day. Reports earlier this week suggested he would miss multiple games, but it now appears he has a chance to avoid any absences altogether. New England's final injury report will provide a better idea of where Henderson stands ahead of Sunday's matchup with the Jets.

headline: Henderson (ankle) remained limited at Thursday's practice, Mark Daniels of MassLive reports.
story: Henderson has been limited in back-to-back practice sessions to kick off Week 6 prep. He'll likely need to upgrade to full participation Friday to avoid carrying an injury designation into Sunday's home game against the Jets, in which second place in the AFC East will be on the line. Corey Kiner would be in line for change-of-pace work behind Rhamondre Stevenson if Henderson sits.

headline: Henderson (ankle) is in pads ahead of Thursday's practice, Doug Kyed of the Boston Herald reports.
story: Henderson was a limited participant at Wednesday's practice, and he looks poised to practice in some capacity again Thursday, though the extent of his participation remains to bee seen. After initial pessimism following his exit from the Week 5 win over the Raiders, Henderson seemingly has a chance to suit up Sunday against the Jets without missing any additional game action.

headline: The Patriots listed Henderson (ankle) as a limited participant in Wednesday's practice.
story: After Henderson was diagnosed with a right high-ankle sprain coming out of Sunday's win over the Raiders, Adam Schefter of ESPN reported Tuesday that the second-year running back would avoid surgery but was expected to miss multiple weeks. While that could still be the case, Henderson's involvement in practice Wednesday -- albeit in a limited capacity -- suggests that the Patriots haven't yet ruled him out from playing Week 6 against the Jets. However, in the more likely event that Henderson ends up sitting out this Sunday, Rhamondre Stevenson would be in store for a larger share of the touches out of the backfield, while Corey Kiner would serve as the top complement to Stevenson.

headline: Henderson (ankle) isn't participating in Wednesday's practice, Doug Kyed of the Boston Herald reports.
story: Henderson's absence hardly comes as a surprise after Adam Schefter of ESPN reported that the running back is likely to miss multiple weeks after sustaining a right high-ankle sprain during this past Sunday's win over the Raiders. Head coach Mike Vrabel has yet to provide an updated timeline for Henderson's return, but the 23-year-old is expected to be officially ruled out for this Sunday's game against the Jets following Friday's practice.

headline: Henderson is expected to miss multiple weeks after he was diagnosed with a right high-ankle sprain following an MRI on Monday, Adam Schefter of ESPN reports.
story: Henderson sustained the injury in the second quarter of Sunday's 45-17 win over the Raiders and was unable to return. Schefter notes that Henderson won't need surgery to address the ankle sprain, so the running back may be able to avoid a stint on injured reserve and the automatic four-game absence that comes with it. Even so, Henderson still looks poised to be sidelined for at least a couple of contests, which will clear the way for Rhamondre Stevenson to take on a heightened role out of the backfield. Corey Kiner will also be in line for increased snaps as the top change-of-pace option behind Stevenson while Henderson is out of the mix.

headline: Henderson (ankle) is slated to undergo further medical testing Monday after exiting Sunday's 45-17 win over the Raiders, Ian Rapoport of NFL Network reports.
story: Henderson carried four times for 22 yards and recorded 16 receiving yards before exiting with just over 12 minutes left in the second quarter after injuring an ankle. Following Henderson's exit, Corey Kiner stepped in as the top complement to Rhamondre Stevenson, finishing the afternoon with six carries for 52 yards and a lost fumble. The Patriots didn't provide many details regarding the extent of Henderson's injury after the game, but the upcoming tests should shed more light on the matter. For now, Henderson can be considered questionable heading into the Patriots' Week 6 game against the Jets on Sunday.

headline: The Patriots ruled out Henderson (ankle) for the remainder of Sunday's game against the Raiders, Evan Lazar of the team's official site reports.
story: Initially considered questionable to return to the game after leaving in the second quarter due to the right ankle injury, Henderson didn't join the Patriots on the sideline to begin the second half before he was ruled out shortly after the third quarter got underway. He'll finish the afternoon with 22 yards on four carries to go with one catch for 16 yards. With Henderson sidelined for the rest of the contest, the Patriots will be left with Corey Kiner as their lone option behind No. 1 back Rhamondre Stevenson.

headline: Henderson suffered a right ankle injury during Sunday's game against the Raiders.
story: After a carry in the second quarter in which he endured an awkward tackle going out of bounds, Henderson limped to the locker room. The Patriots soon considered him questionable to return. Rhamondre Stevenson likely will take on the bulk of New England's backfield reps for as long as Henderson is sidelined, though Corey Kiner also is available for RB snaps.

headline: Henderson will operate as the Patriots' RB1 if Rhamondre Stevenson (knee, questionable) is unable to play against the Raiders on Sunday, Evan Lazar of the Patriots' official site reports.
story: Stevenson was limited in practice all week due to a knee injury, and while he expressed optimism Friday on playing this weekend, head coach Mike Vrabel was not quite ready to give the veteran running back the green light for Sunday's game, per Mark Daniels of MassLive.com. Stevenson's status for Week 5 will be worth a close watch, because if he's ruled out or operates under a snap count, then Henderson would be poised to take over as the Patriots' RB1 for at least one game. Henderson has a 38-141-1 rushing line through three games this season and has caught just one of three targets for six yards in that span.

headline: Henderson rushed 14 times for 42 yards and failed to bring in either of his two targets in the Patriots' 29-26 win over the Bills on Sunday.
story: Henderson struggled to get anything going against an improved Bills run defense, averaging an even 3.0 yards per carry. The second-year pro logged one more carry than backfield mate Rhamondre Stevenson but finished with five fewer rushing yards, and through three games, Henderson is averaging a pedestrian 3.7 yards per tote while only adding one catch for six yards. The 2025 second-round pick's next opportunity for his first breakout effort of 2026 comes in a Week 5 home matchup against a vastly improved Raiders team.

headline: Henderson rushed eight times for 23 yards and brought in his only target for six yards in the Patriots' 35-6 loss to the Jaguars on Sunday.
story: Playing in his second game of the season, Henderson led the Patriots in carries and rushing yards, yet each of those figures were only one more than those generated by backfield mate Rhamondre Stevenson. Henderson had a much more efficient showing in his Week 2 season debut with a 16-carry, 76-yard, one-touchdown showing against the Steelers, but game script had a significant impact on the volume for both of the Patriots' backs Sunday. Henderson will look to get back on track in a key Week 4 road divisional matchup against the Bills next Sunday.

headline: Henderson (ankle) rushed 16 times for 76 yards and a touchdown and wasn't targeted in the passing game during Sunday's 20-3 win over the Steelers.
story: Henderson didn't take long to make an impact in his season debut after sitting out the 13-10 Week 1 loss to Seattle. The 2025 second-round pick opened the scoring with a 39-yard touchdown run 6:38 into Sunday's game and handled 17 touches compared to just seven for Rhamondre Stevenson, who lost a fumble on the drive preceding Henderson's touchdown run. Henderson had 180 carries to Stevenson's 130 during the 2025 regular season. Both running backs are likely to be involved in the Week 3 game plan against the Jaguars.

headline: Henderson (ankle) said Thursday that he's ready to go for Sunday's game against the Steelers, Evan Lazar of the Patriots' official site reports.
story: Henderson sat out the Patriots' Week 1 loss to the Seahawks but has been practicing without limitations ahead of Sunday's matchup with the Steelers. Rhamondre Stevenson handled 23 touches in Henderson's absence last week, but they figure to shift into a near-even split, leaving few, if any, touches for third-stringer Corey Kiner.

headline: Henderson (ankle) was a  full participant in Wednesday's practice.
story: This is a big development for Henderson after his ankle injury kept him out of the season opener. He was a full-go in Wednesday's session, which bodes well for him making his 2026 debut Sunday against the Steelers. The Patriots struggled to run the ball in his absence against the Seahawks, recording just 3.9 yards per carry as a team. Rhamondre Stevenson and Corey Kiner mustered just 62 yards on 24 carries.

headline: Head coach Mike Vrabel said Henderson (ankle) will "do some more" at Wednesday's practice, Mark Daniels of MassLive.com reports.
story: Prior to sitting out the Patriots' Week 1 loss at Seattle, Henderson had been sidelined from practice since Aug. 24. The team held an unofficial session Monday, for which Henderson's activity level wasn't divulged, so how he's listed Wednesday may provide insight into his odds to suit up Sunday against the Steelers.

headline: Coach Mike Vrabel said Henderson (ankle) will practice Monday, Mike Reiss of ESPN.com reports.
story: Henderson missed practice all last week leading up to Wednesday's season-opening loss to the Seahawks, but he's now had an additional four days to recover and appears to have a good chance to make his 2026 debut Sunday against the Steelers. Rhamondre Stevenson slogged his way to 2.8 yards per carry in Week 1 against Seattle, while Corey Kiner filled in as the RB2 and rushed for 11 yards on six carries.

headline: Henry (foot) was limited in Wednesday's practice.
story: After injuring his foot in Week 8 against Miami, Henry played through the limited practice reps last week against the Packers and turned three targets into three grabs for 35 yards. Assuming he didn't suffer a setback, Henry should be fine for Sunday's game against the Lions in Germany.

headline: Henry caught all three of his targets for 35 yards during Sunday's 45-27 loss to the Packers.
story: Henry returned to action after suffering a foot injury in the first half of the Patriots' Week 8 win over the Dolphins and missing the majority of that contest. The tight end was held in check versus Green Bay, finishing with three or fewer catches for the sixth time this season. Henry has now reeled in 32 of 37 targets for 361 yards and two touchdowns over nine contests so far during the 2026 campaign.

headline: Henry (foot) is listed as active for Sunday's game against the Packers, Doug Kyed of the Boston Herald reports.
story: After opening the week with back-to-back missed practices, Henry was able to work in a limited fashion Friday before heading into the weekend with a 'questionable' designation. With his active status confirmed, in the absence of any setbacks or limitations Sunday, Henry a" who leads the Patriots with 29 catches and is second in receiving yardage (326), to go with two TDs through eight games -- will have an opportunity to remain a key target for QB Drake Maye in a New England passing offense that continues to be without top WRs A.J. Brown (knee/ankle) and Romeo Doubs (IR, shoulder).

headline: Henry (foot) "has a realistic chance to play" Sunday against the Packers, Ian Rapoport of NFL Network reports.
story: Henry practiced only once all week and it was a limited appearance Friday, but there is reason to believe he will be available Sunday. His status for Week 9 will officially be revealed when the Patriots release their inactives 90 minutes before Sunday's 4:25 p.m. ET kickoff.

headline: Henry (foot) is listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the Packers, Doug Kyed of the Boston Herald reports.
story: After opening the week with back-to-back missed practices, Henry's designation leaves the door open for him to play heading into Sunday. If he can't play, New England would need to lean more heavily on rookie Eli Raridon at tight end against Green Bay.

headline: Henry (foot) is present for the media-access portion of Friday's practice, Mike Reiss of ESPN.com reports.
story: After missing practice both Wednesday and Thursday, Henry's presence for Friday's session is a positive sign ahead of Sunday's game against the Packers. The Patriots' upcoming injury report will reveal both the tight end's official participation level, as well as his Week 9 game status.

headline: Henry (foot) wasn't spotted at Thursday's practice, Evan Lazar of the Patriots' official site reports.
story: Henry has started Week 9 prep with back-to-back absences after exiting during the Patriots' Week 8 win over Miami. If the veteran tight end is unable to practice in at least some capacity Friday, he'll likely be ruled out for Sunday's game against the Packers, paving the way for rookie third-round pick Eli Raridon to take on an expanded role.

headline: Henry (foot) wasn't on the field for the media-access portion of Wednesday's practice, Mike Reiss of ESPN.com reports.
story: Henry was unable to return to Sunday's 24-19 win over the Dolphins after exiting in the second quarter due to the foot issue. The Patriots haven't provided many details regarding the severity of the injury, but Henry will be sidelined as the team begins Week 9 prep. Henry will have two more chances to potentially practice this week before the Patriots decide whether he'll take a designation into Sunday's game against the Packers.

headline: Patriots head coach Mike Vrabel said Monday that he had no update on Henry's (foot) status heading into Sunday's game against the Packers, Karen Guregian of MassLive.com reports. "I don't have any expectations yet," Vrabel said of Henry. "It's kind of how he responds here. He wasn't able to finish the [Week 8] game. So we'll see where he is, and I know Hunter will do everything he can to get back to help us."
story: Henry recorded three receptions for 30 yards on three targets before exiting in the second quarter of Sunday's 24-19 win over the Dolphins due to the foot issue. The Patriots haven't provided any further word on where exactly Henry stands in his recovery, but more context on that front should arrive when the team releases its first Week 9 injury report Wednesday. Despite his early departure in Week 8, Henry leads the team in receptions (29) and is second to only wideout DeMario Douglas in receiving yards (326) through eight games.

headline: Henry (foot) has been ruled out for the rest of Sunday's game in Miami.
story: Henry exited in the first half of this Week 8 matchup and eventually was ruled out midway through the fourth quarter. He ended with three catches (on three targets) for 30 yards. Eli Raridon will act as the Patriots' top pass-catching tight end for as long as Henry is sidelined.

headline: Henry (foot) is questionable to return to Sunday's game against the Dolphins.
story: Prior to his departure from the contest, Henry had caught all three of his targets for 30 yards. Next up for the Patriots' TE snaps in his absence is Eli Raridon, with Cameron Latu and Tanner Arkin also on hand versus Miami.

headline: Henry secured all seven targets for 71 yards in the Patriots' 30-24 loss to the Bears on Thursday.
story: The veteran tight end was a key contributor throughout the night, finishing with team-high figures in receptions and targets while ending second in receiving yards. All three components of Henry's receiving line also were season-high figures, and he now has between 44 and 71 receiving yards in four consecutive games. Henry will take a 26-296-2 line on 31 targets into a Week 8 road matchup against the Dolphins on Sunday, Nov. 1.

headline: Henry caught four of five targets for 48 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 26-19 win over the Jets.
story: Henry's seven-yard touchdown in the fourth quarter proved to be the game-winning score, putting New England ahead 23-16. After not finding the end zone the first four weeks of the season, Henry has scored in back-to-back games. The veteran tight end has been held under 50 yards receiving in five of six contests. He's the definition of a touchdown-or-bust fantasy bet ahead of Thursday's game with the Bears.

headline: Henry caught three of four targets for 44 yards and a touchdown during Sunday's 45-17 win over the Raiders.
story: Henry was able to reel in at least three passes for the fourth time this season, and his biggest moment of the game came in the second quarter when Drake Maye connected with him for an 11-yard score. The tight end has now caught 15 of 19 targets for 177 yards and a touchdown over the first five games of the season.

headline: Henry finished with five receptions for 62 yards on five targets in Sunday's 29-26 win over the Bills.
story: The catch and yardage totals were season-best marks for Henry, who took the field for 49 of the Patriots' 76 offensive snaps (64.5 percent). With fellow tight end Eli Raridon (ankle) making an early exit from the contest and potentially at risk of missing the Patriots' Week 5 game against the Raiders, Henry could be called upon to handle a heftier workload next Sunday.

headline: Henry caught one pass (on two targets) for five yards during the Patriots' 35-6 loss to the Jaguars on Sunday.
story: The Patriots offense struggled as a whole Sunday, with Drake Maye completing 14 of 25 passes for 199 yards (8.0 YPA) and two interceptions. Even with A.J. Brown (ankle, IR) sidelined for the last two weeks, Henry has logged just four catches for 45 yards on seven targets, and he's well behind pace to match his 60-768-7 line (on 87 targets) across 17 regular-season games in 2025. Up next is a Week 4 road tilt against the Bills, whose defense held Chargers tight end Oronde Gadsden catchless on three targets in a Week 3 win for Buffalo.

headline: Henry caught three of five targets for 40 yards in the Patriots' 20-3 win over the Steelers on Sunday.
story: In the team's first game without A.J. Brown (ankle), Henry ended up pacing the Patriots with his five targets, though Drake Maye spread the ball around to nine different pass catchers. While Henry led the team in looks, Romeo Doubs turned his four targets into three catches for a game-high 96 receiving yards. After two contests this season, Henry has six catches for 66 scoreless yards. He's one of many in the touchdown-or-bust bucket at tight end for fantasy.

headline: Brown (knee/ankle) was a limited participant in Wednesday's practice.
story: Brown last played in Week 7, but the wideout's return to a limited practice Wednesday has him trending in the right direction as Sunday's game against the Lions in Munich approaches. The Patriots' top WR now has two more opportunities to upgrade his practice participation before the team's Week 10 injury designations are assigned Friday.

headline: Brown (knee) returned to practice Wednesday, Evan Lazar of the Patriots' official site reports.
story: Brown's return to practice comes hours after coach Mike Vrabel confirmed to reporters that the wideout will travel to Munich, where the Patriots face the Lions on Sunday. Brown missed the past two games and didn't practice at all last week.

headline: Brown (knee) is traveling with the Patriots to Germany, Evan Lazar of the Patriots' official site reports.
story: Brown missed the past two games and didn't practice last week, but it sounds like he has at least some chance to return for Sunday's game against the Lions in Munich. Patriots coach Mike Vrabel did say Wednesday that not all of the injured players traveling for the game will end up playing, per Doug Kyed of the Boston Herald.

headline: Brown (knee) is trending toward traveling with the Patriots for their trip to Munich, where the team will face the Lions this coming weekend, according to Mark Daniels of MassLive.com.
story: Per Mike Reiss of ESPN.com, coach Mike Vrabel indicated that for now the team plans for the wideout to make the trip, but a decision on that front has yet to be locked in. In Brown's second consecutive missed game, Sunday against the Packers, DeMario Douglas, Mack Hollins, Efton Chism and Kyle Williams handled the Patriots' Week 9 WR duties.

headline: Brown (knee) won't be available for Sunday's game against the Packers, Mark Daniels of Masslive.comreports.
story: Following a trio of consecutive DNPs, Brown is slated to sit out a second consecutive contest. In his absence, DeMario Douglas, Efton Chism and Kyle Williams are available to handle Week 9 duties, while Mack Hollins (calf) -- who has been designated to return from IR -- is a candidate to be activated this weekend, and if that occurs he could step into a key role in his return to the lineup. As for Brown's potential availability for the Patriots' Week 10 contest versus the Lions in Munich, coach Mike Vrabel indicated that he doesn't know yet, per Doug Kyed of the Boston Herald.

headline: Brown (knee/ankle) remained sidelined at practice Friday, Doug Kyed of the Boston Herald reports.
story: With three consecutive DNPs looming, Brown doesn't seem likely to be available Sunday against the Packers. If Brown is ruled out later Friday, the stage would be set for DeMario Douglas, Efton Chism, Kyle Williams and potentially Mack Hollins (calf) -- who has been designated to return from IR -- to handle New England's Week 9 WR duties.

headline: Brown (ankle/knee) was a non-participant at Thursday's practice, Rob Demovsky of ESPN.com reports.
story: Thursday's injury report confirms Brown's absence after he wasn't spotted earlier in the day. Brown has missed the team's first two practices leading up to Sunday's game against the Packers, suggesting he's fighting an uphill battle in his effort to avoid missing a second consecutive game. He has dressed for only three of New England's first eight games. DeMario Douglas, Efton Chism, Kyle Williams and possibly Mack Hollins (calf) would lead the Patriots' wide receiver room Sunday if Brown sits again.

headline: Brown (ankle/knee) isn't present for the portion of Thursday's practice open to media viewing, Evan Lazar of the Patriots' official site reports.
story: Brown appears set for a second straight missed practice after sitting out Wednesday's session on the heels of his absence during New England's Week 8 win over Miami. He'll have one more chance to practice Friday and will likely have to participate in some capacity to avoid being ruled out for Sunday's game against the Packers.

headline: Patriots head coach Mike Vrabel said that Brown (knee/ankle) won't practice Wednesday, Doug Kyed of the Boston Herald reports.
story: Brown was sidelined for New England's Week 8 win over Miami, and with another absence from practice on tap, the wideout's status for Sunday's game against the Packers is cloudy. On the plus side for the Patriots, Mack Hollins (calf) could return from injured reserve this weekend to bolster a wideout corps that also includes DeMario Douglas, Efton Chism and Kyle Williams.

headline: When asked whether Brown (ankle/knee) might practice at some point this week, coach Mike Vrabel said Monday, "We'll see," Doug Kyed of the Boston Herald reports.
story: Brown was inactive for Sunday's 24-19 win over the Dolphins, and Vrabel's comment Monday implies that the wideout's status for this weekend's game against the Packers is uncertain at this stage. In Brown's absence versus Miami, DeMario Douglas, Efton Chism and Kyle Williams paced the Patriots' Week 8 WR corps.

headline: Brown (knee/ankle) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Dolphins, Ian Rapoport of ESPN and NFL Network reports.
story: Brown entered the weekend with the questionable tag despite being held out of practice both Thursday and Friday, and the knee injury that flared up during Wednesday's session is severe enough for the veteran wide receiver to miss Sunday's AFC East tilt. With Brown sidelined, the Patriots' pass-catching group will be led by DeMario Douglas, Efton Chism and tight end Hunter Henry. Brown's next opportunity to play is Week 9 against the Packers on Sunday, Nov. 8.

headline: Brown (ankle/knee) is questionable for Sunday's game at Miami, Evan Lazar of the Patriots' official site reports.
story: Patriots coach Mike Vrabel deemed Brown questionable after Friday's practice, in which the wideout didn't participate. Vrabel told reporters that Brown's knee flared up during Wednesday's practice and prevented him from finishing the session, per Doug Kyed of the Boston Herald. Brown then missed practice Thursday and Friday, putting his availability in serious doubt ahead of a 4:25 p.m. ET kickoff at Miami on Sunday.

headline: Brown (ankle/knee) was not spotted at Friday's practice, Evan Lazar of the Patriots' official site reports.
story: Brown was limited Wednesday and missed practice Thursday, with reports confirming a flare-up in his knee. He's managed chronic/degenerative knee problems throughout his career, typically managing to play even when the issue flares up. That said, the back-to-back absences from practice suggest Brown is in danger of missing Sunday's game at Miami, potentially leaving DeMario Douglas, Efton Chism and Kyle Williams as New England's top three WRs.

headline: Brown (ankle/knee) was officially listed as a non-participant at Thursday's practice, David Furones of the South Florida Sun Sentinel reports.
story: Thursday's injury report confirms earlier reporting from Ian Rapoport of NFL Network that Brown isn't practicing Thursday. According to Rapoport, Brown recently had a knee issue flare up, which has the wide receiver's status for Sunday's game against the Dolphins in doubt. Brown has six catches for 75 yards on 16 targets in two games since returning from a four-game absence due to an ankle injury.

headline: Brown (knee/ankle) is sidelined Thursday by a knee issue that flared up, and the wide receiver's status for Sunday against the Dolphins is up in the air, Ian Rapoport of NFL Network reports.
story: Brown is contending with a new knee injury in addition to the ankle injury through which he has played the last two weeks after missing the previous four. The wideout's fantasy managers should start forming contingency plans in case he sits out Sunday against the Dolphins, though Brown could change the narrative by returning to practice Friday.

headline: Brown (ankle/knee) was not present during the media-viewing portion of Thursday's practice, Mike Reiss of ESPN.com reports.
story: Brown looks to be trending in the wrong direction after being listed as a limited participant at Wednesday's practice. He has caught just six of 16 targets for 75 yards in two games since returning from a stint on IR due to an ankle injury. Brown's activity level Friday could be pivotal for his availability Sunday against the Dolphins.

headline: Brown was a limited participant in Wednesday's practice due to knee and ankle injuries.
story: The Patriots are remaining cautious with Brown, who is apparently nursing a knee issue in addition to getting continued maintenance for the high-ankle sprain that kept him out for four games. Brown was limited in two practices ahead of a Thursday night game against the Bears but still played 92 percent of the offensive snaps in the 30-24 loss. A similar rep-management plan could be in place for Brown going into Sunday's game against the Dolphins.

headline: Brown brought in three of six targets for 48 yards in the Patriots' 30-24 loss to the Bears on Thursday.
story: Brown entered the night looking to put a fairly forgettable Week 6 return from injury behind him, but the veteran wideout could only slightly improve his numbers in the high-scoring loss. He was fairly quiet until the second half, when he had 16- and 14-yard grabs. Brown did finish second in targets on the night for New England, but Drake Maye focused most on tight end Hunter Henry and running back Rhamondre Stevenson, who saw a combined 12 targets. With Romeo Doubs (IR, shoulder) out for at least three more games, Brown will have a chance to see elevated volume in a Week 8 road matchup against the Dolphins on Sunday, Nov. 1.

headline: Brown (ankle) does not carry an injury designation going into Thursday's game against the Bears.
story: Brown turned in a full practice Wednesday, and that was enough to take him off the injury report going into the Week 7 primetime matchup with Chicago. He returned from a four-game absence in Week 6 and played 76 percent of the offensive snaps against the Jets, recording three catches for 27 yards on 10 targets. Brown and the Patriots will face a Bears defense that allows 9.8 yards per target to opposing receivers.

headline: Brown (ankle) was listed as a limited participant on Tuesday's practice report.
story: Brown returned from a four-game absence this past Sunday against the Jets. He's been limited in each of the first two sessions of Week 7 prep, and the veteran wide receiver told reporters after Tuesday's practice that his ankle is "feeling good," per Doug Kyed of the Boston Herald. Wednesday's injury report should clarify whether the Patriots' top WR will be fully cleared for Thursday night's game against the Bears.
