story: Black should be fine to handle his normal role Sunday against the Seahawks as Christian McCaffrey's direct backup. The rookie running back has turned 20 carries into just 55 yards (2.75 YPC) over the last three games following a strong Week 1 debut in Australia against the Rams.

headline: Black turned six carries into 13 yards during the 49ers' 24-14 win over the Broncos on Sunday.
story: Black's longest carry of the day went for five yards, with four of his other touches going for two yards or fewer. With Christian McCaffrey clearly leading the backfield, Black's workload will be volatile on a week-to-week basis and dependent on game script. The 49ers will hit the road for Week 5 in an NFC West showdown against the 3-1 Seahawks.

headline: Black turned four carries into 17 yards and failed to haul in his lone target during the 49ers' 36-30 win over the Cardinals on Sunday.
story: Black accumulated 95 scrimmage yards on 22 touches through the first two games of the season while working behind Christian McCaffrey, but the rookie observed most of Sunday's game from the sidelines, seeing the field for only eight of the 49ers' 54 offensive snaps (14.8 percent). Keeping McCaffrey healthy is a top priority, but Black's workload is likely to remain erratic and dependent on game script. The 49ers will remain home in Week 4 to host the Broncos this Sunday.

headline: Black (groin) rushed seven times for 25 yards and wasn't targeted in Sunday's 35-13 win over the Dolphins.
story: Black suited up for his second NFL contest after being listed as questionable coming into the game. He actually had two more rushing yards than Christian McCaffrey, but McCaffrey scored two touchdowns on 10 carries and added four catches for 43 yards. Black is poised to continue splitting the rushing workload with CMC in Week 3 against the Cardinals, though McCaffrey remains the preferred option in valuable goal-line and passing situations.

headline: Black (groin) is active for Sunday's Week 2 matchup against the Dolphins, Nick Wagoner of ESPN.com reports.
story: The rookie running back was reported to be trending up for Sunday's contest earlier Sunday, and his availability now has been made official. Black will therefore once again serve as the primary backup to Christian McCaffrey, a role that afforded the former 15 touches (14 carries, one reception) across 28 snaps in a Week 1 win over the Rams in Melbourne, Australia.

headline: Black (groin) is on track to play Sunday against the Dolphins, Adam Schefter of ESPN reports.
story: Black popped up on Thursday's injury report as a limited participant due to a groin injury, and he was given a questionable designation after getting in another limited session Friday. While there is reason to believe he will take the field Sunday, his availability will not be confirmed until the 49ers release their inactives 90 minutes before Sunday's 4:25 p.m. ET kickoff.

headline: Black (groin) is listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the Dolphins, Cam Inman of The San Jose Mercury News reports.
story: Black made a surprise appearance on Thursday's practice report as limited due to a groin issue, and he wasn't able to do enough Friday to enter the weekend without a designation for Week 2 action. His status may not be confirmed until about 90 minutes before Sunday's 4:25 p.m. ET kickoff, but if Black is inhibited or sidelined, Jordan James would be the primary reserve RB behind starter Christian McCaffrey.

headline: Black was limited at Thursday's practice due to a groin injury, Matt Maiocco of NBC Sports Bay Area reports.
story: Black did not show up on Wednesday's injury report, but he was unable to get a full session in a day later. The extent of his injury is uncertain, but his status will be updated again Friday when the 49ers release their final report before Sunday's matchup with the Dolphins.

headline: Watkins caught all four of his targets for 86 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 38-17 win over the Raiders.
story: Watkins set a new career high in receiving yards, thanks in large part to a 37-yard touchdown catch in the third quarter, which was the first of his NFL career. He has taken on a larger role over the past two games during the absences of Mike Evans (Achilles) and Deebo Samuel (hamstring), as Watkins had 56 receiving yards on six targets to lead San Francisco's wide receivers in Week 7 prior to the team's Week 8 bye. If at least one of Evans or Samuel remains sidelined in Week 10, Watkins would be poised to maintain an expanded role against a weak Dallas defense.

headline: Watkins brought in three of six targets for 56 yards in the 49ers' 29-20 loss to the Falcons on Sunday.
story: With the 49ers' receiving corps down all of Mike Evans (Achilles), Deebo Samuel (hamstring), De'Zhaun Stribling (IR, ankle) and Demarcus Robinson (IR, ankle), Watkins saw an expanded role and made good use of the opportunity. All three of Watkins' catches went for first downs, and he finished third on the team in receiving yards and targets while also tying for that slotting in receptions. The 2025 fourth-round pick's performance was encouraging, but he's likely to slide back down the depth chart since the wide-receiver room could be much healthier by the time San Francisco returns to action against the Raiders on Sunday, Nov. 8, following the Week 8 bye.

headline: Watkins could take on a significant role Sunday against Atlanta with Mike Evans (Achilles) and Deebo Samuel (hamstring) both sidelined, Brooke Evans of the 49ers' official site reports.
story: Watkins already saw a big jump in participation this past Monday versus Washington, tallying a season-high 76 percent offensive snap share in Samuel's absence. However, he drew just one target, which he caught for a 22-yard gain. Now that Evans will also be out of action, Watkins seems likely to be deployed often again Sunday, though Brandin Cooks and Jacob Cowing should also get opportunities to step into larger roles. Finally, Christian Kirk (calf), who is currently on IR, may be activated ahead of the matchup versus Atlanta, and he could also factor into the equation in what would be his 49ers debut.

headline: Watkins caught his lone target for 22 yards during the 49ers' 23-17 win over the Commanders on Monday.
story: Watkins connected with Brock Purdy for a big gain early in the second quarter, and all three of wideout's catches this season have gone for 20-plus yards. Watkins' 47 offensive snaps ended up leading all 49ers wide receivers, and the second-year pro's role in the passing game could expand in Week 7 against the Falcons, depending on the availability of Mike Evans (Achilles) and Deebo Samuel (hamstring).

headline: Watkins recorded two receptions for 60 yards on two targets in Sunday's 36-30 win over the Cardinals.
story: Making his 2026 debut after he was a healthy inactive for the 49ers' first two contests, Watkins took the field for 15 of the team's 54 offensive snaps and was able to make a mark with 34- and 26-yard grabs. He still finished fifth among 49ers receivers in playing time, but he could see an uptick in opportunities if the rib strain Mike Evans suffered Sunday prevents him from playing Week 4 against the Broncos.

headline: Watkins (coach's decision) is inactive for Sunday's game against the Dolphins.
story: Watkins will be a healthy scratch for a second consecutive game, and his next chance to play is Week 3 against the Cardinals on Sept. 27. Mike Evans, Deebo Samuel and Demarcus Robinson will lead the 49ers' wide receiver group in Week 2.

headline: Kittle caught four of seven targets for 58 yards in Sunday's 38-17 win over the Raiders.
story: Kittle had at least three more targets than any teammate Sunday but finished 28 receiving yards shy of Jordan Watkins' team-leading total, while Brock Purdy's two touchdown passes went to Christian McCaffrey and Watkins. Sunday's output marked Kittle's third-lowest yardage total of the season, but the star TE recorded at least four catches for a seventh consecutive game. He'll look to add to his season totals of 38 catches for 483 yards and five touchdowns in Week 10 against the Cowboys.

headline: Kittle brought in eight of 10 targets for 88 yards and lost a fumble in the 49ers' 29-20 loss to the Falcons on Sunday.
story: Kittle led the 49ers across the board in receptions, receiving yards and targets on an afternoon in which the team was down Mike Evans (Achilles) and Deebo Samuel (hamstring), and in which Christian McCaffrey missed the entire second quarter due to a quadriceps injury. All three components of the veteran tight end's receiving line were also season-best figures, but Kittle's lost fumble at the Falcons' 19-yard line with 57 seconds remaining following a 22-yard catch snuffed out any hope of a comeback for the Niners. Despite the unsavory conclusion to Sunday's game, Kittle will remain a key target for Brock Purdy in a Week 9 home matchup against the Raiders on Sunday, Nov. 8, following a Week 8 bye.

headline: Kittle brought in five of eight targets for 69 yards and a touchdown in the 49ers' 23-17 win over the Commanders on Monday night.
story: Kittle was one of Brock Purdy's most effective targets on the night, finishing with the 49ers' second-highest reception, receiving yardage and target totals. The athletic tight end also was on the other end of Brock Purdy's one touchdown pass, recording an 11-yard scoring grab to cap off the opening possession of the night. Kittle has at least four receptions in five consecutive games and Monday night's receiving yardage total or higher in four of his first six contests of the season, affording him plenty of momentum heading into a Week 7 road matchup against the Falcons on Sunday.

headline: Kittle (illness) caught five of six targets for 24 yards in Sunday's 32-29 win over the Seahawks.
story: Kittle had an uncharacteristic third-down drop on San Francisco's opening drive but caught his other five targets to finish second on the 49ers in receiving yards despite playing through an illness. Mike Evans easily led the team with seven catches for 113 yards and a touchdown on 10 targets in Sunday's win. Kittle will have an extra day to recover before the Commanders come to town for Monday Night Football in Week 6.

headline: The 49ers announced that Kittle is dealing with an illness but will play in Sunday's game against the Seahawks, Nick Wagoner of ESPN.com reports.
story: Kittle remains without an official designation for Sunday's contest, so despite being under the weather, the expectation is that he'll play without any limitations. After tearing his Achilles in a Jan. 11 wild-card round win over the Eagles, the seven-time Pro Bowler has staged a successful comeback so far during the 2026 campaign. Through four games, Kittle has produced a 16-244-4 receiving line on 22 targets.

headline: Kittle secured four of six targets for 70 yards and a touchdown in the 49ers' 24-14 win over the Broncos on Sunday.
story: Kittle was having an unremarkable day until just before the two-minute warning, when he brought in a tight-end screen from Brock Purdy, turned upfield and raced 56 yards to the end zone to extend what had been a thin 17-14 lead for the 49ers. Kittle finished second in receptions and receiving yards on the afternoon for San Francisco, while also tying for runner-up status in targets. Kittle now has at least 70 receiving yards in three straight games, affording him plenty of momentum heading into a Week 5 road matchup against the Seahawks next Sunday.

headline: Kittle brought in six of seven targets for 82 yards and two touchdowns in the 49ers' 36-30 win over the Cardinals on Sunday.
story: Kittle led the 49ers in receptions, receiving yards and targets on the afternoon, marking what may have been his return to both full health and a full workload following last January's Achilles tear. The veteran tight end struck from 10 and 20 yards out for his pair of fourth-quarter scoring grabs, his first multi-TD tally since Week 11 of last season. Kittle now has hit or exceeded the 80-yard mark in consecutive games, and he should remain heavily involved in a Week 4 home matchup against a Broncos defense that tends to funnel passing toward the middle of the field due to its outstanding cornerback play.

headline: Kittle caught all four of his targets for 80 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 35-13 win over the Dolphins.
story: Kittle gained half of his yardage on a 40-yard catch to start the second half, and he scored a 12-yard touchdown three plays later. He had just 12 receiving yards in the Week 1 win over the Rams, as Kittle returned from an Achilles tear sustained in January. Kittle will try to build on Sunday's strong performance in Week 3 against the Cardinals.

headline: Kittle (Achilles) practiced fully Friday and does not have an injury designation for Week 2, according to David Furones of the South Florida Sun Sentinel.
story: Kittle was limited at San Francisco's first two practices of the week, but he was able to get in a full session Friday. As such, consider him ready to go for his team's Week 2 matchup with the Dolphins.

headline: Kittle (Achilles) practiced in a limited capacity Thursday, Matt Maiocco of NBC Sports Bay Area reports.
story: Kittle continues to operate with a cap on his practice reps in the early going this season, which isn't a surprise considering he tore his right Achilles nine months ago. In Week 1 against the Rams in Melbourne, Australia, he recorded two catches (on five targets) for 12 yards on a 46 percent snap share, more or less looking like his normal self. Because WRs De'Zhaun Stribling (ankle), Ricky Pearsall (knee) and Christian Kirk (calf) are all sidelined for varying lengths of time, Kittle stands to benefit in the 49ers' passing game, assuming he's active on a weekly basis.

headline: Kittle (Achilles) was limited in practice Wednesday, Nick Wagoner of ESPN.com reports.
story: Kittle operated with a cap on his practice reps last week before returning to action just nine months removed from tearing his right Achilles in a wild-card win at Philadelphia. In the 49ers' Week 1 victory against the Rams in Melbourne, Australia, he started, played 30 of 65 offensive snaps and gathered in two of five targets for 12 yards. San Francisco may continue to take it easy on Kittle in the early going with the long term in mind, but his status for game days doesn't appear to be in any question.

headline: Purdy completed 17 of 25 passes for 232 yards, two touchdowns and one interception in Sunday's 38-17 win over the Raiders. He added seven rushing attempts for 40 yards and a touchdown.
story: Purdy gave the 49ers a 14-0 lead with a one-yard rushing touchdown in the first quarter, then added a 12-yard touchdown pass to Christian McCaffrey in the second quarter and a 37-yard touchdown pass to Jordan Watkins in the third. Unfazed by the numerous injuries to San Francisco's wide receivers, Purdy has a 17:5 TD:INT through the air to go with a pair of rushing scores heading into a Week 10 road matchup against the Cowboys. Having led the 49ers to a 7-1 record, the fourth-place finisher in the 2023 MVP race is making a strong case for the award at the halfway point of the 2026 campaign.

headline: Purdy completed 27 of 40 passes for 288 yards with one touchdown and two interceptions and added two carries for five yards in the 49ers' 29-20 loss to the Falcons on Sunday.
story: Purdy put together an impressive passing yardage total, especially considering he was down both Mike Evans (Achilles) and Deebo Samuel (hamstring), along with De'Zhaun Stribling (IR, ankle) and Demarcus Robinson (IR, ankle). He also lost Christian McCaffrey for the entirety of the second quarter due to a leg injury that the star back eventually returned from, but the scarcity of his top pass catchers eventually led to a more mistake-filled performance than usual. The multi-interception tally was Purdy's first of the season, and the two picks led to 10 points for the Falcons. Purdy should have a chance to work with a deeper pass-catching corps in a Week 9 home matchup against the Raiders on Sunday, Nov. 8, as the Week 8 bye should offer multiple receivers a chance to recover from their respective injuries.

headline: Purdy completed 21 of 29 passes for 264 yards with one touchdown and no interceptions while adding five rushes for 28 yards in the 49ers' 23-17 win over the Commanders on Monday night.
story: Purdy took multiple sacks for the second straight game after not being taken down over the first four contests, but the veteran signal-caller otherwise had a mostly clean night that included a robust average of 9.1 yards per attempt. Purdy's passing yardage total also was his third highest of the campaign, and he kept his season-long touchdown-pass streak alive when he connected with George Kittle on an 11-yard scoring strike to cap off the opening drive of the night. Purdy completed passes to seven different targets overall, and he now boasts a 14:2 TD:INT heading into a Week 7 road matchup against the Falcons on Sunday.

headline: Purdy completed 19 of 29 passes for 189 yards, two touchdowns and one interception in Sunday's 32-29 win over the Seahawks. He also rushed five times for six yards and threw a successful two-point conversion.
story: Seattle's talented defense made life tougher for Purdy than it had been up to this point, as he committed his first turnover since Week 1 and took his first three sacks of the season. Purdy nonetheless did enough to keep the 49ers undefeated. He threw a two-yard touchdown pass to Mike Evans in the first quarter and a seven-yard touchdown pass to Brandin Cooks in the fourth, the latter of which Purdy followed up with a two-point conversion to Evans. The Seahawks responded with a field goal to tie the game at 29-29, but Purdy led the 49ers into position for Eddy Pineiro's go-ahead 44-yard field goal with 1:56 remaining. San Francisco's defense delivered the game-winning stop as Purdy and the 49ers improved to 5-0 heading into a Week 6 MNF home game against the Commanders.

headline: Purdy completed 19 of 30 passes for 218 yards with two touchdowns and no interceptions while adding 10 carries for 29 yards in the 49ers' 24-14 win over the Broncos on Sunday.
story: Purdy performed admirably against a tough Broncos defense, and his legs helped him to yet another sack-free afternoon despite the challenge posted by Denver's aggressive unit. Purdy didn't fire his first touchdown pass of the day until the 4:15 mark of the third quarter, hitting Deebo Samuel from one yard out to snap a 3-3 tie. The veteran signal-caller then sealed San Francisco's victory with a 56-yard scoring strike to George Kittle just before the two-minute warning, and Purdy remained free of interceptions for the third straight game. Purdy has a league-leading 11 touchdown passes and has yet to be brought down through four games, but he'll have a stiff challenge on his hands in a Week 5 road matchup against the Seahawks next Sunday.

headline: Purdy completed 15 of 27 passes for 297 yards with four touchdowns and no interceptions and rushed twice for 34 yards in the 49ers' 36-30 win over the Cardinals on Sunday.
story: Purdy's completion percentage was below his usual standards, but the fifth-year signal-caller more than made up for it with some effective downfield passing and his quartet of scoring tosses. His yardage total also got a boost from an 80-yard hook-and-lateral play in the first quarter between Mike Evans and Deebo Samuel that the latter took all the way to the house from San Francisco's 20-yard line, which served as the quarterback's first touchdown pass of the day. Purdy would go on to connect with Evans (23 yards) and George Kittle (10 and 20 yards) for his other three scoring tosses, with the final one of those coming two plays after a holding penalty on the talented tight end nullified a winding 45-yard touchdown run by the athletic quarterback. Purdy now boasts a 9:1 TD:INT and 789 passing yards over his first three games heading into a tough Week 4 home showdown against the Broncos next Sunday.

headline: Purdy completed 20 of 22 passes for 287 yards and two touchdowns in Sunday's 35-13 win over the Dolphins. He also rushed three times for 30 yards and a touchdown.
story: Purdy was in complete command of the offense throughout Sunday's lopsided win, throwing only two incompletions while finishing as the team's leading rusher for the cherry on top. The 49ers have been one of the league's best teams in the early going, outscoring the Rams and Dolphins by a combined margin of 62-20 heading into a Week 3 home game against the Cardinals. Purdy has contributed six total touchdowns during this hot start, including third-quarter touchdown passes of 12 yards to George Kittle and six yards to Kyle Juszczyk against the Dolphins following Purdy's two-yard touchdown run in the second quarter.

headline: Jones tallied seven tackles (three solo) during Seattle's win over the Cardinals on Sunday.
story: Jones finished tied for second on the team in tackles behind Julian Love during Sunday's victory. Jones has now racked up seven or more tackles in all nine of his outings to start the season and will look to keep producing next week versus the Raiders.

headline: Jones (ankle) does not carry an official injury designation ahead of Sunday's game versus Arizona, John Boyle of the Seahawks' official site reports.
story: Jones popped up on the Seahawks' injury report with an ankle issue Thursday, but he was able to log a full practice Friday and is on track to play Sunday. He is the NFL's third leading tackler on the season going into a Week 9 contest against a pass-heavy Cardinals offense.

headline: Jones (ankle) was a limited participant at the Seahawks' practice Thursday, John Boyle of the team's official site reports.
story: Jones was added to the injury report with an ankle injury Thursday after he was considered to be a full participant at Wednesday's walkthrough practice. The linebacker will have one more chance to log a full practice prior to Sunday's matchup with the Cardinals.

headline: Jones recorded 13 tackles and a defensed pass in Monday's Week 8 loss to Chicago.
story: Jones not only led Seattle in stops in the loss, he also tied the season-high mark he first established in Week 1 versus New England. The veteran linebacker continues to be an impactful IDP asset in his sixth NFL campaign, as he ranks third in the NFL with 81 tackles through eight weeks. Jones has recorded at least eight stops in every one of his appearances this season.

headline: Jones notched nine tackles (five solo) Sunday in a 20-3 win against Kansas City.
story: Jones had a three-game streak of recording at least one sack snapped, but he remained highly productive. The veteran linebacker has now tallied exactly nine tackles in three straight games and has posted at least eight stops in each of his seven contests this season. Overall, Jones is tied for third in the NFL with 68 tackles through seven games.

headline: Jones recorded nine tackles (five solo), including 1.0 sacks, in Thursday night's 17-14 overtime loss to the Broncos.
story: Jones has now recorded a sack in three straight games and has at least eight tackles in all six contests to kick off the 2026 campaign. He's up to 59 tackles (31 solo), including 3.0 sacks, and three pass breakups, with one interception, on 99.5 percent of the Seahawks' defensive snaps.

headline: Jones recorded 12 total tackles (six solo), including 1.0 sacks, and added an interception during Sunday's 30-23 win over the Chargers.
story: Jones was masterful in Week 4, leading the team in tackles in the victory. The linebacker was able to get to quarterback Justin Herbert for his first sack of the season in the second quarter before intercepting a pass from the QB later in the quarter. Jones has now compiled 41 total tackles (21 solo), including 1.0 sacks, and intercepted a pass over four contests to open the 2026 campaign.

headline: Jones (neck) was a full participant in Thursday's practice, Brady Henderson of ESPN.com reports.
story: Jones opened the week as a limited practice participant due to a neck issue. That limited practice was a precautionary measure given his full participation in Thursday's session, and the 2021 third-rounder is well on track to play in Sunday's road game against the Commanders. Jones has 21 tackles (12 solo) through the first two games of the regular season.

headline: Jones (neck) was a limited participant at the Seahawks' practice Wednesday, John Boyle of the team's official site reports.
story: Jones secured eight total tackles (four solo) during the team's 31-7 win over Arizona in Week 2, and he appears to have suffered a neck injury during the contest. The linebacker's ability to practice in any capacity to open the week is a positive sign, and he'll have two more chances to log a full practice before Sunday's matchup with the Commanders.

headline: Jones recorded eight tackles (four solo) during Sunday's 31-7 win at Arizona.
story: One thing limiting Jones' production in Week 2 was the fact that the Cardinals' offense simply couldn't stay on the field - he played 48 defensive snaps Sunday after playing 71 defensive snaps in Week 1. He's still firmly on the IDP radar going into a Week 3 tilt against the Commanders.

headline: Williams (shoulder) did not participate at practice Wednesday, John Boyle of the Seahawks' official site reports.
story: Williams was sidelined for Sunday's game versus the Cardinals due to a shoulder injury, and now his status for Week 10 is in question. He'll likely need to return to practice in some capacity Thursday or Friday to put himself on track to play Sunday at Las Vegas.

headline: Williams (shoulder) is officially listed as out for Sunday's game versus Arizona, John Boyle of the Seahawks' official site reports.
story: Williams was not able to practice at all during the week after hurting his shoulder during Monday's game versus the Bears, and he'll be sidelined for his first contest this season in Week 9. In his absence, Mike Morris projects to see an increase in snaps on the defensive line.

headline: Williams (shoulder) did not participate at the Seahawks' practice Thursday, John Boyle of the team's official site reports.
story: Williams suffered a stinger during the team's Week 8 loss to the Bears, and he has now been forced to miss the team's first official practice of the week Thursday. The defensive lineman will have one more chance to practice Friday before he'll potentially receive an injury designation for Sunday's contest versus Arizona.

headline: Williams sustained a stinger during Monday's game against the Bears and is questionable to return.
story: The defensive end made three tackles (two solo) before exiting. Mike Morris and Rylie Mills are Seattle's available backups at defensive tackle.

headline: Williams (Achilles) was a full practice participant Friday, Gregg Bell of Sports Radio 93.3 KJR Seattle reports.
story: Williams was limited Thursday due to an Achilles issue, but it appears the problem was only minor, as the veteran defensive end upgraded to full participation Friday. As such, he doesn't seem to be at risk of missing the Monday night matchup. Williams has continued to play a key role along the Seahawks' defensive line, though he hasn't logged a sack since taking down the quarterback in each of his first three games of the campaign.

headline: Williams (Achilles) was a limited participant at the Seahawks' practice Thursday.
story: Williams opened the week with a limited session Thursday as a result of an Achilles issue. The defensive lineman's ability to practice in any capacity is a positive sign, and he will have two more chances to log a full practice prior to Monday night's matchup with Chicago.

headline: Williams (ankle) does not have an injury designation for Sunday's game against the 49ers, Bob Condotta of The Seattle Times reports.
story: Williams was a full practice participant Friday, which was enough for the veteran defensive lineman to fade an injury tag after working through an ankle issue all week. He has 13 tackles (nine solo), including 3.0 sacks, through the first four games of the regular season.

headline: Williams (ankle) did not participate at the Seahawks' practice Thursday, John Boyle of the team's official site reports.
story: Williams was limited to open the week at Wednesday's practice, but he was unable to participate one day later. He is dealing with an ankle injury, but head coach Mike Macdonald said Monday that he expects Williams to play Sunday versus the 49ers. The defensive lineman will have one more chance to practice Friday and erase any concern about his availability for Week 5.

headline: Head coach Mike Macdonald said Monday that he expects Williams (ankle) to be available for this Sunday's NFC West showdown against the 49ers, Tim Booth of The Seattle Times reports.
story: Williams suffered an ankle injury during the Seahawks' 30-23 win over the Chargers in Week 4 and did not return, finishing the game with just one quarterback hit and zero tackles. His practice participation over the coming days will shed light on his status for Week 5, but if he cannot play or operates under a snap count, then Jarran Reed and Rylie Mills would both be in line for more defensive snaps against San Francisco.

headline: Williams (ankle) is questionable to return to Sunday's game against the Chargers.
story: Prior to his departure, Williams recorded just one quarterback hit. Jarran Reed and Rylie Mills should see more snaps alongside Byron Murphy while Williams nurses his injury.

headline: Hall (back) did not participate at practice Wednesday, John Boyle of the Seahawks' official site reports.
story: Hall only played 29 of the Seahawks' 53 defensive snaps in Week 9 versus the Cardinals, and that he's dealing with a back injury might be part of the reason why. He'll probably have to upgrade to full participation at practice Thursday or Friday to avoid carrying an injury designation into the weekend.

headline: O'Toole (hamstring) was a full participant in Friday's practice, Gregg Bell of Sports Radio 93.3 KJR Seattle reports.
story: O'Toole was held out of Week 7 against the Chiefs due to a hamstring injury, but his ability to practice in full Friday indicates that he'll be available against the Bears on Monday. He has three tackles (one solo) and one fumble recovery across four regular-season games while contributing mostly on special teams.

headline: O'Toole (hamstring) is inactive for Sunday night's game against the Chiefs.
story: The second-year linebacker has played almost exclusively on special teams across 12 career regular-season appearances. He has three tackles (one solo) across four games this season.

headline: The Seahawks activated Bradford (knee) from injured reserve Saturday, and he does not carry an injury designation into Sunday's game against the Chiefs, John Boyle of the Seahawks' official site reports.
story: Bradford has been given the green light to return from a five-game absence due to a knee injury. He should reclaim his starting spot at right guard for Sunday night's game.

headline: Bradford (knee) does not have any injury designation ahead of Sunday's game against the Chiefs, John Boyle of the Seahawks' official site reports.
story: Bradford remains on IR with a knee injury but has been cleared of any injury tag tied to the issue. The Seahawks will need to decide whether to maintain the 53-man roster spot or bring Bradford back for Sunday's game.

headline: Bradford (knee) was designated to return from injured reserve by the Seahawks on Monday, John Boyle of the team's official website reports.
story: Bradford has been on IR since Sept. 23 while recovering from a knee injury, and he will now have his 21-day practice window opened ahead of Week 7. The offensive lineman is eligible to return to action against the Chiefs on Sunday, and his status at the team's first practice of the week Tuesday will shed more light on his chances to do so.

headline: The Seahawks placed Bradford (knee) on injured reserve Wednesday, John Boyle of the team's official site reports.
story: Bradford missed the team's Week 2 win over the Cardinals and will now be forced to sit out at least another four games before he's eligible to return. In his absence, Christian Haynes will likely serve as Seattle's starting right guard.

headline: Bradford (knee) has been ruled out ahead of Sunday's game against the Cardinals, John Boyle of the Seahawks' official site reports.
story: Bradford was unable to practice Friday, downgrading his participation level after two limited sessions earlier in the week. The starting right guard will be unable to suit up to defend Drew Lock, leaving Christian Haynes as the most likely option to start Sunday's game.

headline: Bradford (knee) is listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the Cardinals, John Boyle of the Seahawks' official site reports.
story: Bradford was limited in the Seahawks' first two practices of the week before sitting out Friday's session altogether. If Bradford is indeed inactive on game day, Christian Haynes is set to start at right guard.

headline: Bradford (knee) was a limited participant in practice Thursday,  Corbin K. Smith of Emerald City Spectrum reports.
story: The guard was limited Wednesday as well and is also now dealing with a hip injury, per Smith. Christian Haynes is Bradford's backup.

headline: Lock (right elbow/oblique) was limited at Wednesday's practice, John Boyle of the Seahawks' official site reports.
story: Lock is tending to a lingering right elbow injury and a new oblique issue. Head coach Mike Macdonald said tests Monday came back "good," and Lock's will be managed as Week 10 prep goes on, per Gregg Bell of Sports Radio 93.3 KJR Seattle. Lock's ability to begin the week with some practice reps generally is a good sign, but his status will continue to be watched to ensure he's good to start Sunday's contest at Las Vegas.

headline: Seahawks coach Mike Macdonald said Monday that Lock's tests on his oblique injury were "good," and the issue is something the QB is expected to manage ahead of Sunday's game against the Raiders,  Gregg Bell of The Tacoma News Tribune reports.
story: As a result, it seems likely that Lock's practice reps will be managed this week in order to prepare him for another starting assignment, with fellow signal caller Sam Darnold -- who was inactive in Week 9 -- not ready to return to the lineup this weekend. The Seahawks have a bye in Week 11, which may afford Darnold enough time to return to action Nov. 29 against the 49ers, but barring any setbacks it looks like Lock is bound to fill in again, backed up by Jalen Milroe.

headline: Seahawks coach Mike Macdonald said after Sunday's 17-3 win over the Cardinals that Lock sustained an oblique injury during the game, leaving Lock's availability for Week 10 against the Raiders up in the air, Bob Condotta of the Seattle Times reports.
story: Lock finished the win over Arizona, completing 19 of 28 passes for 175 yards and a touchdown while adding five rushing attempts for 16 yards. His lone touchdown pass was a seven-yard connection to AJ Barner with 15 seconds left in the first half. Sam Darnold (quadriceps) sat out Sunday's win and may not be ready to return against the Raiders. If both Lock and Darnold sit out, 2025 third-round pick Jalen Milroe would make his first regular-season start.

headline: Lock (right elbow) doesn't have a designation for Sunday's contest against the Cardinals, John Boyle of the Seahawks' official site reports.
story: Lock logged three consecutive limited sessions this week due to the right elbow injury that has relegated him to inactive status as the emergency third quarterback the last two games. However, with his status now cleared up for Week 9 action, he's set to fill in for Sam Darnold (quadriceps/ribs) for at least one contest. In two previous appearances (one start) in place of Darnold in Weeks 1 and 2, Lock completed 35 of 48 passes (73 percent) for 422 yards, four touchdowns and no interceptions and had two carries for 13 yards. Jalen Milroe will back up Lock on Sunday.

headline: Lock (right elbow) practiced in a limited capacity Thursday, John Boyle of the Seahawks' official site reports.
story: Lock is poised to fill in for Sam Darnold (quadriceps/ribs) this Sunday against the Cardinals, but the former still has some work to do to avoid a designation for that contest after a second straight capped session to begin Week 9 prep. Friday's injury report will reveal if Lock's right elbow issue is behind him, though he appears close to being healthy, as he told Brady Henderson of ESPN.com on Thursday that it's "doing a lot better... (It) felt great to get under center, rip some balls yesterday."

headline: Lock (right elbow) was limited at Wednesday's walkthrough, John Boyle of the Seahawks' official site reports.
story: The Seahawks ruled out Sam Darnold (quadriceps/ribs) for Sunday's game against the Cardinals, which places Lock in line for his second start of the campaign. However, Lock suffered a right elbow injury during Week 7 prep that left him as Seattle's emergency third quarterback the last two games. Assuming he gains clearance to suit up in Week 9, he'll be under center for Sunday's NFC West matchup.

headline: Lock (elbow) is slated to start Sunday's game against the Cardinals, per NFL reporter Andrew Siciliano.
story: Siciliano adds that Lock has an elbow injury that the team will manage during the week, but he's nonetheless set to get the starting assignment Sunday with fellow signal caller Sam Darnold unavailable due to quad and rib issues. Beyond this weekend, it's possible that Lock's QB1 stint could continue given that Mike Garafolo of NFL Network reports that Darnold is viewed as week-to-week, according to coach Mike Macdonald.

headline: Lock (coach's decision/elbow) is inactive for Monday's matchup with the Bears but serving as the team's emergency quarterback, John Boyle of the Seahawks' official site reports.
story: The quarterback is nursing an elbow injury and entered the day with a questionable tag. Now, he can only play against Chicago if Sam Darnold and Jalen Milroe have to exit the contest.

headline: Lock (elbow) is listed as questionable for Monday's game against the Bears, Curtis Crabtree of Fox 13 Seattle reports.
story: Lock's practice reps during Week 8 prep were limited by a lingering elbow injury on his throwing arm. He opened the season as the Seahawks' backup QB and started in Week 2 against the Cardinals, but it's possible that he operates as Seattle's emergency third quarterback for a second consecutive game. In that case, he would not be allowed to play Monday unless both Sam Darnold and Jalen Milroe were to leave the game.

headline: Lock (elbow) was a limited participant in Friday's practice, John Boyle of the Seahawks' official site reports.
story: Lock continues to work through a right elbow injury, which led to him operating as the Seahawks' emergency third quarterback against the Chiefs in Week 7. He'll have one more chance to increase his practice participation and avoid an injury designation ahead of Monday's game against the Bears.

headline: Lock (elbow) was a limited participant at the Seahawks' practice Thursday.
story: Lock remained limited at practice Thursday after logging three straight limited sessions before being ruled out for the team's Week 7 win over the Chiefs. The quarterback has been dealing with an elbow injury, and he will have two more chances to notch a full practice prior to Monday night's matchup with the Bears.

headline: Lock (elbow) is inactive but serving as the Seahawks' emergency third quarterback for Sunday night's contest against the Chiefs, Curtis Crabtree of Fox 13 Seattle reports.
story: Lock was limited at practice throughout the entire week with a right elbow injury and he will likely have the night off Sunday. Lock will only be eligible to enter the game if both starter Sam Darnold and primary backup Jalen Milroe are unable to continue.

headline: Lock (elbow) is listed as questionable ahead of Sunday's game against the Chiefs, John Boyle of the Seahawks' official site reports.
story: Lock logged three consecutive limited practices during Week 7 prep. The backup quarterback's throwing arm remains a problem, leaving it unclear whether he will suit up for Sunday's game or if Jalen Milroe will be active for the contest.

headline: Lock (elbow) was a limited practice participant Thursday, John Boyle of the Seahawks' official site reports.
story: Lock has now been limited in each of Seattle's past five practice sessions, though he was able to suit up last Thursday against Denver. It seems likely that he'll be active again for this Sunday's matchup against Kansas City, though Seattle's practice report Friday should provide more clarity in that regard. If Lock does indeed suit up Sunday, he'll again work as Sam Darnold's backup.

headline: Lock (elbow) was a limited participant in Wednesday's practice, Corbin K. Smith of EmeraldCitySpectrum.com reports.
story: Lock remains limited in practice as the string of arm issues continues. The backup quarterback will need to practice both Thursday and Friday to have a shot at avoiding an injury designation ahead of Sunday's game against the Chiefs.

headline: Lock (forearm) won't carry an injury designation into Thursday night's matchup with Denver, John Boyle of the Seahawks' official site reports.
story: Lock remained limited at practice for the third straight day Friday as he continues to deal with a right forearm injury, but the quarterback will be good to go for Week 6. The 29-year-old will operate in his typical role as the team's primary backup behind starting quarterback Sam Darnold on Thursday night versus the Broncos.

headline: The Seahawks listed Lock (forearm) as a limited practice participant on Tuesday's estimated report, Curtis Crabtree of Fox 13 Seattle reports.
story: Lock is working through a right forearm injury. Jalen Milroe would step in as Seattle's backup QB behind Sam Darnold if Lock is not cleared to play against Denver on Thursday.

headline: Lock (forearm) was listed as a limited participant on Monday's estimated practice report, John Boyle of the Seahawks' official site reports.
story: It's unclear when Lock picked up the injury, given that he did not play a single snap during Sunday's 32-29 loss to San Francisco. He's got two more chances to increase his practice participation, but if he cannot play against the Broncos on Thursday, then Jalen Milroe would serve as the Seahawks' backup quarterback behind Sam Darnold.

headline: Lock will return to a backup role for Sunday's game at Washington after coach Mike Macdonald said Friday that Sam Darnold (glute) is "going to play," John Boyle of the Seahawks' official site reports.
story: After Darnold suffered a right glute injury on Seattle's first possession of the season Week 1 against the Patriots, Lock directed the offense for the next seven-plus quarters, leading the team to two victories while completing 35 of 48 passes (73 percent) for 422 yards, four touchdowns and no interceptions and rushing twice for 13 yards. With Darnold back in action this weekend, though, Lock's time as the starter is over for now.

headline: Lock completed 19 of 26 passes for 235 yards with three touchdowns and no interceptions in Sunday's 31-7 victory over Arizona.
story: Lock didn't make it too hard on himself, looking for superstar wide receiver Jaxon Smith-Njigba early and often. The duo connected for an 82-yard score in the first quarter before later adding touchdowns of seven and 12 yards in the second half. Lock has tossed four touchdowns over the first two weeks, all of which have been to Smith-Njigba. The quarterback has completed 35 of 48 passes for 422 yards with four scores so far this season, and he could be asked to start another contest Week 3 versus the Commanders while Sam Darnold (hip) continues to recover.

headline: Lock will start Week 2 against the Cardinals with Sam Darnold (glute) unavailable, Curtis Crabtree of Fox 13 in Seattle reports.
story: Darnold will miss Week 2 as expected, prompting the Seahawks to tab Lock as the starter. Lock was competent in relief of Darnold in the season opener, completing 16 of 22 passes for 187 yards and a touchdown. Importantly, Lock was clean on the turnover front. He will lead the Seahawks for at least the upcoming road game against the Cardinals, which puts him on the radar in superflex and two-quarterback formats.

headline: Shaheed (knee) was a full participant in Wednesday's practice, John Boyle of the Seahawks' official site reports.
story: Shaheed suffered a knee injury during a Week 7 win against the Chiefs and missed the last two games as a result. Now that he's unhindered on the practice field, though, he'll resume his standing as Seattle's No. 2 WR and primary kick and punt returner

headline: Shaheed (knee) is listed as out for Sunday's game against the Cardinals, Gregg Bell of 933 KJR reports.
story: With Shaheed out last week, Tory Horton handled a 72 percent route share in Seattle's loss to Chicago. It'll likely be a similar look this week with Horton and Cooper Kupp taking most of the WR snaps alongside Jaxon Smith-Njigba. The big difference will be under center, where Drew Lock is filling in for Sam Darnold (quad) for the second time this season.

headline: Shaheed (knee) didn't participate at the Seahawks' practice Thursday, John Boyle of the team's official site reports.
story: Shaheed has now missed back-to-back practices to open the week as he continues to work his way back from the knee injury that forced him to miss the team's Week 8 loss to Chicago. The wide receiver's chances to play Sunday versus Arizona seem thin, so Tory Horton could serve as the team's No. 3 option at wide receiver again in Week 9.

headline: Shaheed (knee) did not practice Wednesday, John Boyle of the Seahawks' official site reports.
story: Shaheed missed Monday night's loss to the Bears, which allowed Tory Horton to log a season-high 43 offensive snaps, which he turned into a 3-26-0 receiving line on six targets. Horton would again be in line for WR3 duties if Shaheed needs to sit Sunday against Arizona.

headline: Seahawks head coach Mike Macdonald said Tuesday that Shaheed (knee) has a chance to play Sunday against the Cardinals, Brady Henderson of ESPN.com reports.
story: Shaheed was sidelined for the first time all season in Monday's 34-17 loss to the Bears, after his knee injury kept him from practicing throughout the week. In Shaheed's absence, Tory Horton handled elevated snaps as the Seahawks' No. 3 wideout behind Jaxon Smith-Njigba and Cooper Kupp, while George Holani served as the team's top kickoff returner. Shaheed may need to turn in a full practice at some point during Week 9 prep to put himself on track to return to action Sunday.

headline: Shaheed (knee) has been ruled out for Monday's game against the Bears, Curtis Crabtree of FOX 13 Seattle reports.
story: Shaheed will miss his first game of the 2026 season due to a knee injury that he sustained during the Seahawks' Week 7 win over the Chiefs. Tory Horton and Velus Jones are the top candidates to operate as Seattle's returners on kickoffs and punts, and Horton and Cooper Kupp should see a bump in offensive snaps in Shaheed's absence. Shaheed's next opportunity to play is Week 9 against the Cardinals on Sunday, Nov. 8.

headline: Shaheed (knee) didn't practice Friday, John Boyle of the Seahawks' official site reports.
story: Shaheed suffered a knee injury in the first half of this past Sunday's win against the Chiefs and wasn't able to return. Since then, head coach Mike Macdonald told Brady Henderson of ESPN.com that the "early returns are positive" on Shaheed, but with no on-field work yet this week he likely will need to mix into drills Saturday to have a chance to play Monday versus the Bears.

headline: Shaheed (knee) did not practice Thursday, John Boyle of the Seahawks' official site reports.
story: Shaheed was injured in last Sunday night's win over the Chiefs, but indications are he avoided a serious injury. If he's unable to play Monday night against the Bears, Tory Horton will slot into WR3 duties behind Jaxon Smith-Njigba and Cooper Kupp.

headline: Shaheed (knee) is unlikely to practice Thursday, Curtis Crabtree of Fox 13 Seattle reports.
story: Coach Mike Macdonald provided the update Thursday, stating that the wideout is "doing well" but was not quite ready to return to practice. Shaheed exited Sunday's win over the Chiefs with a knee injury, which is not expected to keep him out long-term. He gets an extra day to rehab as the Seahawks get ready for their Monday Night Football matchup with the Bears.

headline: Seahawks coach Mike Macdonald said Monday that the early returns on Shaheed's knee injury are positive, Brady Henderson reports.
story: Shaheed logged 22 snaps and caught two of his three targets for one yard before exiting Sunday's 20-3 win over the Chiefs. While Macdonald's initial assessment of the wideout's knee issue is encouraging, Shaheed's status will nonetheless be worth monitoring as next Monday's game against the Bears approaches.

headline: Shaheed (knee) won't return to Sunday's game against the Chiefs.
story: Shaheed didn't return after halftime due to a knee injury. The wide receiver and standout special teams return man will have an extra day to recover before the Seahawks face the Bears on MNF in Week 8.

headline: Shaheed (knee) is questionable to return to Sunday's game against the Chiefs, Curtis Crabtree of FOX 13 Seattle reports.
story: Shaheed didn't come out for the second half, as Tory Horton returned the second-half kickoff in Shaheed's stead. Prior to getting hurt, Shaheed caught two of three targets for one yard while adding a 32-yard punt return.

headline: Shaheed (hip) was a full participant in Thursday's practice, John Boyle of the Seahawks' official site reports.
story: Shaheed was limited Wednesday but appears to be on track for his normal role Sunday against the Chiefs. Playing behind Jaxon Smith-Njigba and Cooper Kupp in an offense that likes to use multiple tight ends, Shaheed has yet to get going in the receiving department this season, as he has just 14 catches for 162 yards through six contests.

headline: Shaheed (hip) was limited in Wednesday's practice, Corbin K. Smith of EmeraldCitySpectrum.com reports.
story: It's the first time Shaheed has been listed on the injury report this season. A popular summer breakout candidate, it hasn't yet happened for Shaheed this season, as he has just 14 catches for 162 yards on 27 targets through six games. He's added 39 rushing yards and a touchdown on four carries. Shaheed can't be trusted in fantasy lineups until he shows some sort of reliable floor or even a ceiling performance.

headline: Shaheed brought in five of eight targets for 66 yards, rushed once for two yards, returned three kickoffs for 77 yards and ran back three punts for 39 yards in the Seahawks' 17-14 overtime loss to the Broncos on Thursday. He also caught a two-point conversion pass and committed two fumbles, recovering one.
story: Shaheed's extremely busy stat line included season-high totals across all three components of his receiving line. The veteran speedster tied for second in receptions and was the runner-up in receiving yards as well for the Seahawks on the night, but his lost fumble likely cost Seattle points since it was recovered at the Broncos' 34-yard line late in the first half. Shaheed did provide a critical two-point conversion grab after a George Holani fourth-quarter touchdown to bring the Seahawks within three points, and Shaheed also was the intended target on Sam Darnold's interception in overtime that led to Denver's game-winning field goal. Shaheed will carry a modest 14-162-0 line on 27 targets into a Week 7 home showdown with the Chiefs on Sunday, Oct. 25.

headline: Shaheed caught two of four targets for 23 yards while also adding 86 kickoff-return yards during Sunday's 32-29 loss to the 49ers.
story: Shaheed was held to two or fewer catches for the fourth time in five games, and he has yet to score a touchdown through the air this year. The wide receiver played a season-low 28 offensive snaps in Week 5, and his upside is rather low as a fantasy asset at the moment. On the year, Shaheed has caught nine of 19 targets for 96 yards while adding three carries for 37 yards and a touchdown and 359 yards as a kick returner.

headline: Shaheed caught one of three targets for 20 yards in Sunday's 30-23 win over the Chargers. He added two carries for 33 yards and a touchdown.
story: Shaheed had been mostly nonexistent through the first three games of the season, totaling 57 yards on seven touches, but he was able to break out for a long touchdown in this one, scoring from 28 yards out as a rusher in the second quarter. With Jaxon Smith-Njigba completely dominating the targets in Seattle's passing game, Shaheed has remained a low-floor fantasy option early on in 2026.

headline: Shaheed caught two passes on three targets for 14 yards during the Seahawks' 33-31 loss to the Commanders on Sunday, He also returned three punts for 29 yards and added 63 yards on two kickoff returns.
story: Shaheed continued to operate as the Seahawks' primary return man, and his 31 offensive snaps were third-most among Seattle wide receivers behind Jaxon Smith-Njigba (58) and Cooper Kupp (45). Shaheed has yet to find the end zone this season, with his last touchdown taking place in the 2025 NFC divisional round against the 49ers, when he took the game's opening kickoff 95 yards to the house. The Seahawks will play five of their next six games at home, starting this Sunday against the winless Chargers.

headline: Shaheed caught three of six targets for 35 yards while also adding a four-yard rush, 29 yards on three punt returns and two kickoff returns for 47 yards during Sunday's 31-7 win over Arizona.
story: Shaheed found himself more involved as a pass catcher during Week 2, finishing second on the team in both targets and catches behind Jaxon Smith-Njigba. The wide receiver logged 39 snaps on offense, which was nine more than Cooper Kupp (30) in the contest. Shaheed will look to continue to establish himself as the No. 2 option at wide receiver Week 3 versus the Commanders.

headline: Wilson didn't log any snaps during Sunday's win over the Cardinals.
story: Wilson averaged 18.2 carries for 66.7 yards over six games between Week 2 and Week 7, culminating with a 24-100-1 rushing line against Kansas City. However, that opportunity came while Jadarian Price and Zach Charbonnet were on IR. Both running backs returned ahead of the Week 8 matchup against Chicago, and Wilson hasn't played a single offensive snap in two games since. As long as Charbonnet and Price are both healthy, it appears Wilson is going to be relegated primarily to a special-teams role, if he plays at all.

headline: Wilson played just seven snaps -- all on special teams -- in Monday's 34-17 loss to the Bears.
story: After logging double-digit carries in six of the Seahawks' previous seven games while scoring four touchdowns and averaging 66.4 scrimmage yards during that span, Wilson fell out of the game plan entirely in Week 8. With Zach Charbonnet (knee) getting cleared to make his 2026 debut, Jadarian Price (chest) returning from injured reserve and George Holani still on hand as an option on passing downs, the Seahawks had no reps available out of the backfield for Wilson. Unless Charbonnet or Price succumbs to another injury, Wilson's playing time on offense will likely remain scarce moving forward.

headline: Wilson is welcoming back Zach Charbonnet (knee) and Jadarian Price (chest) to the Seahawks backfield for Monday's game against the Bears, John Boyle of the team's official site reports.
story: Seattle cleared Charbonnet to make his season debut on its final Week 8 injury report before the team activated Price from injured reserve Monday, which means the latter is available for his first game action since Week 3. Wilson operated as the Seahawks' lead runner the last four contests, racking up 85 touches for 359 yards from scrimmage and four total TDs. He'll certainly cede some of those reps to the combination of Charbonnet and Price, but the possibility exists that he ends up taking on the most work among the trio if the team eases one or both back in.

headline: Wilson rushed 24 times for 100 yards and a touchdown while catching his lone target for 15 yards in Sunday's 20-3 win over the Chiefs.
story: Wilson recorded the second 100-yard rushing performance of his career, having accomplished that feat in Week 12 of last season with the Packers. He put the game away with a 21-yard rushing touchdown with 3:47 remaining in the fourth quarter. That was his third touchdown run in the past four games, during which Wilson has racked up 294 rushing yards on 79 carries (3.7 YPC), covering for lackluster efficiency with heavy rushing volume. He could face a significant influx of competition for carries as soon as Week 8 against the Bears, as Jadarian Price (chest) will be eligible to return from IR, while Zach Charbonnet (knee), who was inactive Sunday, could make his season debut after being activated from the reserve/PUP list Thursday.

headline: Wilson will be the lead back for Sunday's game against the Chiefs after Zach Charbonnet (knee) was ruled out ahead of that contest, John Boyle of the Seahawks' official site reports.
story: Charbonnet was a full participant in practice all week and was activated from the reserve/PUP list Thursday. However, he's not been given the green light to play, which means Wilson will lead the Seahawks' backfield yet again for Sunday's contest while George Holani and Velus Jones provide depth. Wilson has logged at least 20 carries in three of the Seahawks' last five games, and over that span he has turned 85 rushes into 300 yards and two touchdowns while catching five passes (on eight targets) for 50 yards and a score.

headline: Wilson rushed 14 times for 52 yards and failed to bring in his only target in the Seahawks' 17-14 overtime loss to the Broncos on Thursday.
story: Wilson had 12 of his 14 carries in regulation while once again serving as the Seahawks' lead back, and he averaged under 4.0 yards per rush attempt for the fourth straight game. He was held without a catch for the first time in three contests, however, capping his overall fantasy production in the low-scoring defeat. Zach Charbonnet (knee) has been back at practice for the last two weeks and must be activated from the reserve/PUP list by next Thursday to avoid having to miss the rest of the season, so Wilson's days in a meaningful role appear to be drawing to a close.

headline: Wilson rushed 20 times for 61 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 32-29 loss to the 49ers. He also caught both of his targets for 11 yards and lost a fumble.
story: Wilson followed up his two-touchdown performance in Week 4 against the Chargers with a two-yard rushing score in the first quarter against the 49ers, but he proceeded to lose a fumble in the second quarter. Fellow running back George Holani also lost a fumble, and Sam Darnold threw two interceptions in a sloppy performance from Seattle's offense. Zach Charbonnet (knee) isn't expected to be activated from the reserve/PUP list ahead of Thursday's game against the Broncos, while Jadarian Price (chest) remains on IR, so Wilson is poised to remain Seattle's lead back in Week 6.

headline: Wilson racked up 21 carries for 81 yards and one touchdown and added three catches (on four targets) for 39 yards and another TD during Sunday's 30-23 win versus the Chargers.
story: In the wake of Jadarian Price's placement on injured reserve due to a chest issue, Wilson got the first chance to pace the Seahawks backfield, and he parlayed the second-highest touch count of his career into his second ever outing with 100-plus yards from scrimmage and his second two-TD performance. Meanwhile, fellow RB George Holani received eight touches, which he turned into 20 total yards. Until Zach Charbonnet (knee, reserve/PUP list) is able to return to action, Wilson figures to be Seattle's lead runner.

headline: With Jadarian Price (chest) out for Sunday's game against the Chargers, Wilson is expected to take on an expanded role out of the backfield, Gregg Bell of The Tacoma News Tribune reports.
story: Wilson actually leads the Seahawks in carries (32) this season, but he's been splitting work with Price (28 carries) and George Holani (15) in what has been a three-man weave out of the backfield. Wilson is averaging just 3.4 yards per carry but could flirt with 20 rushing attempts Sunday, putting him very much in the fantasy RB2/3 mix.

headline: Wilson turned nine carries into 14 yards during the Seahawks' 33-31 loss to the Commanders on Sunday.
story: Wilson saw his role expand during a Week 2 win over the Cardinals after Jadarian Price left the game due to a chest injury, taking 21 carries for 92 yards. Wilson returned to a rotational role alongside George Holani in Week 3 after Price was cleared to play, but the former Packer still led the backfield with nine carries. Wilson has 32 carries for 109 yards (3.4 YPC) through the first three games of the season, and it looks like the Seahawks may be shifting to a committee approach with Price not yet seizing the lead role -- a committee that will get more crowded when Zach Charbonnet (knee) eventually comes off the PUP list.

headline: Wilson will be the Seahawks' RB2 for Sunday's game against the Commanders after Jadarian Price (chest) was cleared to play, John Boyle of the team's official site reports.
story: Wilson ended up logging 21 carries for 92 yards during the Seahawks' Week 2 win over the Cardinals, with most of those touches coming after Price left the game in the fourth quarter due to a chest injury. Price doesn't have a designation for Week 3, so Wilson and George Holani will provide backfield depth for Sunday's road tilt.

headline: Wilson rushed 21 times for 92 yards and failed to catch his only target in Sunday's 31-7 win over Arizona.
story: Wilson stepped into a larger workload Week 2, partially due to rookie running back Jadarian Price exiting the game with a chest injury in the fourth quarter. The 92 rushing yards were Wilson's highest total since he notched 107 yards and two scores on 28 totes in Week 12 of the 2025 campaign while with the Packers. Wilson could handle the lion's share of touches in the backfield against the Commanders in Week 3 if Price is forced to miss the contest.

headline: Kupp caught three of four targets for 32 yards during the Seahawks' 17-3 win over the Cardinals on Sunday.
story: All three of Kupp's catches came on the same offensive drive midway through the third quarter, which ended with a 45-yard field goal by Jason Myers. The Seahawks had Drew Lock under center due to the absence of Sam Darnold (quadriceps/ribs), but Lock is now dealing with an oblique injury that could prevent him from playing in Week 10 against the Raiders on Nov. 15. Jalen Milroe would be the next man up at quarterback for Seattle, which would lower the floors for Kupp and the rest of the Seahawks' pass catchers. Kupp has a 22-238-2 receiving line on 34 targets through nine regular-season games.

headline: Kupp caught one of three targets for a seven-yard touchdown Monday in a loss to the Bears.
story: Kupp had another low target share, but he at least made the most of his only catch by hauling in a seven-yard TD early in the fourth quarter. That score probably isn't going to be enough to inspire confidence in him in fantasy, though, given that the veteran wideout has drawn three or fewer targets in six of his eight games this season. Kupp's seven receiving yards Monday also were a season-low mark, and there simply doesn't seem to be much room for any wideout aside from Jaxon Smith-Njigba to regularly find success in Seattle's offense given Smith-Njigba's massive target share. With that said, Kupp at least will have a favorable matchup in Week 9, as he'll face an Arizona defense that has surrendered 11 receiving TDs to wideouts this season, tied for the most in the NFL.

headline: Kupp caught both of his targets for 20 yards in a 20-3 win over the Chiefs on Sunday.
story: Kupp entered Sunday's contest on the heels of a 10-target performance against the Broncos in Week 6. However, the veteran wideout saw only two looks from Sam Darnold, with the veteran quarterback relying heavily on favorite target Jaxon Smith-Njigba, who finished with a 9-150-1 line on 12 targets. Kupp has logged three targets or fewer in five of seven regular-season games, though he could see a slight bump in opportunities if Rashid Shaheed (knee) is unable to play against the Bears in Week 8.

headline: Kupp caught five of 10 targets for 50 yards during the Seahawks' 17-14 overtime loss to the Broncos on Thursday.
story: Kupp accumulated 15 targets through the first five games of the regular season, but the veteran wide receiver was peppered Thursday by Sam Darnold, who attempted a season-high 51 passes. It was the first time since Week 12 of the 2024 season (with the Rams) that Kupp saw double-digit targets, and he finished second in that category Thursday behind Jaxon Smith-Njigba (16). Kupp's best days are behind him, but he's a valuable safety blanket for Darnold in the passing game. Kupp will bring a 16-179-1 receiving line (25 targets) into Seattle's Week 7 bout against the Chiefs on Sunday, Oct. 25.

headline: Kupp caught two of three passes for 15 yards during Sunday's 32-29 loss to the 49ers.
story: It was the fourth time in five games this season that Kupp saw three targets or fewer, with Jaxon Smith-Njigba pacing the Seahawks' pass catchers with a 5-102-1 receiving line on eight targets during Sunday's loss. There's no expectation that Kupp will recapture the form he had during his tenure with the Rams, and he figures to be limited to a complementary role in the Seahawks' offense. That said, Smith-Njigba has popped up on each of Seattle's first two estimated practice reports as a limited participant due to an ankle injury. That is worth monitoring ahead of Thursday night's road game against the Broncos, whose defense will likely be without star outside cornerback Pat Surtain (ankle).

headline: Kupp caught one of two targets for 13 yards in Sunday's 30-23 win over the Chargers.
story: Kupp played 34 of 60 offensive snaps and ran 17 routes on Sam Darnold's 26 dropbacks. The veteran wide receiver has failed to reach 50 receiving yards in any of the first four games, totaling nine grabs for 114 yards and a touchdown on 12 targets. He's well off the fantasy radar with Jaxon Smith-Njigba dominating the looks in Seattle.

headline: Kupp caught four of five targets for 46 yards and a touchdown during Sunday's 33-31 loss to the Commanders.
story: Kupp was able to take advantage of the return of quarterback Sam Darnold in Week 3, connecting with Darnold for a seven-yard score with 2:55 left in the fourth quarter. The wide receiver doubled his season total in targets Sunday, and he has now caught eight of 10 targets for 101 yards and a touchdown over three games so far in his second season with Seattle.

headline: Kupp (back) was a full participant at the Seahawks' practice Thursday, Brady Henderson of ESPN.com reports.
story: Kupp opened the week with a limited practice due to a back injury, but he now appears to be back to full health. It is the second straight week that the wide receiver has been limited Wednesday before logging a full session Thursday. He'll look to take advantage of the return of quarterback Sam Darnold (glute) on Sunday against the Commanders.

headline: Kupp (back) was limited in Wednesday's practice, John Boyle of the Seahawks' official site reports.
story: The veteran receiver dealt with the back issue in practice last Wednesday before being upgraded to full work Thursday. He could follow a similar path this week. Kupp has just four catches for 55 yards on five targets through two games, as Jaxon Smith-Njigba has dominated the targets and big plays for Seattle.

headline: Kupp caught both of his targets for 20 yards in Sunday's 31-7 victory versus Arizona.
story: Kupp wasn't very productive, but that was the case for all of Seattle's wideouts aside from Jaxon Smith-Njigba, who dominated with nine catches for 155 yards and one touchdown. The only other Seahawks player to log more than Kupp's two targets was Rashid Shaheed, who put up a 3-35-0 line on six targets. Through two weeks, Kupp has tallied a modest four receptions for 55 yards. With Smith-Njigba dominating the targets in Seattle's passing game, Kupp may struggle to put up consistent production this season.

headline: Kupp (back) was a full participant at the Seahawks' practice Thursday, Bob Condotta of The Seattle Times reports.
story: Kupp opened the week with a limited session Wednesday as a result of a back injury, but he was able to erase any concern about his availability for Week 2 with a full practice one day later. The wide receiver caught two of three targets for 35 yards in the team's 13-10 win over New England on Sept. 9, and he'll be working with Drew Lock at quarterback against the Cardinals on Sunday.

headline: Kupp was a limited participant in Wednesday's practice due to a back injury, John Boyle of the Seahawks' official site reports.
story: Kupp may have tweaked his back during the Seahawks' 13-10 win over the Patriots in Week 1, when he played 39 of 50 snaps on offense (78.0 percent) and finished with two catches on three targets for 35 yards. Kupp's status for Sunday's NFC West tilt against the Cardinals doesn't appear to be in serious jeopardy, and he'll have two more chances to increase his practice participation and avoid an injury designation for Week 2. The Seahawks' pass catchers figure to see a downtick in production with Drew Lock starting at quarterback for the injured Sam Darnold (lower body).

headline: Pili (back) has been ruled out to face Arizona on Sunday, John Boyle of the Seahawks' official site reports.
story: Pili has missed four games this season, including last Monday's loss to Chicago. He'll be sidelined again this Sunday, as he's dealing with a back injury. Pili's absence probably won't make huge waves in the Seahawks' defensive rotations, as he's logged just 19 defensive snaps through four contests.

headline: Pili (back) is inactive for Monday night's game against the Bears, John Boyle of the Seahawks' official site reports.
story: The nose tackle popped up on the injury report with a back issue Friday and missed the last two practice sessions of the week. Pili has only played 19 defensive snaps in four games this season.

headline: Pili (neck) was a full practice participant Wednesday and Thursday, John Boyle of the Seahawks' official site reports.
story: Pili didn't play against Washington in Week 3 but appears to be good to go for this Sunday's matchup versus the Chargers. However, he was a nominal part of Seattle's defense over the first two weeks, logging just six defensive snaps and four snaps on special teams.

headline: Pili (concussion) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Commanders.
story: Pili drew the questionable tag for Sunday after ending Week 3 prep with back-to-back limited practices. He has not progressed enough in the league's concussion protocol to play against Washington, and his next chance to take the field is Week 4 against the Chargers on Sunday, Oct. 4. Rylie Mills and Mike Morris are both in line to see a slight bump in defensive snaps due to Pili's absence.

headline: Pili (concussion) has been ruled out for the remainder of Sunday's game against the Cardinals, John Boyle of the Seahawks' official site reports.
story: Pili has entered the league's concussion protocol and will miss the rest of Sunday's game. The defensive tackle will need to progress through the five-step protocol and be cleared by an independent neurologist to return to the field. Rylie Mills is now the sole reserve defensive tackle available to the Seahawks in Sunday's game.

headline: Pili (head) is being evaluated for a potential concussion after exiting Sunday's game against the Cardinals.
story: Pili exited the first quarter of Sunday's game with a head injury. The defensive tackle will be evaluated by the Seahawks' medical staff as well as an independent neurologist to determine if Pili has suffered a concussion or if he's cleared to return.

headline: Nelson underwent a minor procedure on his injured knee Monday, Gregg Bell of Sports Radio 93.3 KJR Seattle reports.
story: Nelson is currently considered week-to-week, although head coach Mike Macdonald said the team isn't planning to place Nelson on injured reserve. The 2018 first-round pick will likely target the Week 12 matchup versus San Francisco to make his return, and Grey Zabel will likely start at left guard in his absence.

headline: Nelson (knee) has been ruled out ahead of Sunday's game against the Cardinals, Gregg Bell of Sports Radio 93.3 KJR Seattle reports.
story: Nelson is set for knee surgery due to an issue the veteran offensive guard has been having with cartilage fragments. Ian Rapoport of NFL Network said Friday that the plan is for Nelson to avoid IR and return to the Seahawks after the team's Week 11 bye. Grey Zabel is set to start at left guard for Sunday's game.

headline: Nelson (knee) did not participate at the Seahawks' practice Thursday, John Boyle of the team's official site reports.
story: Nelson was listed as a limited participant at the team's walkthrough practice Wednesday, but he took a step backwards at the team's first official practice of the week. The offensive lineman made his Seattle debut in Monday night's loss to the Bears, and he appears to have picked up a knee injury in the contest. Nelson will have one more opportunity to return to practice before Sunday's contest against Arizona.

headline: The Seahawks acquired Nelson from the Colts on Tuesday in exchange for a 2027 third-round draft pick and a 2028 fifth-round draft pick, Adam Schefter and Ian Rapoport of ESPN report.
story: After a 2-5 start to the season, the Colts already found themselves on the periphery of the AFC playoff picture and opted to cash out on the eight-time Pro Bowl left guard before he became an unrestricted free agent this offseason. In Seattle, Nelson will join 2025 first-round pick Grey Zabel to form one of the NFL's better guard tandems. The Seahawks are hoping that the addition of Nelson can help open up more running room for a ground attack that has averaged just 3.9 yards per carry through the first seven weeks of the season.

headline: Nwosu (ankle) is officially listed as out for Sunday's game versus the Cardinals, John Boyle of the Seahawks' official site reports.
story: Nwosu sat out Monday's game versus the Bears with an ankle injury, and after missing practice Thursday and Friday, he'll miss his second straight game in Week 9. With Nwosu in street clothes, Derick Hall should start on the edge opposite veteran DeMarcus Lawrence on Sunday.

headline: Nwosu (ankle) is inactive for Monday's clash with the Bears, John Boyle of the Seahawks' official site reports.
story: The linebacker didn't practice all week and came into the day with a doubtful tag. Derick Hall should be the next man up to replace him.

headline: Nwosu (hip) is active for Sunday Night Football versus Kansas City.
story: Nwosu is good to go for Week 7, as expected. The linebacker failed to record a tackle for the first time this season in the team's Week 6 loss to the Broncos, and he figures to have plenty of chances to get back on track against the Chiefs.

headline: Ian Rapoport of NFL Network reports that Nwosu (hip) is expected to be cleared to play against the Chiefs on Sunday.
story: Nwosu popped up on Thursday's injury report as a limited practice participant due to a hip injury. His practice reps were restricted again Friday, but it looks like the veteran linebacker will be a go for Sunday night's contest. Nwosu has accumulated 15 tackles (nine solo), including 1.0 sacks, three pass defenses and one forced fumble through six regular-season games.

headline: Cross (ankle) has been ruled out for Sunday's Week 9 tilt against the Cardinals, John Boyle of the Seahawks' official site reports.
story: Cross will miss his second straight game while tending to a high-ankle sprain he suffered in Week 7 against Kansas City. He wasn't able to participate in practice at all this week, and it's unclear when he'll be ready to return to the fold. Josh Jones could start again at left tackle in Cross's stead Sunday.

headline: Cross (ankle) did not participate at the Seahawks' practice Thursday, John Boyle of the team's official site reports.
story: Cross was considered as a non-participant at the team's walkthrough practice Wednesday, and he has now missed the team's first official practice of the week. The offensive lineman hasn't practiced at all since suffering an ankle injury in Week 7 against Kansas City, and he appears to be trending towards missing a second straight game Sunday versus the Cardinals.

headline: Cross (ankle) has been ruled out for Monday's game against the Bears, John Boyle of the Seahawks' official site reports.
story: Cross was held out of practice all week due to an ankle injury he suffered during the Seahawks' Week 7 win over the Chiefs. Josh Jones will likely start at left tackle in the absence of Cross, whose next chance to play is Week 9 against the Cardinals on Sunday, Nov. 8.

headline: Cross underwent an MRI and was diagnosed with a high ankle sprain, Ian Rapoport of NFL Network reports.
story: Cross suffered the injury during Sunday's win over the Chiefs. While an official return date hasn't been established, there is hope he can get back on the field in "one or two weeks." With Cross on the shelf, Josh Jones is the favorite to start in Week 8 versus Chicago and beyond.

headline: Cross exited Sunday night's game against the Chiefs with an ankle injury and did not return.
story: With Cross out, veteran Josh Jones took over at left tackle for Seattle. Cross will have an extra day to try and get ready for next Monday night's game against the Bears.

headline: Darnold (quadriceps), who won't play this coming Sunday at Las Vegas, is expected to return in Week 12 at San Francisco on Sunday, Nov. 29 after a Week 11 bye, Gregg Bell of Sports Radio 93.3 KJR Seattle reports.
story: Darnold is one week removed from suffering a quad injury and cracked ribs in a Week 8 loss to the Bears, which sidelined him Sunday against the Cardinals and will keep him in street clothes in Week 10. For as long as Darnold is sidelined, Drew Lock (oblique) is lined up to be the Seahawks' starting quarterback.

headline: Seahawks head coach Mike Macdonald said Monday that Darnold (quadriceps/ribs) won't be available for Sunday's game against the Raiders, John Boyle of the team's official site reports.
story: Meanwhile, Macdonald noted that the Seahawks got a "good exam" for Drew Lock, who is nursing an oblique injury but is expected to be able to play through the issue and make a second straight start in Week 10. With a bye on tap for the Seahawks in Week 11, Darnold will benefit from some extended time to recover from his injuries and will turn his focus toward returning to action Nov. 29 versus the 49ers.
